title: Run pySCENIC
text:
In this part, we will run the pySCENIC pipeline. This pipeline has three parts and especially the first part requires a lot of computational power. Although this could in theory be done on a personal computer, I recommend using the TSCC for that.
In addition to the loom file we created in the previous part, we need some additional files for the mouse genome and mouse transcription factors. These can be downloaded from the SCENIC website. We need the
The last three files can be found on https://resources.aertslab.org/cistarget/

title: Run pySCENIC
text:
Run SCENIC
More details on the workflow can be found in this publication.

Infer gene regulatory network
In the first step a gene regulatory network is created. This is the most computational intensive step. I did have some issues to get this working on the supercomputer (for some reasons that I did not understand the dask framework caused an error). But using a fallback option by running arboreto_with_multiprocessing.py work flawlessly. The downside of that is, that I cannot use multiple nodes (but it can use multiple cores).
Create a file called pyscenic_grn.sh with the following content. Make sure to adapt e-mail address and paths in the script for your needs. Make sure, that you have the conda environment created on the supercomputer too.
#!/bin/bash
#PBS -q home-yeo
#PBS -N pyscenic_grn
#PBS -l nodes=1:ppn=16
#PBS -l walltime=30:00:00
#PBS -o pyscenic_grn.out
#PBS -e pyscenic_grn.err
#PBS -m abe
#PBS -M mheeg@ucsd.edu

echo "running"

# activate conda
source /home/mheeg/mambaforge/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate pyscenic

#navigate to project folder
cd /home/mheeg/scratch/pySCENIC

# this in the command that would use the dask framework.
# pyscenic grn 'pySCENIC_input.loom' 'mm_mgi_tfs.txt' -o adj.tsv --num_workers 16

# this is the command without dask
arboreto_with_multiprocessing.py \
    pySCENIC_input.loom \
    mm_mgi_tfs.txt \
    --method grnboost2 \
    --output adj.tsv \
    --num_workers 16 \
    --seed 777

# when this is done, we can automatially sumbit the next job
# but you can also do this manually
echo "submitting next job"
qsub pyscenic_ctx.sh

echo "done"
Finally, submit the job by running qsub pyscenic_grn.sh. For my dataset, this step took approximately 14 hours.


Module generation and Motif enrichment and TF-regulon prediction
Again create a files called pyscenic_ctx.sh
#!/bin/bash
#PBS -q home-yeo
#PBS -N pyscenic_ctx
#PBS -l nodes=1:ppn=16
#PBS -l walltime=12:00:00
#PBS -o pyscenic_ctx.out
#PBS -e pyscenic_ctx.err
#PBS -m abe
#PBS -M mheeg@ucsd.edu

echo "running"

# activate conda
source /home/mheeg/mambaforge/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate pyscenic

#navigate to project folder
cd /home/mheeg/scratch/pySCENIC

# --mode 'custom_multiprocessing` because I had issued with dask....
pyscenic ctx adj.tsv mm10__refseq-r80__10kb_up_and_down_tss.mc9nr.feather  mm10__refseq-r80__500bp_up_and_100bp_down_tss.mc9nr.feather --annotations_fname 'motifs-v9-nr.mgi-m0.001-o0.0.tbl' --expression_mtx_fname 'pySCENIC_input.loom'  --output 'motifs.csv'  --num_workers 16 --mode 'custom_multiprocessing'

# submit next job
echo "submitting next job"
qsub pyscenic_aucell.sh

echo "done"
Submit with qsub pyscenic_ctx.sh or automatically from the first step.


Cellular enrichment (AUCell step)
Again, we create a bash script called pyscenic_auc.sh
#!/bin/bash
#PBS -q home-yeo
#PBS -N pyscenic_aucell
#PBS -l nodes=1:ppn=16
#PBS -l walltime=8:00:00
#PBS -o pyscenic_aucell.out
#PBS -e pyscenic_aucell.err
#PBS -m abe
#PBS -M mheeg@ucsd.edu

echo "running"

# activate conda
source /home/mheeg/mambaforge/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate pyscenic

#navigate to project folder
cd /home/mheeg/scratch/pySCENIC

pyscenic aucell 'pySCENIC_input.loom'   'motifs.csv'    --output 'pySCENIC_output.loom'   --num_workers 16

echo "done"
Submit with qsub pyscenic_auc.sh or automatically from the second step.

title: Run pySCENIC
text:
Visualization of SCENIC’s AUC matrix
Next, load the relevant data from the loom file that was created in the script pyscenic_auc.sh. Then we calculate a UMAP and a TSNE from the AUC matrix (AUC values for each regulon for each cell)
import json
import zlib
import base64
import umap
from MulticoreTSNE import MulticoreTSNE as TSNE

# collect SCENIC AUCell output
lf = lp.connect( 'pySCENIC/pySCENIC_output.loom', mode='r+', validate=False )
auc_mtx = pd.DataFrame( lf.ca.RegulonsAUC, index=lf.ca.CellID)
lf.close()


# UMAP
runUmap = umap.UMAP(n_neighbors=10, min_dist=0.4, metric='correlation').fit_transform
dr_umap = runUmap( auc_mtx )
pd.DataFrame(dr_umap, columns=['X', 'Y'], index=auc_mtx.index).to_csv( "scenic_umap.txt", sep='\t')
# tSNE
tsne = TSNE( n_jobs=10 )
dr_tsne = tsne.fit_transform( auc_mtx )
pd.DataFrame(dr_tsne, columns=['X', 'Y'], index=auc_mtx.index).to_csv( "scenic_tsne.txt", sep='\t')

Add the AUC results to the anndata object
Here, we combine the results from SCENIC and the Scanpy analysis into a SCope-compatible loom file
# scenic output
lf = lp.connect( 'pySCENIC_output.loom', mode='r+', validate=False )
meta = json.loads(zlib.decompress(base64.b64decode( lf.attrs.MetaData )))
#exprMat = pd.DataFrame( lf[:,:], index=lf.ra.Gene, columns=lf.ca.CellID)
auc_mtx = pd.DataFrame( lf.ca.RegulonsAUC, index=lf.ca.CellID)
regulons = lf.ra.Regulons
dr_umap = pd.read_csv( 'scenic_umap.txt', sep='\t', header=0, index_col=0 )
dr_tsne = pd.read_csv( 'scenic_tsne.txt', sep='\t', header=0, index_col=0 )
###
Fix regulon objects to display properly in SCope:
auc_mtx.columns = auc_mtx.columns.str.replace('\(','_(')
regulons.dtype.names = tuple( [ x.replace("(","_(") for x in regulons.dtype.names ] )

# regulon thresholds
rt = meta['regulonThresholds']
for i,x in enumerate(rt):
    tmp = x.get('regulon').replace("(","_(")
    x.update( {'regulon': tmp} )
Concatenate embeddings (tSNE, UMAP, etc.)
tsneDF = pd.DataFrame(adata.obsm['X_tsne'], columns=['_X', '_Y'])

Embeddings_X = pd.DataFrame( index=lf.ca.CellID )
Embeddings_X = pd.concat( [
        pd.DataFrame(adata.obsm['X_umap'],index=adata.obs.index)[0] ,
        pd.DataFrame(adata.obsm['X_pca'],index=adata.obs.index)[0] ,
        dr_tsne['X'] ,
        dr_umap['X']
    ], sort=False, axis=1, join='outer' )
Embeddings_X.columns = ['1','2','3','4']

Embeddings_Y = pd.DataFrame( index=lf.ca.CellID )
Embeddings_Y = pd.concat( [
        pd.DataFrame(adata.obsm['X_umap'],index=adata.obs.index)[1] ,
        pd.DataFrame(adata.obsm['X_pca'],index=adata.obs.index)[1] ,
        dr_tsne['Y'] ,
        dr_umap['Y']
    ], sort=False, axis=1, join='outer' )
Embeddings_Y.columns = ['1','2','3','4']
Create the Metadata for the loom file
metaJson = {}

metaJson['embeddings'] = [
    {
        "id": -1,
        "name": f"Scanpy t-SNE (highly variable genes)"
    },
    {
        "id": 1,
        "name": f"Scanpy UMAP  (highly variable genes)"
    },
    {
        "id": 2,
        "name": "Scanpy PC1/PC2"
    },
    {
        "id": 3,
        "name": "SCENIC AUC t-SNE"
    },
    {
        "id": 4,
        "name": "SCENIC AUC UMAP"
    },
]

metaJson["clusterings"] = [{
            "id": 0,
            "group": "Scanpy",
            "name": "Scanpy leiden default resolution",
            "clusters": [],
        }]

metaJson["metrics"] = [
        {
            "name": "nUMI"
        }, {
            "name": "nGene"
        }, {
            "name": "Percent_mito"
        }
]

metaJson["annotations"] = [
    {
        "name": "Leiden_clusters_Scanpy",
        "values": list(set( adata.obs['leiden'].astype(np.str) ))
    },
    {
       "name": "Tissue",
       "values": list(set(adata.obs['tissue'].values))
    },
    {
       "name": "Dataset",
       "values": list(set(adata.obs['dataset'].values))
    },
]

# SCENIC regulon thresholds:
metaJson["regulonThresholds"] = rt

for i in range(max(set([int(x) for x in adata.obs['leiden']])) + 1):
    clustDict = {}
    clustDict['id'] = i
    clustDict['description'] = f'Unannotated Cluster {i + 1}'
    metaJson['clusterings'][0]['clusters'].append(clustDict)
    
clusterings = pd.DataFrame()
clusterings["0"] = adata.obs['leiden'].values.astype(np.int64)
Assemble loom file row and column attributes
def dfToNamedMatrix(df):
    arr_ip = [tuple(i) for i in df.values]
    dtyp = np.dtype(list(zip(df.dtypes.index, df.dtypes)))
    arr = np.array(arr_ip, dtype=dtyp)
    return arr

col_attrs = {
    "CellID": np.array(adata.obs.index),
    "nUMI": np.array(adata.obs['total_counts'].values),
    "nGene": np.array(adata.obs['n_genes'].values),
    "Leiden_clusters_Scanpy": np.array( adata.obs['leiden'].values ),
    "Tissue": np.array(adata.obs['tissue'].values),
    "Dataset": np.array(adata.obs['dataset'].values),
    "Percent_mito": np.array(adata.obs['pct_counts_mt'].values),
    "Embedding": dfToNamedMatrix(tsneDF),
    "Embeddings_X": dfToNamedMatrix(Embeddings_X),
    "Embeddings_Y": dfToNamedMatrix(Embeddings_Y),
    "RegulonsAUC": dfToNamedMatrix(auc_mtx),
    "Clusterings": dfToNamedMatrix(clusterings),
    "ClusterID": np.array(adata.obs['leiden'].values)
}

row_attrs = {
    "Gene": lf.ra.Gene,
    "Regulons": regulons,
}

attrs = {
    "title": "sampleTitle",
    "MetaData": json.dumps(metaJson),
    "Genome": 'mm10',
    "SCopeTreeL1": "",
    "SCopeTreeL2": "",
    "SCopeTreeL3": ""
}

# compress the metadata field:
attrs['MetaData'] = base64.b64encode(zlib.compress(json.dumps(metaJson).encode('ascii'))).decode('ascii')
Create a final loom file that can be inpsected in: SCOPE
lp.create(
    filename = 'pySCENIC_final.loom' ,
    layers=lf[:,:],
    row_attrs=row_attrs, 
    col_attrs=col_attrs, 
    file_attrs=attrs
)
lf.close() # close original pyscenic loom file

title: Convert gene symbols
text:
Converting gene symbols to ENSEMBL IDs in R is fast and easy.
require(org.Mm.eg.db)
​
symbols = c("Tox", "Id2")
​
# convert SYMBOL to ENSMBL
ensembl = AnnotationDbi::mapIds(
  x = org.Mm.eg.db,
  keys = symbols,
  keytype = "SYMBOL",
  column = "ENSEMBL"
)

# > ensembl
#                  Tox                  Id2 
# "ENSMUSG00000041272" "ENSMUSG00000020644" 
​
# And back
AnnotationDbi::mapIds(
  x = org.Mm.eg.db,
  keys = ensembl,
  keytype = "ENSEMBL",
  column = "SYMBOL"
)

# ENSMUSG00000041272 ENSMUSG00000020644 
#              "Tox"              "Id2" 
Sometimes the ENSEMBL IDs have a version, e.g. ENSMUST00000178862.1, we need to remove everything after the .. This can be done using regex matching.
ids = "ENSMUST00000178862.1"
stringr::str_remove(ids, "\\.[0-9]+$")

title: Making bone marrow chimeras
text:
Bone marrow chimeras
You will need ~20 million bone marrow cells to inject for each recipient mouse. Plan out congenic backgrounds so you will be able to distinguish recipient from donor mouse cells.
Day -1

Make low pH, antibiotic water for irradiated mice.

Add 2L of tap water to autoclaveable bottle.
Add ~0.48mL HCl and shake.
Dip pH indicator strip into bottle and adjust pH to be between 2.5 and 3.5 (pH ~3.0)
Autoclave on liquid setting for at least 20min.
Add 25mg (1.25mL of bottle in 4°) Polymyxin B and 1g Neomycin to the water after its cooled to touch.
Store water with foil in refrigerator.


Day 0

Irradiate bone marrow recipients two times with 4.5 Gy SIX HOURS APART. Each time, this is what the settings should be: 225 kV 17.7 mA config radpls pie, shelf 1, 4.5 Gy, 2 min 46 seconds

*This dose was optimized to yield 100% mouse survival and 85-95% chimerism.
Bone marrow recipient animals

Pepboy CD45.1+ Thy1.2+

Bone marrow donor animals

Fgl2-/- HSCs, CD45.2+ Thy1.2+
WT HSCs, CD45.2+ Thy1.2+



Euthanize the donor mice: 8 Fgl2-/- mice, 10 B6 mice
Spray the donor mice with 70 % ethanol and cut the abdominal skin, peel down over legs.
Remove the feet and harvest femur and tibia, scraping away muscle.
Transfer the legs to cold PBS.
Remove excess flesh from the leg bone using scissors and forceps and gauze.
Cut off the ends of the bones, and place the bones in PBS
Once all bones are collected, transfer to petri dishes with 10mL media.
Flush the bones using a 23-gauge needle for the tibia and 21 gauge for the femur with a 10 ml syringe. Refilling with petri dish PBS or fresh PBS as needed.
Once finished (bones should look white with no red in them), make a single-cell suspension of all the marrow and filter using a 70um filter. Wash each side of the petri dish 1-2x with PBS. Use another 50 ml conical for the washes. Count both tubes.
Pool cells from all mice and count cells.



Spin and filter once more. Resuspend to 40 million cells/ml (20 million cells per 500 ul per mouse adoptive transfer)
Inject 500ul of bone marrow cell suspension i.v through penile vein. If using retroorbital, resuspend so there are 20 million cells per 250 ul per mouse adoptive transfer.

Day 0 – Week 8

Allow mice to recover in sterile cages in sterile room with 150 mls antibiotic water
Replace antibiotic water 2x a week.
Six weeks post transplantation, recipient mice can be analyzed for the presence of donor-derived cells via flow cytometry.

Week 6 & 8

Bleed mice with 5mm lances, fill heparinized capillaries and dump in 5mL FACS tube with 4mL lysis buffer.
Spin tubes down, aspirate supernatant and add 4mL lysis buffer and resuspend.
Spin tubes down again, aspirate supernatant and transfer all volume to 96-well round bottom plate.
Add to 300uL with lysis buffer, and transfer 40uL to isotype well (combine so one isotype well per cage).
Spin plate down, flick.
Resuspend in 50uL antibody master mix.



CD4- PB (1:100)
CD8- PO (1:100)
CD3- BV786 (1:200)
CD45.1- FITC (1:100)
CD45.2- PE-Cy7 (1:100)
CD19- PerCP (1:100)
Fgl2- PE (1:300)
CD11b- APC (1:200)



Incubate at 4C for 30 minutes.
Wash 1x with 200uL FACS buffer.
Resuspend in 75uL FACS buffer, transfer to microtubes, flow.

NOTE: All BM transferred (including CD8 T cells) should be CD45.2; none should be CD45.1, in both WT and KO recipients.

title: Bleeding Mice for transduction check_ATM
text:
Preparing Blood

Get blood tubes - 1 for each mouse.
Label blood tubes so that you know which mouse is bled into each.
Bleed animal into blood tube with 1 ml of PBS + EDTA.
Store blood at 4 C for one dahy if you are not going to use it that day. PAUSE
Spin the blood at 6000 rpm for 4-5 min.
Aspirate and discard supernatant.
Add 1 ml Ack and resuspend the pellet.
Incubate at room temp for 5 - 10 min.
Spin at 6000 rpm for 4-5 min.
Aspirate and discard supernatant. Be careful not to aspirate the pellet.
Resuspend pellet in 200 ul FACS buffer.
Transfer to a labelled 96 well V-bottom plate.
Make antibody master mix by preparing a 1:200 dilution of each antibody in FACS buffer.
50 ul of FACS buffer per sample + 100 ul in addition (just in case)
Spin 96-well plate at 2000 rpm for 2 min.
Discard supernatant be flicking once over the sink.
Add 50 ul antibody master mix to the wells and resuspend. Keep on ice.
Incubate on ice or at 4 C in the dark for 15 min.
Add 150 ul FACS buffer.
Spin at 2000 rpm for 2 min and discard the supernatant by flicking once over the sink.
Add 200 ul FACS buffer and resuspend.
Spin at 2000 rpm for 2 min and discard supernatant by flicking once over the sink.
Add 200 ul of FACS buffer, resuspend cells, and transfer to FACS tubes on ice.

title: Blood phenotyping P14 and OT1 mice
text:
PHENOTYPING
** for P14 mouse line, using blood

Before starting, obtain 96-wells plate, add 100uL EDTA in PBS (same as blood collection tubes) per well needed, make sure to space the wells for easy access and prevent cross-contamination
Collect mouse needed to phenotype
Set up isoflourane

1.5 oxygen, 5% isoflourane

After anesthetized the mouse, snip tail and collect blood into wells. Make sure to label for clarity

Only need 1 drop of blood
Can dip tail lightly into liquid if the blood does not drop down

After harvested the blood, add 100uL ACK to each well with blood, lyse for ~5mins.
Centrifuge for 2mins @2000 RPM. Discard supernatant.
If pellet is still red, add 100uL ACK to each well with blood and continue lysing for another ~5mins, then wash with FACS buffer (~180uL) and spin and discard supernatant.
While lysing, prepare the antibodies for staining: CD90.2/Thy1.2, CD90.1/Thy1.1, CD8, CD45.1, CD45.2, Valpha2, Vbeta5

Check panel to make sure fluorophores will work on selected cytometer
Antibody master mix: make ~100uL/well

After cells are finished lysing, centrifuge @2000 RPM for 2 mins. Discard supernatant and stain with 100uL of ab mixture per well.
Incubate on ice for 15mins.
After incubation, add FACS buffer (~180uL) to the wells and wash @ 2000 RPM for 2 mins
Discard supernatant and fix with 1%PFA at RT for 15mins.
Wash with FACS buffer and resuspend in 200uL of facs buffer
Cover wells with parafilm and wrap plate in foil, to protect from evaporation and light
Fixed cells can be kept in the fridge (or CR) until needed (max time ~couple of days)
Transfer contents over to FACS/bullet tube before running
Running:

Looking for Valpha2+ in CD8 population for indications of P14+
Check for indication of strains

section: B16 Tumor processing protocol obtained from Nicole. Thanks Nicole
text:
B16 Tumor processing protocol obtained from Nicole. Thanks Nicole

Tumor tissue dissociation
Use scissors and chop tumor into small pieces inside 50ml falcon turned on its side (should look like mush).
Add 10ml collagenase solution, washing scissors off and tissue down the side of the tube.
Incubate for 30 min @ 37°C in shaking incubator.
Pour through cell strainer into a new 50mL conical, mash through cell strainer, and add 10mL RP5 (RPMI +5% serum) to wash cells down.
Put tubes on ice while processing other tumors.
Before spinning, add 2mL 1x ACK to each tube, and vortex each tube for 30 seconds to further disassociate lymphocytes from tumor cells.
Spin down at 1600 rpm for 6 min.

title: B16 Takedown 2026-03-25_ATM
text:
Percoll

Make sure you see a pellet, then pour supernatant out.
Resuspend each sample in 5 mL 44% percoll solution, make sure pellet is well resuspended, and transfer to a 15ml round bottom tube (bacteria culturing tube).
Place glass pasteur pipette in conical and add 2 mL 67% percol solution to top of pipette to make a bottom layer. Don’t disturb after adding!
Spin at 21°C at 2000 rpm for 20 min, set acceleration to 3 and brake to 0
Check for an interphase between the two layers and transfer it to 15 mL conical (usually about 2 mL).
Fill to top with RP5 then spin at 1600 rpm for 4 min.

title: B16 Takedown 2026-03-25_ATM
text:
Ficoll

Make sure you see a pellet, then pour supernatant out.
Resuspend each sample in 5 mL RP5, place glass pasteur pipette in conical and add 2 mL Ficoll (Corning Lymphocyte Separation Media MT25072CV) to top of pipette to make a bottom layer. Don’t disturb after adding!
Spin at 10°C at 2000 rpm for 15 min, set acceleration to 9 and brake to 9
Check for an interphase between the two layers and transfer it to 15 mL conical (usually about 2 mL).
Fill to top with RP5 then spin at 1600 rpm for 4 min.
Resuspend pellet in 1mL RP5 - cells are now ready to transfer to plates for staining.

title: Protocol_Caecum_Orthotopic_MRC
text:
PROCEDURE: Orthotopic implantation into the Caecum wall
We will use an orthotopic implantation model for colon that requires implantation of colon cancer cells into the cecum of mice, as described by Céspedes MV et al., 2007. (See Orthotopic microinjection of human colon cancer cells in nude mice induces tumor foci in all clinically relevant metastatic sites, Am J Pathol. 2007 Mar;170(3):1077-85.). We would like to evaluate how direct orthotopic cell microinjection, between the mucosa and the muscularis layers of the cecal wall of mice, drives tumor foci to the most relevant metastatic sites and impacts the immune response.
Summary: Mouse colon cancer cells (e.g., MC-38 cells) will be grown to confluence using standard aseptic cell culture technique, harvested for injection, and resuspended in serum-free DMEM at a concentration of 4 x 10^7 cells/mL. Mice will be anesthetized with ketamine/xylazine, prepared in a sterile fashion, and the cecum will be exteriorized through a middle abdominal incision. 2 x 10^6 cells in 50μl will be slowly injected into the cecum wall between the mucosa and the muscularis layers through a 250-um diameter micropippette. Animals will be euthanized after 90 days, or when they appear lethargic, whichever occurs first.
Cecum injection:

Ketamine (100 mg/kg) / Xylazine (10 mg/kg) combination will be administered via intraperitoneal injection. Depth of anesthesia will be confirmed by verifying an absence of response to ear, toe, and/or tail pinch.
After induction of anesthesia, under sterile conditions (sterile instruments, surgical PPE per policy), the middle abdomen will be shaved with an electric razor, and scrubbed with Betadine, after which the surgical site is wiped with 70% ethanol, and re-painted with Betadine.
The animal is then draped appropriately, and using sterile gloves and instruments, a middle abdominal incision will be made and a a 250-um diameter micropippette will be used to inject 50μl of cell suspension (up to 2x10^6 cells resuspended in serum-free DMEM) into the cecum wall between the mucosa and the muscularis layers under a binocular lens (23 magnification), with an approximate 30° angle and its tip introduced 5 mm into the cecal wall. The delivery of tumor cells will occur within the subserosa. Alternatively, 2-10 mm3 tumor pieces derived from subcutanous tumors will be sutured to the caecum wall using 3-0 Vicryl.
Slight pressure with a cotton stick will be done at 32 mm from the injection point in the direction of the pipette axis. The pipette is pulled out and clean the area around the injection with 3% iodine to avoid seeding of unlikely refluxed tumor cells into the abdominal cavity. Any potential bleeding will be controlled by using a cotton swab.
The wound will be closed in two layers, with running 4-0 Vicryl, and nylon or polypropylene sutures for the skin. Mice will be monitored for anesthesia withdrawal as well as an increase or change in respiratory rate and/or pattern. The length of anesthesia will be approximately 20 minutes so the variance from normothermic conditions should be minimal. A heat lamp will be used if the mice do not begin to recover and move after 20 minutes of anesthesia. Care will be taken to ensure the mice do not overheat by keeping the lamp far enough away that it is comfortable for surgeon’s hands to rest there.
Respiratory rate and depth will be monitored until mouse is able to right itself after mouse is subject to surgery. The animal is then placed back into its cage, observed until fully recovered from anesthesia, and returned to its rack.
Mice will be weighed at the time of surgery and once a week following orthotopic implantation. If an animal appears to be losing weight, then the frequency of weighing will increase to every other day. Pain will be assessed as described in IACUC guidebook, 2002ed, (http://grants.nih.gov/grants/olaw/GuideBook.pdf) and treated by analgesia Buprenorphine (0.05-0.1mg/kg) administered initially at time of surgery and then SC or IP twice daily or more frequently if pain is indicated, but no more than every 6 hours as needed for at least 48 hours. We give this with ketoprofen SC 1-2 mg/kg given before surgery and again 24 hours later. If an animal loses greater than 20% of their body weight, or if it appears that the animal is in distress as outlined by the criteria above in “monitoring of clinical signs”, it will be euthanized prior to the planned time point.

Significant differences between groups will be determined using a Student’sttest (two-tailed unpaired) when the data met the normal distribution tested by the D’Agostino test. If the data does not meet this test, a Mann-Whitney test will be used.

title: M1.tail_prep_genotyping
text:
Genotyping Procedure
Tail Prep


Cut ~1 cm of mouse tail (or smaller) and place in labelled epi tube (colorful tubes)


Thaw tail juice in 37ºC water and turn on shaker calibrated at 55ºC at 1000rpm


Add 400μl of tail juice into tail sample


Shake tails at 55ºC at 1000rpm for 1 hour (or even o/n until digested)


Add 150μl of 5M NaCl to each sample and vortex


Spin samples at max speed for 5 minutes





While samples are spinning, label new (clear) tubes





Transfer 400μl of supernatant to a new tube (clear tube)


Add 250μl of isopropanol to each sample and vortex


Spin samples at max speed for 5 minutes


Discard the supernatant by dumping into a waste beaker


Wash pellet with 500μl of 70% EtOH and vortex


Spin samples at max speed for 5 minutes


Discard supernatant by dumping over waste beaker and air dry pellet overnight





Fold paper towels between drying rack rows and leave tubes to dry upside down





The next day, resuspend pellets in 200μl of Ultrapure water


PCR


Use PCR Calculator to calculate amount of ingredients needed to make master mix and write down in lab notebook





Master Mix Ingredients
Amount (μl)




5X Buffer



MgCl2



Primer 1



Primer 2



Primer 3



dNTP



Taq



Ultrapure H2O






Thaw DNA samples, master mix ingredients (above), and positive/negative controls





Keep all ingredients on ice





Label PCR strip tubes corresponding to DNA samples, positive control, negative control, and water


Label epi tube with PCR type and “master mix”


Add PCR ingredients to labelled epi, starting with Ultrapure water (largest volume). Vortex to mix ingredients and spin down for 5 seconds (short).


Add 22μl of master mix to each PCR tube


Add 3μl of each DNA sample to its corresponding PCR tube (25μl total in PCR tube)


Spin down PCR tube strip


Run samples in PCR machine - select correct program for the type of PCR (ER-Cre, ID2, etc)


Gel electrophoresis
2.5% Gel | Small | Big | | 1.5% Gel | Small | Big |
—————- | ——- | ——— | | —————- | ——- | ————– |
Agarose Powder | 2.5 g | 5.0 g | | Agarose Powder | 1.5 g | |
1X TAE Buffer | 100 ml | 200 ml | | 1X TAE Buffer | 100 ml | |
Microwave Time | ~2 min | ~3.5 min | | Microwave Time | ~2 min | ~3 min 30 sec |
Ethidium Bromide | 4 μl | 8 μl | | Ethidium Bromide | 4 μl | 8 μl |
*amount depends on agarose % or size of gel


Clean bottle by clearing away excess gel and dispose in designated waste bucket


Place the bottle on scale and tarr it. Add 4g* of agarose powder to bottle


Add 100ml* of 1X TAE buffer


Microwave bottle for ~2min*





Do not leave the microwave unattended. Solution should not bubble over the top.





Using silicone oven mitts, swirl bottle until solution runs clear


Cool down the solution.


Add 4g* of ethidium bromide and swirl to mix.


Assemble mold and place desired comb into mold. Pour solution slowly over mold to minimize bubbles.





Use a pipette tip to move bubbles away from the comb and to the side.





Allow gel to cool on bench or in cold room for 10-15 minutes


Carefully remove comb from gel


Place gel mold into gel electrophoresis box





Buffer should be changed once a day or more as needed





Add 10μl of DNA ladder (ER-Cre = 100bp) to first well


Load 20μl of each PCR sample into a well


Attach electrodes with black electrode in the back (DNA side) and red in front. Set up for 100V for 1 hour and run the gel.





Check at about 30-45 minutes to make sure samples don’t run off the gel


Imaging

text:
Each vial of Liberase TL research grade (Roche 5401020001) makes 20 mL Liberase solution. Normally prepare 3–4 vials at a time.
Add 2 mL RPMI plus supplementary complement per vial of lyophilized enzyme and place on ice to reconstitute for 20 minutes.
Add 5 mL RPMI plus supplementary complement to each vial after reconstitution (7 mL total). Mix with a stripette before transferring to a 50 mL tube.
Bring to 20 mL per vial with 13 mL RPMI plus supplementary complement. For example, if pooling two vials, bring the 50 mL tube to 40 mL total.
Add 100 µL of 1 mg/mL DNase per 20 mL Liberase solution (200 µL for 40 mL). Use Sigma bovine DNase.

title: Liberase Skin Protocol
text:
Harvest

Shave the right and left flanks, then perfuse mice with 10 mL HBSS.
Harvest both ears, separate dorsal and ventral sides, and place in 1 mL Liberase solution.
Harvest 3 cm flank skin (1.5 × 2 cm area) into 1.5 mL Liberase solution.

title: Liberase Skin Protocol
text:
Process flank skin

Incubate for 30 minutes at 37°C in a water bath in Liberase solution.
Peel epidermis from dermis and return it to the same Liberase tube.
Chop the skin.
Incubate for a further 80 minutes at 37°C in a water bath.
Transfer to 3 mL RP-10 and triturate 30 times with a transfer pipette.
Filter through a 70 µm nylon filter cone into a fresh tube, rinsing the filter with RP-10.
Centrifuge and aspirate RP-10 from the pellet. The pellet is ready to stain.

title: Liberase Skin Protocol
text:
Process ear skin

Incubate for 120 minutes at 37°C in a water bath in Liberase solution.
Chop the ears.
Transfer to 3 mL RP-10 and triturate 30 times with a transfer pipette.
Filter through a 70 µm nylon filter cone into a fresh tube, rinsing the filter with RP-10.
Centrifuge and aspirate RP-10 from the pellet. The pellet is ready to stain.

title: Liberase Skin Protocol
text:
Notes

Flank skin has two incubations: 30 minutes before peeling/chopping, then 80 minutes at 37°C. Ear skin has one 120-minute incubation before chopping and filtering.
Peel flank skin gently but thoroughly enough to see the white, stringy epidermal material removed.
Do not over-chop the skin: chop vigorously for no more than 40–60 seconds to protect viability.

title: Mouse Saliva Test Protocol (Sjogren’s Syndrome Project)
text:
Mouse Saliva Test Protocol
Using Schirmer’s test and Saliva Weight test

Preparing Pilocarpine solution:


*Note: Powdered Pilocarpine found in chemical stock
*Note: Can prepare/store at 4°C stock solution at 5 mg Pilocarpine/mL PBS.


For injections, dilute the 4°C stock solution 1:100 in ddH20 or PBS.
For a 5 mL solution, do the following:

Add 4950 ul ddH20
Add 50 ul Pilocarpine (of 5 mg/mL PBS solution)

Injections:

Use 10 ul/g body weight of mouse.




Inject Pilocarpine solution s.c. under sterile conditions.

Wait at least 5 minutes after pilocarpine injection before tests.

Schirmer’s test (zone quick test)

Wipe excess saliva from mouth of mouse prior to test.
Using forceps, place hook of phenol thread behind the teeth and on the tongue.
Place mice on its side on dry surface. Time for 2 minutes duration.
Measure thread (in mm) according to complete red color change.

Saliva Weight test (epi-kimwipe)

Have pre-weighed 1.5 mL eppendorf tubes filled with rolled up quarter sized kimwipes (roughly 2’’ x 2’’) ready.
Wipe excess saliva from mouth of mouse prior to test.
Using forceps, place kimwipe roll behind teeth. Place mice facedown onto dry surface. Time for 5 minutes duration.
Post-weigh eppendorf-kimwipe tubes to calculate saliva (in mg).

title: Lymphnode processing
text:
Filtering the cells

Get a 15ml conical tube and place a nitex filter over the opening
Transfer the cells from petri-dish over to the conical tube by passing it through the filter
After all the cell with media has been transferred, rinse the petri-dish with some RP5 and transfer the contents through the filter to collect any remaining cells on the dish to the tube.

title: Fetal Liver Chimeras
text:
Fetal Liver Chimeras
Day 1:

Any timed mating females pregnant on day E14-14.5 can be used.
Sac pregnant female and remove both horns of the uterus from the abdominal cavity.
Cut along the bottom of the horns, avoiding blood from the surrounding vessels (this is maternal blood and can contaminate the fetal samples). Place uterus in a petri dish with RP5 media to rinse.
Remove the embryos from the uterus and amniotic sac. This is most easily done with forceps. Be careful to keep the embryo intact and to avoid contamination with maternal blood.
Place separated embryos in another petri dish with media to rinse.
Store each embryo in a 12 or 24 well plate in a couple of mLs of RP5. Wrap the edges of the plate in parafilm and store at 4C. Be careful to avoid knocking the plate over.
For genotyping take a hand or foot from each embryo. PCRs must be completed as soon as possible.

Day 2:

Remove the fetal liver (using forceps) and place in 500ul of RP5. Be more concerned with getting all of the liver cells, extra tissue taken during this step will be filtered out later.
Pipet up and down vigorously to resuspend the liver cells. Filter sample into a new tube.
Use 5ul to count cells and 5ul to stain for congenic markers (CD45.1 and CD45.2).
When staining fetal liver ALWAYS Fc block for five minutes and stain the cells for a full 15. It’s usually hard to see 45.1 and 45.2 positive cells at this stage.
Select recipient mice based on congenic markers. Mice should be no younger than four weeks, six is better. Males preferable
Irradiate recipient mice with 1000 rad (900 if they are really small).
Process RAGko bone marrow in media (Id2ko mice have a defect in APCs so we use RAGko cells to solve this problem).
Each mouse should receive an absolute minimum of 3x10^6 fetal liver cells. 5x10^6 is optimal. Even up to 10x10^6 is fine. However, normalize the number of fetal liver cells per mouse for each group (EG: make sure recipients getting KO cells get the same number of cells as recipients getting WT cells). Add 1/10th the number of RAGko bone marrow cells (EG: if you’re injecting 5x10^6 fetal liver cells add 5x10^5 RAGko bone marrow cells).
Wash the cells with sterile PBS (media can cause rejection. However, since the mice have been irradiated if you have very few cells you can skip this step). Resuspend in correct amount of PBS (each mouse should receive it’s cells in 200ul).
Inject cells ASAP into the tail veins of recipient mice (cells don’t do too well in PBS for long periods of time).
Recipient mice should receive antibiotics in their drinking water for 2 weeks (changed weekly).

title: Lymphocyte isolation from mouse tissues
text:
Lymphocyte isolation from mouse tissues
Materials

RP-5 (RPMI with 5% BGS)
CMF medium
DTE solution
Collagenase solution
44% and 67% Percoll solutions
PBS
Cell strainers
15 ml and 50 ml conical tubes
Glass Pasteur pipettes

Can use iterative takedown media calculator here: https://protocols.heeg.io/recipes/takedown/#interactive-calculator
IV Labeling for T Cell Resident Memory (TRM) Panels

3 minutes prior to sacrifice, inject mice retro-orbitally with 200 μl antibody mix containing 3 μg of the labeling antibody (e.g. 15 μl CD8a-APC-Cy7 + 185 μl PBS)
Sacrifice mice, remove small intestine and spleen, place in ice-cold RP-5 or CMF, and trim off fat

Intraepithelial Lymphocyte (IEL) Preparation

Place paper towels on desk and wet with CMF
Wet gut with CMF, cut out Peyer’s patches and clean out fecal matter
Cut the small intestine in half lengthwise and then into small (~1 cm) pieces. Keep the tissue wet during the entire time.
Place in flask and wash 2× with CMF, pouring out contents carefully to retain tissue
Discard CMF carefully and replace with ~30-50 ml prewarmed DTE
Incubate on a 37°C stir plate for 30 minutes
Pour contents into a 50 ml conical tube with cell strainer

Kidney, Salivary Gland (SG), Liver, Lung, and Fat Processing

Clean organs, remove fat and capsule
Cut into small pieces in a 50 ml conical tube
Add prewarmed collagenase solution:

Salivary Gland, Fat & Kidney: 10 ml
Liver: 20 ml
Lung: 5 ml

Incubate for 30 minutes at 37°C (1 hour for lung)
Mash through cell strainer

Percoll Gradient Separation
Proceed as follows for both IEL and other organ preparations:

Centrifuge at 1600 rpm for 4 minutes to pellet single cell suspension
Verify pellet formation, then carefully discard supernatant and wipe top of conical tube
Resuspend each sample in 5 ml of 44% Percoll solution, ensuring the pellet is well resuspended

For liver, prepare two Percoll gradients per sample

Place a glass Pasteur pipette in the conical tube and add 2 ml of 67% Percoll solution to the top of pipette to create a bottom layer. Do not disturb after adding!
Centrifuge at 21°C at 2000 rpm for 20 minutes, with acceleration set to 4 and brake to 0
Locate the interphase between the two Percoll layers and transfer it to a 15 ml conical tube (approximately 3 ml)
Fill the tube with PBS, mix by inverting and centrifuge at 2000 rpm for 5 minutes


Tip
Ensure thorough mixing when adding PBS, otherwise the interphase might remain intact


Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 μl of RP-5 media

title: Staining Blood
text:
Staining Blood:

Spin blood tubes at 5000 RPM for 5 minutes
Suck off PBS (clear supernatant)
Resuspend blood pellet in 1x Ack; Incubate ~10 minutes at room temperature
Spin at 5000 RPM for 5 minutes (should see a white pellet)
Suck off supernatant leaving a white pellet behind
Resuspend pellet in 150 microliters of FACs buffer and trasfer to a “v”-bottom plate
Spin the plate at 2000 RPM for 1 minute; flick the plate to get rid of supernatant
Add 50 microliters of stain to each well and mix with pipette
Incubate the plate for about 20 minutes on ice
Add 150 microliters of FACs buffer to the well; spin at 2000 RPM for 1 minute and flick the plate
Resuspend pellet in 150 microliters of FACs buffer; spin 2000 RPM for 1 minute and flick the plate
Resuspend the pellet in 150 microliters FACs buffer and transfer to the FACs tubes
Analyze the samples on the FACs machine

Run out on gel, remove band

Use HindIII for 3’ southern and NcoI for 5’ southern

Run out gel


-Pour 0.8% gel (measure out 400ml of TAE and add 20ul EtBr) in a large mold with one row of wells at the top
-run at 40V overnight


Southern Blot Transfer


-take a picture of the gel to make sure restriction digest worked (should see a smear of DNA, not bands)
-cut out relevant part of gel, measure size, mark top left corner
-rotate for 5 min in 0.2N HCl (no longer!), must be made fresh!
-wash with DI water
-rotate for 20 min with 0.4M NaOH
-set up blot:


4 squares chromatography paper (1 cm bigger than gel) dry
2 squares chromatography paper (1 cm bigger) wet in NaOH
Hybond-xl membrane (exact size of gel) wet in NaOH (corner marked same as gel)
Gel (don’t need to invert)


-surround gel with parafilm to prevent short circuiting


3 squares chromatography paper (exact size) wet in NaOH
two long wicks, with one end in dish holding NaOH, and tapered ends that rest on top of the gel
weight


-allow transfer to occur for 1.5-2 hours (ok to go over, membrane is charged to hold DNA-> also means no need to crosslink)


Probe Preparation

denature probe:



-heat the tailshaker up to 98C
50ng probe template DNA
0.5ng lamda HindIII digestion DNA (for ladder labeling)
10ul random nonmers
add H2O to 34ul
-incubate 10 min at 98C
-don’t forget to also denature sheared salmon sperm DNA (25ul/blot)
-(while waiting heat up hyb ovens to desired Temp: 68C for 5’P2 and 65C for 5’ probe #3)
-cool on ice 1 min


Radiolabel probe


-Add: 10ul 5X dCTP buffer
1 ul Klenow
5ul P32 dCTP
-incubate 10 minutes at 37C
-add 2ul Stop mix
-clean on G50 spin colums:
-vortex tubes before use
-break off botton and loosen cap
-spin at 3K rpm for 1 min into collection tube to get rid of liquid
and form column
-toss flow through and collection tube, replace with labeled eppie
with 2.5ul 2M NaoOH
-add probe mix directly to column
-spin 3Krpm for 2 min
-toss column and keep probe in eppie (can leave at RT until
membrane is ready)


Hybridization of probe to membrane


-after the blotting is finished remove chromatography paper and gel
-add 10 ml quikhyb solution hyb tube (incubate in oven while waiting for blot to finish to prewarm)
-add 25ul denatures salmon sperm DNA and coat sides of tube
-roll membrane and put in tube (DNA side facing in), try and keep edges from overlapping
-prehyb for 30min in hyb oven
-add radiolabeled probe to hyb tube (wash with 1mL quikhyb from tube)
-incubate rotating for 1 hr
-put plastic shields in front of ovens


Washing the membrane


-pour off quikhyb buffer (blotting the rim to prevent spills) and add ~10 mL 2X SSC 0.1% SDS, rotate 10 min
-repeat wash with 2X SSC 0.1% SDS, twice with 0.2X SSC 0.1% SDS and twice with 0.1 SSC 0.1% SDS
-during the last wash blank the phosphoimager screen
-pour off remaining wash solution, remove membrane and place DNA side down on a piece of saran wrap, cover the back of the membrane completely, folding all sides in to prevent evaporation and contamination
-tape blot to the phosphoimager screen (on the side with the grid) and add the blank side
-store for 72-98hrs for good exposure


Reading Blots


-Use imager in the Aria room
-open typhoon program (change acquisition mode to storage:phospho)
-run and save (remember which squares your blots are on)


PRAY!!!

title: RNA extraction with Trizol
text:
RNA extraction with Trizol (adapted from Kyla)


Thaw Trizol sample at RT.


Add 2ul glycoblue


Add chloroform


For 500ul Trizol, use 100ul chloroform
For 1000ul Trizol, use 200ul chloroform


Shake vigorously for approx 15s


Incubate 2-3 min at RT


Centrifuge 15 min at 12000g, 4C


Carefully transfer aqueous phase to a fresh tube (work on ice from this point)


Pipet in circular motion, avoid interphase by leaving generous amount of aqueous phase
For 500ul Trizol, transfer ~250ul
For 1ml Trizol, transfer ~500ul


Add isopropanol (flick, do not pipette)


For 500ul Trizol, add 250ul isopropanol
For 1ml Trizol, add 500ul isopropanol


Centrifuge 20 min at 12,000g, 4C


Then remove supernatant with pipette tip


Wash with 1ml cold 75% EtOH (make fresh using DNAse/RNAse-free water)


Flick to loose pellet


Centrifuge 15 min at 7,400g, 4C


Pipette of as much EtOH as possible. Use 10ul micropipettor for small volume
Dry 10-15 min


Resuspend RNA pellet in 10ul nuclease-free water


Incubate 10-15 min at 55-60C . Proceed to DNAse I digestion.


DNAse I digestion (from Turbo DNA-free procedure)


Add 1ul 10X Turbo Dnase buffer and 1ul Turbo Dnase to sample. Mix gently.


Incubate 20-30 min at 37C


Add 2ul of resuspended DNA Inactivation Reagent and mix well.


Incubate 5 min, RT. Mix occasionally.


Centrifuge 1.5 min at 10,000g


Transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube. Avoid pellet.

title: Precipitation of RNA
text:
Precipitation of RNA/DNA:

Add 1 μL/100 μmL of glycogen (at 2.5 mg/mL) or 1 μmL/100 μmL of tRNA when precipitating <10 μg/mL of product.
Add 0.1 volume NaOAc 3M pH 5.3 or NH4OAc 10M, vortex.
Add 2.5-3.5 volume 100% EtOH.
Freeze thaw 3x at –80ºC.
Spin 20 minutes maximum speed in 4ºC tabletop.
Remove supernant and add 750 μL of cold 70% EtOH.
Aspirate supernant carefully avoiding pellet.
Dry briefly.

title: PFA - 16 percent
text:
Edward Yang – 11/1/08
16% PFA – for 500 mL

Materials
350mL DI H20
80 grams of dry PFA
50 mL 10x PBS
Very large beaker (1 liter flat bottom)
500mL beaker (round)
Magnetic stir/ heat plate
Magnetic stir bar
Thermometer
pH meter
10-12N HCL
10-12N NaOH
Method – EVERYTHING is done in the chemical hood

Fill 500mL beaker with 350mL DI H20 and place into very large beaker. Fill large beaker with H20 until covering ~2/3 of 500mL beaker. Place thermometer in outer water bath.

Heat to between 60-70 degrees C. Do not exceed 70 degrees C as that is the flash point of PFA.

Weigh out 80g of dry PFA in the hood. Place magnetic stir bar (and start stirring) into 500mL beaker and then pour in dry PFA slowly.
Use plastic pipet to pipet in 1-2 pipet-full’s worth of NaOH. Watch temperature to make sure it’s at ~65 degrees C.

As PFA begins to go into solution, pipet in NaOH dropwise to improve solubility, conservatively.

Add NaOH dropwise until PFA completely goes into solution. The color of the solution should be completely clear/transparent.

Once in solution, pour in 50mL of 10x PBS, fill the rest up to the 500mL line with DI H20, and stir until mixed.

Turn off heat, pour out outer water bath, and fill with cold/RT water. Cool PFA solution until room temperature.
pH the solution to about 7.2-7.4 pH using HCL.
Sterile filter PFA using ~0.1 micron filter. Label with date and 16%.

title: RNA extraction using Trizol
text:
RNA extraction with Trizol (adapted from Kyla Omilusik)


Thaw Trizol sample at RT.


Add 2ul glycoblue


Add chloroform


For 500ul Trizol, use 100ul chloroform
For 1000ul Trizol, use 200ul chloroform


Shake vigorously for approx 15s


Incubate 2-3 min at RT


Centrifuge 15 min at 12000g, 4C


Carefully transfer aqueous phase to a fresh tube (work on ice from this point)


Pipet in circular motion, avoid interphase by leaving generous amount of aqueous phase
For 500ul Trizol, transfer ~250ul
For 1ml Trizol, transfer ~500ul


Add isopropanol (flick, do not pipette)


For 500ul Trizol, add 250ul isopropanol
For 1ml Trizol, add 500ul isopropanol


Centrifuge 20 min at 12,000g, 4C


Then remove supernatant with pipette tip


Wash with 1ml cold 75% EtOH (make fresh using DNAse/RNAse-free water)


Flick to loose pellet


Centrifuge 15 min at 7,400g, 4C


Pipette of as much EtOH as possible. Use 10ul micropipettor for small volume
Dry 10-15 min


Resuspend RNA pellet in 10ul nuclease-free water


Incubate 10-15 min at 55-60C.


Optional: DNAse I digestion (from Turbo DNA-free procedure)


Add 1ul 10X Turbo Dnase buffer and 1ul Turbo Dnase to sample. Mix gently.


Incubate 20-30 min at 37C


Add 2ul of resuspended DNA Inactivation Reagent and mix well.


Incubate 5 min, RT. Mix occasionally.


Centrifuge 1.5 min at 10,000g


Transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube. Avoid pellet.


qPCR
2X Sybr 10ul
primers (0.6uM) 5ul
water 2.3ul
ROX ref dye (optional) 0.3ul
cDNA* (1:10 diluted) 2ul (*from 50k cells)
-——

title: DNA Prep for Genotyping
text:
DNA Prep for Genotyping


Cut a small piece of mouse tail (0.5-1 mm)


Add 400ul tail juice. Shake at 55C for a minimum of 45 min or until tail dissolved.


Add 150ul 5M NaCl to each tube.


Vortex and spin at max speed for 5 min


Take off ~400ul supernatant and place in a clean new epp. Discard pellet.


Add 250ul isopropanol to each tube of supernatant. Vortex and spin max speed for 5 min. DNA pellet should be visible (maybe small).


Remove supernatant from pellets and discard.


Add 500ul 70% EtOH to each pellet. Spin 5 min max speed.


Remove 70% EtOH and allow pellets to dry for 30 min to overnight.


Resuspend in 250ul water.

title: LLB_GutPrep2017
text:
Lara Labarta-Bajo (Zuniga Lab) - Protocol is a combination of the Surh lab and Goldrath lab protocols
Materials:
- Hot-plate stirrer (Scilogex)
- Tissue chopper - McIlwain tissue chopper
- 50ml pyrex conicals
- Stirring magnets
- Stripping buffer:
PBS1x + 3% FBS + 10mM EDTA + 20mM HEPES + Pen/Strep (100u/ml pen, 100ug/ml strep), 1mM Na-pyruvate
- Enzyme media:
RPMI + 3% FBS, 20mM HEPES, Pen/Strep (100u/ml pen, 100ug/ml strep), 1mM Na-pyruvate +*on day of harvest add
0.4mg/ml Collagenase D (Roche) and DNAse I 10ug/ml (Roche)
- Percoll 100% (9 parts of Percoll from commercial bottle + 1 part of PBS 10x)
d-1 Prepare:
- Rinse 50ml conicals with ddw
- Prepare stripping buffer (30ml/sample per IEL).
- Prepare RPMI 5% FBS (as re-suspension media)
- Prepare PBS 5% FBS (to wash)
- Prepare enzyme media w/o enzymes (20ml per sample)
d0 Harvest
- Turn on stirrer and set at 37ºC
- Put stripping buffer at 37ºC
- Enzyme media at 37ºC
- Set centrifuge at RT. Pull out Percoll and keep at RT
- Set up big collection container (waste)
- Thaw collagenase and DNase at RT
- Collect SI and colon, remove fat (cotton swabs are useful), remove PP’s, empty fecal contents by gently pressing it down with your scissors. Cut it longitudinally, fold and cut in 1cm pieces. 
*Keep tissues in PBS- they should never be dry
- Wash x3 with PBS5% directly into 50ml Pyrex conical
- Add 30ml Stripping buffer and stir for 20min at 37ºC
- Shake a bit and collect soup (these are your IEL!) into 50ml falcon. Add RPMBI5% to Pyrex conical and collect some more. Add RPMI5% up to 50ml in conical and keep on ice until Percoll.
- Wash remaining tissue in PBS5% once and strain through tea strainer
- Pick gut pieces and Chop 2x with tissue chopper and add to 30ml enzyme media (in pyrex conical)
- Stir for 45min at 37ºC
- Pipette up and down 3 times with automatic pipette (10ml glass pipette) and
- Filter through cell strainer & spin down
- Re-suspend in 5ml 44% Percoll then add up to 2ml of 67% Percoll below
- Spin 20min 2,000 rpm (NO brake) and collect interphase with Pasteur pipette
- Collect interphase in 15ml falcon tubes, fill up with 5%RPMI and spin down at 2,000rpm for 8min.
- Re-suspend pellet in desired counting volume and continue with your staining.

objectID: protocols/Goldrath_Protocols/The Master Folder/MRC/STAINING PROTOCOL FOR FLOW.html
href: protocols/Goldrath_Protocols/The Master Folder/MRC/STAINING PROTOCOL FOR FLOW.html
title: STAINING PROTOCOL FOR FLOW
text:
STAINING PROTOCOL FOR FLOW
- Obtain your cells after TIL isolation
- Count them
- Pellet cells you want to stain onto a 96-well plate. For staining it is always best to use a U-bottom or a V-bottom plate, rather than flat-bottom plates.
1) L/D staining: re-suspend cells at 100 million cells/ml* (it will be around 25-50ul per sample) in 1xPBS + 1/1000 Live/Dead dye. 
Note: if you are staining a spleen or an organ with lots of cells, stain 5 million cells. If you were looking at rare, non-abundant populations you would have to stain 10 million or more. 
Note*: staining concentrations of up to 200milion cells/ml will work just fine.
2) Incubate for 10min on ice (or at 4C) (in the dark)
3) After the 10 min, add 200ul of PBS1x+3%FBS (no need to re-suspend), and spin down 1,500rpm 5min. Flick plate to remove SNT (this is just a washing step)
4) Add surface antibody mix**, re-suspend pellets and incubate for 20min on ice (or at 4C) and in the dark. After that, add 200ul of PBS1x+3%FBS (no need to re-suspend), and spin down 1,500rpm 5min. Flick plate.
   - **Surface antibody mix consists of surface antibodies diluted in Facs buffer.
5) Re-suspend pellet in 25-50ul of Foxp3 fix solution (contains 1 part of fixation/permeabilization concentrate + 3 parts of fixation/permeabilization diluent - make it fresh every time you need it). Incubate for at least 30min (and up to overnight). 
6) Add 200ul of PBS1x+3%FBS (no need to re-suspend), and spin down at 2,000 rpm for 5min (you can spin down faster now because your cells are dead). Flick plate. 
   - Add 250ul PBS1x and leave cells like that if you want to leave them overnight.
7) On the next day (or same day after fixation), spin down at 2,000rpm 3-5min, flick to remove SNT.
8) Re-suspend cells in antibody mix containing intracellular and intranuclear antibodies. IMPORTANT: this antibody mix has to be made in 1X Permeabilization buffer (it is made of the detergent saponin, that will reversibly permeabilize the membrane to allow antibodies to go in). To make 1X permeabilization buffer, dilute 10XPermeabilization buffer (brown color) in ddw. 
9) Incubate cells with intracellular/intranuclear antibodies in 1XPerm buffer for 30min-1h at room temp. Note: standard staining time for intracellular antibodies (such as cytokines, granzymes) is typically 30min and for transcription factors is 1h. I personally tend to mix all of them in my stainings, so I end up staining everything for 1h at RT (and it looks great).
**Some tips for this protocol:
- To ensure intracel/intranuclear antibodies give me the brightest signal, I always stain for them the day I will run FACS. 
- If you are only doing intracellular staining for proteins that are in the cytoplasm, the Foxp3 ebio kit is not required. It would be enough to, after L/D and surface stain, to fix your cells for 10min in 1% PFA (in PBS1x), wash it off, then leave in PBS1x overnight until you are ready to stain intracellularly. Then, stain intracellularly in saponin solution (1XPerm buffer) for 30min-1h at RT (I prefer 1h)
- If you follow the vendor’s protocol for intracellular/intranuclear staining kits, they typically add washing steps with the saponin. I personally never do them because 1) you lose cells the more you wash/flick, 2) vendors try to make you use more reagent so that you have to re-stock faster.

title: FilipinIII_stain
text:
Filipin III Fluorescence Staining of Free Cholesterol in Immune Cells for Flow
Filipin Complex: Sigma (F-9765)
Stock: 25 mg/ml in DMSO
Working Solution: 0.05 mg/ml in Perm/Wash Buffer

Perform surface stain in FACS buffer
Wash cells with FACS buffer 1X
Thoroughly resuspend cells in 100 ul of BD Cytofix/Cytoperm solution per well and incubate for 20 min at 4C in the dark. Avoid cell aggregation by vortexing prior to adding the Cytofix/Cytoperm solution
Wash cells 2X in a buffer that contains saponin (BD Perm/Wash buffer)
Stain cells with 100 ul of filipin working solution for 2h at room temperature (protected from light)
Rinse 2X with PBS
Keep protected from light and at 4C

title: TIL_prep_MC38_sc_MRC
text:
Lymphocyte Tissue Preparation from subcutaneous tumors
Miguel Reina-Campos 10/2019

Inject 3ug of iv antibody (ie 15ul CD8a-APC-Cy7 + 185ul PBS). 3-4 min after, sack the mice (cd).
Open skin by incision in the lower part of the back and use hands to expose tumor
Resect tumor and place in P24 well on ice, if tumor is large enough can be split into two:

Dry well for histology (frozen – OCT) is needed
RP5 media for flow

Collect draining lymph node by exposing it through the fat and remove it with tweezers
Collect spleen
Weight tumors before starting tissue prep

Start with tumor processing:

Mince tissue with scissors in a 50 ml falcon. Alternatively chop down with a razor blade in a P60 plate on ice.
Add Collagenase-I digestion in 5ml in the 50 ml falcon and incubate @37C for 30 min

Collagenase-I recipe – Prepare under the hood
-2ml HG (aliquoted in the -20 fridge) – Do not refreeze aliquot
-200ul 1M MgCl2 (J’s bench)
-200ul 1M CaCl2 (J’s bench)
-10ml Fetal Bovine Serum
-QS to 200ml w/RPMI 1640 1x
100x HG STOCK SOLUTION (STERILE): makes 500ml
59.58g HEPES
14.6g L-glutamine B-grade
500ml (QS to line) RPMI 1640 1x
use stir bar to mix
pH to 7.5 (will take 10-20ml 5N NaOH)
make 10ml aliquots
store @20oC in freezer long-term
While tumors are dissociating, process spleens and lymph nodes and leave them on ice

Filter digested tumors using a 70 um filter (reuse filter for same samples), rinse it with cold PBS. Use syringe plunger to dissociate tumor chunks through the filter.
Centrifuge at 1600 rpm 4 min
After centrifugation and filtration of tumors, resuspend pellet in 5ml 44% Percoll using a 10 ml pipette.

1x PERCOLL STOCK (STERILE): makes 500ml
450ml Percoll (Sigma P1644)
50ml 10x DPBS w/o Ca Mg
keep sterile
store @4<sup>oC in fridge long-term
if removed 50ml from original 500ml percoll bottle to make room for DPBS, bring this to 1X too, do not discard.
44% PERCOLL: makes 100ml
WILL NEED AT LEAST 5ml PER TISSUE (IEL+LP) PER MOUSE
44ml 1x Percoll (recipe above)
56ml RPMI 1640 1x
store @4<sup>oC in fridge overnight
DOE: bring to RT
67% PERCOLL: makes 100ml
WILL NEED AT LEAST 2ml PER TISSUE (IEL+LP) PER MOUSE
67ml 1x Percoll (recipe above)
33ml 1x DPBS w/o Ca Mg
store @4<sup>oC in fridge overnight
DOE: bring to RT

Add the 44% percoll-cell suspension into a 15ml Falcon tube
Insert a glass Pasteur pipette and deliver 67% Percoll to the bottom of the tube.
Spin 20 min at 2,000 rpm (NO brake) and collect interphase with Pasteur pipette into 15ml falcon tubes, fill up with RP5 and spin down at 2,000 rpm for 8min.
Re-suspend pellet in desired counting volume and continue with your staining.

title: RNA Isolation from Sorted Cells
text:
RNA Isolation from Sorted Cells
and
cDNA preparation

Sort ~50K cells of interest into 500 ul of Trizol. Careful not to dilute Trizol too much – Sort into media, spin down and resuspend in Trizol if necessary.
Extracted cells in Trizol can be kept at -80C.
Thaw Trizol:cells @ RT
Add 100 ul chloroform.
Vortex 15 seconds.
Incubate 2-3 minutes at RT.
Centrifuge 15 min at 12000 g at 4C – Work on ice from now on.
Transfer aqueous phase to new clean tube ~250 ul (if 500 ul were used).
Add 1ul glycoblue.
Add 300 ul isopropanol.
Incubate at -80C for at least 1h.
Centrifuge 20 min at highest speed 4C.
Remove supernatant.
Wash with 500 ul 75% ethanol (cold).
Centrifuge 15 min at 7400g 4C.
Remove ethanol and air dry (10 min).
Resuspend in 20 ul water.

Remove DNA contamination

Add 2ul of 10X TURBO DNase Buffer and 1ul TURBO DNase to 20 ul of RNA, and mix gently
Incubate at 37C for 20-30 min
Add resuspended Inactivation Reagent (2ul to 23 ul mix), and mix well
Incubate 5 min at RT, mixing occasionally
Centrifuge at 10000g for 1.5 min and transfer the RNA to a fresh tube

cDNA preparation – Assuming RNA comes from same amount of cells
Quantify with Qubit/Nanodrop

Use kit (pink box @ -20C): Mix 8 ul RNA, 1ul dNTP, 1ul random hexamer (50 ng/ul).
Incubate at 65C for 5min.
Prepare 2X reaction mix in order – Make MasterMix

10x RT buffer – 2 ul
25 mM MgCl2 – 4 ul
0.1 M DTT – 2 ul
RNase out – 1ul

Add 2X reaction to RNA.
Incubate at RT for 2 minutes.
Add 1ul superscript II to each tube.
PCR program:

RT 10 min
42C 50 min
70 15 min

Chill on ice.
Add 1 ul RNAse H and incubate 37C 20 min.

title: Cell Trace Violet labeling
text:
Cell Trace Violet labeling

Prepare CTV stock by adding 20ul DMSO to one vial of reagent.
Warm cells in PBS (w/o Ca++ and Mg++) for 10min at 37’C
Dilute cells to 10x10^6cells/ml
Add 1ul of CTV in DMSO to each ml of cell suspension in PBS.
Vortex gently to ensure equal exposure to dye
Incubate cells for 20min at 37’C in the dark
Add 5X of staining volume of culture medium containing at least 1% protein to cells. Incubate for 5 min.
Pellet cells by centrifugation and wash 2X
Resuspend and plate out.

title: Genotyping PCR info
text:
Genotyping PCR info
Vhl flox
The following primers were used to detect 1-lox and 2-lox alleles of Vhlh: FwdI (5′-CTGGTACCCACGAAACTGTC-3′), FwdII (5′-CTAGGCACCGAGCTTAGAGGTTTGCG-3′), and Rev primer (5′-CTGACTTCCACTGATGCTTGT CACAG-3′). The Vhlh 2-lox allele was identified as a ∼460-bp band, the 1-lox allele was detected as a ∼260-bp band, and the wild-type allele was detected as a ∼290-bp band.
For some reason we only use the two highlighted primers. I assume because we’re not attempting to detect the ~260 bp band of the 1-lox allele.
These are also different from the JAX PCR primers will generate similar product sizes though. Although JAX PCR protocol does not utilize 3 primers.
hif1a flox
Hif-1α 1-lox and 2-loxalleles were detected with following primers: Fwd1 (5′-TTGGGGATGAAAACATCTGC-3′), Fwd2 (5′-GCAGTTAAGAGCACTAGTTG-3′), and Rev (5′-GGAGCTATCTCTCTAGACC-3′). The wild-type allele was identified as a ∼240-bp band, the 2-lox allele was detected as a ∼260-bp band, and 1-loxallele was detected as a ∼270-bp band.
Same for the HIF1a PCR, we for some reason do not check for the 1-lox allele which is approximately 270 bp
hif2a flox
The WT, 2-loxP, and 1-loxP allele can be distinguished by a multiplex PCR [primer (P) 1: 5′-CAGGCAGTATGCCTGGCTAATTCCAGTT-3′; P2: 5′-CTTCTTCCATCATCTGGGATCTGGGACT-3′; P3: 5′-GCTAACACTGTACTGTCTGAAAGAGTAGC-3′]. The WT allele produces a 410-bp fragment (P1 and P2), the 2-loxP allele produces a 444-bp fragment (P1 and P2), and the 1-loxP allele produces a 340-bp fragment (P1 and P3)
Andrew ordered truncated versions of these primers, which are different than the genotyping primers suggested on the jax website. These are labeled as hif2380, hif2 381, and hif2430.
Have had issues with these primers so will order the Jax pair of primers as well, will label these HIF2FJax and HIF2RJax.
HIF2FJax: 5’ GAG AGC AGC TTC TCC TGG AA 3’
HIF2RJax: 5’ TGT AGG CAA GGA AAC CAA GG 3’
Yields different band sizes as follows:
Mutant = ~220 bp
Heterozygote = 182 bp and ~220 bp
Wild type = 182 bp
PCR Protocol 94, 59, 72

text:
Procedure:

End-Repair



Use End-it DNA End-repair Kit from Epicentre


uL
DNA+H2O 34
10X End Repair Buffer 5
2.5mM dNTPs Mix 5
10mM ATP Mix 5
END-IT enzyme mix 1
total 50


Incubate for 45 min at room temperature.
Mini-elute purification (Zymo DNA Clean&Concentrator). Elute it twice in 16ul of EB
Total elute volume is 32uL.

2. Addition of an ‘A’ Base to the 3’ End of the DNA fragments

Incubate for 30 min at 37C.
Mini-elute purification (Zymo DNA Clean&Concentrator).
Elute it in 8ul of EB

3. Ligation of Adapters to the Ends of the DNA Fragments
uL
DNA 8
2X Ligation Buffer 10
Adaptor 1 ( Adaptor was diluted 1:10 in DDW before add it)
Quick Ligase 1
total 20

Incubate for 20 min. at room temperature. Add 1 uL of NEB USER. Incubate at 37C for 15 minutes.
Mini-elute purification (Zymo DNA Clean&Concentrator). Elute twice in 10ul of EB (reuse). Total elute volume is 10uL.

Note: If you use NEB adaptor, remember to add 1uL USER Enzyme to incubate at 37C for 15 min after ligation.
4. Size selection of library using Gel purification
Materials
Nanosep MF Filter tube(VWR Cat.29300-642)
SYBR Gold (Invitrigen S11494)
Method
Prepare the Gel
• Prepare 8 % polyacrymide gel or buy:
40 % acryl (29:1) 6mL
5X TBE 3mL
ddH2O 21mL
10%APS 300uL(Fresh Made)
TEMED 40uL (Add it in fumehood)
Running buffer is 0.5X TBE . (600 ml/gel)
Run the Gel
• Add 6x Bromo phenol blue/xylene cyanol loading dye into the amplified library to make it 1X.
• Choose log ladder, load 10uL into the first line and the last line,.
• Load all samples into 8% polyacrymide gel every other line.
• Run at 200volt for 70 min, when the yellow dye reaches the bottom of the gel.
Stain and Cut the gel
• Gel Staining
Use a glass container for staining
Staining Buffer( Prepare in Glassware bottle)
(100ml 1X TAE, 10uL 10,000 x SYBR Gold )
Put gel into staining buffer and gently shake for 10min.
Cover the plate by foil to avoid the light.
• Excise bands from 200bps to 500bps with a clean scalpel.
• Minced the gel piece by using a 0.5ml tube with holes in the bottom. (Put the 0.5mL tube into a 1.5mL or 2mL tube, and centrifuge at 14k for 3 min. Make holes with a needle.)
• Add 400uL EB Buffer to cover the gel pieces, Shake for O/N at 37oC.
DNA Precipitation
• Transfer the supernatant to Nanoseq column , spin 2 min @ 14k.
• Transfer the rest of things in the sample tube to the column, spin 2 min @ 14k.
• Add EB Buffer to bring to a total volume of 400ul.
• Add 45uL 3M NaOAC(ph 5.2) and vortex to mix.
• Add 2ul glycogen(20mg/ml) and 1.2mL cold 100% ETOH, vortex.
• Freeze at -80°C for 1h (or O/N), spin 13.8K for 30min in cold room or @4<sup>oC. Remove supernatant.
• Wash with 1mL 70% EtOH, vortex, spin for 15min @13.8k rpm, remove all traces of EtOH, air dry
5 minutes (pellet turns clear).
• Resuspend precipitated DNA in 10ul EB.

title: CB4.Mitochondria dyes
text:
MitoTracker Green FM probe (FITC)
What for: stains total mitochondria, it measures mitochondrial mass / cell content
MW 671.88
Stock Solution 1 mM
DMSO volume 74.42 µL
Working Solution 25 nM
D.F. 1:40,000 (dilute 1:40 in warm PBS and then 1:1,000 into final sample tube)
Use working concentrations of 25–500 nM
MitoTracker Deep Red FM probe (APC)
What for: labels ‘healthy’ mitochondria with robust proton gradient, it measures respiration
MW 543.58
Stock Solution 1 mM
DMSO volume 91.98 µL
Working Solution 25 nM
D.F. 1:40,000 (dilute 1:40 in warm PBS and then 1:1,000 into final sample tube)
Use working concentrations of 25–500 nM
MitoSOX Red (BV605 or PE)
What for: measures superoxide accumulation
Make a 5 mM stock solution of MitoSOX reagent by dissolving the contents of the vial in 13 µL of anhydrous DMSO
Working Solution 5 µM
D.F. 1:1,000 (into final sample tube)
Optimize the staining solution concentration between 100 nM to 5 µM to maximize signal-to-noise ratio and minimize cellular toxicity.
Additional Notes
Include unstained controls & FMOs
Work on congenically mixed cells to avoid technical biases
Steps
Goal is to have 1-5 million cells/tube
Centrifugation steps carried out at 400g for 3 minutes


Equilibrate one vial of dye at room temp, then resuspend it


Count the cells from each condition and place them into individual FACS tubes


Wash cells in warm PBS and resuspend them in 1 mL of warm PBS


Add 1 µL of dye to each FACS tube with the cell suspension (dilution 1:1,000)


Stain for 20 minutes in the incubator at 37 ºC


Quickly wash cells in warm PBS


Stain for 10 minutes at RT dark in PBS



Congenic staining + reporter genes



Wash cells in warm PBS


Acquire samples


MitoSOX Red (PE-Texas Red)
Materials

MitoSOX Red (#M36008): 5 mM stock (dissolve 50 μg vial in 13 μL anhydrous DMSO; aliquot and store at -20°C protected from light; stable for months).
HBSS with Ca/Mg (pre-warmed)
FACS buffer: PBS + 2% FBS (ice-cold).
Centrifuge at 4°C

Step-by-Step Protocol
Resuspend cells in ice-cold FACS buffer at 1–2 × 106 cells/mL.
Aliquot 100–500 μL (0.5–2 × 106 cells) per tube for samples/controls.
Prepare fresh 5 μM working solution: Dilute 5 mM stock 1:1000 (5 µM) in pre-warmed (37°C) HBSS (with Ca/Mg; no serum).
Centrifuge cells; aspirate supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 500 μL of 5 μM MitoSOX solution per tube.
Vortex gently to mix.
Incubate 20 min at 37°C in dark (water bath or incubator; gentle agitation optional).
Stop reaction: resuspend cells in 3 mL ice-cold FACS buffer; centrifuge (300–400 × g, 5 min, 4°C).
Aspirate supernatant from MitoSOX-washed cells.
Resuspend in 50 μL Fc block solution; incubate 5–10 min on ice.
Without washing, add live/dead + surface antibody cocktail (in FACS buffer; total final volume 100 μL per tube, i.e., 50 μL Fc + 50 µL antibody mix).
Vortex gently.
Incubate 20 min on ice (or 4°C), dark (longer for dim markers like PD-1).
Add 2 mL ice-cold FACS buffer; centrifuge (300–400 × g, 5 min, 4°C).
Resuspend in 200 μL ice-cold FACS buffer.
Filter through 40 μm strainer into FACS tubes to remove clumps.
Keep on ice/dark until acquisition (analyze within 1–2 hours; MitoSOX signal can drift).
MitoTRACKER Deep Red (APC)
Materials

MitoTracker Deep Red FM (M22426): for 1 mM solution, dilute 1 x 50 µg vial with 92 µL of anhydrous DMSO, final dilution (for T cells) is 1:100,000 (10nM)
HBSS with Ca/Mg (pre-warmed)
FACS buffer: PBS + 2% FBS (ice-cold).
Centrifuge at 4°C

Step-by-Step Protocol
Resuspend cells in ice-cold FACS buffer at 1–2 × 106 cells/mL.
Aliquot 100–500 μL (0.5–2 × 106 cells) per tube for samples/controls.
Prepare fresh 10 nM working solution: Dilute 1 mM stock 1:100,000 (10 nM) in pre-warmed (37°C) HBSS (with Ca/Mg; no serum).
Centrifuge cells; aspirate supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 500 μL of 10 nM MitoTracker solution per tube.
Vortex gently to mix.
Incubate 20 min at 37°C in dark (water bath or incubator; gentle agitation optional).
Stop reaction: resuspend cells in 3 mL ice-cold FACS buffer; centrifuge (300–400 × g, 5 min, 4°C).
Aspirate supernatant from MitoTracker-washed cells.
Resuspend in 50 μL Fc block solution; incubate 5–10 min on ice.

Incubate 20 min on ice (or 4°C), dark (longer for dim markers like PD-1).
Add 2 mL ice-cold FACS buffer; centrifuge (300–400 × g, 5 min, 4°C).
Resuspend in 200 μL ice-cold FACS buffer.
Filter through 40 μm strainer into FACS tubes to remove clumps.
Keep on ice/dark until acquisition (analyze within 1–2 hours; MitoTracker signal can drift).
MitoSTATUS Red (APC)
Materials

MitoStatus Red (BD Biosciences): 0.2 mM solution in DMSO, final dilution is 1:20,000 (10 nM). Add 460 μL of anhydrous DMSO directly to the 50 μg vial.
HBSS with Ca/Mg (pre-warmed)

Resuspend cells in ice-cold FACS buffer at 1–2 × 106 cells/mL.

text:
Hi Seahorse Assay on sorted cells with the Seahorse HS Mini instrument

Day before – hydrate sensor cartridge by filling all wells of calibration plate with 200 uL water. Don’t forget to include the surrounding wells (which need 400 uL each).

Incubate at 37C in a non-CO2 incubator overnight.

Day before – Prepare XFp PDL or HS PDL Miniplates – obtain the XFp PDL Miniplates and remove the foil seal(s) from the plate(s) that will be used. Place the plates in a non-humidified, non-CO2 37 °C incubator overnight.

Once you have sorted cells of interest!

Spin cells at 500g for 5 minutes without topping up the tubes – aspirate gently with pipette
Resuspend cells in 100 µL Seahorse XF media and count
Adjust volume to concentration of 200,000 cells in 50 µL (125,000 cells minimum requirement)
Add sterile water to the moat around the cell culture wells, 400 μL per chamber.
Plate cells in wells B-C-D for WT and E-F-G for KO (in 50 uL of XF media)
Plate 50 µL of XF media in wells A and H as background
Centrifuge the plate at 500g for 5 minutes – verify cell adherence and monolayer
Gently lift the silicone inserts from the plate using the provided tool (do not remove entirely)
Spin the plate again for 1 minute
Remove the silicone inserts entirely.
Gently add 130uL of XF media (to avoid detaching adhered cells)
Incubate at 37C in a non-CO2 incubator for 1hr
Replace the water in the sensor cartridge with XF calibrant (200ul/well),

Incubate at 37C in a non-CO2 incubator for 30 minutes

Resuspend Mitochondrial Stress test reagents in desired assay media.
After cartridge is incubated for 30 minutes – add reagents to injection ports
Run sensor cartridge with calibration plate
Add plated cells to the HS Mini + run Mitochondrial Stress Test

Reagents to Make
Seahorse XF Media
RPMI (9.7 mL) + 1mM pyruvate (100 µL) + 2mM L-glutamine (100 µL) + 10mM glucose (100 µL)
pH – 7.4 – incubate the final XF Assay Medium at 37 °C until ready for use
Component Concentrations
*** See page 14 of the Mito Stress Test user guide***
Resuspend using Seahorse XF Media
Port A - 1.5 µM Oligomycin
Port B - 1.0 µM FCCP
Port C - 1.0 µM FCCP
Port D - 0.5 µM Rotenone + Antimycin

title: General Seahorse Protocol
text:
Goldrath Lab – XF96 – Seahorse protocol
Materials needed:
XF Calibrant (catalog #100840-000 individually or in pack with sensor cartridge)
XF Cell Plate (catalog #101085-004 individually or in pack with sensor cartridge)
XF Sensor Cartridge (FluxPak catalog #102310-001 [18 sensor plates])
Buffer and glucose free media of Choice pH = 7.4 (we have Seahorse XF Assay Media catalog #102352-000)
Glucose – Final Concentration 2g/L
L-glutamine – Final concentration 2mM
Optional materials (depending on tests needed to be run on cells):
XF Cell Mito Stress Test Kit (catalog #101706-100)
Purpose is to evaluate mitochondrial function of cells (all these chemicals could be ordered separately from Sigma)

Components:


Oligomycin – PORT A (10 uM in port)



FCCP – PORT B (10 uM in port)
Antimycin A – PORT C (10 uM in port)
Rotenone – PORT C (10 uM in port)

XF Glycolysis Stress Test Kit (catalog #102194-100)
Purpose is to evaluate glycolytic function of cells
Components:

Glucose – PORT A (10 mM in port)
Oligomycin - PORT B (10 uM in port)
2-Deoxy-D-glucose PORT C (1 M in port)

Procedure:

Turn on instrument and start the Seahorse software (at least 4 hours ahead of time) to allow it to prewarm to 37°C.
XF Sensor Cartridge must be hydrated from 4-72 hrs prior to running the assay on the XF96 instrument. Cartridges cannot be hydrated for longer than 72 hours as this results in breakdown of the materials in the cartridge itself.


Equilibrate the sensor cartridge by adding 200 μl of XF Calibrant pH 7.4 to each well of the utility plate that comes with the sensor cartridge.


Incubate up to 72 hours at 37°C without CO2 (if incubating for longer than 24 hours they recommend parafilming the plate to avoid evaporation)


Prepare and add compounds to XF Sensor Cartridge injection ports (optional)





Prepare all solutions as recommended by assay kit protocols and add to injection ports as needed.


Allow compounds to incubate in a non-CO2 37°C incubator as well once added to the Sensor Cartridge.


Prepare Cell Plate to be read

Prewarm your assay media (add glucose if necessary for assay DO NOT ADD if running Mitochondrial Stress Test) to 37°C.
Coat cell plate with BD Cell-Tak prior to plating of T cells

20 μl of Cell-Tak solution is necessary to coat the XF 96 well cell plates.
To coat a whole plate, make the Cell-Tak solution by combining:

2000 μl 0.1M pH 8.0 bicarbonate buffer (filter-sterilized if growing cells in plate)
12.58 μl 1N NaOH
25.15 μl Cell-Tak




Mix solution well and coat all wells within 10 minutes
Incubate for a minimum of 20 minutes at 37°C (longer is not a problem, even if everything evaporates)
Pour off/aspirate Cell-Tak solution and wash with 200 μl sterile water 2x to remove all bicarbonate (very important step may affect readings on Seahorse if residual bicarbonate is present)
Plates can be air dried and stored at 2-8°C for up to two weeks for later use.




Count T cells and prepare single cell suspension for even seeding. For the XF96 we have yet to test in vivo activated cells, but for in vitro activated T cells a density of 2x10^5 - 2.5x10^5 has been optimal for achieving good ECAR and OCR readings.
Add cells to wells of cell plate as needed in a volume of 50 μl and spin plate down at 200 RCF for 5 minutes to gently plate them into the Cell-Tak.
Bring volume of each well carefully up to necessary volume for measurements to be done.

225 μl if not adding compounds or performing stress tests.
150 μl if performing mitochondrial or glycolytic stress tests.

Place cell plate in 37°C non CO2 incubator for at least 30 minutes to warm up and equlibrate (if plate has not been in a CO2 incubator up to this point, it can be immediately read if it is warm).




Begin protocol on XF96 Instrument and begin calibration of the sensor plate.



After ~25 minutes calibration will be complete and cell plate can be added for measurement of cells.



Depending on assay, measurements will take possibly ~2 hrs then software will produce a message asking you if the assay is complete and whether you’d like to eject the sensor and cell plate. Click yes and logout and exit the software. If no one else is using the Seahorse please turn off the heater within the instrument (Software will ask if you’d like to leave it on).

title: Western Blot Protocol
text:
Western Blot Protocol
Quantify Protein (BCA Protein Assay)

Dilute Standard in 96 well flat bottom plate

Add 184 ul of H2O to the first well of the column then 100ul to the rest of the wells in the column. Add nothing to the last well
Add 16ul of BSA (2mg/ml) to the first well and then do 1:2 dilutions down the column (transfer 100ul).
Standard curve 16ug, 8ug, 2ug, 1ug, 0.5ug

Dilute samples in 96 well flat bottom plate

Add 2ul of sample to 98ul of H2O

Mix reagent A to B in a 50:1 mixture (5mL A to 100mL B) and add 100ul to samples. Add to lowest [BSA] up to highest [BSA] then add to samples.
Incubate at 37°C for 15min (or until samples turn purple)
Read in plate reader @ 560nm
Determine protein concentration using standard curve. Calculate volume of sample needed for 15ug.

Sample Preparation:










Sample Volume
Sample Buffer (4x 1x)
Reducing Agent (10x1x)
H2O
Total Volume




Volume determined above
5ul
2ul
Make up volume
20ul




Heat @ 70°C for 10mins
Spin down for about 1 min@ max speed
Store at -20°C

If stored at -20°C, thaw samples then heat for a few minutes @ 70°C and spin down @ max speed


Electrophoresis

Make 1L of running buffer (20X1X)

50mL running buffer, fill to 1L in graduated cylinder with water
Take 200mL and place in a second graduated. Add 500ul of antioxidant (do this immediately before you are going to run you gel).

Set up gel apparatus

Wash gel wells with running buffer and take the tape off
Place 200ml of running buffer with antioxidant solution from 1b. in the middle part of the gel box and check for leaks
Pour running buffer from 1a. on the outside

Load 7ul of ladder and 20ul of sample (all of sample that you prepared above)
Run @ 100V for 5 minutes, check, then turn up

Transfer

Set up transfer apparatus
Make up transfer buffer

Add 100mL 10X transfer buffer into a graduated cylinder. Fill to 500mL with H2O then add 200mL methanol. Fill to 1L with H2O (if you add methanol directly to undiluted 10X transfer buffer, you will cause precipitation)

Cut membrane to size slightly smaller than filter paper. Do not touch the membrane (the membrane will get dirty from protein from your hands).
Set up 3 small plastic containers and fill with methanol, dH2O, or transfer buffer respectively

Place membrane in methanol for 30sec to 1 min, then rinse in dH2O, then transfer buffer, allowing it to sit transfer buffer while you proceed

Fill large glass dish with transfer buffer and put in transfer holder black side down

Crack open gel and cut off wells at the bottom
In holder place foam, 2 filter papers, gel, membrane, 2 filter papers, and then foam. Roll out the bubbles and close holder under transfer buffer

Place holder in apparatus (black to black), then place in cold room on stir plate. Pour transfer buffer from bowl into the apparatus
Run at 70V (around 200mA) for 80min.

Check after 5min that the timer is working
May check periodically to make sure that the transfer is running and no errors have occurred.


Blocking

Make up blocking buffer in 50mL conical

BSA (5%) or milk in TBS-0.1% tween-20 (ex. 2.5g BSA per 50ml)

Take blot out and place in container. Pour blocking buffer (10-20mL) to cover blot. Do not pour directly on the blot.
Place on shaker 1-2 hrs @ RT or @4°C overnight

Primary

Dilute primary Ab in blocking buffer from above.
If you need to work with a small volume of Ab, Place blot in a bag that is sealed on 3 sides, then add ~ 2ml of diluted Ab and seal the top. Label the blot then place face down on the shaker. Shake 1-2hr @ RT or @4°C overnight (this will depend on the primary antibody you are using).
If you can work in a larger volume of Ab. Add 10ml of diluted Ab to container that you blocked in. Shake 1-2hr @ RT or @4°C overnight (this will depend on the primary antibody you are using).
Cut open bag and place blot in container (or pour of primary Ab from container) and rinse the blot 3x quickly with TBS-0.1% Tween-20. Depending on your primary Ab, you may be able to reuse it several times so you can store it at 4°C until next use otherwise discard down sink).
Wash 3x in TBS-0.1% Tween-20 for at 15-20 mins each time

Secondary

Dilute secondary Ab (1:10,000) in blocking buffer from above. Add secondary Ab for 45mins shaking @RT.
Rinse blot in TBS-0.1% Tween-20 3x for 15- 20mins each time

Developing

Remove all liquid from container that blot was washing in.
More sensitive ECL kit

Make 4mL of a 1:1 mixture of the reagents and add to the blot
Leave on for 5 mins then aspirate off

Less sensitive ECL kit

Make 4mL of a 1:1 mixture of reagents and add to the blot
Leave on for 1 min then aspirate off

Pick up blot with forceps (make sure you pick up by edge of blot) and let drip onto a kimwipe to remove last bits of developing reagent. Place blot into a plastic divider inside cassette and gently remove bubbles with fingers.
Develop in dark room as soon as possible

Draw ladder before removing membrane from cassette


Stripping

Add 174ul β-Mercaptoethanol to 25ml of stripping buffer – work in fumehood as this will stink.
Place blot in hybridization tube and add stripping buffer (in hood). Place in heated spinner @ 70°C for 30 min with counter balance tube.
Discard buffer in fume hood with water running.
Rinse tube with dH2O water until there are no bubbles and you can’t smell the stripping buffer anymore.
Place blot in container with TBS-0.1% Tween-20 and shake for 2-3x 15-20mins @ RT.
Start at blocking step
