title: Western blot
text:
Western blot
Sample Prep
1. Add 2-ME (under chemical fume hood) to lysates at 1:10 concentration into Laemmli sample buffer at time of sample prep.
2. Boil samples in thermal cycler at 95C for 5 minutes
3. Prepare and load 30 ug (10-100ug total protein per well) samples (refer to excel sheet from BCA) into wells and proceed with WB. Dilute as needed with sample buffer to ensure equal protein loading across wells. If you have extra empty wells, fill with buffer + loading buffer to ensure even running of the gel
Protein ladder in Coopersmith freezer- using 5-6 ul is sufficient
SDS-PAGE
4. Run gel at 90V for the first 30 min. After the band has consolidated and made it through the stacking gel section, you can bump up gel to 150V for remaining time (20-40 min). Keep an eye on the gel.
5. When blue bands reach black line on the gel cassette, stop electrophoresis chamber.
6. Take out cassette and crack open using green key
7. Image gel on the imager if interested in protein concentration (similar to Coomassie)
After turning machine on, navigate to Application 🡪 Protein gels 🡪Stain free gel
Exposure: faint bands
Expose gel by hitting camera in bottom right of screen
Transfer
8. While gel is being exposed, prepare the transfer sandwich
9. Pour transfer buffer in one container and 100% methanol in another
10. Dip sandwich pads into transfer buffer and place one stack at bottom of transfer sandwich in the Turboblot platform.
11. Prepare the PVDF membrane next by soaking membrane in 100% methanol until membrane becomes clear (30s-1min) and then dip into transfer buffer before putting membrane onto the transfer stack.
*Make sure there are no bubbles under the membrane
12. Place gel on top of membrane and make sure there are no bubbles here either. Use roller to gently roll out any bubbles between membrane and gel.
*Picture on sheet above Turbo transfer if you have questions about these steps*
13. Place top sandwich stack on top of the gel and close the cassette
*Make sure the iron prongs in the back are present (sometimes they come off)
14. Run the Turboblot on the mixed MW protocol (7 min) and select the number of gels you are transferring
Membrane Blocking
15. During transfer, prepare 2.5% BSA TBS-T
16. After transfer, place membrane (check to make sure ladder has transferred to the membrane) in a box to block for 1 hour in 2.5% BSA TBS-T
*If membrane dries out, soak in methanol and then transfer buffer prior to putting it into the blocking solution
17. After blocking, wash membrane 3x for 5 min each rocking at RT (one by Yvonne’s bench and chemical fume hood in Ford lab) with TBS-T
Primary and Secondary Ab Incubations
18. Dilute primary abs according to manufacture instructions in 1% BSA-TBST and place on rocker at 4C overnight.
Use 1:500 – 1:1000 p.AKT antibody (CST, 4060S) in 1% BSA
19. The next morning, wash membrane 3x for 5 min each rocking at RT (one by Yvonne’s bench and chemical fume hood in Ford lab) with TBS-T
20. Dilute secondary abs according to manufacture instructions in 1% BSA-TBST and place on rocker at RT for 1 hour
Use 1:5000 goat anti-rabbit (abcam, ab205718) in 1% BSA
21. At end of incubation, wash membrane 3x for 5 min each rocking at RT
Imaging
22. During last wash, bring membranes to Coopersmith lab and use the ECL reagents to image
23. Make an ECL substrate mix of 1:1 with the clear and brown bottles (to the left of the electrophoresis chamber)
*Can use Clarity max instead of Clarity if you want brighter bands
24. Drain membrane well and add ECL reagent and tilt the box back and forth for 1 min
25. During 1 min, turn on imager
26. After turning machine on, navigate to Application 🡪 Blots 🡪Chemiluminescence
Optimal exposure (if nothing shows up you can expose for longer amounts of time)
Expose gel by hitting camera in bottom right of screen
27. Export the membrane image using a flash drive and quantify using Biorad software if desired.

title: DNA extraction from CD8
text:
DNA extraction from CD8
Qiagen DNA blood extraction kit

Add ethanol to wash buffer concentrates if this is a new kit. If an old kit,look for evidence of ethanol being added to concentrate by prior user.
Heat up thermal mixer to 56C
Reconstitute protease if in lyophilized form. Otherwise, reconstituted solution will be in 4C
After collecting the cells, spin and pipette off the supernatant. Important here to get all of the sup without disturbing the pellet
Resuspend cell pellet in 200 ul of PBS
Add 20 ul of protease/sample and mix by pipetting
Add 200 ul buffer AL. Mix by vortexing
Incubate at 56C for 10 min. Centrifuge briefly to remove drops from lid
Add 200 ul of 98-100% ethanol. Vortex. Centrifuge briefly to remove drops from lid
Pipette mixture onto QIAamp mini spin columns + 2 ml collection tube and centrifuge at 6000xg (8000 RPM) for 1 min. Discard flow through and collection tube
Place spin column in new 2 ml collection tube and add 500 ul buffer AW1. Centrifuge at 6000xg (8000 RPM) for 1 min. Discard flow through and collection tube
Place spin column in new 2 ml collection tube and add 500 ul buffer AW2. Centrifuge at full speed for 3 min. Discard flow through and collection tube
Put spin column into new collection tube and spin at full speed for 1 min. This eliminates possible AW2 buffer carryover to next step.
Place spin column in new 1.5 ml centrifuge tube (not collection tube) and add 200 ul of distilled water and incubate at RT for 1 min
Centrifuge at 6000xg (8000 RPM) for 1 min to elute DNA
Measure DNA concentration and 260/280 on nanodrop. Continue to PCR amplification or freeze at -80

Sanger Sequencing Prep
Preparation of PCR product:

FWD primer = 2.5 ul (of 1:10 dilution)
RVS primer = 2.5 ul (of 1:10 dilution)
Q5 high fidelity polymerase master mix 2x = 25 ul
Genomic DNA = 150-250 ng (usually do around 200 ng)
H20 = fill up to 50 ul

Run PCR product

Middle thermal cycler Q5 program is 1 hour and 45 min

Running gel

Follow the protocol in the lab gel area
Load 16.67 ul of PCR product and 3.33 ul of 6x loading dye
Load ladder in first well, followed by samples
Run gel for 100V for 30 min

Submitting to Eton:

8 ul/sample for PCR products (8 ul for each reaction)
Primer are prepared at 5 ul in 5 uM concentration (5 ul of each fwd and rvs for every reaction, keep primers separate)
Go up to 50 ul with H20 after taking out genomic DNA amount and master mix amount (30 ul)

End Repair:

Check Kappa Hyperprep kit for adaptor concentration to use

Proliferation assay: T cell activation and CFSE labeling
We usually do this assay before ordering bulk FBS so as to pick the best lot number.


Get naive spleen(s) from young mouse, process, and Ack .


Coat 96-well plate with goat anti-hamster and anti-CD3




Goat anti-hamster: dilute the ab in PBS at 1:50 (100 ul per well)


Pipet 100 ul to the well and swirl
Incubate at 37C for at least 1 hr
Flick off the liquid and wash with PBS twice

- anti-CD3: repeat the same thing but use anti-CD (1:1000)
leave in 4C for prolonged storage


Enrich for T cells




follow MACS Streptavidin Microbeads protocol online
for biotinylated ab cocktail, use: NK1.1, F4/80, MHCII, B220, CD11b, and TER-119 at 1:200 and 500ul per spleen




Labeling T cells with CFSE



- Save some cells for unstained control and compensation set up


follow “Labeling T cells with CFSE” protocol on Goldrath server (skip step 5)




Plate the labeled cells in coated plate


100 ul of stained cells in testing media (1 mil cell/ml)
+ 100ul of testing media with 2X anti-CD28 (1:1000)


Record CFSE signal for 0hr, 24 hr, 48hr, 72hr, and 96hr on FITC channel. Suggested stain set



FITC* CFSE (for detection only)
eF450 CD8a
PE Cy7 CD4
APC Cy7 CD44

*Cell at 0 hr is very bright in FITC adjust PMT so that FITC peak is at maximum.
After 24 hr, FITC brightness will reduce but you should still have a single peak. This peak should represent your undivided T cells.

title: Trizol RNA Isolation
text:
Sort ~50K cells of interest into 500 μl of Trizol. Be careful not to dilute Trizol too much

Sort into media, spin down and resuspend in Trizol if necessary.

Extracted cells in Trizol can be kept at -80°C.
Thaw Trizol:cells @ RT
Add 100 μl chloroform.
Vortex 15 seconds.
Incubate 2-3 minutes at RT.
Centrifuge 15 min at 12000 g at 4°C -
Work on ice from now on.
Transfer aqueous phase to new clean tube ~250 μl (if 500 μl were used).
Add 1μl glycoblue.
Add 300 μl isopropanol.
Incubate at -80°C for at least 1h.
Centrifuge 20 min at highest speed 4°C.
Remove supernatant.
Wash with 500 μl 75% ethanol (cold).
Centrifuge 15 min at 7400g 4°C.
Remove ethanol and air dry (10 min).
Resuspend in 10 μl water.







Tip



Make sure to take off all ethanol (with P10)

title: Histology Ultimate Protocol-REVISED
text:
Epic Histology Protocol – for Spleen and Lymph Nodes
Tissue Processing

Materials

4% Formaldehyde/Paraformaldehyde(PFA) – see PFA protocol

Make fresh from high concentration stock each time
Use 15 conicals – enough to cover spleen/LN

5% Sucrose/ 4% formaldehyde (4mL sucrose, 3mL 37% formaldehyde, 20mL PBS)
10% Sucrose
30% Sucrose
OCT, Cryo-molds cassette, and dry ice
Fisherbrand Superfrost-Plus microscope slides
1x PBS

Method
Fixation and Dehydration

Sacrifice mouse and harvest spleen/ lymph nodes.
Drop organs into 4% formaldehyde/5% sucrose conicals IMMEDIATELY upon removal and place on ice.

Attach tubes to BellyDancer or something with rotation, or periodically rotate/tap to make sure fixative penetrates all directions.
Leave organs in fixative (4% formaldehyde) at least a combined 6 hours at 4°C

If sac’ing late in the day, okay to leave in solution overnight
Incubate in 5% Sucrose for at least 2 hours.





Aspirate out the fixative and pour in 9 mL of 10% Sucrose solution (w/ 4% formaldehyde is tissues have not been incubated for at least 6 hrs yet)

Incubate for 2-3 hrs at 4°C.




Replace 10% Sucrose with 30% Sucrose and incubate at 4 degree C° overnight or for the full day if it’s been fixed overnight already.


Embedding

Put processed organs into respective small Petri dishes with fresh OCT and use to:

Wash residual sucrose off by rolling around in OCT.

Fill up a Cry-mold cassette completely with OCT

Place the tissue at the bottom of the cassette, making sure that there are no bubbles

Place cassettes with tissues/OCT on a flat block of dry ice until OCT has turned opaque white
Store all blocks in labeled boxes in -80°C.

Fixation and Slide Preparation for Staining

Materials

Fixing reagent of choice: -20°C Acetone, 4% Formaldehyde (Stock 37% Formaldehyde w/ 5-10% methanol as preservative), 4% Paraformaldehyde (PFA, 100% pure formaldehyde)

See protocol for making 20% PFA (4% PFA easily degrades)

Coplin jars for acetone fixations
1X PBS (ridiculous amounts) – use 10X PBS for dilutions rather than 1X stocks
Coplin jars or slide holder chambers (for many samples) for washes
Glass slide holder (compatible with slide holder chamber)
Pap pen (creates liquid repelling barrier around sample)
Large Kimwipes
Thawed sample slides (no ice crystal damage): less than 5 minutes


Method

Fixation (pick one of following fixatives): After samples are thawed

-20°C Acetone – Harshest but cleaner fixation method, will destroy GFP and other very sensitive epitopes (protein pulldown/precipitation reaction)/ Note: acetone will smear off all permanent markers

Pour in enough acetone to cold coplin jar to cover sections on slides, AT MOST UP TILL THE FROSTED EDGE WITH WRITING (acetone will smear)
Carefully transport to -20°C and fix for 5 minutes
Carefully pull out slides individually and place on paper towels, allowing acetone to quickly evaporate
After evaporation, wash 3x with 1X PBS in coplin jars, 10-15 minutes each

4% Formaldehyde/ PFA – standard fixation (defer to this first)

Dilute high concentration formaldehyde/PFA stock to 4% in PBS

~50uL/section on each slide (Exp: 3 sections/slide = ~150uL)

Pipet ~50uL onto each sample at RT, careful not to damage section
Fix for 10 minutes
Wash 3x with 1X PBS in coplin jars, 5-10 minutes each time


Pap Penning and Preparation for Blocking/Staining

Lay out slides on paper towels and dry around the glass and individual sections using large Kimwipes (paper towels will form lint). DO NOT TOUCH SECTIONS WITH TOWELS!
Circle each individual section a few times with pap pen, allow to dry
Dip sections into PBS again to retain moisture

Blocking
Materials

Blocking Buffer – the Epic (Gelatin) Block (for 50mL)

1.5mL normal goat serum (3%)
1.5mL normal donkey serum (3%)
1.5-2.0 g BSA
1mL fishscale gelatin (advised to add after some PBS)
25ul Tween20 (0.05%)
50ul Triton-X-100 (0.1%)
250ul 10% Azide (0.05%)
Fill to the 50ml mark w/ 1x PBS
Optional: make ~5 tubes and aliquot into 15mL conicals and freeze to store

Fc Block
Vector Labs Avidin/Biotin blocking kit (if using biotinylated antibodies)
Hydration chamber (basically some sort of plastic sealable container with wet paper towels on the bottom – incubate slides so liquid does not evaporate)
Coplin jars or slide chambers (see fixation materials)
1x PBS

Method

Make master mix: depending on section size, add ~50uL Gelatin Block and ~5uL Fc block per sample

Pipet ~50uL onto pap pen circled section, making sure to cover section

Place slides into hydration chamber and incubate for at least 20-30 minutes

Ok to leave longer: this is a good stopping point if you need to take care of other stuff.

Only if using biotinylated antibodies – Avidin/Biotin block, perform in this order:

Tap slides on paper towel to remove blocking buffer
Apply 1 drop of avidin block onto each section – incubate 15 minutes

Tap slides on paper towel to remove blocking buffer

Apply 1 drop of biotin block onto each section – incubate 15 minutes

Rinse off/rehydrate each slide by dipping a few times into PBS (in Coplin jars)

Aspirate off extra liquid carefully using edges of Kimwipe. DO NOT TOUCH SECTION!

Slides are ready to stain

Staining
Materials

Epic (Gelatin) Blocking Buffer (see Blocking)
Antibodies (see list at end for antibodies and concentrations tested using this protocol)
Coplin jars or slide chambers (see fixation materials)
1x PBS
Hydration chamber (see Blocking)
37° Incubator

Method

Similar to Blocking, aspirate off extra liquid using kimwipes without letting slides completely dry out
Make master mix of respective Primary Ab (including biotinylated Abs) stains in the blocking buffer

Pipet Ab mixture onto sections ~50ul

Place slides into hydration chamber and seal lid
Incubate slides in hydration chamber in 37° incubator for 1 hour (after 1 hour, antibodies/proteins will start to denature)
After 1 hour, EITHER:

Put slides into PBS in coplin jars/slide chamber and wash 3x at 5-10 minutes each
OR, if working with a difficult Ab, move slides in hydration champer with Ab mixture still on into cold room and incubate for another 2-4 hrs. Afterwards, wash as in 5a.

If no secondary Ab is needed, move onto “Mounting”
Pipet on Secondary Ab mixture prepared same way as the Primary

Follow same steps as Primary Ab
Incubate for only 30-45 minutes at 37° (or else high background)

Wash slides 3x in 1x PBS, 5-10 minutes each time

Mounting and Sealing

Materials

Paper Towels
Kimwipes
Mounting Media – Invitrogen Pro-Long Gold Antifade Reagent (I prefer w/o DAPI)

Rest upside down to get rid of bubbles

Nail Polish (Sally Hansen brand, or anything that isn’t too thick)
Fisherbrand glass coverslips

Method

Using Kimwipes, wipe slides of all liquid and smear off some pap pen

Be very careful not to touch the section using Kimwipes
Leave slides in dark area like drawer to dry for a few minutes (not too long)

Apply very small drop of Mounting Media onto each section

NO BUBBLES – If bubbles form, aspirate off using a pipet

Carefully place on coverslips

Technique: place on one edge first and slowly lower onto the other

Carefully apply nail polish to edges of coverslip to seal onto the slide

Technique: do not move the coverslip; if nail polish is too thick, dilute it down with some acetone

Store slides in 4° until ready to view

Contact Information

If you are from the Goldrath Lab and are stuck with anything, you can contact me for assistance, wherever my awesomeness may be:
Edward Yang
edyang86@gmail.com
(626)242-5712
Random tips


37° incubation might not work for everything

For more sensitive staining such as KLRG-1 – stain for 1hr in 37° and then transfer to 4° for another 2-3hrs – overnight. Makes a big difference

Pay attention to appropriate fixation
This protocol works very well on staining for CD11c, CD45.1, CD4, and B220 thus far
CD8 staining can be a little weak
If cutting sections is difficult/rolling:

Use gradual pulling technique (similar to riding the block) by picking off one side of section first and pulling meticulously as it quickly sticks to slide
Warning: can be incredibly frustrating; use caution when cutting very important experiments

Lowering concentration of fixative can if these problems ensue, but higher risk of epitope degradation, especially if working with Thy1.1


Section a certain way… the longitudinal, not lateral, cuts for the spleen
Need a butt load of PBS – suggest using 10x
Be more careful w/ working in the light/sunlight after slides are stained
Everything is variable, whatever works works, and what works for some, will not for others


Microscope and Microscopy Core for Imaging

For confocal images, anything requiring AF647/APC, and stuff you want to publish, use the confocal microscopes at the UCSD SOM Microscopy Core: Olympus FV1000

Contact Jennifer Santini or whoever is the Managing Director of Microscopy Core
http://microscopy.ucsd.edu/ContactUs.html
http://microscopy.ucsd.edu/Reservations.html
She will guide you through all necessary training to use Microscope

Channels

405/Pacific Blue
488/FITC
546/PE
647/APC

Microscope settings

Pixels: no more than 10, any more is usually overkill (prone to bleaching)
1024x1024 is the size I use typically
Focus x2 scan on 512x512 yields best image/speed ratio



Antibodies
This chart below is a bit outdated, but general rule:

Primary antibody – 1:100-1:200 is a good range to start and will likely work

Can titrate up or down based on how dim/bright initial stain is

Secondary antibody – 1:500
AlexaFluor antibodies hold up well against bleaching. PE and FITC antibodies tend to bleach, but APC works pretty well.

Blocking Solutions
   
Background or unspecific staining often occurs for IHC antibody staining. Here we list commonly used blocking solutions during antibody staining procedure to reduce background or unspecific staining.
Peroxidase Blocking Soluiton (3% H2O2 in PBS):
       30% H2O2 ————————- 10 ml
       1X PBS —————————– 90 ml
       Mix well and store at 4 ºC for up to 3 months.
       Block sections for 10 minutes before blocking step or after primary antibody incubation. Note: this solution is recommended for paraffin sections.
 
Peroxidase Blocking Soluiton (0.3% H2O2 in Methanol):
       30% H2O2 ————————- 1 ml
       Methanol ————————– 99 ml
       Mix well and store at 4 ºC.
       Block sections for 20-30 minutes before serum blocking step prior to primary antibody incubation. Note: this solution is recommended for frozen sections. Blocking after primary antibody incubation may cause tissue damage.
 
Avidin/Biotin Block:
       Avidin 0.001% in PBS
       Biotin 0.001% in PBS
       Store these blocking solution at 4 ºC.    
Incubate sections for 10-15 min each and rinse with PBS between steps. Recommended to block before primary antibody incubation.

Normal Donkey Serum Block Solution:

title: IF Staining Protocol basic
text:
Basic Immunofluorescent Staining Protocol for OCT sections

Section frozen sections at 10um.
Dry at RT for 1 hour
Pap pen around tissue
Wash 3x PBS for 10min
Permeabilize if needed (nuclear or intracellular markers) with 0.1% Triton-X in PBS at RT in humidified chamber.

If surface markers only, skip to step 6.
All incubation steps after this will be in humidified chamber.

Block with DAKO block 1h
Wash 3x PBS for 10min
Primary Ab overnight at 4’C in humified chamber. Dilute antibody with DAKO antibody dilution buffer.

Next Day

Wash 3x PBS for 10min
If secondary is needed: Dilute secondary antibody with DAKO antibody dilution buffer (1:500-1:1000). Incubate at RT for 1-2h.
Wash 2x PBS for 10min.
DAPI (dilute 10ul in 1ml). Incubate 1min
Dump DAPI off
Dry slide as much as possible.
Add Vectashield vibrance mounting media and cover with glass coverslip
Let cure for at least 1-2h in the dark at RT (best O/N)


Note: 0.1% Tween 20 in PBS can be substituted for PBS during wash steps

title: General FFPE Protocol_KPC
text:
Tissues except SI

Harvest sample into 10% NBF
Incubate at RT with shaking

Kidney- cut 1 kidney in half. Fix for 24h
Liver- cut into lobes and fix for several hours. Cut into smaller pieces prior for fixation overnight. Fix for 48h. Change 10% NBF after 48h
Spleen- put into fixative 40sec-1min after death. If taking whole spleen, cut into 2 pieces for embedding

Rinse with PBS for 10 minutes 3X
Arrange tissues if needed. (Combine tissues from different samples, orientation)

Embed in 2% LB Agar. (4g in 200ml water, microwave to melt, wait until temp between 42’-55’C)
Place tissues into cryomold and fill with agar. Tap to make sure bubbles do not form.
Pop agar out of mold and place into cassette

Change to 70% Ethanol. Tissues can sit in alcohol as long as you need.

NOTE: If embedding after alcohol, tissue will dry quickly so stay alert and keep it moist.


For Small Intestine (fix first as it degrades quick)

Flush small intestine with BD Fix/Perm solution. Remove as much of the mesentery to keep intestine straight. Holes in SI will make it difficult to flush. (BD fix/perm diluted with 1×PBS at a ratio of 1:2)
Insert crochet needle into proximal part of small intestine. Wet needle prior to insertion.
Place needle with SI into box and cover with 10% NBF
Remove crochet needle and cut longitudinally except the proximal end (for placement later).

If SI starts to bunch up, STOP.
Cut intestine longitudinally with scalpel until it can be removed easily from needle.

Wash SI by dipping several times into PBS
Swiss roll intestine. Secure with 30G needle.
Fix overnight in 10% NBF at RT in 6 well plate
Rinse with PBS for 10 minutes 3X
Embed in 2% LB Agar. (4g in 200ml water, microwave to melt, wait until temp between 42’-55’C)

Slide pin out of swiss roll.

If roll needs to be cut in half: place wet filter paper on petri dish cover. This will allow pins to be secure and prevent SI from sliding around
Pin both ends of swiss roll with 30g pin
Cut in half with scalpel using sliding motion

Place into large cryomold and fill with agar until it covers the SI. Tap to make sure bubbles do not form.
Pop agar out and place into cassette

Change to 70% Ethanol. Tissues can sit in alcohol as long as you need.

NOTE: If embedding after alcohol, tissue will dry quickly so stay alert and keep it moist.

title: Using the cryostat
text:
FRIDAY, 4/10/2026

Transfer tissues from the -80 to -20
Make sure the cryostat is on and is around -16 degrees.
pop sample that you want to section out of the holder.
Grab one of the spiral things, put OCT on it, and let sample bind to it.
Use the little handle on the mounting area to lock the spiral into place.
Trim section to the depth you want.
Put the glass rectangle down
Then change to 10 um and cut section, drop slide on it to get section onto slide and check under brightfield.
Need to use one of the good slides for the final cut.
Store slide in a slide storage rack in the microtome until finished.
lock the cycler into place for clean.
Empty the bottom shavings for cleanup into biohaz.

title: Post-Xenium IF & HE Protocol
text:
Download the original DOCX
Post-Xenium IF & HE Protocol
Miguel Reina-Campos
11/17/23
Updated 1/26/24 by Vida Luna
Slides are kept hydrated in PBS-T (0.05% tween-20 in 1x PBS) after run completion
Retrieve slides and keep at 4ºC. If storing, refresh PBS-T every 3-4 days to avoid bacterial buildup
There is no need to remove the slides from the cassette during IF stain
Reagents:

PBS-T (0.05% tween-20 in 1x PBS)
CAS-block
Xenium cassette plastic covers (2 per slide)
DAKO antibody diluent
Anti-CD8a (unconjugated, Abcam)
1x PBS
Humid chamber (slide chamber with wet paper towels)
Anti-Rabbit AF594
WGA-FITC stock (1 mg/ml)–stored in -20
DAPI stain
Vectashield Antifade Hardset Mounting Reagent
Xylene-based mounting media - Cytoseal XYL

When ready to perform IF:
Wash once with PBS-T (1 mL) 1 min at RT

Block:

Remove PBS-T
add 500 ul of CAS-block
add a plastic cover
Incubate for 2h at RT

Primary:

Remove CAS-block
Add 200 ul of primary Ab diluted in DAKO Antibody diluent per slide
anti-CD8a (Unconjugated, Abcam) 1:200

~50 ul per drop

add a cassette lid
Incubate overnight at 4C in a humid chamber

Wash:

3x wash with 1 mL of regular 1X PBS, 5 min each
In the dark

Secondary:

Add 200 ul of conjugated secondary antibody per slide

Anti-Rabbit AF594 1:200 in DAKO Antibody diluent

1 hour at room temp, add cassette lid

Wash:

3x wash with 1 mL of regular 1X PBS, 5 min each

WGA stain + DAPI

From the 1 mg/mL stock solution of WGA-FITC (kept at -20), thaw the stock and prepare 1 mL of a 10 ug/mL solution in PBS (can refreeze stock after thawing)

1mg/ml 10ug/ml is 1:100 dilution
For 1 ml of PBS, add 10 ul of WGA-FITC stock solution

Add 500 ul of WGA antibody solution per slide
Incubate at RT 15 min protected from the light
Wash 3x with 1mL of regular PBS
Add 500 ul of a 1:1000 DAPI solution in PBS to each slide
Incubate 5 min
Wash 2x with 1 mL of regular PBS
Dismount slide from cassette
Dry carefully and mount coverslip using Vectashield Antifade Hardset Mounting reagent.
Let dry at RT for 20 min
Proceed to slide scanning at 20X using DAPI, FITC (green, WGA), and TRITC (red, CD8a) channels.

Coverslip removal

Soak slides in PBS at 4C overnight
Remove the coverslip by sliding it outside of the slide, DO NOT LIFT. Lifting the coverslip will break/dislodge the tissue
Wash 3x in regular PBS in a plastic container 5 min each
Wash 2x in ddH2O in a plastic contained 5 min each
Stain with Hematoxylin for 15 min
Wash 4x with tap water in a plastic container, 30 seconds each, until water comes out colorless
Dip 4 times in Blueing reagent
Wash 4x with tap water in a plastic container, 30 seconds each
Submerge in Eosin for 2 minutes
Transfer to a 95% etOH container for 3 min
Transfer to a new clean 95% eTOH for 3 min
Transfer to a new clean 100% etOH for 5 min
Transfer to a new clean 100% etOH for 5 min
Transfer to a new clean Xylene for 5 min
Transfer to a new clean Xylene for 5 min
Mount coverslip on the slides using H&E mounting media

Xylene based mounting media – Cytoseal XYL

Let it air dry in the fume hood for 1h
Proceed to scan H&E 20X on the slide scanner

title: 072226 in vitro tumor growth and injection protocol
section: A. Preparing frozen tumor cells for inoculation
text:
A. Preparing frozen tumor cells for inoculation

Tumor cells are stored in the liquid nitrogen storage tank or −150°C chest freezer. Use the storage map to locate the cells and remove the vial from the map once it has been removed from storage.
Carefully and quickly remove the frozen vial(s) from the storage rack, then return the rack to the liquid nitrogen tank.
Rapidly thaw tubes in a 37°C water bath or on the skirt of the hood, then move them to the hood.
Open the vial(s), remove the thawed medium with a 1 mL pipette, and transfer to a culture dish (15 mm). Add the appropriate cell medium (R10, D10, or other) in a volume that covers the plate (20 mL for a 15 mm plate).
Place the plate in a culture incubator and grow cells until the plate is approximately two-thirds to three-quarters confluent. The appropriate confluence may vary by tumor-cell type and may require optimization.
When cells have reached the desired confluence:

Remove the plate from the incubator and carefully aspirate the medium.
Wash once with cold sterile PBS and aspirate.
Add 5 mL trypsin and incubate in the cell-culture incubator for approximately 5 minutes at 37°C.
Add 5 mL medium. Gently wash the plate with a pipette while tilting it to release cells from the plastic surface.
Collect the cell suspension in a 15 mL conical tube and remove a 10 µL aliquot to count cells. Spin the tube while counting.

objectID: protocols/Top_20/072226 in vitro tumor growth and injection protocol.html#b.-tumor-cell-injections
href: protocols/Top_20/072226 in vitro tumor growth and injection protocol.html#b.-tumor-cell-injections
title: 072226 in vitro tumor growth and injection protocol
text:
B. Tumor-cell injections

Resuspend cells at the concentration appropriate to the experiment, based on a 100 µL injection volume. The source gives 250,000 cells per injection for B16-GP33 and 1 × 106 cells per injection for MC38-GP33 as examples. Resuspend cells in PBS or medium for injection.
Transfer cells to Eppendorf tubes or 50 mL conical tubes that accommodate a syringe, and place on ice in disposable tip boxes for transport to the animal facility.
Use 28-gauge insulin syringes. The source suggests approximately one syringe per cage because needles lose sharpness with repeated injections.
In the animal-facility procedure room, prepare the anesthesia chamber:

Place the clear plastic chamber in the hood.
Check oxygen-tank and isoflurane levels; replace or refill as appropriate.
Open the oxygen tank and set isoflurane to 3 or 3.5. Confirm that oxygen is flowing and that the vaporizer reads 1.5–2.0 psi.
Place clean paper towels in the chamber, place mice inside, and wait for slow, deep breathing and no movement.
Remove mice, shave the back area with clippers, and return them to the chamber. Ear punches may be performed at this stage for identification.

Ensure that tumor cells are resuspended by inverting the tube or vortexing. Draw 100 µL cell suspension for each mouse into a syringe.
For subdermal injection, position the back skin by rolling it over a finger or pulling it upward, then insert the needle with the bevel facing up.
Inject 100 µL subdermally, avoiding puncture through the skin that could allow tumor-cell medium to leak and cause unequal doses.
A large bubble should form on the mouse’s back. After injection, weigh the mouse and record its weight, then return it to its home cage. Keep completed cages outside the hood until all mice have recovered before returning cages to the animal room.
After inoculations are complete, return cages to the animal room and put away the isoflurane vaporizer apparatus. If the holding chamber is soiled with urine or feces, wash it; the source instructs not to use ethanol or other cleaners that damage the plastic.

href: protocols/Top_20/072226 in vitro tumor growth and injection protocol.html#c.-monitor-mouse-weight-and-tumor-growth
title: 072226 in vitro tumor growth and injection protocol
section: C. Monitor mouse weight and tumor growth
text:
C. Monitor mouse weight and tumor growth

Monitor tumor growth and begin animal treatments when tumors reach the size or date appropriate to the experiment.
Record observations and mouse weight at each monitoring step. The source states that monitoring and paper records are required by UCSD and must be kept in the mouse room.
Use the following tumor-stage observation schedule from the source:

Stage 1: No visible, palpable, clinical, or behavioral signs of tumor burden — monitor weekly.
Stage 2: Visible or palpable tumors, or changes in appearance or behavior — monitor twice weekly.
Stage 3: Any signs of morbidity or mortality, or subcutaneous tumor diameter greater than 1.5 cm — monitor daily. The source states that animals must be euthanized when a tumor reaches 2 cm in any direction.

title: Infection with LCMV CL13
text:
Use the LCMV CL13 Titer Calculator to calculate the AB or NM stock-virus and PBS volumes needed for infection.


Day -1: Transfer naïve P14 cells (500–1,000) by retro-orbital injection.
Day 0: Infect retro-orbitally with LCMV Clone 13 (2 × 10^6 PFU of AB or NM virus) in 200 µL. Dilute stock with PBS. Note that AB and NM have different titers.



Transfer 2–10 × 10^5 cells retro-orbitally.
Infect with Clone 13 on the same day as cell transfer. Infect retro-orbitally with LCMV Clone 13 (2 × 10^6 PFU of AB and NM virus) in 200 µL. Dilute stock with PBS. Note that AB and NM have different titers.
These are the PFU/mL values of each Clone 13 stock in the Goldrath Lab:



Stock
AB (2015)
NM (2020)




New average PFU/mL
5.15 × 10^7
8.50 × 10^7



Dilute stock in the hood. Dispose of all tips in 10% bleach.
All takedowns must be performed in the hood regardless of timepoint, as Clone 13 is chronic.

title: Cell Trace Violet
text:
This composite protocol combines:

CellTrace Violet protocol (protocols/t_cells/ctv.md)
Cell Trace Violet labeling protocol (protocols/Goldrath Protocols/The Master Folder/Anthony/Cell Trace Violet labeling.md)




Prepare the dye stock. Immediately before use, add the appropriate volume of DMSO to one vial of CellTrace reagent and mix well; frozen stock may also be used. The Goldrath protocol specifies adding 20 µL DMSO to one vial. [Source: protocols/Goldrath Protocols/The Master Folder/Anthony/Cell Trace Violet labeling.md]
Prepare the cells. Pellet cells by centrifugation and remove the supernatant. The Goldrath protocol additionally warms cells in calcium- and magnesium-free PBS for 10 minutes at 37°C, then dilutes them to 10 × 10^6 cells/mL. [Source: protocols/Goldrath Protocols/The Master Folder/Anthony/Cell Trace Violet labeling.md]
Prepare the staining solution. Dilute the CellTrace DMSO stock in pre-warmed (37°C) PBS or another protein-free buffer to a working concentration of 1–10 µM. The t_cells protocol notes that 5 µM is used as a 1:1,000 dilution of stock; the Goldrath protocol specifies 1 µL CTV stock per mL of cell suspension. [Source: concentration guidance from protocols/t_cells/ctv.md; volume guidance from protocols/Goldrath Protocols/The Master Folder/Anthony/Cell Trace Violet labeling.md]
Label the cells. Gently resuspend cells in the dye solution. Vortex gently to ensure equal dye exposure, as specified in the Goldrath protocol. [Source: protocols/Goldrath Protocols/The Master Folder/Anthony/Cell Trace Violet labeling.md]
Incubate. Incubate for 20 minutes at 37°C, protected from light. The t_cells protocol also permits room-temperature incubation. Gentle agitation during staining can improve uniform labeling. [Source: room-temperature option and agitation note from protocols/t_cells/ctv.md]
Quench free dye. Add at least 5× the original staining volume of culture medium containing at least 1% protein and incubate for 5 minutes.
Wash and resuspend. Pellet cells by centrifugation, then resuspend in fresh, pre-warmed complete culture medium. The Goldrath protocol specifies washing cells twice. [Source: twice-wash instruction from protocols/Goldrath Protocols/The Master Folder/Anthony/Cell Trace Violet labeling.md]
Recover and use. Incubate for at least 10 minutes before analysis to allow acetate hydrolysis, then proceed with stimulation, incubation, or analysis. The Goldrath protocol instead concludes by resuspending and plating the cells. [Source: recovery/analysis instruction from protocols/t_cells/ctv.md; plating instruction from protocols/Goldrath Protocols/The Master Folder/Anthony/Cell Trace Violet labeling.md]












Topic
protocols/t_cells/ctv.md
protocols/Goldrath Protocols/The Master Folder/Anthony/Cell Trace Violet labeling.md




Dye stock preparation
Appropriate DMSO volume; frozen stock is acceptable.
Specifies 20 µL DMSO per vial.


Cell preparation
Pellet and remove supernatant.
Warm cells in Ca/Mg-free PBS for 10 minutes at 37°C and use 10 × 10^6 cells/mL.


Dye concentration
Recommends 1–10 µM; notes 5 µM as a 1:1,000 stock dilution.
Uses 1 µL CTV stock per mL of cell suspension; does not state final µM.


Mixing
Gentle resuspension; gentle agitation is suggested.
Specifies gentle vortexing.


Staining temperature
Room temperature or 37°C.
37°C only.


Post-stain handling
Quench, pellet, resuspend in fresh medium, and allow at least 10 minutes for hydrolysis before analysis.
Quench, pellet, wash twice, resuspend, and plate.


Guidance for tracking generations
5–10 µM for five or more generations; 1–2 µM for fewer than five.
No generation-based concentration guidance.



The source protocol files are available here:

title: Transfect and Transduce 1
text: This composite brings together Plat-E transfection, retrovirus collection, and primary CD8 T-cell transduction workflows. Source protocols use different plate formats, reagent amounts, media, and downstream handling. Choose a single compatible source-specific route when the alternatives differ; do not combine quantities across routes without confirming the current lab-approved conditions.

title: Transfect and Transduce 1
text:
Source files

Alex Monell — Transfection
Goldrath Lab — Transfection Protocol
Nicole Sharping — NES 042924 CD8 T cell transduction and double transduction
Maximilian Heeg — Make Retrovirus

title: Transfect and Transduce 1
text:
1. Prepare Plat-E cells
All four sources use Plat-E packaging cells and specify medium without Pen/Strep during the transfection setup.

10 cm or 6-well production route
Derived from: Alex Monell and Maximilian Heeg.

Plate Plat-E cells the day before transfection in medium without Pen/Strep.
For a 10 cm dish, use 2.5 × 106 cells in 10 mL medium. For a 6-well plate, use 0.5 × 106 cells per well in 2 mL medium.
On the following day, replace the medium with fresh Plat-E medium before adding the transfection mixture.



96-well screening route
Derived from: Goldrath Lab.

Plate 2–4 × 104 Plat-E cells per well in a 96-well flat-bottom plate, with a final volume of 200 µL per well.
Use the middle 60 wells for transfection and fill the outer 36 wells with 100 µL medium.
Use Plat-E medium without Pen/Strep. The source defines this medium as DMEM with L-glutamine, 10% FBS, 50 µM BME, and 10 mM HEPES.
At least one hour before transfection, remove 150 µL medium and replace it with 50 µL fresh, warm Plat-E medium without Pen/Strep.



Expanded 10 cm production route
Derived from: Nicole Sharping.

For a full transduction timeline, thaw Platinum-E cells five days before transduction, wash, and expand them on a 15 cm plate in D10.
Two days before transduction, trypsinize, count, and plate 2 × 106 cells per 10 cm plate.

title: Transfect and Transduce 1
text:
2. Transfect Plat-E cells
All sources use pCL-Eco helper plasmid, a plasmid of interest, OptiMEM or serum-free DMEM, Mirus/TransIT-LT1 reagent, a room-temperature incubation, and dropwise addition to cells. Use one complete format below.

Alex Monell 10 cm route
Derived from: Alex Monell.

Prepare Tube 1 with 5 µg pCL-Eco in 550 µL OptiMEM. Aliquot 600 µL into a 15 mL tube and add 10 µg transfer plasmid.
Prepare Tube 2 with 45 µL Mirus reagent and 655 µL OptiMEM.
Add 700 µL of Tube 2 mixture to each Tube 1 aliquot, incubate at room temperature for 20 minutes, then add dropwise to cells.



Goldrath Lab 96-well route
Derived from: Goldrath Lab.

Per transfection well, add 1 µL of 100 ng/µL pCL-Eco and 9 µL OptiMEM to Tube 1, then add 200 ng shRNA plasmid.
Per well, prepare Tube 2 with 0.6 µL Mirus reagent and 9.4 µL OptiMEM.
Add Tube 2 to Tube 1 last, mix, incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature, and add the mixture dropwise to cells.
The source notes that a 6-well format typically uses approximately 0.8–1.2 × 106 cells in 2 mL per well and scales the reagents approximately tenfold.



Nicole Sharping single- or double-plasmid route
Derived from: Nicole Sharping.

Warm 700 µL serum-free DMEM to room temperature.
For a single transduction, add 6 µg plasmid of interest and 2 µg pCL-Eco. For a double transduction, distribute 6 µg total plasmid of interest among the plasmids and add 2 µg pCL-Eco.
Add 30 µL room-temperature TransIT-LT1, mix, incubate at room temperature for 20–30 minutes, then drip the mixture onto cells.
Incubate overnight and replace Plat-E medium with fresh R10 the next morning; retain subsequent medium for virus collection.



Maximilian Heeg 10 cm or 6-well route
Derived from: Maximilian Heeg.

For a 10 cm dish, mix 5 µg pCL-Eco in 550 µL OptiMEM, add 10 µg plasmid, then add a mixture of 45 µL Mirus and 655 µL OptiMEM.
For a 6-well plate, mix 0.5 µg pCL-Eco in 125 µL OptiMEM, add 2 µg plasmid, then add a mixture of 7.5 µL Mirus and 117.5 µL OptiMEM.
Incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature and add dropwise to cells.

title: Transfect and Transduce 1
text:
3. Collect or use retrovirus

Harvest-and-store route
Derived from: Alex Monell and Maximilian Heeg.

The day after transfection, replace old medium with fresh T-cell medium (TCM).
On the next day, harvest the first virus-containing supernatant, store it refrigerated, and add fresh TCM.
On the following day, harvest the remaining supernatant and combine it with the first collection.
Spin at 1600 RPM for 4 minutes, aliquot or use immediately, and freeze stored virus at −80°C. For fresh virus, the sources specify filtration through a 0.45 µm filter.



Direct-use or small-volume harvest route
Derived from: Nicole Sharping and Goldrath Lab.

Nicole Sharping directs changing to R10 the morning after transfection and retaining that medium for transduction; before loading virus onto Retronectin, spin the viral medium to pellet floating Plat-E cells.
Goldrath Lab directs replacing 70 µL with warm T-cell medium on Day 3, harvesting 70 µL supernatant on Day 4, and harvesting/pooling the remaining 170 µL per well on Day 5. The source activates CD8 T cells on Day 4 for next-day transduction.

title: Transfect and Transduce 1
section: 4. Activate and transduce primary CD8 T cells
text:
4. Activate and transduce primary CD8 T cells
Derived from: Nicole Sharping. This is the only supplied source that specifies primary CD8 T-cell activation and Retronectin-based transduction.

On the day before transduction, coat a flat-bottom 6-well plate with anti-CD3 in sterile PBS (5 µg/mL for P14 or 10 µg/mL for wild-type CD8 T cells) for 3 hours at 37°C.
Isolate CD8 T cells, then activate approximately 5 × 106 cells per well in 2 mL R10 with 2 µg/mL anti-CD28 and 50 U/mL hIL-2 for at least 24 hours.
Coat non-tissue-culture-treated 6-well plates overnight at 4°C with 1 mL per viral group of 15 µg/mL Retronectin in sterile PBS.
Remove Retronectin, block with 4 mL R10 per well for 30 minutes at 37°C, and warm the centrifuge to 37°C.
Remove the block, load 1 mL virus per well for 30 minutes at 37°C, replace with a second 1 mL virus aliquot, and incubate for another 30 minutes.
Pellet activated cells, resuspend them in the remaining viral medium with 50 U/mL IL-2, transfer them to the virus-coated wells, and spin at 1600 RPM and 37°C for 45 minutes.
Culture overnight, replace medium with fresh R10 plus IL-2 the next morning, and maintain cells at 1 × 106/mL. The source reduces IL-2 to 25 U/mL at 5–6 days after activation.

title: Transfect and Transduce 1
text:
Similarities and differences among sources








Topic
Similarity
Difference and source attribution




Packaging cells and antibiotic
All sources use Plat-E/Platinum-E packaging cells; each uses or recommends medium without Pen/Strep for the transfection setup.
Nicole Sharping begins with a five-day thaw/expansion timeline, whereas Alex Monell, Goldrath Lab, and Maximilian Heeg begin with plating cells for transfection.


Plate format and density
Each source plates packaging cells before transfection.
Goldrath Lab uses a 96-well format (2–4 × 104 cells/well); Alex Monell and Maximilian Heeg specify 10 cm and 6-well densities; Nicole Sharping specifies 2 × 106 cells per 10 cm plate.


Helper plasmid and reagent
Each source includes pCL-Eco and Mirus/TransIT-LT1 with a plasmid of interest.
Alex Monell and Maximilian Heeg use 5 µg pCL-Eco plus 10 µg plasmid for 10 cm dishes; Goldrath Lab uses 100 ng pCL-Eco plus 200 ng shRNA per 96-well; Nicole Sharping uses 2 µg pCL-Eco plus 6 µg total plasmid.


Complex formation
All sources prepare a DNA/reagent mixture, incubate at room temperature, and add it dropwise.
Nicole Sharping specifies 20–30 minutes in serum-free DMEM; Alex Monell, Goldrath Lab, and Maximilian Heeg specify 20 minutes with OptiMEM-based mixtures.


Post-transfection medium
All sources change or replace medium after transfection before using or collecting virus.
Alex Monell and Maximilian Heeg change to TCM and collect on Days 4–5; Goldrath Lab makes small sequential collections; Nicole Sharping changes to R10 and uses the resulting virus directly for transduction.


Virus storage and processing
All sources produce retroviral supernatant for downstream transduction.
Alex Monell and Maximilian Heeg specify a 1600 RPM, 4-minute clarification and −80°C storage; Maximilian Heeg additionally specifies 0.45 µm filtration for fresh virus. Nicole Sharping instead specifies pelleting floating Plat-E cells immediately before Retronectin loading.


Primary CD8 handling
Virus generated by each source can support a transduction workflow.
Only Nicole Sharping specifies anti-CD3/anti-CD28/IL-2 activation, Retronectin coating, two virus-loading incubations, spinoculation, and subsequent CD8 culture.

title: Transduction Polybrene
text:
Maximilian Heeg — Retroviral transduction
This page is a focused composite of the Polybrene-related steps from Maximilian Heeg’s source protocol. Among the four supplied source files, it is the only file containing a Polybrene workflow.

title: Transduction Polybrene
text:
Maximilian Heeg — Retroviral transduction
This page is a focused composite of the Polybrene-related steps from Maximilian Heeg’s source protocol. Among the four supplied source files, it is the only file containing a Polybrene workflow.

title: Transduction Polybrene
text:
1. Activate T cells
Derived from: Maximilian Heeg.
Activate T cells using CD8 Selection and Activation before transduction.

title: Transduction Polybrene
text:
2. Prepare virus and Polybrene mixture
Derived from: Maximilian Heeg.

Prewarm the centrifuge to 37°C.
Thaw 2 mL retrovirus in a water bath. See Make Retrovirus for virus production.
Make a 70× Polybrene mixture for each 100 µL needed:

8 µL Polybrene
10 µL BME (mercaptoethanol)
82 µL Optimem

Combine virus and Polybrene mixture at 2 µL mixture per 140 µL virus; for example, 2 mL virus requires 28.5 µL mixture.

title: Transduction Polybrene
text:
3. Transduce cells
Derived from: Maximilian Heeg.

Transfer medium from the 6-well plate into a 15 mL Falcon tube and keep it warm. Keep media for different congenic groups separate.
Add virus/Polybrene mixture to activated T cells.
Spin at 37°C for 1 hour at 2000 RPM.
Incubate cells at 37°C for an additional 1–4 hours.
Carefully remove the virus mixture. Pellet the retained original medium, return it to the cells, and add an equal volume of fresh TCM to reach 4 mL per well.

title: Transduction Polybrene
text:
4. Use or culture cells
Derived from: Maximilian Heeg.

For mixed transfer on Day 3, transfer 500,000 total P14 cells and target a 1:1 congenic ratio among Ametrine-positive T cells.
For culture, transfer cells to a T75 flask on Day 3, wash wells with 2 mL TCM into the flask, then add 6 mL TCM plus IL-2 at a final 1:2000 concentration. Add 12 mL more TCM plus IL-2 on Day 4. Day 5 can be used for downstream work such as FACS sorting for RNA isolation.

title: Transduction Polybrene
text:
Source differences
Among the four specified input files, only Maximilian Heeg’s source provides a Polybrene-containing workflow; therefore there are no conflicting Polybrene parameters to compare within this source set. Source: Maximilian Heeg

title: Ex vivo peptide stim
text:
Materials

Freshly isolated lymphocytes or tissue-derived cell suspension
Complete T-cell medium
gp33 peptide or the experiment-specific cognate peptide
Protein transport inhibitor compatible with the cytokines being measured
Optional naïve splenocytes to provide antigen-presenting cells
96-well U-bottom or round-bottom plate for stimulation
96-well V-bottom or round-bottom plate for staining
PBS and FACS buffer
Fc-receptor blocking reagent
Surface-staining antibody panel
Intracellular cytokine antibodies
Appropriate fixation and permeabilization reagents
Single-color compensation controls

title: Ex vivo peptide stim
text:
1. Prepare cells

Harvest the required tissues and prepare single-cell suspensions.
Count cells when the experimental design requires normalization.
Plate cells in a 96-well U-bottom or round-bottom plate.
Ensure that antigen-presenting cells are present. Purified T cells alone cannot efficiently use peptide presented through this workflow (Nicole_s protocols).


Source-attributed plating options

Giovanni_s Protocols/cellular: Count freshly isolated tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and splenocytes. If cells are not counted, plate approximately one-third to one-quarter of the TIL or draining-lymph-node preparation, or 10 µL of spleen suspension prepared in 1 mL.
Giovanni_s Protocols/cellular: To support TIL stimulation, resuspend a naïve spleen in 5 mL medium and add 30 µL per well. Use naïve splenocytes with the same congenic marker as the recipient mice.
t_cells: Resuspend T cells in 100 µL T-cell medium. For TRM samples, add 50 µL congenically distinct splenocytes as an APC spike-in; for splenocyte-only samples, add 50 µL medium instead.
Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse: For spleen samples, plate 5% of the spleen preparation—250 µL from a spleen resuspended in 5 mL. Use a consistent volume across samples and retain cell counts for normalization.
Nicole_s protocols: Plate cells in a 96-well round-bottom plate and centrifuge at 2,000 rpm for 1 minute before adding stimulation medium.
Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse: Centrifuge the plated samples at 1,500 rpm for 3 minutes before replacing the medium.

title: Ex vivo peptide stim
text:
2. Prepare controls

Include a stimulated condition containing cognate peptide and protein transport inhibitor.
Include an unstimulated negative control containing protein transport inhibitor but no peptide.
Keep the cell input and total culture volume consistent between stimulated and unstimulated conditions.
Add a positive stimulation control when needed.


Source-attributed control options

Giovanni_s Protocols/cellular: Use cells treated identically without cognate peptide as the cytokine-negative control. Plain medium is also described as a negative control. Use Cell Stimulation Cocktail at 1:500 as a positive control.
Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse: Prepare either an unstimulated sample for every mouse or one pooled unstimulated control per tissue. The unstimulated medium contains GolgiPlug but no gp33.

title: Ex vivo peptide stim
text:
3. Prepare stimulation medium
Prepare enough medium for all wells plus pipetting excess. The final culture volume is 200 µL per well in all four source protocols.
Choose one of the following source-specific formulations:

Option A — Giovanni_s Protocols/cellular

Standard T-cell medium
gp33 peptide at 1 µM final concentration
Protein Transport Inhibitor Cocktail at 1:500 final dilution



Option B — Nicole_s protocols

T-cell medium
GP33 source aliquot at 1:500
Protein Transport Inhibitor containing brefeldin A and monensin at 1:500

The GP33 stock concentration is not stated in this source; do not interpret 1:500 as a molar concentration without checking the aliquot record.


Option C — t_cells
For each well:

Begin with 100 µL cells in T-cell medium.
Add either 50 µL APC splenocytes for TRM samples or 50 µL additional medium for splenocyte samples.
Add 50 µL stimulation mix.

An example stimulation mix contains:

500 µL T-cell medium
4 µL Protein Transport Inhibitor Cocktail, producing a final 1:500 dilution after addition to the well
2 µL gp33 that has first been diluted 1:100, producing a final gp33 dilution of 1:100,000 from a 1 mM stock, or 10 nM



Option D — Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse

Calculate the required medium as 200 µL multiplied by the number of samples, including unstimulated controls.
Add 500× GolgiPlug at 1:500.
Divide the medium into stimulated and unstimulated portions.
Prepare a 1:10 intermediate dilution of the 4 mg/mL gp33 stock to obtain 0.4 mg/mL.
Add 1 µL of the 0.4 mg/mL intermediate dilution per 1 mL stimulated medium to obtain 0.4 µg/mL final peptide.
Do not add peptide to the unstimulated portion.

title: Ex vivo peptide stim
text:
4. Stimulate cells

Remove the existing medium after the applicable centrifugation step.
Add 200 µL of the selected stimulation medium to each stimulated well.
Add 200 µL matched inhibitor-containing medium without peptide to each negative-control well.
Resuspend cells thoroughly.
Incubate at 37°C:

4 hours: Giovanni_s Protocols/cellular, Nicole_s protocols, and t_cells
4–6 hours: Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse



CD107a timing — t_cells
When measuring CD107a, add the CD107a antibody and gp33 peptide at the beginning of stimulation. Incubate for 30–60 minutes before adding Protein Transport Inhibitor Cocktail for the remainder of the stimulation period.

title: Ex vivo peptide stim
text:
5. Wash and surface stain

Transfer cells to a V-bottom plate if needed (Giovanni_s Protocols/cellular).
Wash cells twice before staining (Giovanni_s Protocols/cellular).
Block Fc receptors.
Stain viability and surface markers using the validated panel.
Wash the cells before fixation and permeabilization.


Detailed surface-staining option — Nicole_s protocols

Add 20–50 µL Fc block to cells in medium and incubate on ice for at least 10 minutes.
Prepare the surface-antibody cocktail in FACS buffer at 100 µL per well.
Centrifuge at 2,000 rpm for 1 minute and remove supernatant.
Add 100 µL staining cocktail and resuspend.
Incubate on ice in the dark for 15 minutes.
Add 180 µL FACS buffer and centrifuge to wash.

title: Ex vivo peptide stim
text:
6. Fix, permeabilize, and stain cytokines
Use a fixation/permeabilization system validated for cytoplasmic cytokines.

Detailed intracellular-staining option — Nicole_s protocols

After surface staining, centrifuge cells at 2,000 rpm for 1 minute.
Resuspend in 100 µL 4% PFA in PBS and incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature in the dark. This preliminary fixation is used in this source to help preserve selected surface antigens and fluorescent reporters.
Add 180 µL FACS buffer, centrifuge, and remove supernatant.
Resuspend in 100 µL BD Cytofix/Cytoperm.
Incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature.
Add 180 µL 1× BD Perm/Wash buffer, centrifuge, and remove supernatant.
Prepare intracellular cytokine antibodies in 1× Perm/Wash buffer at 100 µL per well.
Resuspend cells in 100 µL intracellular staining solution.
Incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature in the dark.
Wash with 180 µL Perm/Wash buffer and centrifuge.
Resuspend in 100 µL FACS buffer for acquisition.

Giovanni_s Protocols/cellular specifies surface staining followed by intracellular staining for effector molecules and cytokines but does not prescribe a particular fixation/permeabilization kit in the source protocol.

title: Ex vivo peptide stim
text:
7. Acquire and analyze

Prepare single-color compensation controls for every fluorophore.
Acquire stimulated and unstimulated samples using identical cytometer settings.
Gate matched populations consistently across all conditions.
Use the no-peptide control to establish cytokine-positive gates.
Report both the frequency of cytokine-positive cells and fluorescence intensity when appropriate.

Nicole_s protocols notes that stimulated cytokine responses and inhibitor choice should be optimized empirically for each cytokine. TNFα, IL-2, IL-17, and IFNγ commonly produce clearer positive populations, whereas IL-4, IL-5, IL-10, and IL-13 may appear primarily as fluorescence-intensity shifts.

title: Propagate LCMV Clone 13
text:
Propagate LCMV Clone 13 virus
BHK media (500 mL):


500 mL DMEM (high glucose, liquid)


50 mL FBS (10%)


5 mL L-glutamine (100x)


5 mL Pen-strep (100x)


25 mL Tryptose phosphate broth (Gibco)


Day -1:


Plate BHK to be ~40-50% confluent the following day. Seed about 5x10 6 BHK cells in a T175 flask the day before infection. The cells will grow to a confluency of 40-50%, corresponding to ~1x107.


Note
BHK cells grow at different rates in different labs and seem to be pretty sensitive. Consider setting up flasks at target multiple confluencies to try to hit the right one on the infection day.
Day 0:


Take photos of the T175 flasks on the light microscope if possible - try to record what a good confluency looks like.


Pipet off media and infect with virus in a limited volume (6 mL for a T175, 3 mL for a T75). The MOI used in the field seems to vary; many people use 0.001-0.01, but Teijaro lab uses an MOI of 0.1.



The lore is that it is important to use a high titer virus to inoculate, but unclear where this line is drawn.


Teijaro adds 5 uL of 2x10 8 PFU/mL stock to 6 mL BHK media to hit a target of MOI 0.1 for 107 cells in a T175.


Allen lab has a stock at 2.58e8/ml (Floor 2 lab -80, rack 00156, box 01649). I added 4 ul per 6 mls of media per flask or 24 ul per 36 mls for 6 T175 flasks



Incubate at 37 Celsius for 90 minutes. Gently tilt and rock the flask every 10-15 minutes.


After 90 minutes, add 19 mL warm BHK media (total 25 mL final).


Incubate for 72 hours.


Day 3
Keep the virus cold for all following steps!


Pipet supernatant into 15 mL conical tubes. The supernatant contains the virus. Be careful, this is a LOT of LCMV. Have bleach handy in case of a spill.


Separate any remaining BHK cells that were aspirated from virus.



Spin at 2000 rpm in a benchtop centrifuge (~800-850 g depending on centrifuge in IMPL-K) for 15 minutes.


Collect the supernatant, transfer to a fresh tube.


Repeat for a total of two centrifugation steps.



Keeping the virus cold, aliquot and snap freeze in liquid nitrogen. Pre-chill cryo-tubes in cold room.


Protocol yields ~20-25 mL virus containing supernatant at a target of ~2x108 pfu/mL.



Infecting at 2x10 6 pfu/mouse (100 uL of 2x10 7 pfu/mL), this corresponds to enough virus to infect 2000 mice per T175 of LCMV Clone 13.



Titrate the virus. Make sure to titrate an aliquot that has been frozen and thawed to get a representative value for what the titer will be when you inject from a thawed aliquot (rather than titrating the supernatant directly).

1. Prepare activation plates
Choose one coating strategy and prepare the plate before beginning the isolation.

Direct anti-CD3 coating — Nicole_s protocols

Begin approximately 3 hours before plating cells.

Add 1 mL per well of a six-well plate. The source uses three wells per spleen-plus-lymph-node isolation.

Goat anti-hamster IgG coating — Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse and t_cells

Begin at least 2 hours before plating cells.
Dilute goat anti-hamster IgG 1:30 in sterile PBS.
Add 550 µL per well of a six-well plate.

Attach the appropriate MACS column to the magnet.
Equilibrate the column with 3 mL MACS buffer and discard this initial flow-through.
Apply the cell suspension to the column.

text:
8. Count cells and assess purity

Resuspend enriched cells in culture medium and count them.
Assess viability when required.
Check CD8 enrichment by flow cytometry when possible.


Source-specific resuspension and purity checks

Nicole_s protocols: Resuspend in 6 mL R10 and count with an automated cell counter.
Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse: Resuspend initially in approximately 500 µL R10, count, and assess viability with Trypan Blue or another method. Stain a pre- and post-isolation aliquot with FITC-CD8β at 1:100, wash once with FACS buffer, and acquire by flow cytometry. The source notes that 90–95% purity may be assumed only when a rapid workflow is necessary.
t_cells: Resuspend in 500 µL TCM, count, and adjust to 2 × 10^6 cells/mL.

title: Mouse CD8 isolation and CD3 activation
section: 9. Plate and activate enriched CD8 T cells
text:
9. Plate and activate enriched CD8 T cells
Use the activation method that matches the plate-coating strategy from step 1.

Direct anti-CD3-coated plate — Nicole_s protocols

Remove the anti-CD3/PBS coating solution and leave the wells free of residual liquid.
Supplement the enriched cells with anti-CD28 at 2 µg/mL and IL-2 at 50 U/mL; the source describes IL-2 as a 1:2,000 dilution.
Plate 2 mL cell suspension per well. The source distributes 6 mL across three wells.
Handle and resuspend the cells gently.
Incubate at 37°C for 24 hours.



Goat anti-hamster IgG-coated plate — Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse

Remove the coating solution.
Wash each well twice with 1 mL R10 and aspirate thoroughly.
Prepare anti-CD3 and anti-CD28, each at 1:500 in R10.
Add 1 mL cell suspension at 2 × 10^6 cells/mL to each well.
Add 1 mL anti-CD3/CD28 mixture to each well.
The resulting total volume is 2 mL, final density is 1 × 10^6 cells/mL, and each antibody is at a final 1:1,000 dilution.
Incubate at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 18–24 hours.

Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse also describes an anti-CD3-coated plate alternative: add anti-CD28 at 1:250 in the 1 mL antibody solution so that the final well concentration is 1 µg/mL after mixing with 1 mL cells.


Goat anti-hamster IgG-coated plate — t_cells

Wash each coated well twice with 1 mL TCM.
Plate 2 × 10^6 cells in 1 mL TCM per well.
Dilute anti-CD3 and anti-CD28, each at 1:500 in TCM.
Add 1 mL antibody mixture to each well and mix gently.
The resulting total volume is 2 mL, final density is 1 × 10^6 cells/mL, and each antibody is at a final 1:1,000 dilution.
Incubate at 37°C until the planned downstream processing time. The source does not specify an exact duration.

Plating Plat-E Cells from Frozen
1. Check if we have D10 media. 2. Get a 50 ml conical, put 30 ml D10 and put in water bath. 3. Use a 15 mL conical tube and add 10 mL D10. 4. Put the conical tube in a 37°C water bath. 5. Move liquid nitrogen container from the southwest rack – 4th box from top. 6. Grab Plat-E cells. 7. Place the frozen Plat-E vial in the water bath until thawed (1–2 min max). 8. ● Don’t change the culture medium during the first three days. It is normal to see some cells floating after the first 24 hours. • Don’t culture cells to complete confluency. Split cells 4X to 6X every two to three days when the culture reaches 70-90% confluency.

title: Virus production in 10 cm - PlatE
text:
Virus production in 10 cm-dish
Day 0: plate 2.5x106 PlatE (or PhoenixE) cells in a 10 cm dish (total volume 8ml) in DMEM complete media without P/S
Day 1: transfection with MIRUS TRANS-LT1 (MIR 2300)
Just before transfection, change the medium adding 12 ml of fresh new media and move the cells back to the incubator
In a 14-ml tube, add in this order

DNA: 10 ug transfer vector + 5ug pCL-Eco
OPTIMEM serum-dree medium to .4 ml total volume, mix well by pipetting and swirl the tube;
Add MIRUS reagent to DNA (3 to 6 ug of MIRUS/ug of DNA). Dispense MIRUS directly into the liquid, dropwise.
Swirl the tube, do not pipette or vortex
Let it stand at RT for 20 to 30 min
Gently add the DNA/OPTIMEM/Mirus complex to the cells, dropwise, in a circular motion.
Put the plate back in the incubator (5% CO2)
16hs after transfection, gently remove the medium and replace with 10 ml fresh medium for virus collection.
Collect the virus at 24 and 48h, store virus in the fridge and pool the fractions at the end; at the end, filter virus through a 0.45 um filter (do not use 0.2).
Store in the fridge and use virus within 24h
Store at -80C long term. Avoid freeze-thawing

Prewarm at RT optimum and MIRUS prior to using

title: ca-p transfection of Phoenix
text:
CALCIUM PHOSPHATE TRANSFECTION OF ΦNX CELLS TO PRODUCE VIRAL SUP.
Day 1: Plate 1 million Phoenix cells per petridish (Falcon 3004; this is a 6cm petridish with a surface area of 21 sq cm) in 4 ml Iscove’s containing 10% FCS + 2-ME + antibiotics. Culture cells ON as usual (no shaking/rocking) in a 37C incubator.
Day 2: Ca-P transfection (Gibco BRL 18306-019)
885 ul water
100 ul 10x HBS
vortex
15 ul 1M NaOH
vortex
Pipet 500 ul 1x HBS soln + 10 ul phosphate soln into tube 1.
Tube 2:
430 ul water
10-20 ug plasmid DNA (prefered conc: 1 ug/ul), mix gently
10 ul Calcium solution, mix gently
50 ul Calcium solution, mix gently
Bubble air in tube 1 and add slowly the mix from tube 2 into tube 1. This will become a milky suspension. Incubate 20 min at RT. Add 10 min before the transfection 4 ul of 30 mM Chloroquine (=15 mg/ml and filter sterile) to the Phoenix cells and mix gently by swirling.
Add the DNA-Ca-P mixture dropwise to the Phoenix cells and incubate them as usual ON at 37C.
Day 3: Replace medium by 4 ml FTOC medium and incubate the Phoenix cells as usual O/N at 37C.
Day 4: Harvest transient virus supernatant. Keep the virus 15 min on ice. Spin 5 minutes 1500 rpm or filter supernatant (to get rid of the few Phoenix cells present in the supernatant; For the FTOC experiments spinning will do the job) and make 0.5 ml or 1 ml aliquots of the viral supernatant. Freeze immediately at -80C. Because freeze steps reduce the transduction efficiency with 50% we thaw an aliquot only once. Phoenix cells are analyzed by FACS for eGFP expression the same day.
What is important, is to do the transfection at the END of day 2 and to replace the medium with FTOC medium at the BEGINNING of day 3. Whatever transfection protocol you will use, the cells won’t like it and therefore this period should be as short as possible. Furthermore, replacing the medium at the beginning of day 3 with FTOC medium gives you the full 24h to accumulate virus before harvesting the supernatant at the beginning of day 4.
The 4 ml FTOC medium will appear orange-yellow just before harvesting, so, I would not advice to decrease the volume any further. It may increase your virus titer but I don’t think many fetal thymocytes will survive the transduction in such exhausted medium. They already have a hard time surviving the transduction protocol as it is now.
What is also important is that the virus supernatant harvesting procedure is performed as fast as possible. After 15 min on ice immediately spin the supernatant and very quickly freeze at -80C.

title: Spin Transfection
text:
Spin Transfection

Warm centrifuge to 300C.
Mix 2 ml Virus Supernatant with 20 ul of DOTAP (DOTAP liposomal transfection reagent from Roche) in a conical tube. Leave on ice for 10min.
Pellet cells intended for infection. Remove supernatant
Transfer virus/DOTAP mix into tube containing cell pellet (2x10^6 cells/ 2 ml virus)
Transfer cells/virus/DOTAP mix into a 24 well plate
Spin for 90min at 30oC at 2500 rpm
Put in 37oC/ 6% CO2 incubator 3-4 hours or O/N
Remove supernatant carefully and add media gently so as to not detach the cells. I usually do this 3-4 hours after transduction and leave a film of media over the cells so not to risk aspirating them.

title: Goldrath Protocols
text:
Reina Lab
Updated 3/25/2026 H.M.
Lentivirus Production in a 10 cm Dish
Materials and Reagents

HEK293T cells
Opti-MEM
10 cm tissue-culture-treated plates
Complete DMEM (See Nicoles Media Recipes)
Trypsin
1X PBS
Packaging plasmids:



pCMV-VSV-G (Addgene #8454). Alternatively pMDG.2
psPAX2 (Addgene #12260)



Lentiviral transfer plasmid
TransIT-LT1 Transfection Reagent
14 mL tube
50 mL conical tubes
5 mL microcentrifuge tubes or other suitable aliquot tubes
0.45 µm filter, optional
Dry ice-cooled ethanol bath (optional)
Follow volumes: Useful Numbers for Cell Culture

Protocol
Day 0: Plate HEK293T Cells

Plate 3.5 × 10⁶ HEK293T cells in one 10 cm dish (MRC)

Dhruv plates 750K-1M 293Ts per well of a 6 well plate.

Use 10 mL complete DMEM per dish or 2ml per well of 6 well
Return the plate to the incubator.

Day 1: Transfection

Approximately 24 hours after plating, transfect the cells using TransIT-LT1.
If the medium appears exhausted or the cells need additional attachment time, replace the medium 3-4 hours before transfection.
For the medium change, add 10 mL fresh complete DMEM (2ml per well of a 6 well) and return the cells to the incubator.
Bring Opti-MEM and TransIT-LT1 to room temperature before use.
Prepare the transfection mixture in a 14 mL tube in the following order:



Add plasmid DNA at an approximately 4:3:1 mass ratio:
15 µg lentiviral transfer plasmid
11 µg psPAX2
4 µg pCMV-VSV-G
30 µg total DNA
Add Opti-MEM to a total volume of 1.5 mL.
Mix by pipetting, then gently swirl the tube.
Add TransIT-LT1 directly into the liquid, dropwise.
Use 3 µL TransIT-LT1 per µg DNA as an optimization range; 90 µL for 30 µg total DNA.
Gently swirl the tube. Do not pipette or vortex after adding TransIT-LT1.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 30 minutes.



Add the DNA/Opti-MEM/TransIT-LT1 mixture to the cells dropwise in a circular motion.
Return the plate to the incubator at 5% CO₂.

Day 2: Medium Change

Approximately 16 hours after transfection, gently remove the medium.
Replace it with 10 mL fresh complete medium for virus collection (R10 for T cells)

Days 3 and 4: Viral Supernatant Collection

Collect the cellular supernatant at approximately 24 and 48 hours after the medium change
Pipette the HEK293T supernatant into a 50 mL conical tube.
Pool supernatant from multiple 10 cm dishes if needed.
Centrifuge at 1600 rpm for 5 minutes.
Optional: Filter the supernatant through a 0.45 µm filter.
Transfer the viral supernatant into 5 mL tubes or another suitable aliquot format.
Freeze in -80C
Prepare single-use aliquots and avoid repeated freeze-thaw cycles.
T cell activation: Follow Lab Protocol from Giovanni
Transduction Option 1: MRC
Coated retronectin plates O/N at 4C or for 2-3 hours at RT

90ul of RN in 5910 of PBS. Coat each well using 900-1000ul of solution.


Block plates with 4ml of R10 for 30 min prior to transduction

After 24 hours of activation, prepare Lib5 and Lib7 lentiviral library supernatants supplemented with: LentiBOOST (Sirion Biotech) at 1:200 dilution. Add both Solution A and Solution B
Add the activated cells to the supplemented lentiviral supernatants. Dhruv has used 3ml of virus with cells, in each well of retronectin coasted plate
Spin-infect the cells at: 800 × g for 3 hours
Following centrifugation, incubate the cells for an additional 4 hours at: 37°C, 5% CO₂
Wash the cells to remove residual viral supernatant and transduction reagents.
Culture the washed cells for 4 days in medium supplemented with: Human IL-2: 20 IU/mL.
Depending on the goal, add mouse IL-7 (2.5ng/mL), and Mouse IL-15: 25 ng/mL
Transduction Option 2: Arlene Sharpe (Naïve T cells)
Coat non-tissue culture–treated 6-well plates with RetroNectin (Takara Bio, Cat. #T100B) at approximately 15 µg/cm² overnight at 4°C.
The next morning, remove RetroNectin and block each well with 2 mL of 2% BSA in PBS−/− for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Remove the blocking solution, add 2 mL lentiviral supernatant per well, and centrifuge at 2,000 × g for 2 hours at 32°C.
Isolate naive CD8⁺ T cells using the Miltenyi Naive CD8a⁺ T Cell Isolation Kit (Cat. #130-096-543).
Plate the cells onto the virus-coated wells in complete RPMI containing 1 mg/mL LentiBOOST and 1 ng/mL recombinant murine IL-7.
Complete RPMI consisted of RPMI 1640 with L-glutamine, 10% FBS, 1% penicillin/streptomycin, 10 mM HEPES, 55 µM 2-mercaptoethanol, 1% sodium pyruvate, and 1% non-essential amino acids.
Culture the cells for 7 days with 1 ng/mL IL-7. Change the medium on days 2 and 5, and add fresh cytokine on day 4.

title: Cloning with HIFI DNA Assembly_KL
text:
Cloning with HIFI DNA Assembly

The principle behind HIFI DNA Assembly is the joining of DNA fragments with ends that share the same sequence (15 – 40bp). There are several good animations on Youtube.
Prep your sequences of interest (Plasmid prep or g-blocks)
If using two plasmids, design primers with overhangs using Snapgene. BE CAREFUL, primers used in the same reaction need to have the same Tm WITHOUT the overhangs. In other words, the difference of Tm between the primers (without the overhangs) has to be max 5C. Use the NEB Tm calculator to calculate the Tm and not Snapgene if you are using the Q5 NEB Master mix for the PCR.
Run the PCR based on the Q5 master mix protocol BUT

-use 1min/kb for the elongation phase
-run the PCR at the Tm of the primers WITHOUT the overhangs

Optional: Add 1ul of DPNI to destroy the substrate for the reaction (because it is methylated). MIX well, incubate at room temperature for 5 min and then at 37C for 60 minutes. (Of note: DPN1 will work in the Q5 PCR buffer or cutsmart buffer. It doesn’t work in water)
Run the product in a gel and isolate the band that corresponds to the right band size. Let the gel run AS LONG AS POSSIBLE to avoid contamination of your band with residual template DNA. Elute with water preferably (to avoid problems with the downstream reaction).
Combine the DNA for the HIFI DNA Assembly reaction. 1:1 vector to insert for a total reaction of 50ng. You don’t have to use 10ul of the Assembly as long as it is 1x (I usually use 5ul of DNA and 5ul of HIFI). Have a mock reaction as a control that you add water instead of HIFI DNA Assembly
Transform two sets of bacteria, one with 2ul of the reaction product and one with 2ul of the DNA from the mock reaction
Next day you should see colonies in the plate with the product and no colonies in the other plate (in reality the majority of the time we see some colonies on the control due to leftover template but the experimental usually has 10x more colonies).
Midi prep a few colonies. Design primers to sequence the new vectors. Send them for sequencing to Genewitz. ALWAYS do this because there are frequent mutations that occur

title: Molecular_Cloning_Workflow
text:
4.2 Procedure
1. Confirm the restriction sites, expected fragment sizes, recommended buffer, incubation temperature, methylation sensitivity, and heat-inactivation conditions.
2. Assemble the reaction on ice. Add water and buffer first, followed by DNA. Add the restriction enzyme(s) last and mix gently.
3. Incubate at the recommended temperature. Use 1 hour as the routine standard. A 30-minute digest may be sufficient for some enzymes (HF); difficult digests may be extended to 2–4 hours. Dhruv typically digests for 4 hours for a complete digest. This may not always be the best option since some enzymes exhibit star activity.
4. Run the digest on an agarose gel with EtBr (4ul for small gel in 100ul). Separate the desired linearized vector or insert from uncut plasmid and unwanted fragments. Typically 1-1.5% agarose gels work well for large fragments.
5. Excise the correct band using UV visualization when available. Purify the DNA with a gel extraction kit and elute in a low volume (20ul)
6. Measure DNA concentration before ligation or HiFi assembly.

title: Molecular_Cloning_Workflow

text: The LsgA Plasmig can be used as a vector to express guide RNAs for Crispr/Cas9. The Plasmid already contains all the “helper” sequences and we only need to add the guide RNA for the gene. It can than be used to create retrovirus using the pCL-Eco packaging plasmid.

title: LsgA Cloning

sgRNA design
Get your guide RNA Sequence from IDT or ChopChop or anywhere else. Do not include the PAM sequence. The length of the guide RNA sould be 20 nucleotides.






Tip



OPTIONAL: Add G to 20 nt sgRNA sequence if it does not start with G to increase transcription.


Design the fwd and reverse oligos:
5’ –CACCGNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN –    3’
3’     –CNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNCAAA –5’

The CACC and the CAAA are the overlapping sequences to the digested plasmid. The G and C are the optimal base before the guide sequence to improve the transcription. NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN is the 20 bp guide RNA.
Order the primers.
