title: FC1.antibody_titration
text:
Date: 02/08/2023
Antibody titration
NOTES:


Before using the antibodies, mix well and spin down in order to avoid antibody aggregates. Alternatively, prepare the antibody mix and spin it before staining.


Have a look to antibody datasheets to know if the staining has to be performed at 37°C (especially for receptors undergoing cell internalization and recycling). Add co-staining with other markers if needed.


Since BV and BUV conjugates are very sensible to the buffer and since we are using them daily in our FACS panels, it is strongly suggested to titrate all the Abs in Super Bright Complete Staining Buffer (Thermo Fisher, catalog #: SB-4401-42).


MATERIALS:

Live/Dead Blue (Thermo Fisher, -80°C, GG reagents box) → Add 50 μL of DMSO to the vial of reactive dye.
ArC™ Amine Reactive Compensation Bead Kit (Thermo Fisher, 4°C, my drawer) → comp beads for Live/Dead Blue
UltraComp eBeads™ Compensation Beads (Thermo Fisher, 4°C, my drawer)
FACS buffer (1X PBS-/- + 2% FBS)
Super Bright Complete Staining Buffer (Thermo Fisher, catalog #: SB-4401-42) –> 5 µL/test to be added directly to the antibody mix
Fix solution depending on the application
Antibody to be titrated
Cells

PROTOCOL

Wash the cells with 2 mL (20X staining volume) of 1X PBS-/- if cells are suspended in complete RPMI, in order to eliminate FBS or BSA that can bind Live/Dead Blue
Prepare Live/Dead Blue mix: for 4 samples (100 µL/test) 10M cells each (19.5 µL ddH2O in which you add 0.5 µL Live/Dead Blue; then add 380 µL PBS-/-)
Add 50 µL Live/Dead Blue mix to each sample tube. Add 50 µL of Fc Block (ready to use at 4ºC) to each sample tube. Incubate 15 min at RT in the dark.
Wash the cells with 2 mL FACS buffer and centrifuge 1600 rpm 4 min
Discard the supernatant
If antibody to titrate goes at 37ºC for 20 minutes than perform now the steps described below for titration and co-stain after.
Add surface co-staining at this step, if needed. Then wash and discard as above. NB: if titrating an intracellular antibody proceed with fixation and permeabilization.
Resuspend the cells into a FACS buffer volume equal to N° tubes (8) X 50 µL
Put 50 µL of FACS buffer (with 5 µL/test of Super Bright Complete Staining Buffer) in all tubes but tube 1



Prepare 115 µL Antibody mix 2X (it will be in excess). The mix has to be prepared in FACS buffer with 5 µL/test of Super Bright Complete Staining Buffer



Add 50 µL Antibody mix in the first two tubes and mix well. Then proceed with serial dilution as described: remove 50 µL of suspension from tube 2 and put it in tube 3, mix well; remove 50 µL from tube 3 and put it in tube 4, mix well, etc. NB: remove 50 uL from tube 7 and toss it as tube 8 is the unstained control
Put 50 µL cell suspension into each tube and incubate 20 min at 4ºC in the dark
Wash with 2 mL of FACS buffer and centrifuge 1600 rpm 4 min
Discard the supernatant
In order to fix cells, add 150 µL of fix buffer (BioLegend – brown bottle) and incubate for 10 minutes. Alternatively, you can fix and perm in the preferred conditions.
Wash cells with 2 mL FACS buffer and centrifuge 1600 rpm 4 min. Alternatively, follow the manufacturer protocol for fixation and permeabilization.
Discard the supernatant
Add intracellular co-staining at this step, if needed. Then wash and discard as above. Alternatively, proceed with intracellular/intranuclear antibody titration as described above (use PermWash instead of FACS buffer and avoid use of SB buffer for intracellular antiobodies).
Resuspend the cells with 200 µL of FACS buffer, keep samples at 4°C until ready for acquisition

Compensation
NOTES:


You can use cells or beads. Use beads preferentially and vortex very well them before using.


For Bigfoot it is mandatory to prepare the unstained control even with cells only to detect and spectral unmix the autofluorescent signal coming from cells. Optional but recommended are the single stained control with cells.


If the antibody is conjugated with tandem dyes, you must use the same antibody to prepare the comps.


PROTOCOL


For each dye make one comp using 1 drop of UltraComp eBeads + Ab at the right titer (if the titer is lower than 0.5 µL use 0.5 µL).


Make the unstained control comp with 1 drop of UltraComp eBeads.


Make the positive control comp for Live/Dead Blue with 2 drops of ArC Amine Reactive beads + 2 µL Live/Dead Blue


Make the negative control comp for Live/Dead Blue with 2 drops of ArC Amine Negative beads (no Live/Dead Blue)


Incubate comps at least for 20 minutes in the dark. NB: If in a hurry you can avoid doing the steps below. Usually bead comps are stable for up to a week.




Wash with 2 mL FACS buffer (DO NOT WASH positive neither negative control comp for Live/Dead Blue) and centrifuge 1600 rpm 4 min
Fix comps with 150 µL of fix solution (FA 1% in HBSS-/- or PFA 1% in HBSS-/-) and incubate for 15 minutes. NB: work under the chemical hood. DO NOT FIX positive neither negative control comp for Live/Dead Blue!
Wash cells with 2 mL FACS buffer and centrifuge 1600 rpm 5 minutes. NB: work under the chemical hood.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend comps with 200 µL of FACS buffer, keep samples at 4°C until ready for acquisition.

title: FC4.TF_buffer_set
text:
Description
The BD Pharmingen™ Transcription Factor Buffer Set is optimized for fixing and permeabilizing cells prior to immunofluorescent staining and flow cytometric analysis of cells that express specific intracytoplasmic and intranuclear proteins. The BD Pharmingen™ Transcription Factor Buffer Set was designed to improve ease-of-use and minimize processing time, to reduce nonspecific staining, to increase the resolution of positively stained cells and to significantly reduce cell loss during fixation, permeabilization and staining procedures. Flow cytometric detection of the many proteins known to be expressed within various intracellular compartments, especially transcription factors, is improved with BD Pharmingen™ Transcription Factor Buffer Set use. This buffer system has been found useful for fixing and permeabilizing a variety of cell types from diverse human and mouse tissues. The buffer system is flexible in supporting multiwell-plate high-throughput and bulk sample analyses and applications that require overnight sample storage. The buffer system has minimal impact on the light-scatter and autofluorescence characteristics of processed cells resulting in characteristics similar to those observed for freshly prepared, highly viable primary cells. In many cases the buffer system was found to be compatible with the immunofluorescent staining of cell-surface antigens both before and after cellular fixation and permeabilization. The buffer system is also compatible with many tandem fluorochromes.

title: FC4.TF_buffer_set
text:
Preparation and Storage
Store undiluted at 4°C.
Keep stock buffers and 1x working solutions at 2-8°C. After opening the BD Pharmingen™ Transcription Factor Buffer Set, use it within six months. If stored without opening, then use before the expiration date indicated on the bottle labels.
Avoid microbial contamination of reagents as incorrect results may occur.
Handle TF Diluent Buffer (Component 51-9008101) in a sterile cabinet or use aseptic practices to preserve the integrity of the solution.

title: FC4.TF_buffer_set

Application Notes
Application
Intracellular staining (flow cytometry)

title: FC4.TF_buffer_set
text:
Recommended Assay Procedure:
Prior to intracellular staining

Prepare single-cell suspensions from lymphoid tissues of interest (eg, human peripheral blood, mouse thymus or lymph node). Label 5-ml round-bottom 12 × 75-mm polystyrene tubes and identify appropriate antibodies for your experiment.
Slowly invert five times the stock BD Pharmingen™ TF Fix/Perm Buffer (4X), TF Diluent Buffer and TF Perm/Wash Buffer (5X) bottles before making working solutions.
Dilute the 4x Fix/Perm Buffer using the TF Diluent Buffer to the necessary volume of 1x Fix/Perm working solution (a typical dilution for 20 tests is 5 ml of 4x Fix/Perm and 15 ml of TF Diluent Buffer). Use the 1x Fix/Perm Buffer working solution for the Intracellular Staining Protocol listed below within an hour of preparation.
Dilute the 5x Perm/Wash Buffer to a 1x Perm/Wash Buffer working solution. (A typical dilution for 20 tests would be 30 ml of 5x Perm/Wash Buffer added to 120 ml of deionized water to yield 150 ml of 1x Perm/Wash Buffer). Use the 1x Perm/Wash Buffer working solution for the Intracellular Staining Protocol listed below. Store the 1x Perm/Wash Buffer at 2-8°C for up to one week.




Image

title: FC4.TF_buffer_set
text:
Routinely Tested

Buffers for intracellular staining should be kept on ice or at 2-8°C throughout the Intracellular Staining Protocol.
Surface Staining: Prepare cell suspension containing 10 million cells per ml in flow cytometry stain buffer, such as BD Pharmingen™ Stain Buffer (FBS) (Cat. No. 554656) or Stain Buffer (BSA) (Cat. No. 554657). Incubate 100 µl of cells per tube with fluorescent antibodies (eg, antibodies specific for CD4, CD8, CD25, CD19) for 30 minutes at 2-8°C. Wash cells one time with 2 ml of stain buffer and move forward with the intracellular staining protocol listed below.

title: FC4.TF_buffer_set
text:
Intracellular Staining Protocol

Fix/Perm: After the cell surface staining procedure is completed, aspirate residual stain buffer. Resuspend cell pellets by brief vortexing and add 1 ml of freshly prepared 1x Fix/Perm Buffer working solution to each tube. Vortex samples for approximately three seconds after adding the Fix/Perm Buffer. Incubate samples at 2-8°C for 40-50 minutes protected from light.
Perm/Wash: Add 1 ml of 1x Perm/Wash Buffer directly to the fixed and permeabilized cells suspended in the 1x Fix/Perm Buffer. Pellet the cells by centrifugation. (Note: All centrifugation steps post Fix/Perm are at 350 g and at 2-8 °C for 6 minutes). Decant or aspirate the supernatants.
Perm/Wash: Add 2 ml of 1x Perm/Wash Buffer to the pelleted cells followed by centrifugation. Decant or aspirate wash buffer.
Intracellular Staining: Add 80-100 µl of 1x Perm/Wash Buffer to cell samples and the fluorescent antibodies specific for intracellular proteins (eg, FoxP3, T-bet and/or IL-17A) and for nonspecific control staining (eg, matching fluorescent Ig isotype controls) to each tube. Vortex tube or rack for 10 seconds and incubate at 2-8°C for 40-50 minutes protected from light.
Perm/Wash: Briefly vortex samples prior to washing. Wash cells with 2 ml of 1x Perm/Wash Buffer. Centrifuge cells. Decant or aspirate the wash buffer.
Perm/Wash: Wash cells with 2 ml 1x Perm/Wash. Centrifuge cells. Decant or aspirate wash buffer.
Sample preparation for flow cytometry: Resuspend cell pellet in 350 µl of flow cytometry stain buffer. Analyze the cells and acquire data using a flow cytometer.

title: FC4.TF_buffer_set
text:
Notes:

Due to the fixation and permeabilization procedure, forward and side light-scatter signals will be slightly different than those of live cells.
The buffer system is optimized for use with fluorescence settings established by using the BD™ Cytometer Setup & Tracking Beads Kit (Cat. No. 642412). However, for your application, minor adjustments in gate and/or detector voltage may need to be made prior to compensation and acquisition.
Target the acquisition for a statistically significant number of events.
A titration of the fluorescent antibody’s optimal staining amount and optimization of the staining time may be required in your application.

Danger : TF Fix/Perm Buffer (4X) (Component 51-9008100) contains 5.0% formaldehyde (w/w) and 1.76% methanol (w/w).

title: FACS protocol sheet
text:
FACS protocol sheet


You will need about 105 – 5x106 cells for FACS staining (optimal = 106) per sample
Spin the cells down

96 well plates or 15 ml conical tubes – 1800 rpm for 5 minutes
Eppendorf tubes – 30 seconds at max

You must first FC block (If you are staining for FC, proceed to next step)

Make master mix of 50 μl FACS buffer/sample plus 0.25 μl FC block/sample (e.g., if you have 8 samples, mix 400 μl FACS buffer + 2 μl FC block)
Resuspend your cell pellet in 50 μl master mix and vortex
Incubate on ice for about 5 minutes

Biotin labeling (If you are NOT biotin labeling, proceed to next step)

Add 0.5 μl biotin antibody per sample
Incubate on ice for 15 minutes
Wash with ~1.5 ml FACS buffer and vortex
Spin
Aspirate and discard supernatant

Add antibodies to your sample in 50 μl
Wash

96 well plates – 2 times in 250 μl FACS buffer
Eppendorf or FACS tubes – 1 time in 1.5 to 3 ml FACS buffer

Fix

Add 50-200 μl Fix buffer
Store at 4°C

title: FC3.intracellular_staining
text:
02/08/2023
Protocol for intracellular staining for flow cytometry
NB: To eliminate potential artifacts due to dead cell contamination, we recommend the use of a Fixable Viability Dye to allow the exclusion of dead cells from the analysis (as described in protocol CB.10). The saponin BD Perm/Wash™ buffer can be used in intracellular cytokine staining to permeabilize cells and to serve as an antibody diluent and cell wash buffer. Because saponin-mediated cell permeabilization is a reversible process, it is important to keep the cells in the presence of saponin during intracellular cytokine staining.
Materials

BD Fix/Perm solution is supplied 4X: prepare 1X with 1 part of Fix/Perm Buffer + 3 parts of Diluent Buffer
BD Perm/Wash buffer is supplied 5X: prepare 1X with 1 part Perm/Wash + 4 parts of distilled water
Sterile FACS washing buffer (1X PBS-/- supplemented with 2% FBS or 1X HBSS-/- supplemented with 2% FBS)
Antibodies
Sample

Protocol

Stain cell surface antigen(s).
After the last wash, aspirate the supernatant and pulse vortex the sample to completely dissociate the pellet.

1. Fix and Permeabilize Cells

Thoroughly resuspend cells in 500 μL of BD Fix/Perm solution per tube and incubate for 40 min at 4°C.
Wash cells in 2 mL BD Perm/Wash™ buffer which can be used as the wash buffer and as the antibody diluent.
Centrifuge samples at 1600 rpm at room temperature for 4 minutes, then aspirate the supernatant.

2. Stain for Intracellular Cytokines

Thoroughly resuspend fixed/permeabilized cells in 100 μL of BD Perm/Wash™ buffer 1X containing a predetermined optimal concentration of a fluorochrome-conjugated anti-cytokine antibody.
Incubate at 4°C for 40 minutes in the dark.
Wash cells with BD Perm/Wash™ buffer 1X.
Centrifuge samples at 1600 rpm at room temperature for 5 minutes, then aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend in 200 uL FACS buffer prior to flow cytometric analysis.



Keep the sample at 4°C till the acquisition.

Critical parameters affecting
                    titers
• TIME: the longer the incubation the lower the titer needed to reach
  saturation

  chemokine receptors give a much higher fluorescence when stained at
  37°C compared to RT or 4°C

  optimized titer  titrate antibodies with the buffer used in the staining

excess to the number of molecules, unless cell number changes
dramatically.

Slide 10: Critical parameters affecting




Extracted slide text

Critical parameters affecting
                    titers
• TIME: the longer the incubation the lower the titer needed to reach
  saturation
• TEMPERATURE: some Abs stain better at certain temperatures, e.g.
  chemokine receptors give a much higher fluorescence when stained at
  37°C compared to RT or 4°C
• BUFFER: intracellular staining (Fix/Perm buffers) can alter the
  optimized titer  titrate antibodies with the buffer used in the staining


Cell number DOES NOT affect the Ab titer. The Ab is always in vast
excess to the number of molecules, unless cell number changes
dramatically.


General rule: the optimized titer can be used to stain up to 10-15

Aspects to consider
•   Compensation can be performed manually (at the
    machine) or automatically (via software)

•   Manual compensation: tedious, need to check carefully
    that positive and negative signals have to match

•   Automated compensation: no errors, if using the right
    controls

•   Manual compensation is impractical in a multicolor
    experiment (roughly 2n pairwise combinations)

•   Changing compensation in a pairwise combination
    affects distribution in other channels.

The 3 golden rules of
             compensation
1. Use a single-stained control that is AT LEAST
   as bright as the test staining

2. Use the same reagent that is being used in
   the staining (valid for tandems such as PE-
   Cy7, APC-Cy7, etc. – for non tandems any
   reagent is OK)

3. Have a paired-negative control with the
   SAME autofluorescence as the positive (cells
   with cells, beads with beads, etc.)

Everything else is not necessary!

Slide 32: “Errors” in compensation




Extracted slide text

“Errors” in compensation

• Properly compensated data may not appear
  rectilinear because of measurement errors (are
  more prominent in case of limited numbers of
  photons, Cy7PE or Cy7APC dyes, with low
  energy)

• Measurement errors are directly proportional to
  the intensity (LOG relationship)

• This effect on compensated data is unavoidable,
  and cannot be corrected with compensation
  (LINEAR correction)

• Compensation does not introduce the error, it only
  REVEALS it because it brings the distribution to the

When light from a laser interrogates a cell, that cell scatters light in all

Slide 37: BRILLIANT DYES STRUCTURE AND FEATURES




Extracted slide text

BRILLIANT DYES STRUCTURE AND FEATURES




These conjugated polymers are comprised of alternating single and double bonds and aromatic units.
This repeating bond structure creates a continuous π-orbital system and extended electronic delocalization.

The Brilliant fluorescent probe resulted from chemical modifications to a polymer that yielded the appropriate
excitation spectrum, water solubility, conjugation ability, and minimal nonspecific binding. Additional violet-excited
fluorescent probes with differing emission spectra have been developed by creating tandem dyes of Brilliant
conjugated with more traditional fluorophores such as Cy3 (the BV570 tandem dye).

Because the number of sites for acceptor dye attachment is controlled synthetically these BV tandems
exhibit far less lot-to-lot variation in the ratio of donor to acceptor dye, and thus less spectral variability,
than PE and similar protein based tandems. Because the number of dye attachment sites is fixed,
repeated optimization of dye stechiometry is not necessary.



Stephen C. De Rosa.            Cytometry Part A 81A:445   2012
Pratip K. Chattopadhyay et al. Cytometry Part A 81A:456   2012

  steered down specific channels with the use of filters.

Slide 37: BRILLIANT DYES STRUCTURE AND FEATURES




Extracted slide text

BRILLIANT DYES STRUCTURE AND FEATURES




These conjugated polymers are comprised of alternating single and double bonds and aromatic units.
This repeating bond structure creates a continuous π-orbital system and extended electronic delocalization.

The Brilliant fluorescent probe resulted from chemical modifications to a polymer that yielded the appropriate
excitation spectrum, water solubility, conjugation ability, and minimal nonspecific binding. Additional violet-excited
fluorescent probes with differing emission spectra have been developed by creating tandem dyes of Brilliant
conjugated with more traditional fluorophores such as Cy3 (the BV570 tandem dye).

Because the number of sites for acceptor dye attachment is controlled synthetically these BV tandems
exhibit far less lot-to-lot variation in the ratio of donor to acceptor dye, and thus less spectral variability,
than PE and similar protein based tandems. Because the number of dye attachment sites is fixed,
repeated optimization of dye stechiometry is not necessary.



Stephen C. De Rosa.            Cytometry Part A 81A:445   2012
Pratip K. Chattopadhyay et al. Cytometry Part A 81A:456   2012

FALSE POSITIVE EVENTS

DEAD CELLS EXCLUSION
Dead cells can nonspecifically bind monoclonal antibody conjugates, potentially leading to false
positive events, particularly when cell frequencies are low.

                                        DYE OPTIONS
1) DNA intercalating dyes (Propidium Iodide, 7AAD, SYTOX etc.)

2) Phosphatidylserine binding dyes (Annexin V)

3) Amino Reactive Viability Dyes (ViD, Zombie etc)



These dyes recognize late apoptotic events. They were found to be stable with no loss in
fluorescent intensity when treated with permeabilization or fixation reagents.
Since these dyes are excited by a variety of lasers and emit light energy at a variety of detectors,
they can be easily incorporated into different panel strategies.

title: Making LCMV stocks
text:
Note



Production of LCMV viral stocks. Protocol adapted from Kay Chung via John Teijaro and modified by Thomas Mann.
The production of LCMV is carried out in BHK (baby hamster kidney) cells.

title: Making LCMV stocks
text:
Reagents:

BHK media (500 mL):
500 mL DMEM (high glucose, liquid)
50 mL FBS (10%)
5 mL L-glutamine (100x)
5 mL Pen-strep (100x)
25 mL Tryptose phosphate broth (Gibco)

title: Making LCMV stocks
text:
Procedure:

Day -1:

Plate BHK to be ~40-50% confluent the following day. Seed about 5x10 6 BHK cells in a T175 flask the day before infection. The cells will grow to a confluency of 40-50%, corresponding to ~1x107.







Note



BHK cells grow at different rates in different labs and seem to be pretty sensitive. Consider setting up flasks at target multiple confluencies to try to hit the right one on the infection day.




Day 0:

Take photos of the T175 flasks on the light microscope if possible - try to record what a good confluency looks like.
Pipet off media and infect with virus in a limited volume (6 mL for a T175, 3 mL for a T75). The MOI used in the field seems to vary; many people use 0.001-0.01, but Teijaro lab uses an MOI of 0.1.

The lore is that it is important to use a high titer virus to inoculate, but unclear where this line is drawn.
Teijaro adds 5 uL of 2x10 8 PFU/mL stock to 6 mL BHK media to hit a target of MOI 0.1 for 107 cells in a T175.

Incubate at 37 Celsius for 90 minutes. Gently tilt and rock the flask every 10-15 minutes.
After 90 minutes, add 19 mL warm BHK media (total 25 mL final).
Incubate for 72 hours.



Day 3






Warning



Keep the virus cold for all following steps!



Pipet supernatant into 15 mL conical tubes. The supernatant contains the virus. Be careful, this is a LOT of LCMV. Have bleach handy in case of a spill.
Separate any remaining BHK cells that were aspirated from virus.

Spin at 2000 rpm in a benchtop centrifuge (~800-850 g depending on centrifuge in IMPL-K) for 15 minutes.
Collect the supernatant, transfer to a fresh tube.
Repeat for a total of two centrifugation steps.

Keeping the virus cold, aliquot and snap freeze in liquid nitrogen. Pre-chill cryo-tubes in cold room.
Protocol yields ~20-25 mL virus containing supernatant at a target of ~2x108 pfu/mL.

Infecting at 2x10 6 pfu/mouse (100 uL of 2x10 7 pfu/mL), this corresponds to enough virus to infect 2000 mice per T175 of LCMV Clone 13.

Titrate the virus. Make sure to titrate an aliquot that has been frozen and thawed to get a representative value for what the titer will be when you inject from a thawed aliquot (rather than titrating the supernatant directly).

title: CB1.Tissue processing for viral titers
text:
Tissue processing for viral titers
Kennidy Takehara
Last updated 11/22/23
Reagents:
Homogenization beads: BioSpec #11079125Z
Tubes for homogenization: Genesee scientific: #21-354
Primer LCMV GP Rev: GCAACTGCTGTGTTCCCGAAA
Primer LCMV GP Fwd: CATTCACCTGGACTTTGTCAGACTC
Collecting tissues:

Collect <30mg of tissues (can use 30ul as reference) into shatterproof homogenizer tubes and immediately place on dry ice. Store in -80 until ready to use

Can also take remaining organ into eppies to keep in -80 as backup, suggest cutting small pieces before freezing.


Processing tissues:
Recommended: label 2 sets of eppie tubes per sample and pre-label RNEasy columns to limit protocol time. Want to work as quickly as possible.

Keep tissues on dry ice (and then ice) while preparing for homogenization
Add 600ul RLT buffer (from RNEasy kit) with one scoop of beads to homogenizer tube

Recommended for tissue: add 10ul BME for every 1mL RLT

Take tubes to Zuniga lab and homogenize (need to be trained by Kennidy or Zuniga lab member)

For homogenizer: 30 seconds, check for chunks and do another 30 seconds if necessary

Spin down entire tube full speed 4 degrees for 10 minutes.
Pipette ~350ul of supernatant into new eppie tube & add one volume 70% ethanol.
Continue with RNeasy kit – pick up with transfer to RNeasy spin column: https://www.qiagen.com/us/resources/download.aspx?id=0e32fbb1-c307-4603-ac81-a5e98490ed23&lang=en
I usually elute in 30ul of H20

Continue with cDNA synthesis: https://protocols.heeg.io/protocols/mol_bio/cDNA.html
All reagents can be found in pink qPCR box or SSIV box
Briefly:

Remove DNA contamination (scale up for 30ul)

Add 2.5ul of 10X TURBO DNase Buffer and 1.25µl TURBO DNase to 25 µl of RNA, and mix gently

May need to adjust these numbers based on how much volume you get from elution

Incubate at 37°C for 20-30 min
Add resuspended Inactivation Reagent (5µl to 28.75 µl mix), and mix well
Incubate 5 min at RT, mixing occasionally

Centrifuge at 10000 x g for 1.5 min and transfer the RNA to a fresh tube
Recommended: nanodrop to get concentration and purity

Anneal primer to template RNA



Heat the RNA-primer mix at 65°C for 5 minutes, and then incubate on ice for at least 1 minute








Component
Volume




50 μM Oligo d(T)20 primer, 50 μM random hexamers, or 2 μM gene-specific reverse primer
1 μL


10 mM dNTP mix (10 mM each)
1 μL


Template RNA (10 pg–5 μg total RNA or 10 pg–500 ng mRNA)
up to 11 μL


DEPC-treated or nuclease-free water
to 13 μL




Use 50uM random hexamers to amplify all RNA, use oligo d(T) primers if want entire RNA fragment (ie for cloning gene)

Prepare RT reaction mix

Vortex and briefly centrifuge the 5× SSIV Buffer.
Combine the following components in a reaction tube.




Component
Volume




5× SSIV Buffer
4 μL


100 mM DTT
1 μL


RNaseOUT™ Recombinant RNase Inhibitor
1 μL


SuperScript® IV Reverse Transcriptase (200 U/μL)
1 μL




Add 7µl RT reaction mix to the annealed RNA (13 µl)

Incubate reactions

If using random hexamer, incubate the combined reaction mixture at 23°C for 10 minutes, and then proceed to next step.
If using oligo d(T)20 or gene-specific primer, directly proceed to next step.
Incubate the combined reaction mixture at 50–55°C for 10 minutes.
Inactivate the reaction by incubating it at 80°C for 10 minutes

Remove RNA

To remove RNA, add 1 μL E. coli RNase H, and incubate 37°C for 20 minutes.

For qPCR:
HPRT SYBR and LCMV GP primers, stock 100μM

Dilute primers: 2.5μl F, 2.5μl R, 195 μl water

I usually dilute cDNA with 20ul of water, for 40ul total of cDNA (enough to repeat if needed)
qPCR rxn:

Primers: 1μl
SYBR 2x: 5μl
cDNA: 4μl

Tips for qPCR:

Group primers together, so at least 2 replicates per sample
Make sure to mix with pipette all reagents
Use same batch of SYBR – make sure have enough before starting
I like to pipette all of my cDNA on one side of well (make sure some in every well) and then flip around and pipette master mix on other side
Make sure to be VERY accurate with pipetting (I like to reverse pipette)
Include cDNA positive control (so know qPCR works with housekeeping) and water control

title: Infection with LCMV CL13
text:
Use the LCMV CL13 Titer Calculator to calculate the AB or NM stock-virus and PBS volumes needed for infection.


Day -1: Transfer naïve P14 cells (500–1,000) by retro-orbital injection.
Day 0: Infect retro-orbitally with LCMV Clone 13 (2 × 10^6 PFU of AB or NM virus) in 200 µL. Dilute stock with PBS. Note that AB and NM have different titers.



Transfer 2–10 × 10^5 cells retro-orbitally.
Infect with Clone 13 on the same day as cell transfer. Infect retro-orbitally with LCMV Clone 13 (2 × 10^6 PFU of AB and NM virus) in 200 µL. Dilute stock with PBS. Note that AB and NM have different titers.
These are the PFU/mL values of each Clone 13 stock in the Goldrath Lab:



Stock
AB (2015)
NM (2020)




New average PFU/mL
5.15 × 10^7
8.50 × 10^7



Dilute stock in the hood. Dispose of all tips in 10% bleach.
All takedowns must be performed in the hood regardless of timepoint, as Clone 13 is chronic.

title: Infection with LCMV CL13
text:

title: Propagate LCMV Clone 13
text:
Propagate LCMV Clone 13 virus
BHK media (500 mL):


500 mL DMEM (high glucose, liquid)


50 mL FBS (10%)


5 mL L-glutamine (100x)


5 mL Pen-strep (100x)


25 mL Tryptose phosphate broth (Gibco)


Day -1:


Plate BHK to be ~40-50% confluent the following day. Seed about 5x10 6 BHK cells in a T175 flask the day before infection. The cells will grow to a confluency of 40-50%, corresponding to ~1x107.


Note
BHK cells grow at different rates in different labs and seem to be pretty sensitive. Consider setting up flasks at target multiple confluencies to try to hit the right one on the infection day.
Day 0:


Take photos of the T175 flasks on the light microscope if possible - try to record what a good confluency looks like.


Pipet off media and infect with virus in a limited volume (6 mL for a T175, 3 mL for a T75). The MOI used in the field seems to vary; many people use 0.001-0.01, but Teijaro lab uses an MOI of 0.1.



The lore is that it is important to use a high titer virus to inoculate, but unclear where this line is drawn.


Teijaro adds 5 uL of 2x10 8 PFU/mL stock to 6 mL BHK media to hit a target of MOI 0.1 for 107 cells in a T175.


Allen lab has a stock at 2.58e8/ml (Floor 2 lab -80, rack 00156, box 01649). I added 4 ul per 6 mls of media per flask or 24 ul per 36 mls for 6 T175 flasks



Incubate at 37 Celsius for 90 minutes. Gently tilt and rock the flask every 10-15 minutes.


After 90 minutes, add 19 mL warm BHK media (total 25 mL final).


Incubate for 72 hours.


Day 3
Keep the virus cold for all following steps!


Pipet supernatant into 15 mL conical tubes. The supernatant contains the virus. Be careful, this is a LOT of LCMV. Have bleach handy in case of a spill.


Separate any remaining BHK cells that were aspirated from virus.



Spin at 2000 rpm in a benchtop centrifuge (~800-850 g depending on centrifuge in IMPL-K) for 15 minutes.


Collect the supernatant, transfer to a fresh tube.


Repeat for a total of two centrifugation steps.



Keeping the virus cold, aliquot and snap freeze in liquid nitrogen. Pre-chill cryo-tubes in cold room.


Protocol yields ~20-25 mL virus containing supernatant at a target of ~2x108 pfu/mL.



Infecting at 2x10 6 pfu/mouse (100 uL of 2x10 7 pfu/mL), this corresponds to enough virus to infect 2000 mice per T175 of LCMV Clone 13.



Titrate the virus. Make sure to titrate an aliquot that has been frozen and thawed to get a representative value for what the titer will be when you inject from a thawed aliquot (rather than titrating the supernatant directly).

Note



This is a protocol that I got from Maurice, Nicholas J (nmaurice@fredhutch.org) for the Lm-OVA variants (N4, Q4, T4)

title: Growing a Listeria stock
text:
Procedure

Inject 3000-4000 CFU into hosts (I just start with the vial in ~3-4mL Brain-heart infusion (BHI) media, with no antibiotic and move to step 9)
Sacrifice mice between 48 and 60 hrs post-infection
Harvest and tease apart spleen in 5ml PBS+0.1% NP40
Plate 200ml of spleen solution onto BHI+erythromycin plate [spread out sequentially to get single colonies]
Incubate for 48 hours
There should be little to no growth after 24 hours – the presence of large colonies at this time point suggests contamination.
Do not grow past 48 hours – overgrowth may occur
Harvest a single colony into 200ml of BHI+ erythromycin (in mc tube)
Take several medium-sized colonies (growth will be heterogeneous)
Grow for 4 hr with shaking 37°C (set speed higher to ensure agitation in mc tubes)
Inoculate 4ml of BHI (no antibiotic at this step) with LM-OVA from previous step
Expand with shaking until broth is mildly cloudy

Add 4ml of bacteria to 26ml of BHI broth in a 50ml Falcon tube (or 200ml flask) (depending on growth kinetics, you could set this up as an overnight)
Expand with shaking for several hours until broth is cloudy, add erythromycin for the last 45-60min of culturing (once the OD is at about 0.6) (I don’t bother with erythromycin since these are stable/do everything sterile)
Read OD: should be at 0.6 – 0.8 before moving on to step 13 (OD can be pushed a little higher; if overgrowth occurs, just add BHI and allow to re-enter log-phase of growth)
Add 15ml of the 40% glycerol stock (40% glycerol stock is 20mL glycerol in 30mL BHI; I sterile filter mine and use fresh) to the 30ml of cloudy bacteria culture
mix gently on ice and aliquot 1ml in screw top cryotubes (keep on wet ice while aliquoting) (I like my LM to be on wet ice to facilitate glycerol uptake for a bit before moving them into the -80°C freezer).
Freeze -80°C

title: Infection with Listeria
text:
Listeria production for Infection






Important



Do everything in a BSL2 TC hood.



Thaw a frozen stock from -80°C (I usually stick in a 37°C H20 bath).
Dilute 1:50 in tryptic soy broth or BHI (no more than 1 month old). For 5 ml broth, use 100μl listeria stock. Grow in 50ml conical. Do not cap conical tightly as air needs to circulate. Secure loose cap with tape. Put biohazard sticker on tube, and put a sign on the shaker as well, warning about biohazard.

Grow in bacterial shaker at 37°C until you reach OD600 of approx. 0.1 (this is mid log phase) then stick culture on ice to stop growth. Anything between .09-11 is OK.

Depending on the dilution of the frozen stock this usually takes between 1.5 and 2 hours


Use disposable plastic 1 ml cuvettes to OD bugs. Parafilm around the top of them before carrying out of the hood.
Take an aliquot of tryptic broth alone for control.


Calculate concentration of listeria. An OD600 of 0.1=2x10e8 cfu/ml. Calculate appropriate ratio. Final concentration should be 5000 cfu/mouse in 200μl. That is 2.5 x 104 pfu/ml.

\(\frac{0.1}{2*10^8} = \frac{[your OD]}{cfu}\) –> \(cfu = [your OD]*2*10^9\)
Usually should have to perform a dilution in the range of about 1:7000. Anything a lot lower or higher is probably incorrect. Since the dilution ratio is so high, perform serial dilution. Do not attempt to dilute entire 5ml of listeria.

Perform serial dilutions in sterile PBS to inject.

Example:

If OD yields concentration of 2.52 x 108 cfu/ml, do a 1:100 dilution
Take 10μl in 990μl PBS concentration now is 2.52 x 106 cfu/ml.
Take the total dilution you have to do and divide by the dilution you already did. That is the rest of the dilution you have to do.

Take 80μl of diluted stock and add to 7920μl PBS. This is the 2nd 1:100 dilution. which should result in 2.52 x 104 cfu/ml. Now you can use this to infect.







Note



Use the interactive calculator at lab.beetletun.de










Important



Bleach all tips and pipets, etc in 10% bleach before disposing as biohazard. When I do FACS staining of cells from infected mice, I flick plates into a 2 L beaker with bleach in the bottom and always use a plate with a lid (until fixed of course).

Dear Ananda and Dhruv,
We provide this detailed protocol and Listeria information sheet to labs that request Listeria mutants we have generated. We are providing you with Listeria monocytogenes expressing the internalin A S192N Y369S mutations (InlAM) that also expresses the gp33 epitope on the 10403s background strain. The InlAM is based on the work of Wollert et al., Cell, 2007. The Lm-gp33 strain was generated by Hao Shen and murinized by my lab. Please cite Sheridan et al., Immunity, 2013 when referencing the InlAM Lm in any publications. Please reach out for any clarifications or questions.
Listeria:
InlAM Lm (10403s)
InlAM Lm-gp33 (10403s)
Sincerely,

Brian S. Sheridan, Ph.D.
Associate Professor
Department of Microbiology and Immunology
Center for Infectious Diseases
Renaissance School of Medicine
Stony Brook University
246 Centers for Molecular Medicine
Stony Brook, NY 11794-5120
Phone: 631-632-4459
Email: brian.sheridan@stonybrook.edu
Listeria monocytogenes Protocol
L. monocytogenes is the causative agent of listeriosis, a food-borne disease of humans and animals. Typical human exposure occurs through ingestion of unpasteurized milk products, vegetables, or prepared meats. Listeriosis can present in healthy adults with symptoms of fever and gastroenteritis. Pregnant women and their fetuses, newborns and the immunocompromised are at great risk of developing severe infections including meningoencephalitis and septicemia that may be fatal. Infection during pregnancy can lead to fetal loss. Pregnant women or women trying to become pregnant should consult your institute’s occupational health division prior to work with this pathogen. Strains that are on the 10403s background are naturally streptomycin resistant. L. monocytogenes is susceptible to gentamicin, penicillin, and ampicillin and as such listeriosis is treated via administration of gentamicin plus penicillin or ampicillin. Lab acquired transmission could be through an aerosol exposure, a splash to the face causing ingestion or to an open wound or exposed mucous membrane, or a needle stick. No confirmed cases of lab acquired listeriosis have ever been reported. Excessively high levels of L. monocytogenes (~3x1011 cfu via consumption of contaminated food) are required for a healthy human to develop signs of gastroenteritis without any associated mortality (Dalton et al., 1997). L. monocytogenes is classified as a risk group 2 agent and is handled under BSL-2 and ABSL-2 procedures and containment.
Per IATA, we don’t consider that Listeria “is transported in a form that, when exposure to it occurs, is capable of causing permanent disability, life-threatening or fatal disease in otherwise healthy humans or animals.” In this context, an exposure constitutes “when an infectious substance is released outside of the protective packaging, resulting in physical contact with humans.” While it is not exhaustive, L. monocytogenes is also not indicated on the UN 2814 table of pathogens. As such, we ship L. monocytogenes as a UN 3373 designation.
We typically ship L. monocytogenes on Brain Heart Infusion (BHI) agar stabs/plates at room temperature. Colonies usually grow during shipment. If no colonies or growth are visible, place them in a 37°C incubator overnight and check for colonies the next day. We recommend colony purification to generate your stocks and that you confirm (via PCR) that the bacteria you requested was shipped.
• The EGDe strain L. monocytogenes internalin A mutation replaces inlA with inlAS192N-Y369S and expressed at native levels (Wollert et al., Cell, 2007).
• The 10403s strain L. monocytogenes internalin A mutation replaces inlA with inlAS192N-Y369S and made similarly (Xayarath et al., Mol Microbiol, 2009 and Sheridan et al., Immunity, 2013) • It is unknown whether these internalin A mutations make L. monocytogenes more pathogenic in humans. However, it increases the binding kinetics to human E-cad and attachment to Caco-2 cells (Wollert et al., Cell, 2007).
• L. monocytogenes strain EGDe (more pathogenic)
o No antibiotic resistance. Use standard aseptic techniques
• L. monocytogenes strain 10403s (less pathogenic; `expression of ova further reduces pathogenicity) o Naturally streptomycin resistant at 5 ∝g/mL (up to 200 ∝g/mL without impaired growth). o Ova expressing L. monocytogenes is also erythromycin resistant at 5 ∝g/mL.
▪ Ova expression is chromosomally inserted and does not require selection after confirmation.
▪ Our Lm-ova is a truncated Ova that does not express the OT-II epitope
o For quantifying bacterial burden, use plates with strept at 50 – 100 ∝g/mL.
Day -1:
• In the afternoon (or evening) inoculate 5 mL of BHI with 5 ∝L L. monocytogenes from stock aliquots • Culture L. monocytogenes ON at 37°C and 220 rpm
Day 0:
• Subculture the L. monocytogenes in the morning using a 1:10 dilution into BHI. Typically, 2 mL of ON culture into 18 mL of BHI for up to 10 mice. Depending on the size of the experiment you may need a larger culture.
• Shake at 37°C in a 50 mL conical flask at 220 rpm
• Incubate until OD600 reaches 0.8 (roughly 90 – 120 min)
• Pellet L. monocytogenes at 6000 rpm 15 min 4°C (we routinely use 4000 rpm at 15 minute in an eppendorf 5810 R centrifuge)
• 20 mL of L. monocytogenes culture at OD600 = 0.8 yields ~ 2x1010 CFU
• To generate glycerol stocks, resuspend pellet in 2 ml sterile PBS and 2 ml sterile 100% glycerol. Aliquot a few larger volumes (500 ∝l) for permanent stocks (from which future batches will be made) and smaller single use aliquots (25 ∝l) for working stocks. Stocks are maintained at -80°C.
• For i.v. infections in Balb/c or C57Bl/6: Above volumes can be adjusted as i.v. infections require a lot less L. monocytogenes. Resuspend pellet in PBS and serial dilute to appropriate titer. Different doses are reported in the literature, but we typically infect 1-2x103 CFU/mouse in 100 ∝L.
• For oral infections in Balb/c or C57Bl/6: Resuspend pellet in 0.5 mL PBS and infect with 50 ∝L (~2x109 CFU/mouse).
o Most labs gavage for oral infections. We use a feeding approach which prevents esophageal microabrasions and direct access of the bacteria to the blood stream. However, some strains or transgenics may have peculiar eating habits that may require gavage (e.g., CBy)
For Foodborne Infection Protocol
• Remove food and water from the mice cages for infections. Food and water deprive for approximately 4 hours prior to infection. The closer to the evening the better they eat. We also cover mice cages with a dark sheet during feeding, away from noise and traffic flow. It is best if a separate room is available.
• Remove 90% of bedding from infection cages to prevent mice from burying their food. You only need enough bedding to sponge urine.
• Place L. monocytogenes on small bread pieces (~0.5 cm3) in cages. The bread should be the smallest size that still absorbs the entire inoculum. Inoculate 1 piece of bread per cage for a single mouse.
• House mice individually during infection to be sure each mouse consumes a single inoculated bread piece.
• Mice fully consume inoculated bread in about 1 hr. Approximately 10% of mice take longer than 1 hr. We provide a maximum of 4 hours before marking mice which do not fully consume inoculated bread (which is very rare). This allows us to longitudinally track any mouse that did not consume a complete inoculum. Condense mice back into their original cages with their original cagemates so that social hierarchies are not disrupted.
Bug Counts (to confirm infection dose)
• Make 10-fold serial dilutions in PBS.
• Plate 10 ∝L of respective dilutions on BHI agar (with antibiotics where appropriate) using loop spreader. In this case, we have an approximate titer so you can plate the appropriate dilution +/- 1 – 2 dilutions.
Bug Counts from Tissue
• Filter sterilize 1% saponin in PBS
• Mush tissues (usually spleen, mes LN, and liver) through 70um mesh cap
• Spin at 4000rpm 15min 4°C
• Resuspend in 1% saponin: MLN in 2 ml, spleen in 3ml, and liver in 5ml
o Guts: Use gentleMACS to disassociate tissues in 9 parts PBS. After disassociation add 1 part 10% saponin (use lung 2 setting 2X)
• Incubate at least 30 - 60 min at 4°C
• Make 10-fold serial dilutions in PBS.
• Plate 10ul of respective dilutions on BHI agar (with antibiotics where appropriate) using loop spreader. Volume plated and dilution strategy may be adjusted for your needs.

title: Vaccinia Stock Production
text:
Vaccinia Stock Production


Begin with 10 – 175 cm2 flasks of confluent TK- cells. (They must be totally confluent)


Aspirate the media (DMEM) and infect each flask with 10 ml of balanced salt solution (BSS) with 0.1% BSA and 0.5-1.0x107 PFU of vaccinia virus. (Stock for the 10 ml is generally made by adding 0.5-1.0x108 PFU to 100 ml of BSS + 0.1% BSA.


Incubate for 2 hours at 37C. Rock flasks every 20 minutes.


Aspirate off BSS/0.1% BSA and virus.


Add 25-30 ml of DMEM with 7.5% fetal bovine serum.


Incubate for 48 hours. All cells should demonstrate marked CPE. If not, incubate until they do.


Collect supernatants from flasks and trypsinize (trypsin versene) any cells that still adhere. Pool cells and supernatants in two 250 ml centrifuge tubes. One wash of flasks with BSS/BSA may be needed. Pellet cells and discard the supernatant. Resuspend in 10mls of BSS/0.1% BSA.


Freeze thaw three times. Sonicate in cup horn sonicator at a setting of 5 for 2 minutes. Vortex well. Total virus yield will usually be about 1-5X1010 pfu.


Dilute in BSS/0.1% BSA to 130 ml, aliquot in 1 ml samples and freeze at –85C.


Note: When making new recombinants, take 0.5 ml of final plaque purification and add 1-1.5 ml BSS/BSA. Infect a confluent 50 cm2 flask of TK- cells for 2 hours. Incubate for 48 hours until CPE is demonstrated. Harvest and pellet virus. Resuspend in 5-6 ml of BSS/BSA. Infect one 175 cm2 flask of TK- with 5 ml of above. From the virus collected from one 175 cm2 flask you can continue with stock production (10 flasks).

title: Extraction of D…cinia Virus
text:
Extraction of DNA from Purified Vaccinia Virus
1. Measure OD260 of purified virus. (Separate protocol) 1 OD260=64ug/ml virus. DNA is equivalent to 4% of the virus mass. Therefore, 1 OD260 equals about 2.5ug DNA.
2. Suspend virus at 50-200ug DNA/ml in 50mM Tris pH 7.8 in a volume of 1.2ml.
3. Add to virus suspension:
0.1ml 1M Tris pH 7.8
0.1ml 10% SDS
0.2ml 60% sucrose (wt/vol)
0.4ml proteinase K (10mg/ml)
Incubate for 4 hours at 37C
4. Carefully extract the DNA. The DNA is very sensitive to shearing.

2X phenol (equilibrated in 50mM Tris pH 7.8)
1x phenol:chloroform (1:1)
1x chloroform

Mix gently by rolling or rocking tube. DO NOT SHAKE. Spin 10 min. at 3000 rpm between extractions. Remove aqueous phase by sucking up gently using pipet tip that has its end cut off.
5. Add Sodium Acetate (pH 7.0 to 0.1M and then 2.5 volumes of ethanol. Mix gently and leave for several hours at -20C.
6. Recover DNA by centrifugation. Wash twice in 95% ethanol and dry. Then dissolve in sterile double distilled water. Measure OD at 260 and 280.
Note: from crude stock use Rnase.
-——
The above is from our lab protocol notebook. My own changes are as follows:
Don’t bother measuring Ods. Do step 2 at 1/10 scale, for 200ul final volume (do duplicates if you’re worried this won’t give you enough DNA). Use sucrose and proteinase K powder, so that you can substitute virus stock for the volume of water they would otherwise take up. Protease K treatment is better at 50C. Extract once with 200ul phenol, once with 500ul chloroform is plenty. I add 16.5ul 3.5M NaAcetate pH 5.2. After thoroughly mixing ethanol, spin at room temperature, freezing is unnecessary. Washing once with 100% ethanol is plenty. Resuspend final DNA in 50ul TE (10mM tris, 1mM EDTA, pH 7). RNAse is not necessary. PCR with 5ul DNA in 50ul reaction volume.
The oligo sequences we use for amplification of any pSC11 insert are:
pSC11-6369 CCACCCGCTTTTTATAGTAAG
pSC11-6610-minus ACGTTGAAATGTCCCATCGAG

title: Vaccinia Titration Plaques
text:
Vaccinia Titration Plaques


Start with confluent 6-well plates of TK- cells. (Generally two 175 cm2 flasks can be plated out in eight 6 well plates for use 24 hours later)


Aspirate the media from TK- cells.


Place 250 ul of each virus dilution per well, with duplicate wells of each dilution, to ensure good counts. 10 fold dilutions are performed in 24 well plates using 1 ml total volumes. 100 ul transfer volume and then mix with a 200-1000 ul pipettor, changing tips with each dilution. Normally, 105, 106, 107 dilutions are plated. Occasionally 108 is needed.


Incubate for 2 hours, rocking every 15 min.


Overlay well with 3.0 ml of 1:1 mixture of 2X EMEM and 1.8% agar.

2X EMEM (500 ml) with
25 ml fetal calf serum
10 ml 100X glutamine
1 ml gentamycin

After 3 days, stain with 2 ml/well of 1.5% neutral red in 1:1 mixture of 2X EMEM and 1.8% agar.


Stain for 6 hours or overnight and count plaques. Remember to include a multiplication factor of 4 because you initially infected with 250 ul of virus.

title: Electroporation of activated CD8
text:
Electroporation of primary activated CD8 T cells
Coat Plates for activation
For goat anti-hamster coated plates

Prepare Antibody-Coated Plate (Start 2+ hrs before plating)
Preparing a 1:30 dilution of Goat Anti-Hamster IgG antibody in sterile PBS.
Coat wells by adding 550 µL of the diluted GAH-IgG solution to each required well of a 6-well round-bottom plate.
Gently tap the plate to ensure the bottom of each well is fully coated.
Place the plate in a 37°C incubator for at least 2 hours (or overnight at 4°C).

Spleen/lymph node harvest and homogenization

Grab spleen and lymph nodes (inguinal, brachial, and axilliary, avoid mLN if you can) and put in a tube with R10
Prepare Single-Cell Suspension by washing spleen/lymph nodes over a 70 uM filter in a petri dish
When spleen in homogenized, place 70 um filter over 50 ml conical
Wash filter by washing the petri dish 2x with 1 ml of RP5
Wash cells 1x at 1600 RPM for 4 min
Dump and add 1 ml ACK lysis and incubate for 4 min
Add 40 ml MACS buffer and spin at 1600 RPM for 4 min
Prepare Biotinylated Antibody Cocktail. The volumes below are per sample (adjust as needed based on cell number, typically for up to  total cells).







Antibody Target






Cell Type Marked for Depletion






Example Volume










NK1.1






NK cells






3 µL








MHC Class II






APCs (B cells, Monos, DCs)






3 µL








CD4






Helper T cells






3 µL








B220 (CD45R)






B cells






3 µL








Ter119






Erythroid lineage cells






3 µL








Ly-6G/Ly-6C (Gr-1)






Granulocytes (Neutrophils)






3 µL








MACS buffer








600 µL







Note: This cocktail targets major non-CD8+ T cell populations. Adjust cocktail based on specific experimental needs or available antibodies.

Negative Selection Staining & Bead Incubation

Resuspend the cell pellet in 500 µL of the freshly prepared Biotinylated Antibody Cocktail (adjust volume based on cell number if necessary, typically ~100 µL per 10^7 cells).
Incubate for 15 minutes at 4°C (in the fridge), protected from light.
Fill the tube with MACS buffer (~10-14 mL). Centrifuge at ~400 x g for 4 minutes. Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 500 µL MACS Buffer. Add 50 µL of streptavidin magnetic beads.
Incubate for 15 minutes at 4°C, protected from light.
Fill the tube with MACS buffer. Centrifuge at ~400 x g for 4 minutes. Discard the supernatant. During centrifuge step, wash MACS column (e.g. LS column) in the magnet by rinsing with 3 ml of MACS buffer. Discard flow through. Don’t let filter dry so add more if needed during centrifuge step.
Resuspend the pellet in 500 µL MACS buffer.





Magnetic Column Separation

Apply the cell suspension onto the column.
Collect the unlabeled cells that pass through the column. This fraction contains the enriched, untouched CD8+ T cells.
Wash the column three times (3x) with 3 mL of MACS buffer each time. Collect these washes and combine them with the initial flow-through.
Centrifuge the collected flow-through at 1600 RPM for 4 minutes. Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the purified CD8+ T cell pellet in a small volume (e.g., 500 µL) of R10. Count the cells using a hemocytometer or automated counter. Determine cell viability (e.g., using Trypan Blue).
Stop here and check CD8 T cell purity by flow (pre and post isolation)

We had 89% purity post isolation of CD8 T cells and 44e6 cells total. Resuspend to 2e6 cells/ml. Plate 1 ml.

Run flow to check purity (can assume 90-95% if in a hurry but always better to flow check)
Stain aliquot of cells with FITC-CD8b (1:100)
Wash 1x with FACS and run on flow.






Cell Plating and Activation

Retrieve the GAH-IgG or anti-CD3 coated plate from the incubator. Carefully aspirate the coating solution from the wells.
Wash each well twice with 1 mL of R10 to remove any residual unbound antibody. Aspirate thoroughly after the final wash.
Dilute anti-CD3 and anti-CD28 antibodies each 1:500 in R10 for GAH-IgG coated wells. Dilute anti-CD28 for the anti-CD3 plate coated wells at 1:250 so there will be 1 ug/ml anti-CD28 in final well.
Add 1 ml of the CD8 T cell suspension (containing cells) to each prepared well.
Add 1 ml of the anti-CD3/CD28 antibody (or just anti-CD28) mixture to each well containing cells (total volume per well = 2 mL). Gently pipette up and down or swirl the plate to mix.

Final concentration: 1 x 106 cells/mL
Final antibody dilution: 1:1000 (effective concentration depends on stock)

Place the plate in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator for 18-24 hours.

CRISPR/Cas9 knock out in primary T cells via electroporation

To make a Cas9/RNA complex, mix guides plus tracr RNA as below in PCR tubes:

gRNA thy1 guide only control
gRNA thy1 guide plus guide of 1st target (Dand5)
gRNA thy1 guide plus guide of 2nd target (Sulf2)

3uL tracr RNA (Alt-R® CRISPR-Cas9 tracrRNA, ATTO™ 550)

Make cytokine mixes

1x buffer recipe, make enough for each rxn:

Take supernatant from the cell pellet using pipets (make sure to take off all remaining liquid from cell pellet to not dilute out the small reaction volume of 25 μl). Resuspend cell pellet in 20μl P3 buffer per reaction.

For cells in culture, split the cells over the original number of cells they were into (e.g., if three wells were originally pooled to do CRISPR on, then split them back into the original 3 wells) for culture

sgThy1 2: 1.62e6 cells total

TGFb stock: 0.2 mg/ml so dilute 1:20,000 total or 1:200 then add 10 ul per ml to get to 10 ng/ml.

Spin at 2000 RPM for 5 min and collect supernatant by pipetting off sup avoiding cells and save at -80 for ELISA.
Collect cells for flow, PCR of genomic DNA for Sanger sequencing validation of knockout, and for RNA extraction -> cDNA synthesis for qPCR validation of knockout.

text:

MRC 11/2019 v1.0
Materials

Neon Electroporator
Electroporation pipette
100 ul kit (tips + R buffer + E buffer)
Recombinant Cas 9 (6.5mg/ml; QB3 Berkley Lab, 39 pmol/uL)
Synthetic RNA (Synthego, ready to use)
Cell of interest

Before
Check if conditions have been previously optimized: https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cell-culture/transfection/neon-transfection-system/neon-transfection-system-cell-line-data.html
If not yet described – Use Optimization protocol and use GFP/Ametrine plasmid in your cells of interest. It highly depends of cell type. Try the 24 protocols and assess for efficiency and survival.
Amount of Reagents
For each electroporation sample, the amount of plasmid DNA/siRNA, cell number, and volume of plating medium per well are listed in the table below. Be sure to use Resuspension Buffer T for primary suspension blood cells and Resuspension Buffer R of all other cell types.

Preparing Cells and RNP mix

Cultivate the required number of cells (see table below for cell amount) such that the cells are 70–90% confluent on the day of the experiment.
Rehydrate the sgRNA stock like this: 3 nmol of sgRNA powder plus 30 ul TE buffer. This will give you a 100 uM (100 pmol/ul) sgRNA stock solution (store at -80C).
Dilute sgRNA like this: 6 ul of 100 uM sgRNA stock plus 14 ul nuclease-free water.
Prepare plates by filling the wells with the appropriate volume of culture medium containing serum and supplements without antibiotics as described in the table below and pre-incubate plates at 37°C in a humidified 5% CO2 incubator.
Prepare this mix:



1.3 ul of diluted sgRNA guide (30 uM)
1 ul TrueCut Cas9 6 uM or 1 ul
12.4 ul Buffer R Incubate this mix for 20 minutes at RT



During those 20 min, prepare a suspension with your cells (50,000-150000 cells, depending on your cells (10 to 20 million cells/ml) in an Eppendorf, and prepare electroporator.
Wash cells once with PBS1x and once with Buffer R.
Resuspend the pellet in 10/100 ul of the CRISPR/Cas9 MIX
Proceed to Electroporation

Electroporation

Fill the NeonTube with 3 mL Electrolytic Buffer (use Buffer E for 10 μL NeonTip and Buffer E2 for 100 μL NeonTip).
Insert the NeonTube into the NeonPipette Station until you hear a click sound (Figure 1).
Transfer the appropriate amount of plasmid DNA/siRNA into a sterile, 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add cells to the tube containing plasmid DNA/siRNA and gently mix. See the table on back side for cell number, DNA/siRNA amount, and plating volumes to use.
Press the push-button on the NeonPipette to the second stop to open the clamp and insert the top-head of the NeonPipette into the NeonTip until the clamp fully picks up the mounting stem of the piston. Gently release the push-button, continuing to apply a downward pressure on the pipette, ensuring that the tip is sealed onto the pipette without any gaps (Figure 2A and B).
Press the push-button on the NeonPipette to the first stop and immerse the NeonTip into the cell-DNA/siRNA mixture. Slowly release the push-button on the pipette to aspirate the cell-DNA/siRNA mixture into the NeonTip.


Note: Avoid air bubbles during pipetting as air bubbles cause arcing during electroporation. If you notice air bubbles in the tip, discard the sample and carefully aspirate fresh sample into the tip again without any air bubbles.


Insert the NeonPipette with the sample vertically into the NeonTube placed in the NeonPipette Station until you hear a click sound.
Ensure that you have selected the appropriate electroporation protocol and press Start on the touchscreen (Figure 5).
The Neondevice automatically checks for the proper insertion of the NeonTube and NeonPipette before delivering the electric pulse.
The touchscreen displays Complete to indicate that the electroporation is complete.
Remove the NeonPipette from the NeonPipette Station and immediately transfer the samples from the NeonTip by pressing the push-button on the pipette to the first stop into the prepared culture plate containing prewarm medium with serum and supplements but without antibiotics (Figure 6).


Discard the NeonTip into an appropriate biological hazardous waste container.


Repeat Steps 5–11 for the remaining samples.


Change the NeonTips after using it twice and NeonTubes after 10 usages. Use a new NeonTip and NeonTube for each new plasmid DNA/siRNA or cell type.


Gently rock the plate to assure even distribution of the cells. Incubate the plate at 37°C in a humidified CO2 incubator.
If you are not using the Neondevice, turn the power switch on the rear to OFF.
Assay samples to determine the transfection efficiency (e.g., fluorescence microscopy or functional assay) or gene knockdown (for siRNA).
Based on your initial results, you may need to optimize the electroporation parameters for your cell type. Refer to the manual for using the 18-well or preprogrammed, 24-well optimization protocol on the Neondevice.

Checking the cleavage efficiency

Resuspend the pellet in 20 ul of 1x ThermoPol (New England BioLabs B9004S) in an eppendorf. Lyse at 95C for 10 min.
Cool the lysate at 4C (in ice) during 5 min.
Add 2.5 ul of Proteinase K 20 mg/ml and incubate at 55 C for 1 hr.
Inactivate proteinase K incubating 15 min at 95C.
Cool the lysate at 4C (in ice) for at least 5 min.
Use the AmpliTaq Gold 360 master mix kit from Life Technologies (REF 43988881, -20C, CRISPR box) to set up the PCR with the designed primers for each CRISPR.

Mix
AmpliGold 2x 25 ul
sgDNA 2 ul
Primers (10 uM F/R) 1 ul
DDW 22 ul
Program:
1. 95C 10 min
2. 95C 30 sec
3. 56C 30 sec
4. 72C 60 sec/per kb (30 sec for an amplicon of 500 bp)
Go 4 to 2, 40 cycles
5. 72C, 7 min
6. 4C, forever

Run 5 ul in a gel. You should see one single band at around 500 bp.
Use the GeneArt Genomic Cleavage Detection kit (Life Technologies Cat A24372) to digest your PCR product:
Combine in 2 different 8-well strip tubes (one will – and the other will be +)

Mix
PCR product 3 ul
10x Detection Reaction Buffer
1 ul DDW 5 ul
Program:
1. 95C 5 min
2. 95C-85C -2C/ sec
3. 85C-25C -0.1C/sec
4. 4C, forever

Following the completion of the re-annealing, proceed to enzyme digestion or store the reaction at -20C. Add 1 ul of Detection Enzyme to the test sample (+), mix well. Add 1 ul of DDW to the test sample (-), mix well.
Incubate at 37C for 1 hr.
Vortex briefly and spin down.
Place at 4C.
Immediately load the entire 10 ul on a 2% gel.

title: Lab Protocols
text:
This is my private collection of lab protocols.
Most of them are from by time as a postdoc at the Goldrath Lab

title: Lab Protocols
text:
Sections
I have tried to organize the protocols in different sections. Sometimes an assignment is not clearly possible. If looking for a protocol, the search function in the top right corner is very useful.

 T cells
This sections contains protocols that mainly deal with T cells (e.g. CD8 selection, CD3/CD28 T cell activation)


 Infections
Here you’ll find protocol for LCMV and Listeria infection as well as protocols to make retrovirus.


 Mice
Everything you need to know about lymphocyte isolation from mouse tissues.


 Molecular Biology
Classic protocols for RNA Isolation, cDNA Synthesis, PCRs and Western
RNA_cDNA_qPCR | RNA | cDNA | qPCR


 Crsipr Design and Cloning
Collected cloning protocols and related source documents moved into the new top-level folder.


 General Cloning
General cloning workflows and supporting protocols that are organized separately from the CRISPR design and cloning collection.


 Histology
Histology, FFPE, OCT, and tissue-processing protocols.


 FACS
Flow cytometry staining, acquisition, antibody titration, and analysis protocols.


 Human Samples
Human PBMC, TIL, tumor-sample processing, and ex vivo stimulation protocols.


 Mitochondria
Calcium flux, Seahorse, mitochondria dye, and related metabolic assay protocols.


 CRISPR-Cas9 Electroporation
Lonza, Neon, and MaxCyte electroporation protocols.


 Transfection
Plat-E, HEK293T, lentivirus production, polybrene, and Retronectin protocols.


 Perturb-seq
Perturb-seq planning guides and sgRNA viral transduction resources.


 Bioinformatics
What’s there to say? The name is self-explanatory. This sections is also known as dry lab.


 Recipes
Potions tutorial and cell media recipes.


 Organizational
How do I book flow time? How do I sort? Where can I find a database of all antibodies.


 Giovanni’s Protocols


 Old Goldrath Protocols


 Top 20 Work in progress


 Contribute
Get involved and learn how to add protocols or correct mistakes. This section also includes a list of shortcodes.

title: RNP_Electroporation_Protocol_GoldrathLab
text:
Cas9 RNP Electroporation Protocol (Seki and Rutt, JEM, 2018)_v2.4
Generated by Katia Faliti
Modified by Jinyong Choi
Re-Modified by Tianda Deng*
*Note: I chose to leave in some components (colored gray) that aren’t necessarily relevant to us now, but could potentially be utilized in the future. So if you’re confused by things that don’t really pertain to you, don’t worry.
Materials

Spleen + I.Ns C57BL/6 mouse.
For activated CD4 T cells:
0.5 x 106 cells/ml
8 ug/ml anti-CD3 (clone l45-2c11, BD)
8 ug/ml anti-CD28 (clone 37.51)
Pre-activation for 2 days before transfection.
For resting CD4 T cells:
Preincubated with 2 ng/ ml rhlL-7 for 24h before transfection.
crRNA and tracrRNA from IDT:
Alt-R CRISPR-Cas9 TracrRNA
Alt-R CRISPR-Cas9 TracrRNA-ATTO 550
(ATTO 550: a fluorochrome excited by yellow laser, PE channel)
Alt-R CRISPR-Cas9 crRNA NTC negative control
Cas9 Protein
IDT Cas9 v3 (10 mg/ml) or
TrueCut Cas9 Protein v2 (5 mg/ml; Invitrogen) or
Cas9 (6.4 mg/ml; QB3 Berkley Lab) *We use this one, it is greatly discounted for UCs.
Neon Transfection System
Neon Transfection System 100uL Kit

Catalog #: MPK10096
*Crispr Guide Design

I use CHOPCHOP for guide design: https://chopchop.cbu.uib.no/ because I think it’s simple to use, there are many alternatives (just google “crispr guide generator”)
When ordering crRNA from IDT, you can check your guides again on their website
Make sure to order crRNA and NOT sgRNA. To learn the difference on more on RNPs, this is a great resource: https://www.idtdna.com/pages/education/decoded/article/crispr-guide-rna-format-affects-genome-editing-outcomes

(Optional if you start from IVT) Preparation of In Vitro Transcription
A 0.3 uM target oligonucleotide mix working solution was prepared by diluting l uL of each target oligonucleotide stock solution (10 uM) in 32 uL nuclease free water.
Use GeneArt Precision gRNA Synthesis kit:
PCR reaction in 25 uL in the following order:

12.5 uL Phusion HF PCR Master Mix 2X
1 uL Tracr Fragment + T7 Primer Mix
1 uL 0.3 uM Target F1/R1 oligonucleotide mix
10.5 uL nuclease-free water

PCR cycles:

Denaturation 98 °C, 10 sec
Denaturation 32 cycles at 98 °C, 5 sec
Annealing at 55 °C, 15 sec
Extension at 72 °C, I min

Purify the PCR products from agarose gel.
16-24 ng for PCR product was used in the IVT reaction (MegaShortScripts T7 Kit), following the instruction.
Incubation at 37 °C for 4 h.
Add 1 uL of Turbo DNAse to the reaction to remove DNA template. Incubate 37 °C for 15 min.
sgRNA was purified using the GeneArt precision kit and eluted in 40 uL RNAse-free water.
(D0)
Isolation SM CD4 T cells and stimulation
Activate with anti-CD3 and anti-CD28 (We have an activation protocol on the server)
*I personally like using 6 well plates for activation and seed between 1-2x106 cells/well.
(D2)
Preparation of crRNA-tracrRNA duplex
To prepare the duplex, each Alt-R crRNA and Alt-R tracrRNA or Alt-tracrRNA-ATTO550 were reconstituted to 100 uM with Nuclease Free Duplex buffer (IDT).
100 μM = 100 pmol/uL = 10 nmol/100 uL = 2 nmol/20 uL
*If you order 10 nmols from IDT, this means resuspend with 100 uL of NF Duplex Buffer (IDT)
Mix oligos at equimolar concentrations in a sterile PCR tube (e.g. 3 uL Alt-R crRNA + 3 uL Alt-R-tracrRNA).
Annealing oligos by heating at 95C for 5 min in a PCR machine, then cool down at RT at least 1 h.
After duplexing, the concentration of crRNA-tracrRNA duplex in solution is now 50 uM (50 pmol/uL).
Precomplexing of Cas9 / RNP
TrueCut Cas9 Protein v2 concentration: 5 mg/mL (1 ug = 6.1 pmol; 30.5 pmol / uL)
IDT Cas9 Protein v2 concentration: 10 mg/mL (1 ug = 6.1 pmol; 61 pmol / uL)
QB3 Berkley Lab Cas9 Protein: 6.4 mg/mL (1 ug = 6.1 pmol; 39 pmol / uL)
Mix gRNA and Cas9 at ~3:1 molar ratio
In a PCR strip, mix 4.8 uL crRNA-tracrRNA duplexes (240 pmol) and 2.0 uL QB3 Cas9 (80 pmol) by gentle pipetting up and down and incubated RT for at least 20 min. Now total 6.8 uL mixture generated per reaction.
*During this 20 minute incubation is typical when I start prepping the activated cells for Electroporation
or
In a PCR strip, mix 4.8 uL crRNA-tracrRNA duplexes (240 pmol) and 1.3 uL IDT Cas9 v3 (80 pmol) by gentle pipetting up and down and incubated RT for at least 10 min. Now total 6.1 uL mixture generated per reaction.
Note: Check the amount of crRNA, tracrRNA and Cas9 protein mixture before the reaction *(meaning make sure you have enough volume).
~2.4 uL crRNA, ~2.4 uL tracrRNA, and ~2.0 uL Cas9 protein are needed per reaction.
For Electroporation with Neon Transfection System

Harvest activated cells and count cell number
Wash with sterile PBS twice: it’s important to remove as much serum as possible since it could interfere with the electroporation
Resuspend cells @ 2x106 cells / 110 uL “R Buffer” (from Neon Kit)


*I have also resuspended at 1.5x106 cells and it worked as well


Aliquot 6.8 uL of RNP mixture into sterile Eppendorf tubes
Carefully add 110 uL of cells (now in R buffer) into each Eppendorf: do not introduce bubbles or you will regret it
Mix carefully with pipette (NO BUBBLES) then incubate the cells and RNP mixture for 3-5 mins
Very carefully fill the Neon Pipette with the cell/RNP mixture without introducing any bubbles!
Electroporate with following settings:

Voltage: 1600
Width: 10 ms
Pulses: 3
*If there are bubbles in the pipette tip during the electroporation, the bubbles will spark and kill off A LOT of cells. Observe the tip as you start the electroporation and if you see a spark, expect dead cells.

After electroporation, transfer the cells into 2mL of TCM + hIL2 in a 6 well plate and move to 37C incubator.

For Electroporation with MaxCyte ATX

Aliquot 57 uL of complete media/well in 24 well plate.
Wash cells with electroporation buffer (Hyclone) once and resuspend the cells at 4 x 107 cells / mL in electroporation buffer.
Aliquot 50 uL of cells into Eppendorf tubes (2 x 106 cells / rxn)
Add 6.8 uL RNP into the cells and mix well. Now total approx. 57 uL.
Transfer the cells/RNP mixture to cuvette (OC-100).
Electroporation with Expended-5 protocol
After electroporation, transfer the cells into 57 uL media in 24 well, and incubate for 20 min in 37C incubator.
Add 1 mL of R10 + BME + NEAA + 10 ng/mL IL-2.

For Electroporation with 4D-Nucleofector Core Unit: Lonza, AAF-1002B

Aliquot 35 uL of complete media/well in 24 well plate.
Prepare 25 uL / rxn P4 buffer + Supplement 1 (20.4 uL + 4.6 uL)
1 x 106 murine T cells resuspended into 23.5 or 22.2 uL or 21 uL of P4 buffer (Primary Cell 4D-Nuclcofector X Kit S (32 RCT, V4XP-4032; Lonza)).
Mix T cells with 11.5 or 12.8 uL or 14 uLRNP in round bottom 96 well and incubate for 2 min at RT. Now total 35 uL
Transfer the cells+RNP mix to Nucleofection cuvette strips (4D-Nuclcofector X Kit S; Lonza)
Electroporate the cells the 4D-Nucleofector.
Pulse for activated murine T cells: CM137
Pulse for resting murine T cells: DS 137
After electroporation, transfer the cells into 35 uL media in 24 well plate, and incubate for 20 min in 37C incubator.
Add 1 mL of R10 + BME + NEAA + 10 ng/mL IL-2.

(D3)
Transfection efficiency & Transfer

Check transfection efficiency ATTO 550 fluorescence (PE channel) by flow 1-3 day after transfection
Prep cells for in vivo transfer

I use tide to calculate the Knockout efficiency. http://shinyapps.datacurators.nl/tide/ The site advises to to sequence a stretch of DNA ~700bp enclosing the designed editing site. This region upstream of the break site is used to align the sequencing data of the test sample with that of the control sample.

CD4-BV510, L/D-eF780, crRNA-ATTO 550 (PE channel of LSRII-2 and Fortessa), and Ab for target protein

title: CB6.CRISPRCas9 KO
text:
CRISPR/Cas9 knock out in primary T cells and in vivo transfer

Materials


Lonza 4D-NucleofectorTM System (near Xenium)
P3 primary cell 4D Nucleofector electroporation kit (Lonza, Cat# V4XP-3032 for electroporation wells, Cat# V4SP-4032 for cuvettes) (under Nicole’s bench at RT)
P3 buffer: make fresh on the day, mix 3.6 μl reagent 1 with 16.4 μl diluent per reaction (Lonza Nucleofector kit) *Though Lonza tech support said it’s good for a month in 4’C. (inside Nicole’s bucket at 4ºC)
Recombinant Cas9 protein, 40uM, @ -80ºC (middle shelf, rightmost rack, Cas9 Box, 10 µL aliquots)
20bp gRNAs+80mer scaffold with chemical modification
R10 (RPMI + 10% FCS, glutamine, antibiotics, 50 nM BME, NEAA, HEPES)

Enrich CD8+ T cells – naïve or activated

If naïve, do CD8 enrichment prior to protocol
If activated, activate 24hr prior to this protocol.

CRISPR/Cas9 electroporation

To make a Cas9/RNA complex, mix guides plus tracr RNA as below in PCR tubes:

gRNA thy1 guide only control
gRNA thy1 guide plus guide of 1st target
gRNA thy1 guide plus guide of 2nd target
etc.




want to do 3:1 molar ratio of guide RNA to Cas9 enzyme.
Thy1 AC guide at 100uM concentration.
Experimental guides are at 100uM concentration.
Set up as follows:

Control

3uL thy1 AC crRNA guide from IDT (Box ‘Nicole’ at -20ºC)
3uL tracr RNA (Alt-R® CRISPR-Cas9 tracrRNA, ATTO™ 550) (Box ‘Nicole’ at -20ºC)

Experimental (x number of groups needed)

1.5uL thy1 AC crRNA guide from IDT



1.5uL guide of experimental guide (Alt-R CRISPR-Cas9 crRNA from IDT)
3uL tracr RNA (Alt-R® CRISPR-Cas9 tracrRNA, ATTO™ 550)





Incubate in PCR machine at 95’C for 5 minutes, then immediately remove at put at RT in the dark for 1 hour for annealing.
Add 1.9uL 40uM Cas9 enzyme to each tube (-80’, middle shelf, middle rack). DO NOT MIX. Gently flick the tube to mix sgRNAs with Cas9 and spin down briefly to collect drops from the sides of the tube. Incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature for complex formation.
Turn on Lonza 4D-NucleofectorTM System: select wells, pulse code (see below) and solution (P3 primary).
Make a P3 buffer mix below per reaction and keep at room temperature.

1x buffer recipe, make enough for each rxn:

Supplement 1: 3.6uL
P3: 16.4uL


Take 10mL of R10 plus 50U/ml hIL2 (a 1:2000 dilution), and put into a waterbath to warm to 37deg.
Count cells, then spin down cells in large volume (use 50 mL conical) of STERILE, RT PBS to remove potential RNase contamination from FCS containing media before electroporation (IMPORTANT). Can do 2-10x10^6 cells per reaction.
Immediately after complex formation, transfer cells into Eppendorf tubes in 1 ml of PBS, and spin down on a tabletop centrifuge at 5000 RPM for 5min room temperature). It is important to prepare everything before resuspending the cells in P3 buffer to minimize the time that cells are exposed to the buffer.
Take supernatant from the cell pellet using pipets (make sure to take off all remaining liquid from cell pellet to not dilute out the small reaction volume of 25 μl). Resuspend cell pellet in 20μl P3 buffer per reaction
Transfer 5 μl of CRISPR/Cas9 RNP into the 20 μl P3 buffer with cells and mix gently.
Transfer the 25 μl cell/RNP mix to the bottom hole of a well of the Lonza nucleofector strip. Be careful to not create any bubbles. (keep time of cells in P3 buffer as short as possible as it is cytotoxic to the cells).
Electroporate cells by putting the nucleofector strip into the Lonza nucleofector and as depicted, start the program

Naïve CD8 T cells: use DN100 program in P3 buffer
Activated CD8 T cells: use DS137 program in P3 buffer

After electroporation (a few seconds) add 130 μl of 37°C pre-warmed R10 media into the well containing electroporated cells and rest cells for 10 minutes in the incubator (5% CO2, 37°C).
In the meantime, prepare a 6-MW plates with R10 and IL-2 at 15 U/mL
Dilute 1:3.33 the leftover R10 + IL-2 (50 U/mL) from step 6: 600 µL of R10+IL-2 with 1400 µL of R10 plain (final 15 U/mL)
After the 10-minute incubation is done split the cells over the original number of cells they were into (e.g., if three wells were originally pooled to do CRISPR on, then split them back into the original 3 wells)
Incubate for overnight/24 hrs

title: Jurkat electroporation
text:
Jurkat Electroporation with Lonza Electroporator

Place 1.5 mls of antibiotic free R10 in each well of a 12 well plate (one for each cuvette sample) and equilibrate at 37C for 15-30 min.
Collect Jurkats from 6 T75 flasks and place into 2 50 ml conicals. Take aliquots to count cells.

Cell count: 1.3e6, 80 mls. 104 million cells (2 tubes total), 97% viability

Aliquot number of cells needed (10 million cells per sample (n=7)) 70 million.
Spin at 100xg for 10 min.
During Jurkat centrifugation, take out plasmids from -20C. *IMPORTANT NOTE: plasmid solution added should not exceed 10% of reaction volume, 100 ul in this case so can only add 10 ul of plasmid max.

Pmaxgfp = positive control, use 2 ug per solution (4 ul)
MF12 (plasmid + BirA + GFP) = 2.05 ug/ul
5 ug = 2.44 ul of MF12
10 ug = 4.88 ul of MF12
20 ug = 9.75 ul of MF12
MF15 (plasmid + BirA + GFP + Fcgr2b) = 2.48 ug/ul
5 ug = 2.01 ul of MF15
10 ug = 4.02 ul of MF15
20 ug = 8.04 ul of MF15

During centrifugation, make nucleofector solution. Add 82 ul of nucleofector solution V and 18 ul of supplement 1 for each sample. _7_ samples = (82 * 7) = 574 ul of nucleofector solution V. _7_ samples = (18 * 7) = 126 ul of supplement 1.
Aspirate all of supernatant (very important to get all of supernat)
Resuspend in # of samples * 100 ul (700 ul) room temp nucleofector solution (nucleofector solution V + supplement 1 at a 4.5 to 1 ratio)
Aliquot 100 ul into different tubes and add respective plasmid
Add solution to cuvette slowly, making sure there are no air bubbles in cuvette and that the media gets to the bottom of the cuvette. Tap lightly if necessary.
Clean off metal panels on cuvette with a chemwipe.
Run Jurkat high viability protocol on the electroporator. It is fast, but I swear it does electroporate!
Return to hood and slowly add 500 ul of prewarmed antibiotic free media from 37C
Use supplied Pasteur pipette to take all the solution out. Be careful not to pipette up and down. Just slowly draw the solution out of the cuvette and into the 12 well plate.
Repeat for each sample *IMPORTANT NOTE: nucleofector solution is toxic to cells so cells will die as time progresses (no more than 15 min) so batch samples accordingly.
Swirl plate gently and incubate at 37C overnight.

Transfection validation

Take plate and transfer media to tubes
Spin cells down, dump supernatant.
Add pool left in tube to wells in a 96 well plates
Wash 1x with FACS.
Resuspend cells in 50uL of master mix in FACS wash.
Incubate at 4C for 20 minutes.
Wash cells 1x with FACS wash.
Repeat but wash with PBS instead of FACS.
Make up L/D Blue solution by diluting 1:1000 of the stock to stain with 100uL per sample in PBS
10 samples= 1mL PBS, add 1uL L/D stock.
For the comp, use 1 drop Arcs+ beads, 100uL PBS, and 1uL L/D stock. Let stain for 20-30min.
Resuspend in 100uL L/D solution.
Incubate in dark at 4C for 25min.
Add 100uL FACS buffer to cells and spin down and flick plate.
Wash 1X with FACS.

title: growing sphingomonas and pneumococcus
text: S. pneumoniae URF918 cultured in Todd-Hewitt broth (BD) at 37 °C in an incubator at 5% CO2 were collected at a mid-log phase and then washed twice in PBS. For induction of pulmonary infection, mice were anesthetized with isoflurane and restrained on a small board. Mice were inoculated with S. pneumoniae (1 × 106 to 1 × 107 colony-forming units in a volume of 50 μl per mouse) by insertion of a 24-gauge catheter into the trachea. For induction of systemic infection, S. pneumoniae (1 × 107 colony-forming units) were injected intravenously into mice. At 6 h (spleen) spleen cells were collected and CD19− cells positive for the α-GalCer-loaded CD1d tetramer were analyzed immediately after isolation for intracellular cytokines without restimulation or pretreatment with brefeldin. Bacteria is plated at 100 μl on 5% (vol/vol) sheep blood Mueller-Hinton agar plates and cultured for 18 h, followed by colony counting.

*Keep everything on ice*
