title: Generation of V… CV-1 Cells
text:
Generation of Vaccinia Recombinants in CV-1 Cells

Start with a confluent T-25 flask of CV-1 cells. Figure about 5 x 106. These cells are grown in DMEM with FCS, Splitting requires trypsin (1X concentration) with no special considerations. The cells grow somewhat slowly, so during heavy usage, 1:5 splits are appropriate. However, the cells can be reseeded quite sparsely for maintenance.
Wash the cells 1X with DPBS. Infect the cells with normal WR vaccinia virus (CR19) at 0.05 pfu/cell or 2.5x105 pfu total in BSS/BSA. Incubate at 37C/9% CO2 for 2 hours rocking every 15-20 min. Note: I use 1ul of CR19, with titer ~1x108pfu/ml.
30 min. before the end of infection, start transfection of DNA. We used to use Cellphect kit by Pharmacia, but I find that Lipofectamine 2000 or Fugene works about 5-10 X better. For LF2000, we use about 5ul miniprep DNA, 6ul LF2000. Note: Centrifuge the (nonsterile) DNA minipreps at high speed for 1 min. to pellet any infectious contaminants prior to pipetting.
Aspirate off virus and add 3.5ml DMEM +7.5% FCS plus 3.5ul gentamycin (1:1000) (optional)
Add the DNA/lipofectamine and incubate for 48 hours.
Harvest the cells by trypsinization with versene. Pellet cells by centrifugation. Resusp. in 0.5 ml BSS/BSA and freeze thaw (dry ice/37C water bath) three times. Sonicate for 2 min. in a cup horn sonicator at maximal intensity. Store at –80C. Follow with three plaque purifications.

title: Listeria production-KPC
text:
Listeria production for Infection
Do everything in a BSL2 TC hood.

Thaw a frozen stock from -80oC- 2nd shelf, 1st rack. (I usually stick in a 37 degree H20 bath).
Dilute 1:50 in tryptic soy broth (no more than 1 month old). For 5 ml broth, use 100ul listeria stock.
Grow in 50ml conical. Do not cap conical tightly as air needs to circulate. Secure loose cap with tape. Put biohazard sticker on tube, and put a sign on the shaker as well, warning about biohazard.
Grow in bacterial shaker at 37 oC until you reach OD600 of approx. 0.1 (this is mid log phase) then stick culture on ice to stop growth. Anything between .09-.11 is OK.

At a 1:50 dilution of the frozen stock this usually takes between 1.5 and 2.5 hours.
Use disposable plastic 1 ml cuvettes to OD bugs. Parafilm around the top of them before carrying out of the hood.
Take an aliquot of tryptic broth alone for control.

Calculate concentration of listeria. An OD600 of 0.1=2x10e8 cfu/ml. Calculate appropriate ratio. Final concentration should be 5000 cfu/mouse in 200ul. That is 2.5 x 10^4 pfu/ml.


0.1 / 2x10e8 cfe = your O.D / cfe
Usually should have to perform a dilution in the range of about 1:7000. Anything a lot lower or higher is probably incorrect. Since the dilution ratio is so high, perform serial dilution. Do not attempt to dilute entire 5ml of listeria.


Perform serial dilutions in sterile PBS to inject.

If OD yields concentration of 2.52 x 10^8 cfu/ml, do a 1:100 dilution.

Take 10ul in 990ul RPMI- concentration now is 2.52 x 10^6 cfu/ml

Then from diluted stock, do 1:100 dilution again.

Take the total dilution you have to do and divide by the dilution you already did. That is the rest of the dilution you have to do. Take 80ul of diluted stock and add to 7920ul RPMI. This is the 2nd 1:100 dilution, which should result in 2.52 x 10^4 cfu/ml. Now you can use this to infect.


5000 cfu iv for B6 mice (for balbs the typical dose is 2000). Peak CD8 response for primary is day 7. I often got about 8-13% of CD8s in the spleen responding by tetramer or IFNg.
Bleach all tips and pipets, etc in 10% bleach before disposing as biohazard. When I do FACS staining of cells from infected mice, I flick plates into a 2 L beaker with bleach in the bottom and always use a plate with a lid (until fixed of course). I know this is overkill compared to Bevan Lab procedures, but there’s always someone pregnant around here!

text:
Listeria production:
Ok, here’s the instructions from Phil on making freezes of Listeria
(this is how I make what I sent you):
Hope the cells got to you fine. I asked Ingrid, our lab manager, about
Freezing Listeria, and basically what you want to do is take what the saturated
frozen cultures that you have currently, and inoculate a large BHI culture to grow for
during the day (e.g., 200 ul into 100 ml) until it reaches a log phase OD 600 of ~0.2.
Then just freeze them directly in the BHI in aliquots (we do 1 ml aliquots). You can then take those and thaw them anytime to grow another culture to OD 0.1 to infect mice (I put 200 ul into 5 ml BHI, it takes about 2.5 hrs to get to OD 0.1). Hope this helps.
Here are instructions for growing Listeria:
Thaw a frozen stock (I usually stick in a 37 degree H20 bath). Dilute
1:50 in tryptic soy broth (no more than 1 month old). I usually make
10-20 mls. Grow at 37 until an OD600 of approx. 0.1 (this is mid log
phase) then stick culture on ice to stop growth. At a 1:50 dilution of
the frozen this usually takes between 1.5 and 2.5 hours. An OD600 of
0.1=2x10e8 cfu/ml. Perform serial dilutions in sterile PBS to inject
5000 cfu iv for B6 mice (for balbs the typical dose is 2000). Peak CD8
response for primary is day 7 I think. I often got about 8-13% of CD8s
in the spleen responding by tetramer or IFNg.
I do everything is in a BSL2 TC hood. Use disposable plastic 1 ml
cuvettes to OD bugs and I parafilm around the top of them. Bleach all
tips and pipets, etc in 10% bleach before disposing as biohazard. When

L beaker with bleach in the bottom and always use a plate with a lid
(until fixed of course). I know this is overkill compared to Bevan Lab
procedures, but there’s always someone pregnant around here!
<This protocol is from Max 2021>
Procedure
Growing a stock
Growing a Listeria stock
This is a protocol that I got from Maurice, Nicholas J (nmaurice@fredhutch.org) for the Lm-OVA variants (N4, Q4, T4)
Our former technician, who was a bit eccentric, wrote this (and it isn’t formatted for the N4/Q4/T4, which are chromosomally integrated) I’ll note where our practices differ in red:
Procedure

Inject 3000-4000 CFU into hosts (I just start with the vial in ~3-4mL Brain-heart infusion (BHI) media, with no antibiotic and move to step 9)
Sacrifice mice between 48 and 60 hrs post-infection
Harvest and tease apart spleen in 5ml PBS+0.1% NP40
Plate 200ml of spleen solution onto BHI+erythromycin plate [spread out sequentially to get single colonies]
Incubate for 48 hours


There should be little to no growth after 24 hours – the presence of large colonies at this time point suggests contamination.
Do not grow past 48 hours – overgrowth may occur

�. Harvest a single colony into 200ml of BHI+ erythromycin (in mc tube) Take several medium-sized colonies (growth will be heterogeneous)
7. Grow for 4 hr with shaking 37C (set speed higher to ensure agitation in mc tubes) �. Inoculate 4ml of BHI (no antibiotic at this step) with LM-OVA from previous step

Expand with shaking until broth is mildly cloudy
Add 4ml of bacteria to 26ml of BHI broth in a 50ml Falcon tube (or 200ml flask) (depending on growth kinetics, you could set this up as an overnight)
Expand with shaking for several hours until broth is cloudy, add erythromycin for the last 45-60min of culturing (once the OD is at about 0.6) (I don’t bother with erythromycin since these are stable/do everything sterile)
Read OD: should be at 0.6 – 0.8 before moving on to step 12 (OD can be pushed a little higher; if overgrowth occurs, just add BHI and allow to re-enter log-phase of growth)
Add 15ml of the 40% glyercol stock (40% glycerol stock is 20mL glycerol in 30mL BHI; I sterile filter mine and use fresh) to the 30ml of cloudy bacteria culture
mix gently on ice and aliquot 1ml in screw top cryotubes (keep on wet ice while aliquoting) (I like my LM to be on wet ice to facilitate glycerol uptake for a bit before moving them into the -80°C freezer).
Freeze -80C

title: Caspase 3_7&7AAD ex vivo staining
text:
Caspase 3/7 & 7AAD Staining
Staining prep

Transfer the cells and supernatant to flow tubes
Wash wells 1x with media.
Combine samples for controls.
Spin down at 1200rpm for 5min.
Resuspend in 200uL and transfer into a 96 well round bottom plate for staining.
Spin plate down at 1200rpm for 5 min. Flick.

Surface staining for surface panel

CD4-PB (1:100)
CD14/19- BV510 (1:200)
Thy1.1- BV711 (1:100)
PD-1- BV786 (1:200)
CD8- PE (1:100)
FCGRIIB/STREP-APC (1:200)
CD44- APC-Cy7 (1:300)
Leave FITC and PerCP open for caspase and 7AAD

Caspase/7AAD staining
*As caspase/7AAD stain does not get washed out, cells continue to stain even after the incubation. Therefore, make sure all your comps and experiment are set up on the cytometer so you can directly run your samples. If this is not possible, incubate the samples in caspase and 7AAD stain in shifts (e.g. one tissue type at a time) as staining will continue and your last samples will be more stained than the first run ones. This is a technical difference and you could mistake it for biological.

Thaw caspase reagent.
Resuspend wells in 50 ul of counting beads and move to FACS tubes.
Make sure heat block is at correct temp. Heat block positive controls for 5 min at 95C.
Make 1:1000 stock solution of caspase (1 ul per 1 ml of FACS) and add 50 ul into sample (1:2000 final dilution—I promise!) Add to all samples except FMO.
When positive controls/comps are done on the heat block, add 50 ul of caspase solution and incubate tubes at 37C for 20 min.
Make 7AAD solution (1:500 dilution) and add 100 ul of 7AAD into 100 ul of solution caspase+cells, making a final dilution of 1:1000.
Let incubate for 5 min in drawer in dark at RT. Then go to flow!

title: TCR signaling phospho-flow
text:
Phospho-flow of TCR signaling
Day -1
Coat Plate

Make a 5 ug/ml anti-CD3 solution and 2 ug/ml anti-CD28
Add 50 ul of PBS to 96 well flat bottom plate and incubate overnight at 4C

Day 0
Cell Stimulation

Transfer cells after isolation or culture from well to 50 ml conical vials and wash well 2x with media by spinning cells 1500 RPM for 5 min
Dump media and resuspend wells in serum-starved media.
Make conditions of interest such as protein that induces cell death, promotes proliferation, etc. Use PBS or buffer as a control.
Plate 2e6 cells to uncoated wells for unstim controls and then to anti-CD3/28 coated wells (+/- protein of interest) for 5, 10, 15, 30 min stim. Ideal to have different plates if you can to not disrupt the other time frames.
Incubate at 37C for 5, 10, 15, 30 minutes
With each timepoint, aspirate cells, wash well 1x with 100 ul FACS and put into 96 U bottom wells

Samples

Starved media unstim controls
5 ug/ml CD3, 2 ug/ml anti-CD28 in starved media



Phospho-protein controls: pERK isotype, pSLP76 isotype, pZap70 isotype, pS6 isotype
Whole protein controls: ERK, SLP76, S6, ZAP70

MeOH Fix/perm for phospho-flow (Byron Au-Yeung lab)

Wash 1x with FACS
Aspirate all FACS and resuspend in 4% paraformaldehyde
Fix cells for 10 min with 4% paraformaldehyde (150 ul) in the dark at 4C or on ice.
Spin down and wash cells 1x with FACS and aspirate sup
Perform surface staining
Wash 1x with FACS
Add 40 ul of ice cold 90% MeOH (kept in freezer, diluted with water) dropwise, vortex (repeat 3x)
Incubate on ice for 30 min
Wash with FACS, spin, aspirate.
Rehydrate with 50 ul of FACS for 15-20 min
Wash with FACS, spin, and aspirate.
Stain with intracellular master mix for 30 min at 4C.
Wash 2x with FACS
Flow

title: pSTAT5 Protocol
text:
Download the original PDF

AD060409 pSTAT5 Protocol
Ananda Goldrath Laboratory Andrew/Mark pSTAT5 Protocol Protocol from BD adapted/optimized for 96 well plates by MPR, written up/also used successfully by ALD. BD Phosflow lyse/fix buffer Cat#558049 BD Phosflow Perm buffer III Cat#558050 (stored at RT in brown bottles). BD PE antiStat5 pY694 Cat#612567 (comes very diluted…make sure you have ~6ul for each sample)
Treat cells in 96 well plate in ~100ul volume (need room for fix buffer, do not exceed 125ul if in V bottom plate on ice. Mix well with multichannel. Make sure you have unstimulated cells as controls.
Place in 37 degree water bath on top of rack to ensure rapid transition to 37 deg temp. Careful to have water level just right so plate does not flood. After seeing MPR data, I decided on 25 min for IL2/15 treatment of PyMT TIL. You can tilt the plate slightly as you put in down to avoid air bubbles under your cell containing wells. Other times may work better or worse for your application. Mark used the 37 TC incubator instead of the water bath for all 37 steps.
At 25 min, remove from water bath, set on paper towel to dry, and add 1:1 amount of 2X lyse/f ix buffer. This is made by adding 1.5mls of water to 1ml of 5X lyse/fix concentrate (scale volumes up or down accordingly for the number of cells you have). Use multichannel and pipette up and down several times gently to mix. Media will change from red to yellowish. (Example, if you had 100ul of cells, add 100ul of lyse/fix)
Put back in 37 degree water bath for 10 minutes.
Remove plate, dry bottom by setting on paper towels, and spin down 500xg (~2000RPM in our centrifuge) for 8 min.
Flick off super and resuspend in 250ul of RT PBS (no ca2+/Mg2+)
Pellet as before.
Flick off super and resuspend in 100ul of 1X Perm Buffer III. This seems to be alcohol based, so transfer quickly before it drips out of the end of the tips (b/c of vapor pressure?) Let sit on ice for 30 min.
Pellet, flick of super, and resuspend in 250ul FACS buffer (PBS/BGS/azide). Repeat and flick off super again.
Resuspend in FACS buffer plus Abs.
Resuspend cells in 30ul (to conserve antibodies). I used the following mix: 19ul CD8aFITC (1/60 dilution) 110ul pStat5 PE (1/10) 10ul CD4 PerCP (clone GK1.5) (1/110) 19ul CD44APC (1/60) in 950ul FACS buffer. Looking at the results, I believe you could use 1/2 the CD44 (or use at ~1/100), but keep the FITC high at ~1/50) Stain 30‐60 min at RT in dark. Wash as usual and run samples.
Note that not all antibodies work on fixed cells, and those that do in general have to be used at a higher concentration than on live cells. There are some web resources for antibodies that have been successfully used on cells fixed in this manner, for example:
www.bdbiosciences.com/docs/Validated_Cell_Surface_Markers.xls
June 4, 2009

Classify the antigens.

Define a gating strategy.

Assess reagent availability.

title: GFP:YFP Filters
text:
The filter setup depends on your particular machine and how the lasers/filters are set up inside.
there are some examples of setup you can look at online
http://www.cyto.purdue.edu/hmarchiv/Current/1356.htm
use a 510/21BP  plus the 505LP dichroic in the FITC channel plus a
550/30 BP with a 525LP dichroic in the PE channel. The 525LP replaces
the usual 550LP.
http://www.cyto.purdue.edu/hmarchiv/Current/1355.htm
            LP          BP
YFP          525LP             530/30
GFP          502LP             510/20
http://www.cyto.purdue.edu/hmarchiv/Current/1354.htm
 For YFP 550/30BP with the 525LP en for GFP 510/20BP with (or without)
the 505LP.
Most likely you won’t have those filters at your core and I suggest buying it from Omega Filters https://www.omegafilters.com,  they cost about $200 each. Since they are a jack-of-all-trades mirror maker, make sure you order the right size for the FACS machine. 
Goldrath Lab specifications:
525DRLP and 510DF21 from Omega Filters were fitted on Aria and LSRII, Fortessa
These three machines are set up differently because of the laser configuration,
For LSRII, GFP takes place of FITC and YFP takes place of PERCP5.5.  I used 510/21+502LP for GFP and 530/30+525LP for YFP. (Monica Macal/Louise knows how to change it)
For Fortessa, GFP takes place of FITC and YFP takes place of PE.  I used 510/21+502LP for GFP and 525/30+525LP for YFP. There are pictures of filter configuration posted on the side wall. (Martin/Kyla/Louise knows how to change it)
For Aria, it is the same as Fortessa. There are also pictures of filter configuration on the side of the filter panel. (The pictures made by Karen is pretty self-explainable)
(note 530/30, 525/30 , and 535/30 are pretty much interchangeable here, 510/20 is interchangeable with 510/21, 502LP is interchangeable with 505LP, depending on the current filters you have)
If you have any problem figuring out the filters setup, ask somebody with extensive knowledge of the laser/filters, or just BD support technician(in person).
Compensation for FACS analysis
The key thing is to get really bright controls for GFP/YFP singles. Also, try to keep the voltages of both GFP and YFP the same, otherwise the signal will bleed too much, Start with 500 V each. Also the same compensation can be used again and again unless things are looking funny.

title: FC2.surface_staining
text:
02/08/2023
Protocol for surface staining for flow cytometry
NB: many chemokine receptors recycle continuously through early endosomes , so if you freeze the endocytic pathway you can only address the fraction that is on the surface. If you stain at RT (or even 37°C) you can hit a much larger fraction, and get better signal. It is important to titrate your antibodies under the conditions you will be staining during experiments.
Materials

Live/Dead Fixable Viability Kit
ArC Amine Reactive Compensation Beads (Life Technology)
ArC Amine Reactive Negative Beads (Life Technology)
Compbeads Anti-mouse Ig K (BD) or UltraComp eBeads (eBioscience)
Sterile FACS washing buffer (1X PBS -/- supplemented with 2% FBS or 1X HBSS -/- supplemented with 2% FBS )
Fix solution: formaline (FA) 1% in HBSS-/- or in PBS 1X-/-
Antibodies
Sample

Protocol

wash the sample with 2mL (20 X Vstaining) of HBSS-/- o 1X PBS-/- (in order to eliminate FBS or BSA that can bind Live/Dead)
centrifuge 4 minutes at 1600 rpm at RT
aspirate the supernatant
make Live/Dead mix for 4 samples of around 10 million cells each (add 1 uL Live/Dead in 19 uL H2O; then add 380 uL PBS-/-)
add 50 uL of Live/Dead mix to each sample and 50 µL of Fc Block (ready to use solution) and incubate for 15 minutes RT in the dark
wash the sample with 2 mL of FACS buffer
centrifuge 4 minutes at 1600 rpm at RT
aspirate the supernatant
make the Ab mix in FACS buffer
add 100 uL of Ab mix to each sample and incubate for 20 minutes 4°C in the dark.
wash the sample with 2 mL of FACS buffer
centrifuge 4 minutes at 1600 rpm at RT
aspirate the supernatant
fix the sample with 150 uL of Fixation Buffer (BioLegend – brown bottle)
incubate 10 minutes at 4°C
wash the sample with 2 mL of FACS buffer
centrifuge 4 minutes at 1600 rpm at RT
aspirate the supernatant
resuspend the sample with 200 uL of FACS washing buffer
keep the sample at 4°C until the acquisition

Fluorescence compensation
Compensation controls are required for each fluorochrome and should contain both a positive and a negative population. Be sure to use specific beads: for mouse anti-Human antibodies use Compbeads Anti-mouse Ig K (BD), for rat anti-Human antibodies use UltraComp eBeads (eBioscience). For some antibodies it is recommended to use cells for compensation.

Gently vortex beads
Put 30 uL of beads and add the 1 µL of the antibody in a FACS tube. For the negative control: put beads alone.
For Live/Dead positive: 2 drops of ArC Amine Reactive Compensation Beads + 2,5 uL of Live/Dead. For Live/Dead negative: 2 drops of ArC Amine Reactive Negative Beads. NB: at the end of incubation, do not fix neither wash the Live/Dead comps!
Incubation for 20 minutes at RT in the dark
wash the tube with 2 mL of FACS buffer
fix the sample with 150 uL of Fixation Buffer (BioLegend – brown bottle)
incubate 10 minutes at 4°C
wash the sample with 2 mL of FACS buffer
centrifuge 4 minutes at 1600 rpm at RT
aspirate the supernatant
resuspend the sample with 200 uL of FACS washing buffer
keep the sample at 4°C until the acquisition

title: 012725 NES - Flow cytometry staining
text:
Flow cytometry staining techniques
Nicole Scharping February 2025
Flow cytometry is an extremely useful technique that can provide you with a LOT of data at once, but it can be complicated. This is a straightforward set of protocols to stain and run samples fairly easily.
Table 1




Analyzer


Lasers


Colors available


Software






BD Fortessa



Blue (488)  Red (621)  Violet (405)


Yellow-green (561)




FITC/488/NBD/BODIPY/GFP/YFP PerCP-Cy5.5 APC/AxF647/660/MitoDR, APC-Cy7, AxF700


Pac Blue/BV421/V450, BV510/Ametrine, BV605, BV650, BV711, BV786


PE/RFP/Cherry, PE-594/MitoOr, PE-Cy7



FACSDiva




Recipes for FAC buffer (for analysis)

500 mL 1X PBS
2% (10 mL) FBS
1:1000 Sodium azide

Basic surface staining (includes Alternative Protocol: Fixation)

Aliquot your cells in a 96-well round or V bottom plate
Add 20-50uL FC block into wells with cells in media, put on ice for minimum 10min (longer is ok)
During the FC block, make up your staining cocktail in FACS Buffer (1XPBS + 2% FCS), make enough for 100uL per well.
Spin the plate down at 2000rpm for 1 min
Flick off the supernatant into the sink. Some like to use a vacuum and suck the individual supernatants off, I never found much utility in this.
Aliquot 100uL into each well as appropriate (you can use a multichannel if there’s a lot of samples). Resuspend up and down with a multichannel pipet. DO NOT reuse tips for multiple rows
Incubate on ice in the dark for 15 minutes.
Add 180 uL of FACS buffer to each well and spin down (this is a wash step).
Resuspend in 100 uL of FACS buffer and move to FACS tubes.
Make single color controls with beads (see protocol below)
Analyze on flow cytometer.


Alternate Protocol: Fixation
If you cannot run the samples immediately (remember, they are still live cells), you can fix them. Paraformaldehyde (4% made up in PBS) is the most common fixation method for flow cytometry. It is fast and works very well, while still preserving cellular structure. Some antigens are lost with PFA fixation.


After the wash step (step 8) spin, resuspend cells instead in 100 uL of 4% PFA in PBS. Incubate at room temperature in the dark for 20 minutes.
Add 180 uL of FACS and spin down.
Resuspend pellet in 100 uL of FACS buffer. Seal the plate with Parafilm around the outside, wrap in foil, and store at 4 deg for up to 7 days (could last longer)
Make single color controls with beads (see protocol below)

Cytoplasmic intracellular staining I (for cytoplasmic proteins)
includes Alternate Protocol: Intracellular Cytokine Staining)
For most intracellular (but non-nuclear) proteins, this protocol will suffice to stain fairly well. As always, though, this is heavily antibody dependent.

Surface stain the cells as normal.
After the wash step, spin down cells at 2000 rpm for 1 min.
First, resuspend cells instead in 100 uL of 4% PFA in PBS. Incubate at room temperature in the dark for 20 minutes. (This step helps preserve certain surface stains like Tim3, as well as ametrine expression in transduced cells)
Add 180 uL of FACS and spin down.
Resuspend cells in 100 uL BD CytoFix/CytoPerm, kept at 4 deg in a brown bottle.
Incubate at RT for 20 min.
Add 180 uL of BD PermWash (10X solution kept at 4 deg in a clear bottle, dilute into ddH20).
Spin down and flick off.
During the spin, make up a staining solution as you would for surface staining (100 uL/well), but make it up in BD PermWash rather than FACS buffer.
Resuspend cells in 100uL of staining solution per well and incubate at RT in the dark for 30 minutes.
Wash with 180 uL of PermWash and spin down.
Resuspend in 100 uL FACS buffer and move to FACS tubes.
Run on analyzers or parafilm the plate, wrap in foil, and store at 4 deg for up to 7 days.
Make single color controls with beads (see protocol below)

Alternate Protocol II: Intracellular cytokine staining
This protocol is used to detect the frequency of cytokine producing cells in a mixed culture, as well as the amount of cytokine produced (by MFI). Cytokines are measured by first stimulating the cells in the presence of a protein transport inhibitor (usually brefeldin A or monensin, which collapse the Golgi or late ER, respectively), then doing cytoplasmic staining using anti-cytokine antibodies. For some cytokines, like TNFa, IL-2, IL-17, and IFN-g, these assays work beautifully. For other cytokines, such as IL-4, -5, -10, and -13, the effects are much less so, relying on shifts of MFI rather than a large shift of cytokine positive cells. Stimulation times, protein transport inhibitor choices, and stimulation type for each of these cytokine should be determined empirically.

Harvest and stimulate your cells

Peptide mix

Plate cells in 96 well round bottom plate, spin down at 2000 RPM for 1 minute
Add 200uL T cell media per well with cells (there must be some APCs in the mix somewhere, purified T cells would not be able to use this method) in the presence 1:500 peptide (GP33 aliquots in Goldrath TC freezer) and 1:500 Protein Transport Inhibitor (mixture of brefeldin A and monensin)
Resuspend using multichannel
Stim for 4hr at 37deg (in incubator)


Surface stain your cells according to Basic Protocol.
Fix/perm the cells and stain your cytokine by the intracellular cytoplasmic protocol.
Resuspend in FACS buffer and analyze, or store at 4 deg in the dark for up to 3 days.
Make single color controls with beads (see protocol below)

Nuclear intracellular staining
This protocol allows for identification of cells based on their expression of transcription factors and other nuclear proteins. The staining reagents used to accomplish this, however, are very harsh, and can dramatically changing forward/side scatter profiles and potentially hiding some antigens. In addition, fluorescent proteins used in reporter constructs will leech out, deadening their signal. Including a 4% PFA fix before the nuclear fix helps decrease this effect.

Stain cells as in Basic Surface staining protocol.
After the wash step, spin down at 2000rpm for 1 minute.
First, resuspend cells instead in 100 uL of 4% PFA in PBS. Incubate at room temperature in the dark for 20 minutes. (This step helps preserve certain surface stains like Tim3, as well as ametrine expression in transduced cells)
Add 180 uL of FACS and spin down.
During the spin, dilute 1 part eBioscience Fix/Perm Concentrate into 3 parts Fix/Perm Diluent. Make enough for 100 uL per well.
Resuspend cells in 100uL of Fix/Perm and incubate 20 min at RT in the dark.
During the incubation, make up your nuclear stain (in the Perm Buffer), enough for 100uL per well.
After 20min, for the wash, add 180 uL of eBioscience 1x Perm buffer (diluted to 1x ddH2O) and spin down.
Resuspend cells in 100 uL staining buffer and incubate for 30 m RT in the dark.
Add 180 uL of Perm buffer and spin down.
Resuspend in 100 uL FACS buffer and move to tubes.
Analyze immediately or parafilm seal, wrap in foil, and store for 3-5 d at 4 deg.
Make single color controls with beads (see protocol below)

Single color controls
For single color controls, I use OneComp eBeads™ Compensation Beads. The beads include positive and negative population for each sample, as only ~half of the beads bind antibody (therefore the other half is your negative control). This only works for using antibodies from mouse or rat sources (rabbit antibodies or dyes do not work here). For flow on the Fortessa X20, something like FITC vs A488 are interchangeable. On a spectral cytometer, this would not be the case.

Vortex beads, then add one drop per tube. Make enough tubes for each fluorophore ‘color’ you have. If you have a reporter or dye than cannot be used as beads, still make a tube for these colors.
Add 1uL of antibody for the appropriate single color per tube. For tubes representing reporter or dye, pick an antibody with a fluorophore that would be read out in the same channel and add to tube. Vortex to mix.
Let single color control tubes sit in the dark at RT for at least 10min.
After incubation, add 200uL FACS buffer per tube. THERE IS NO WASH STEP. Samples are now ready to run.

title: Cloning with HIFI DNA Assembly_KL
text:
Cloning with HIFI DNA Assembly

The principle behind HIFI DNA Assembly is the joining of DNA fragments with ends that share the same sequence (15 – 40bp). There are several good animations on Youtube.
Prep your sequences of interest: plasmid prep or g-blocks (resuspended at 25 ng/µL)
If using two plasmids, design primers with overhangs using Snapgene. BE CAREFUL, primers used in the same reaction need to have the same Tm WITHOUT the overhangs. In other words, the difference of Tm between the primers (without the overhangs) has to be max 5C. Use the NEB Tm calculator to calculate the Tm and not Snapgene if you are using the Q5 NEB Master mix for the PCR.
Run the PCR based on the Q5 master mix protocol BUT

-use 1min/kb for the elongation phase
-run the PCR at the Tm of the primers WITHOUT the overhangs

Optional: Add 1ul of DPNI to destroy the substrate for the reaction (because it is methylated). MIX well, incubate at room temperature for 5 min and then at 37C for 60 minutes. (Of note: DPN1 will work in the Q5 PCR buffer or cutsmart buffer. It doesn’t work in water)
Run the product in a gel and isolate the band that corresponds to the right band size. Let the gel run AS LONG AS POSSIBLE to avoid contamination of your band with residual template DNA. Elute with water preferably (to avoid problems with the downstream reaction).
Combine the DNA for the HIFI DNA Assembly reaction. 1:1 vector to insert for a total reaction of 50ng. You don’t have to use 10ul of the Assembly as long as it is 1x (I usually use 5ul of DNA and 5ul of HIFI). Have a mock reaction as a control that you add water instead of HIFI DNA Assembly
Transform two sets of bacteria, one with 2ul of the reaction product and one with 2ul of the DNA from the mock reaction
Next day you should see colonies in the plate with the product and no colonies in the other plate (in reality the majority of the time we see some colonies on the control due to leftover template but the experimental usually has 10x more colonies).
Midi prep a few colonies. Design primers to sequence the new vectors. Send them for sequencing to Genewitz. ALWAYS do this because there are frequent mutations that occur

title: Protocol for CRISPR amplicon sequencing 2025-11-06 (etr_PxVJqvYTzT) Custom_low_plex_LsgA_cloning_MRC
text:
Custom CRISPR Cas9 screens in the LsgA backbone
using Illumina-compatible libraries
Miguel Reina-Campos – Goldrath Lab
07/13/2022
Objective: Clone ~150 sgRNAs covering 50 genes (~3x sgRNAs/gene) in the LsgA vector for customizable screening pools in CD8 T cells

Order OligoPools

Forward library: 5’ Phospho-CACCNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN
Reverse library: 5’ Phospho-AAACNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN


Annealed oligos will look like this:
5’ Phospho-CACCNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN
NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNCAAA-5’ Phospho
*The 5’ Phosphate will allow ligation to occur using dephosphorylated BbsI-linearized LsgA vector.
Design your sgRNA sequences and upload to IDT to order oPools Oligo Pools
Order two different pools of single-stranded DNA oligos, Forward library and Reverse library.
Price: 10 pmol/oligo, 120 sgRNA sequences.
Each sequence is 24 nts * 120 = 2880 nts total, charged at oPools DNA Base 1 ($109 / pool) + $1.65 * 120 = $109 per pool and $198 for 5’ phosphorylation for a total of $307 per pool.


Vector Preparation: LsgA library vector



Digest and dephosphorylate 20 ug of vector with BbsI for 1h at 37C. Set up the following reaction:

100 ul reaction

10X rCutSmart Buffer 10 uL
LsgA vector (20 ug)
HF-BbsI (NEB) 3 uL
Alkaline Phosphatase Quick CIP (NEB) 5 uL
Water Fill to 100 uL

Run in a 0.8 % Agarose TAE Gel using wide combs
Purify linearized dephosphorylated oligo using QIAGEN Gel purification kit
Resuspend in ~40 ul of ddH2O

sgRNA oligo annealing

IDT oligopools come as a dried DNA pellet with 10 pmols of each oligo.
Resuspension in 100 ul of ddH2O generates 1 uM stock for each oligo. For a 155 oligo-pool, this makes a ~150 uM ssDNA.

Anneal sgRNA ssODN:

1 uL Forward library (Final concentration of each oligo ~100 nM)
1 uL Reverse library (Final concentration of each oligo ~100 nM)
1 uL 10X T4 Ligation Buffer (NEB)
7 uL ddH2O

Put the phosphorylation/annealing reaction in a thermocycler using the following parameters:


37oC 30 min
95oC 5 min
ramp down to 25oC at 6oC/min
keep at RT


Ligation

1:1 ligation ratios
Vector is 7Kb while oligos are 24 nts, which makes the vector ~300x bigger than the insert.
Include a “No insert negative control”
25 ng of 7kb dsDNA vector in 10 ul reaction makes for a ~550 pM

Dilute annealed library 1:200 (100 nM to 500 pM)
Set up ligation reaction in a total volume of 10 ul


Dephosphorylated BbsI-linearized LsgA vector backbone 25 ng (550 pM)
1:200 Annealed sgRNA library 1 uL
10X Ligase buffer 1 uL
ddH2O Fill to 10 uL


Test Transformation

A series of test transformations will be performed to verify correct inserts and successful ligations with low background. Two serial transformations will be performed, as a single transformation of the ligation product generates many mixed peaks during Sanger sequencing of colony PCR product.

Primary transformation with high efficiency chemically competent cells (Stbl3 cells).



Add 0.5uL ligation to 20 uL Stellar cells, and gently tap to mix.
Incubate on ice for 30 minutes.
Heat-shock 45s @ 42oC.
Incubate on ice for 2 min.
Add 300 uL pre-warmed SOC and incubate for 1 hour at 37oC.
Plate 200 uL on pre-warmed plates (save the remaining recovery at RT or 4C).
Incubate O/N at 37oC.
*Set up as many plates as needed - test transformation to obtain ~1k to 4k colonies per plate.
*Limit culture time to ~16h to prevent colonies from overgrowing

Got ~5k colonies per plate on the first try, with ~200 colonies in the vector-only plate (negative control). Vector only might self-religate in the absence of an insert (~50 to 200 colonies is normal background).

Plasmid prep: If your negative control shows <5% background colonies, it is safe to proceed.
Scrape plates with 1.5 mL of LB and purify plasmid and prepare midi-prep. This is the plasmid library prep used for large-scale transformation, although it could be also used for the screen - subsequent steps are needed for verification of equal sgRNA representation.
Secondary transformation with subcloning efficiency in Stbl3 cells.



Add 1ul of the prepared plasmid to 15-20uL of DH5a and gently tap to mix.
Incubate on ice for 2 minutes
Heat-shock 30s @ 42oC
Incubate on ice for 2 min
Add 980 uL SOC
Plate 1/50x (~20uL) in 6 different plates for each sample.
Plate 6 plates per
Incubate O/N at 37oC

Pick as many colonies from each plate as needed. The rule of thumb is to pick one colony for every 5 sgRNAs (~20%, ie 30 colonies for 155 sgRNas) – make minipreps and sequence using hU6. This QC makes sure the ration of the un-inserted religated vector is low, and that inserts are correctly cloned in the vector

Align the Sanger sequence output to the library vector map in your favorite cloning software (e.g. SnapGene) to ensure the sgRNAs were cloned properly
The 19 to 20bp corresponding to the unique protospacer sequence should not align it the vector. Search for this sequence in the list of sgRNAs in your oligo pool. If 70-90% of the sequences match to the correct library (you will likely see some oligo synthesis errors and sequencing errors), it is safe to proceed with the large-scale transformation.

*No sequences should perfectly align to the library vector at the protospacer region. This would indicate that the parental vector was incompletely digested and the stuffer sequence is present in the library.
**It is also extremely unlikely that any sgRNA appears multiple times in a random set of 10 colonies. Repeated sequences are an indication that one species from the oligo pool is very overrepresented.

Large Scale Transformation

If the test transformation worked, use the plasmid library prep from step 5c. to transform Stbl3 bacteria following this protocol:

Pre-warm LB/carbenecillin plates 3-4 hours ahead of time.
Thaw Stbl3 cells on ice
Add 10 ng plasmid to 50 uL Stbl3 cells
Heat shock at 42 C for 30 seconds
Leave on ice for 2 minutes
Add 950 uL of SOC media
Incubate at 37 C for one hour
Plate 10X LB Agar Carbenicillin plates



Scrape Plates

Add 15-25 mL LB for the initial scrape. Transfer to a clean collection tube. Add an additional 5-15 mL LB and transfer to collection tube. If you are scraping multiple plates, place your collection tube on ice. Once you are finished scraping, spin at 4,000 rpm for 20 min. The pellet should be tight. Pour off media and freeze pellet or proceed with plasmid preparation.

Plasmid Preparation

Qiagen or Sigma midi, maxi, mega or giga plasmid prep kits. Make sure columns are dry prior to the final elution. Wet columns will give a low recovery.

9) Prepare Samples for Illumina Sequencing

Illumina sequencing of the resulting plasmids is advised to ensure the resulting plasmid libraries from this protocol are correct, have a large fraction of sgRNAs that match perfectly to the expected library, and the relative fractions of each sgRNA are tightly distributed. You only need ~100 sequencing reads per sgRNA in the library to be able to validate the library (ex. 12K reads), so you can include your samples as a <5% spike- in other sequencing runs.
To sequence your libraries, follow Step 3 of the sequencing sample prep protocol with the following modifications:

If you are spiking into a sequencing sample with high diversity, such as an RNA-seq experiment, you can omit the Set A/B strategy and just sequence with Set A primer pairs and sequencing primer
For the PCR, perform one 100uL PCR per library. If you have cloned multiple sublibraries, PCR each individually with a different sample index to allow you to detect any cross-contamination or sample mix-ups (although be careful to not introduce this during the PCR!).
Substitute the genomic DNA input into the PCR with 100ng library plasmid.
Only perform 15 cycles of PCR.

Amplicon sequence:
TTCGATTTCTTGGCTTTATATATCTTGTGGAAAGGACGAAANNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNGTTTTAGAGCTAGAAATAGCAAGTTAAAATAAGGCTAGTCCGTTATCAACTTGAAAAAGTGGCACCGAGTCGGTGCTTTTTTGAATTC 3’

These primers are first used to amplify plasmid-coded amplicon from genomic DNA. IMPORTANT: These primers will amplify a 96 bp from the LsgA, and a 1962 bp from the LMG (containing the sgFdft1). Purify lower band by gel if necessary to clean.

LsgA_amplicon_F: 5’TTTCTTGGCTTTATATATCT 3’
LsgA_amplicon_R: 5’GACTAGCCTTATTTTAACTT 3’

PCR
Q5 2X
Vt=50
Touchdown PCR: 10 cycles starting at 61 C in -0.5 C delta
Everything else standard for Q5 protocol
Followed by 25 cycles at Ta 56
Extension times 7 sec
Purified with Qiaquick PCR purification kit

PCR for amplification of the plasmid region with addition of Nextera Handles (P5, P7 tags)

Nextera-Handle-F (P5tag):
5 ‘ TCGTCGGCAGCGTCAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAGTTTCTTGGCTTTATATATCT 3’
Nextera-Handle-R (P7tag):
5 ‘ GTCTCGTGGGCTCGGAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAGGACTAGCCTTATTTTAACTT 3’
This will amplify a 163 PCR product.
Use 2X Q5 high fidelity DNA polymerase protocol with 20 cycles.
Amplicon:
5’ to 3’
TCGTCGGCAGCGTCAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAGTTTCTTGGCTTTATATATCTTGTGGAAAGGACGAAANNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNGTTTTAGAGCTAGAAATAGCAAGTTAAAATAAGGCTAGTCCTGTCTCTTATACACATCTCCGAGCCCACGAGAC

Purify PCR product with AMPure XP beads 2X ratio and perform Indexing PCR:

(https://teichlab.github.io/scg_lib_structs/methods_html/Illumina.html)
Use Q5 2X polymerase
Vt=50 ul
16 cycles, TA = 58 C, extension 10 seconds
After PCR, AMPure XP purification with 2X beads ratio
Indices were taken from illumina-adapter-sequences_1000000002694-00.pdf
Sample 1 example
F501 (i5-index-handle): AATGATACGGCGACCACCGAGATCTACACTAGATCGCTCGTCGGCAGCGTC
R701 (i7-index-handle): CAAGCAGAAGACGGCATACGAGATTCGCCTTAGTCTCGTGGGCTCGG
This will generate a 232 bp PCR amplicon (F501 R701 index example):
AATGATACGGCGACCACCGAGATCTACACTAGATCGCTCGTCGGCAGCGTCAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAG’TTTCTTGGCTTTATATATCTTGTGGAAAGGACGAAANNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNGTTTTAGAGCTAGAAATAGCAAGTTAAAATAAGGCTAGTCCTGTCTCTTATACACATCTCCGAGCCCACGAGACTAAGGCGAATCTCGTATGCCGTCTTCTGCTTG
Green: i5, i7
Black: index,
blue: handle P5 and P7 Nextera,
yellow: internal primer used for genomic amplification,
purple: sgRNA sequence
‘: starts reading read 1.
Sequencing math:

10K cell outputs should provide a 64X sgRNA coverage
Every cell should have only one copy of the sgRNA -> 10K sgRNAs
500 reads per sgRNA * 10K sgRNAs = 5M reads per sample
Some samples have 100K, to 230K cells
19 samples * 5M = 95M 300 M minimum
For sequencing read length: the sgRNA sequence starts at 69 nts from the i5 index, and 106 nts from the beginning of the DNA fragment.

Miseq Reagent Kit v3 (https://www.illumina.com/systems/sequencing-platforms/miseq/specifications.html)
Experimental Setup LCMV infection Model


Enrich and in vitro activate P14 Cas9-eGFP donor cells (SOP)


Transduce (SOP)



LsgA pool + LMG-Cd19 -> Cd19-pool


LsgA pool + LMG-Fdft1 -> Fdft1KO-pool

Transfer sorted P14 cells into B6 recipients and infect with LCMV (SOP)


Bleed at day 7 pi to check proportions of TE and TMP for proper expansion


Take Down at day 14 pi, and sort 10K Ame+ GFPhigh P14 from

text:
Retroviral transduction of CD8+ T cells

Have virus ready or start making virus following our protocol at day -1.
Day 1 (4-5pm). Anti-CD3/anti-CD28 stimulation
Purify CD8s by negative selection – Follow our protocol
Day 2 (3-4pm). Retroviral Transduction (24hours post stimulation; mitotic phase is 22-26 hrs post stim, which is the optimal time for transduction)

*Pre spin centrifuge at 4000rpm, 40C– to get it up to 37C or as close to it as possible


*If making virus: Collect viral media and filter with a 0.45 um syringe filter to remove cell debris (alternatively centrifuge at 3000 rpm 10 min). Store it at -80 C.

*If virus was stored at -80, pre-warm at 37C.

Remove ~1.8 ml of media (from the 2ml on the 6well plate). And set it aside for after spin infection.
Add 1 mL viral media (filtered) supplemented with 8ug/ml polybrene (1/1000) and BME 50 mM (1/1000) to each well. Double polybrene if double transduction (1/500).
Spin at 2000 rpm for 60 min at 37° (or as close as practical) to infect cells (120 min for double transduction).
Place them in the incubator for 2h.
Remove ~900 uL of viral media or aspirate, and replace with 2 mL old CD3/CD28 activation media + 2ml of fresh TCM media. Put in incubator.

Day 3 (8-9am) - Add IL-2 (10 ng/mL r-human IL-2),

Pool CD8 T cells from the 6 well plates into a 50 ml conical and centrifuge 1600 rpm 5 min.
Resuspend in 20 ml of TCM media containing 10 ng/ml r-human IL-2 and transfer to T75 flask
Day 4 (5-6pm). Transfer activated T cells




Wash CD8 T cells from the flask in cold PBS 2x




Resuspend in 1ml an count them in the hemocytometer
Cell Media

500 ml RPMI (ref 10-041 CV, with L-glutamine and 25 mM HEPES),

text:
Reporter-gene transduction of P14 into LCMV Armstrong infected mice for tissue embedding
CD8 Selection and activation (GFP, tdTomato, mCherry, Ametrine plasmids)
Day 1

Dilute GAH IgG antibody 1:30 in sterile PBS
Aliquot 550 ul/ well in a 6 well plate. Distribute antibody + PBS across the wells
Incubate plate at 37C for 2 hours
Harvest spleen from P14 mice and homogenize over 70 um filter
Centrifuge at 1600 RPM for 4 min and dump
Resuspend pellet in 1-2 ml ACK and incubate at room temp for 5-6 min
Neutralize with 3-4 ml MACS
Count cells

125 million cells

Centrifuge at 1600 RPM for 4 min and aspirate supernatant
Add 40 ul MACS buffer for every 10 million cells

500 ul

Add 10 ul CD8 antibody biotin cocktail for every 10 million cells

125 ul antibody cocktail

Mix well
Incubate at 4C for 5 min
Add 30 ul MACS buffer for every 10 million cells

375 ul buffer

Add 20 ul biotin micro beads for every 10 million cells

250 ul beads

Mix well
Incubate at 4C for 10 min
Rinse LS column by adding 3 mls of MACS buffer when incubation step in step 17 has a few minutes left
Apply single cell suspension to column (avoid getting on edge of column)
If less than 500 ul, complete to 500 ul before adding to column
Collect flow through as this represents the unlabeled CD8 fraction (biotin antibodies label all other cells besides CD8 in this negative selection kit)
Wash column with 3 mls of MACS and combine with eluent in step 22
Count cells in this fraction- these are your CD8!

35 million cells

Dilute cells to 2e6 cells/ml

17.5 mls

Wash GAH-ab coated wells 2x with 1 ml TCM
Plate 2e6 cells in 1 ml TCM
Dilute anti-CD3 and anti-CD28 antibodies 1:500 in TCM
Stock concentration of anti-CD3 and anti-CD28 is 1 mg/ml, final should be 1 ug/ml (adding 2 ug/ml because diluted 2x)
Add 1 ml CD3/28 antibody mix to each well, pipette to mix
Incubate at 37C for 24 hours

Day 2
Retroviral transduction of P14

Prewarm centrifuge to 37C
Thaw virus in water bath
Make polybrene mix (70x). For 100 ul of viral solution use:

8 ul polybrene
10 ul BME
82 ul OptiMEM

Combine virus + polybrene mix. For 140 ul virus, add 2 ul polybrene mix (e.g. 2 ml virus, add 28.5 ul polybrene mix)
Transfer media from 6 well into 15 ml conicals, keep warm and separate between P14 backgrounds
Add virus mix to activated T cells
Spin at 37C for 1 hr, 2000RPM
Incubate plate at 37C 1-4 hours
Carefully remove virus mix
Spin down old media from step 5 and add same amount of fresh TCM (total volume is 4 mls per well in the end)
Incubate for 24 hours at 37C

Day 3

Perform sort

Use the following gating strategy to calculate number of P14 to adoptively transfer




Singlets Lymphocytes CD8/VA2 CD8/fluorescent marker

title: Lentivirus Production and Transduction
text:
Reina Lab
Updated 3/25/2026 H.M.
Lentivirus Production in a 10 cm Dish
Materials and Reagents

HEK293T cells
Opti-MEM
10 cm tissue-culture-treated plates
Complete DMEM (See Nicoles Media Recipes)
Trypsin
1X PBS
Packaging plasmids:



pCMV-VSV-G (Addgene #8454). Alternatively pMDG.2
psPAX2 (Addgene #12260)



Lentiviral transfer plasmid
TransIT-LT1 Transfection Reagent
14 mL tube
50 mL conical tubes
5 mL microcentrifuge tubes or other suitable aliquot tubes
0.45 µm filter, optional
Dry ice-cooled ethanol bath (optional)
Follow volumes: Useful Numbers for Cell Culture

Protocol
Day 0: Plate HEK293T Cells

Plate 3.5 × 10⁶ HEK293T cells in one 10 cm dish (MRC)

Dhruv plates 750K-1M 293Ts per well of a 6 well plate.

Use 10 mL complete DMEM per dish or 2ml per well of 6 well
Return the plate to the incubator.

Day 1: Transfection

Approximately 24 hours after plating, transfect the cells using TransIT-LT1.
If the medium appears exhausted or the cells need additional attachment time, replace the medium 3-4 hours before transfection.
For the medium change, add 10 mL fresh complete DMEM (2ml per well of a 6 well) and return the cells to the incubator.
Bring Opti-MEM and TransIT-LT1 to room temperature before use.
Prepare the transfection mixture in a 14 mL tube in the following order:



Add plasmid DNA at an approximately 4:3:1 mass ratio:
15 µg lentiviral transfer plasmid
11 µg psPAX2
4 µg pCMV-VSV-G
30 µg total DNA
Add Opti-MEM to a total volume of 1.5 mL.
Mix by pipetting, then gently swirl the tube.
Add TransIT-LT1 directly into the liquid, dropwise.
Use 3 µL TransIT-LT1 per µg DNA as an optimization range; 90 µL for 30 µg total DNA.
Gently swirl the tube. Do not pipette or vortex after adding TransIT-LT1.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 30 minutes.



Add the DNA/Opti-MEM/TransIT-LT1 mixture to the cells dropwise in a circular motion.
Return the plate to the incubator at 5% CO₂.

Day 2: Medium Change

Approximately 16 hours after transfection, gently remove the medium.
Replace it with 10 mL fresh complete medium for virus collection (R10 for T cells)

Days 3 and 4: Viral Supernatant Collection

Collect the cellular supernatant at approximately 24 and 48 hours after the medium change
Pipette the HEK293T supernatant into a 50 mL conical tube.
Pool supernatant from multiple 10 cm dishes if needed.
Centrifuge at 1600 rpm for 5 minutes.
Optional: Filter the supernatant through a 0.45 µm filter.
Transfer the viral supernatant into 5 mL tubes or another suitable aliquot format.
Freeze in -80C
Prepare single-use aliquots and avoid repeated freeze-thaw cycles.
T cell activation: Follow Lab Protocol from Giovanni
Transduction Option 1: MRC
Coated retronectin plates O/N at 4C or for 2-3 hours at RT

90ul of RN in 5910 of PBS. Coat each well using 900-1000ul of solution.


Block plates with 4ml of R10 for 30 min prior to transduction

After 24 hours of activation, prepare Lib5 and Lib7 lentiviral library supernatants supplemented with: LentiBOOST (Sirion Biotech) at 1:200 dilution. Add both Solution A and Solution B
Add the activated cells to the supplemented lentiviral supernatants. Dhruv has used 3ml of virus with cells, in each well of retronectin coasted plate
Spin-infect the cells at: 800 × g for 3 hours
Following centrifugation, incubate the cells for an additional 4 hours at: 37°C, 5% CO₂
Wash the cells to remove residual viral supernatant and transduction reagents.
Culture the washed cells for 4 days in medium supplemented with: Human IL-2: 20 IU/mL.
Depending on the goal, add mouse IL-7 (2.5ng/mL), and Mouse IL-15: 25 ng/mL
Transduction Option 2: Arlene Sharpe (Naïve T cells)
Coat non-tissue culture–treated 6-well plates with RetroNectin (Takara Bio, Cat. #T100B) at approximately 15 µg/cm² overnight at 4°C.
The next morning, remove RetroNectin and block each well with 2 mL of 2% BSA in PBS−/− for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Remove the blocking solution, add 2 mL lentiviral supernatant per well, and centrifuge at 2,000 × g for 2 hours at 32°C.
Isolate naive CD8⁺ T cells using the Miltenyi Naive CD8a⁺ T Cell Isolation Kit (Cat. #130-096-543).
Plate the cells onto the virus-coated wells in complete RPMI containing 1 mg/mL LentiBOOST and 1 ng/mL recombinant murine IL-7.
Complete RPMI consisted of RPMI 1640 with L-glutamine, 10% FBS, 1% penicillin/streptomycin, 10 mM HEPES, 55 µM 2-mercaptoethanol, 1% sodium pyruvate, and 1% non-essential amino acids.
Culture the cells for 7 days with 1 ng/mL IL-7. Change the medium on days 2 and 5, and add fresh cytokine on day 4.

title: Fugene 6 mediated transfection of Phoenix cell
text:
Fugene 6 mediated transfection of Phoenix cell for retrovirus production
Day 0

Inoculate Phoenix cells (4x10^6) in 10cm dish

Day 1

Warm medium (DMEM, 10% FCS, PSG; Optimem, serum free) to 37oC
Transfer 10 ug of plasmid into eppendorf tube
Dilute 30ul of Fugene in 170 ul of serum free Optimem (3ul Fugene: 1ug of DNA)
Add 3 (Fugene/media) into 2 (plasmid DNA) dropwise. Incubate at RT for 15min.
Change media of culture on Phoenix cells to 8 ml of DMEM, 10% FCS, PSG.
Add Fugene/DNA mix to culture dish dropwise.
Culture cells ON at 37oC.

Day 2

Aspirate media (remember this is now virus containing material-handle properly) and replace with 8ml of Optimem, 10% FCS, PSG OR media you intend to grow the cells you will be transducing with the virus with.

Day 3 and 4

Collect the supernatant. Carefully add another 8ml media to the Phoenix culture (for day 4 harvest). Centrifuge collected supernatant to remove floating cells and debris and aliquot in samples of size you intend to sue at each transduction.
Store at -80oC.

Note: Phoenix cells tend to detach easily at high densities. So it is important to be very careful when adding fresh media to them. Slow and to the plate wall does it.
Fugene 6 Transfection reagent from Roche.
When Phoenix cells are ~60% split 1:4.

title: NES 042924 CD8 T cell transduction and double transduction
text:
Purpose: To introduce genetic modifications to in vitro cultured mouse T cells.
Timeline
Day -5

Break out Platinum-E Retroviral Packaging Cells for Ecotropic virus (Plat-E cells), stored in the liquid nitrogen.

Thaw cells until no longer frozen on skirt of the hood (2-3 minutes)
Move cells to 15 ml conical, add fresh D10 media to wash.
Spin cells down at 1600 RPM for 4 minutes, then plate onto 15cm plate with 15-20 ml D10. Culture at 37 degrees.


Day -2

Trypsinize cells from plate (5ml trypsin [Trypsin-EDTA, Mediatech] for 3 minutes, stop with 5ml D10), count cells, and plate 2x106 onto 10cm plates (for as many transductions as needed).

Day -1

Two options

Transfect Plat-E cells for single transduction (single plasmid)

Put 700uL serum-free DMEM (SF-DMEM) into a 1.5ml epiendorf, warm to room temperature
Add 6ug plasmid of interest and 2ug pCL-ECO helper plasmid to SF-DMEM. Pipette to mix well
Add 30uL room-temperature Mirus Bio TransIT-LT1 Transfection Reagent (Fisher) to SF-DMEM. Pipette to mix well.
Let sit at room temperature for 20-30 minutes to allow micelles to form.
Drip SF-DMEM onto previously-plated Plat-E cells
Let sit overnight, change plat-E media to fresh R10 first thing the next morning. Do not change media again until transduction, as you are now collecting retrovirus.

Transfect Plat-E cells for double transduction (2+ plasmids)

Put 700uL serum-free DMEM (SF-DMEM) into a 1.5ml epiendorf, warm to room temperature
Add total 6ug plasmid of interest (e.g. if doing a double transduction, add 3ug of each) and 2ug pCL-ECO helper plasmid to SF-DMEM. Pipette to mix well
Add 30uL room-temperature Mirus Bio TransIT-LT1 Transfection Reagent (Fisher) to SF-DMEM. Pipette to mix well.
Let sit at room temperature for 20-30 minutes to allow micelles to form.
Drip SF-DMEM onto previously-plated Plat-E cells
Let sit overnight, change plat-E media to fresh R10 first thing the next morning. Do not change media again until transduction, as you are now collecting retrovirus.



Day 0

Activate T cells

Coat a flat-bottom, 6-well plate with 5ug/ml anti-CD3 (for P14) OR 10ug/ml anti-CD3 (for WT CD8 T cells) in sterile PBS. Coat enough wells for ~5million CD8 per well. Allow antibody to adhere to the plastic by incubating at 37 degrees for 3hr hours.
Sacrifice mice, dissect spleen and lymph nodes according to the dissection protocol, and isolate CD8 T cells according to T cell isolation protocol or sorting protocol.
Pipette off excess PBS in 6 well plate.
Add isolated CD8 T cells (~5million per well in 2ml R10) to each well + 2ug/ml anti-CD28 + 50U/ml CETUS hIL-2. Add gently to not disturb anti-CD3 coated on plate.
Let cells activate at least 24 hours at 37 degrees.

Coat plate with retronectin for next day

Prepare 1ml sterile PBS + 66x dilution factor retronectin (initial conc = 1000ug/ml, final conc = 15ug/ml) for each retroviral group.
Coat 6 well plate (non-tissue culture treated) with 1ml retronectin per well for each retroviral group.
Seal the plate with parafilm and incubate O/N in the fridge (4deg).


Day 1

Transduce T cells

carefully remove retronectin from wells with pipette (tilt the plate)
add 4 ml of R10 to each well to block aspecific sites (first ml drop-by-drop)
incubate 30min @ 37°C (while this is happening, start warming up centrifuge you will be using for transduction to 37deg).
Take viral media off transfected plat-E cells and spin down to pellet any floating plat-E cells. These tubes can sit in the hood while you are using them to coat virus on the retronectin plate.
Remove R10 from retronectin plate and add 1ml of virus and incubate 30min @ 37°C
Remove virus and add new 1ml of virus and incubate 30min @ 37°C
Remove virus again.
Remove T cells from yesterday’s activation plate (pipette media on cells multiple times with P1000 pipette) Spin down activated cells, and resuspend in remaining viral media (about 7ml left). Add 50U/ml IL-2.
Put cells in viral coated plate, wrap plate in cellophane, and spin the cells at 1600 RPM at 37 degrees for 45min.
After spin is complete, unwrap cellophane and put cells back into 37 degree incubator, culture overnight, and change media to fresh R10+IL2 in the morning.


Day 2-10

Culturing T cells

As appropriate for your experiment, continue culturing your cells or adoptively transfer into mice.
Keep cells at 1x106/ml by counting every day. When cells need to expand, add additional R10 + IL-2.
5-6 days after activation, switch cells to 25U/ml IL-2 (1:4000 dillution) to become more rested.
Cells should continue to proliferate until 7-10 days after activation. Cells will stop proliferating but still be viable 10-14 days after activation. For cytokine competency to be assessed post day 7, the cells will need to be reactivated.

title: Transfection Protocol
text:
Transfection-96 well plate format
Day 1

Plate 2-4x104 Plat E cells/well in 96-well flat bottom plate (total volume 200uL/well)

Only use middle 60 wells, fill outer 36 wells with 100uL media
For six well plates- we typically use ~0.8-1.2x106 cell per well in 2mL and typically scale everything up by 10

Plate cells in Plat E media without Pen/Strep

Plat E media = DMEM + L-glut, 10% FBS, 50uM BME, 10mM HEPES


Day 2

Remove 150uL of media from Plat E cells and add back 50uL of fresh, warm Plate E media without Pen/Strep

At least 1 hr prior to transfection

Prep for transfection

Warm mirus transfection agent and opti-mem to room temperature
Tube 1

Add 1uL of 100ng/uL of Pcl-Eco (helper plasmid) + 9uL of Opti-mem media per transfection well

i.e. if you are transfecting 10 wells, add 90uL of Opti + 10uL of Pcl-Eco to Tube 1

Add 200ng of shRNA plasmid per well (2uL of 100ng/uL) to Tube 1

i.e. for 10 transfection wells add 20uL


Tube 2: mirus/Opti Mix

Add 0.6 uL of mirus transfection reagent +9.4 uL of Opti-mem per transfection well

i.e. for 10 wells add 6uL mirus + 94uL of Opti-mem to Tube 2


Add Tube 2 to Tube 1 and mix well

Always add mirus/opti mix (Tube 2) last and mix well

Incubate for 20min rm temp

After 20min incubation add shRNA mixture to Plat E cells dropwise

Day 3

Replace 70uL of Plat E media with 70uL of warm T cell media

Day 4

Harvest 70uL of RV supernatant and replace with 70uL of fresh T cell media
We typically activate CD8 T cells here for transducing the following day

Typically getting 40-80% transduction with this protocol


Day 5

Harvest all of RV supernatant and pool for transduction (final 170uL/well)

title: Spleen and Lymph Node Prep
text: This combined reference preserves the approaches from the two original protocols. Confirm the appropriate tissue, media, centrifuge setting, and ACK lysis conditions with the current lab-approved procedure before starting.

title: Spleen and Lymph Node Prep
text:
Original protocols

Cell Prep from Lymph nodes and/or Spleen
Spleen processing

title: Spleen and Lymph Node Prep
text:
Combined procedure

1. Collect and prepare the tissue

Collect spleen and/or lymph nodes into media.
Use the starting medium and volume appropriate to the selected original protocol:

Lymph node and/or spleen approach: approximately 5 mL RPMI.
Spleen-only approach: a plate containing media (RP5), then approximately 3 mL RP5 in a small petri dish per spleen.




2. Disrupt and filter the tissue
Choose the method that matches the original protocol being followed.

Cell-strainer method: Place a cell strainer in a 6 cm petri dish containing approximately 5 mL RPMI. Pour the tissue into the strainer and use the bottom of a syringe plunger to grind it through. Remove the strainer and transfer the cells and RPMI to a 15 mL conical.
Microscope-slide/Nitex method: Grind a spleen in RP5 with the rough surfaces of two microscope slides. Rinse the slides with RP5 and collect the cells in the petri dish. Pass the suspension through a Nitex filter into a 15 mL conical, then rinse the dish with RP5 and filter the rinse to recover remaining cells.



3. Pellet the cells
Use the centrifugation setting from the source protocol selected above.

Lymph node and/or spleen approach: 1800 rpm for 5 minutes.
Spleen-only approach: 1600 RPM for 4 minutes.

Discard the supernatant while retaining the pellet.


4. Lyse red blood cells with ACK

Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL ACK buffer.
Use the ACK exposure specified by the selected source protocol:

Lymph node and/or spleen approach: incubate at room temperature for 1 minute, then add approximately 13 mL RPMI and mix.
Spleen-only approach: use 1 mL of 1X ACK for approximately 5 minutes, or until the mixture appears clear and lysed. Dilute ACK first if it is not 1X.

Centrifuge again using the selected protocol’s setting, then discard the supernatant and retain the pellet. The spleen-only source notes that the pellet should be white at this stage.



5. Finish the cell preparation

For the lymph node and/or spleen approach, resuspend in RPMI, pass through a cell strainer into a 50 mL conical, take an aliquot to count cells, then pellet again at 1800 rpm for 5 minutes before resuspending in the desired medium at the desired concentration.
For the spleen-only approach, resuspend the final pellet in 1 mL RP5, TCM, or MACS for the next step.

title: Infection with Listeria
text:
Listeria production for Infection






Important



Do everything in a BSL2 TC hood.



Thaw a frozen stock from -80°C (I usually stick in a 37°C H20 bath).
Dilute 1:50 in tryptic soy broth or BHI (no more than 1 month old). For 5 ml broth, use 100μl listeria stock. Grow in 50ml conical. Do not cap conical tightly as air needs to circulate. Secure loose cap with tape. Put biohazard sticker on tube, and put a sign on the shaker as well, warning about biohazard.

Grow in bacterial shaker at 37°C until you reach OD600 of approx. 0.1 (this is mid log phase) then stick culture on ice to stop growth. Anything between .09-11 is OK.

Depending on the dilution of the frozen stock this usually takes between 1.5 and 2 hours


Use disposable plastic 1 ml cuvettes to OD bugs. Parafilm around the top of them before carrying out of the hood.
Take an aliquot of tryptic broth alone for control.


Calculate concentration of listeria. An OD600 of 0.1=2x10e8 cfu/ml. Calculate appropriate ratio. Final concentration should be 5000 cfu/mouse in 200μl. That is 2.5 x 104 pfu/ml.

\(\frac{0.1}{2*10^8} = \frac{[your OD]}{cfu}\) –> \(cfu = [your OD]*2*10^9\)
Usually should have to perform a dilution in the range of about 1:7000. Anything a lot lower or higher is probably incorrect. Since the dilution ratio is so high, perform serial dilution. Do not attempt to dilute entire 5ml of listeria.

Perform serial dilutions in sterile PBS to inject.

Example:

If OD yields concentration of 2.52 x 108 cfu/ml, do a 1:100 dilution
Take 10μl in 990μl PBS concentration now is 2.52 x 106 cfu/ml.
Take the total dilution you have to do and divide by the dilution you already did. That is the rest of the dilution you have to do.

Take 80μl of diluted stock and add to 7920μl PBS. This is the 2nd 1:100 dilution. which should result in 2.52 x 104 cfu/ml. Now you can use this to infect.







Note



Use the interactive calculator at lab.beetletun.de










Important



Bleach all tips and pipets, etc in 10% bleach before disposing as biohazard. When I do FACS staining of cells from infected mice, I flick plates into a 2 L beaker with bleach in the bottom and always use a plate with a lid (until fixed of course).

title: Labeling T cells with CFSE
text:
Labeling T cells with CFSE…Beautiful Peaks Guaranteed

Wash lymphocytes in PBS 0.1%BSA twice to remove FCS.
Resuspend at 2x 107 cells/mL in PBS 0.1%PBS which has been prewarmed to 37C. Add 2μL of 5mM CFSE stock (in DMSO) per mL of cells while vortexing for 10μM final. This step is very important for getting good, tight peaks: you want all of the cells to get exposed to the same concentration of CFSE at the same time (use a 50 mL tube if labeling more than 5 mLs of cells, also I would not suggest labeling more than 10 mLs at a time if possible).
Incubate t 37C in dark for 10 minutes.
Top off tube with cold RP20% FCS spin down and wash twice more.
For last wash, put cells through nytex and wash in RPMI no FCS, count before spinning down and resuspend in RPMI (no FCS) at appropriate concentration (don’t do this last wash until you are headed to the mousehouse).

title: Making LCMV stocks
text:
Note



Production of LCMV viral stocks. Protocol adapted from Kay Chung via John Teijaro and modified by Thomas Mann.
The production of LCMV is carried out in BHK (baby hamster kidney) cells.

title: Making LCMV stocks
text:
Reagents:

BHK media (500 mL):
500 mL DMEM (high glucose, liquid)
50 mL FBS (10%)
5 mL L-glutamine (100x)
5 mL Pen-strep (100x)
25 mL Tryptose phosphate broth (Gibco)

title: Making LCMV stocks
text:
Procedure:

Day -1:

Plate BHK to be ~40-50% confluent the following day. Seed about 5x10 6 BHK cells in a T175 flask the day before infection. The cells will grow to a confluency of 40-50%, corresponding to ~1x107.







Note



BHK cells grow at different rates in different labs and seem to be pretty sensitive. Consider setting up flasks at target multiple confluencies to try to hit the right one on the infection day.




Day 0:

Take photos of the T175 flasks on the light microscope if possible - try to record what a good confluency looks like.
Pipet off media and infect with virus in a limited volume (6 mL for a T175, 3 mL for a T75). The MOI used in the field seems to vary; many people use 0.001-0.01, but Teijaro lab uses an MOI of 0.1.

The lore is that it is important to use a high titer virus to inoculate, but unclear where this line is drawn.
Teijaro adds 5 uL of 2x10 8 PFU/mL stock to 6 mL BHK media to hit a target of MOI 0.1 for 107 cells in a T175.

Incubate at 37 Celsius for 90 minutes. Gently tilt and rock the flask every 10-15 minutes.
After 90 minutes, add 19 mL warm BHK media (total 25 mL final).
Incubate for 72 hours.



Day 3






Warning



Keep the virus cold for all following steps!



Pipet supernatant into 15 mL conical tubes. The supernatant contains the virus. Be careful, this is a LOT of LCMV. Have bleach handy in case of a spill.
Separate any remaining BHK cells that were aspirated from virus.

Spin at 2000 rpm in a benchtop centrifuge (~800-850 g depending on centrifuge in IMPL-K) for 15 minutes.
Collect the supernatant, transfer to a fresh tube.
Repeat for a total of two centrifugation steps.

Keeping the virus cold, aliquot and snap freeze in liquid nitrogen. Pre-chill cryo-tubes in cold room.
Protocol yields ~20-25 mL virus containing supernatant at a target of ~2x108 pfu/mL.

Infecting at 2x10 6 pfu/mouse (100 uL of 2x10 7 pfu/mL), this corresponds to enough virus to infect 2000 mice per T175 of LCMV Clone 13.

Titrate the virus. Make sure to titrate an aliquot that has been frozen and thawed to get a representative value for what the titer will be when you inject from a thawed aliquot (rather than titrating the supernatant directly).

title: Cas9 Electroporation with Lonza 2
text: This composite contains the Lonza P3 workflows from four sources. They differ in preparation of CD8 cells, experimental-guide and Cas9 input, controls, and post-electroporation culture. Use one complete source-specific option for each difference and confirm current lab-approved conditions before beginning.

title: Cas9 Electroporation with Lonza 2
text:
Source files

Alex Monell — Cas9 Nucleofection_ATM
Kelsey Bennion — Electroporation of activated CD8
Giovanni Galleti — CB6.CRISPRCas9 KO
Nicole Sharping — 062923 CRISPRCas9 KO in primary T cells for in vivo transfer with Lonza - single guides

title: Cas9 Electroporation with Lonza 2
text:
1. Prepare CD8 T cells

Enrichment or prior activation
Derived from: Alex Monell, Giovanni Galleti, and Nicole Sharping.
Enrich naïve CD8 T cells before electroporation, or activate cells 24 hours beforehand. These sources specify Lonza P3 buffer, DN100 for naïve CD8 cells, and DS137 for activated CD8 cells.


Complete isolation and activation route
Derived from: Kelsey Bennion.
Kelsey provides a full route from spleen and lymph-node collection through ACK lysis, negative magnetic CD8 selection, purity assessment, and anti-CD3/anti-CD28 activation for 18–24 hours.

title: Cas9 Electroporation with Lonza 2
text:
2. Assemble RNP complexes
Derived from: Alex Monell, Kelsey Bennion, Giovanni Galleti, and Nicole Sharping.

Use 100 µM crRNA and tracrRNA with a stated 3:1 guide-RNA-to-Cas9 molar ratio.
For a Thy1-only control, combine 3 µL Thy1 crRNA and 3 µL tracrRNA.
For experimental conditions, use the source-specific crRNA and Cas9 amounts shown in the differences table.
Anneal guide and tracrRNA at 95°C for 5 minutes, then hold at room temperature in the dark for 1 hour.
Add 40 µM Cas9, gently mix and briefly spin down, then incubate at room temperature for 20 minutes.

title: Cas9 Electroporation with Lonza 2
text:
3. Prepare cells and P3 buffer
Derived from: Alex Monell, Kelsey Bennion, Giovanni Galleti, and Nicole Sharping.

Prepare P3 buffer at room temperature: 3.6 µL Supplement 1 plus 16.4 µL P3 per reaction.
Prewarm R10 with 50 U/mL IL-2 to 37°C.
Count 2–10 × 106 cells per reaction, wash in sterile room-temperature PBS, and pellet at 5000 RPM for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Remove residual liquid completely and resuspend each pellet in 20 µL P3 buffer. Limit the cells’ time in P3 buffer.

title: Cas9 Electroporation with Lonza 2
text:
4. Electroporate cells
Derived from: Alex Monell, Kelsey Bennion, Giovanni Galleti, and Nicole Sharping.

Mix 5 µL RNP with 20 µL cells in P3 buffer.
Transfer the 25 µL mixture to the bottom of a Lonza nucleofector strip well without introducing bubbles.
Run DN100 for naïve CD8 cells or DS137 for activated CD8 cells.
Immediately add 130 µL prewarmed R10 and rest cells for 10 minutes at 37°C and 5% CO2.

title: Cas9 Electroporation with Lonza 2
text:
5. Recover and analyze cells

Direct recovery and in vivo transfer
Derived from: Alex Monell and Nicole Sharping.
Recover cells from the strip, wash with an additional 150 µL R10, and add 700 µL prewarmed R10 to reach 1 mL total. Count with Trypan Blue; both sources note 20–50% T-cell loss. For in vivo transfer, resuspend in PBS at the desired concentration and retain cells for flow or Sanger validation.


Overnight recovery
Derived from: Giovanni Galleti.
Prepare R10 plus 15 U/mL IL-2 by combining 600 µL R10 plus 50 U/mL IL-2 with 1400 µL plain R10. Return cells to their original number of wells and culture overnight or for 24 hours.


Extended culture and validation
Derived from: Kelsey Bennion.
Kelsey describes cytokine replenishment every 48 hours, 25 U/mL IL-2 or TRM-polarization medium, and downstream collection for flow, genomic-DNA/Sanger, RNA/qPCR, and supernatant ELISA analyses.

title: Growing a Listeria stock
text:
Note



This is a protocol that I got from Maurice, Nicholas J (nmaurice@fredhutch.org) for the Lm-OVA variants (N4, Q4, T4)

title: Growing a Listeria stock
text:
Procedure

Inject 3000-4000 CFU into hosts (I just start with the vial in ~3-4mL Brain-heart infusion (BHI) media, with no antibiotic and move to step 9)
Sacrifice mice between 48 and 60 hrs post-infection
Harvest and tease apart spleen in 5ml PBS+0.1% NP40
Plate 200ml of spleen solution onto BHI+erythromycin plate [spread out sequentially to get single colonies]
Incubate for 48 hours
There should be little to no growth after 24 hours – the presence of large colonies at this time point suggests contamination.
Do not grow past 48 hours – overgrowth may occur
Harvest a single colony into 200ml of BHI+ erythromycin (in mc tube)
Take several medium-sized colonies (growth will be heterogeneous)
Grow for 4 hr with shaking 37°C (set speed higher to ensure agitation in mc tubes)
Inoculate 4ml of BHI (no antibiotic at this step) with LM-OVA from previous step
Expand with shaking until broth is mildly cloudy

Add 4ml of bacteria to 26ml of BHI broth in a 50ml Falcon tube (or 200ml flask) (depending on growth kinetics, you could set this up as an overnight)
Expand with shaking for several hours until broth is cloudy, add erythromycin for the last 45-60min of culturing (once the OD is at about 0.6) (I don’t bother with erythromycin since these are stable/do everything sterile)
Read OD: should be at 0.6 – 0.8 before moving on to step 13 (OD can be pushed a little higher; if overgrowth occurs, just add BHI and allow to re-enter log-phase of growth)
Add 15ml of the 40% glycerol stock (40% glycerol stock is 20mL glycerol in 30mL BHI; I sterile filter mine and use fresh) to the 30ml of cloudy bacteria culture
mix gently on ice and aliquot 1ml in screw top cryotubes (keep on wet ice while aliquoting) (I like my LM to be on wet ice to facilitate glycerol uptake for a bit before moving them into the -80°C freezer).
Freeze -80°C
