title: Antibody Titration
text:
Before starting

Review the antibody datasheet for recommended buffer, staining temperature, and incubation time. Some internalizing or recycling receptors may require staining at 37°C (Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS).
Mix antibodies thoroughly and briefly spin them down to reduce aggregates. An antibody master mix may instead be prepared and spun before staining (Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS).
Select cells containing a clearly identifiable positive and negative population.
Choose a dilution range broad enough to bracket the expected optimum.
Include an unstained sample and the required single-color compensation controls.
For tandem dyes, use the same antibody conjugate in the compensation control (Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS).

title: Antibody Titration
text:
Materials

Cells containing positive and negative populations for the target antigen
Antibody to be titrated
Optional co-staining antibodies
Calcium- and magnesium-free PBS
FACS buffer: PBS with 2% FBS
Fc block
Compatible viability dye
Fixation and permeabilization reagents appropriate for the target
96-well plate or flow-cytometry tubes
Compensation beads appropriate for the antibody fluorophores and viability dye
Optional Super Bright Complete Staining Buffer


Additional materials — Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS

Live/Dead Blue reconstituted with 50 µL DMSO
ArC Amine Reactive Compensation Bead Kit
UltraComp eBeads
Super Bright Complete Staining Buffer, 5 µL per test



Additional materials — Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse

Foxp3 eBioscience fixation/permeabilization kit for transcription factors or other intranuclear targets
BD Cytofix/Cytoperm kit for cytokines or other cytoplasmic targets

title: Antibody Titration
text:
1. Prepare cells

Count the cells and divide equal numbers among the titration conditions.
Wash once with PBS.
If cells are suspended in complete RPMI, wash thoroughly with PBS to remove FBS or BSA before using an amine-reactive viability dye (Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS).


Cell-input options

Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS: The viability-dye example is calculated for 10 × 10^6 cells per sample and uses eight tubes.
Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse: Combine suitable positive and negative cells when needed. The source example uses approximately 60 × 10^6 total cells and plates 2 × 10^6 cells per well.

title: Antibody Titration
text:
2. Viability stain and Fc block

Prepare the selected viability dye according to its product instructions.
Resuspend each sample in 50 µL Fc block.
Add 50 µL viability-dye mix.
Incubate for 15 minutes at room temperature in the dark.
Wash and remove the supernatant.


Viability-dye options

Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS: Prepare Live/Dead Blue mix for four samples by combining 19.5 µL water with 0.5 µL dye, then adding 380 µL PBS. Wash afterward with 2 mL FACS buffer and centrifuge at 1,600 rpm for 4 minutes.
Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse: Use APC-Cy7 live/dead dye at 1:500. Wash once with 100 µL FACS buffer.

title: Antibody Titration
text:
3. Design the dilution series
Prepare antibody solutions at 2× the desired final concentration when equal volumes of antibody solution and cell suspension will be combined.

Example plate series — Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse



Well
Final antibody dilution




1
1:50


2
1:100


3
1:200


4
1:400


5
1:800


Control
Unstained



The source begins the serial dilution at 1:25 so that adding it to an equal volume of cell suspension produces a 1:50 final dilution.


Eight-tube series — Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS

Resuspend cells in 50 µL FACS buffer per tube.
Add 50 µL FACS buffer to every tube except tube 1. Add 5 µL Super Bright Complete Staining Buffer per test when appropriate.
Prepare at least 115 µL of a 2× antibody mix in the same staining buffer.
Add 50 µL antibody mix to tubes 1 and 2.
Mix tube 2 and transfer 50 µL from tube 2 to tube 3.
Continue mixing and transferring 50 µL through tube 7.
Remove and discard 50 µL from tube 7. Tube 8 remains the unstained control.

title: Antibody Titration
text:
4. Surface-antibody titration

Add the selected antibody dilution to each sample.
Add optional surface co-staining antibodies at their established titers.
Incubate for 20 minutes at 4°C in the dark unless the antibody datasheet requires another condition.
Wash and remove the supernatant.


Tube workflow — Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS

Add 50 µL cell suspension to each tube containing the prepared dilution.
After staining, wash with 2 mL FACS buffer.
Centrifuge at 1,600 rpm for 4 minutes.
If the target antibody requires 20 minutes at 37°C, perform its titration under that condition before adding the remaining surface co-stain.



Plate workflow — Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse

Resuspend cells in 50 µL surface-staining solution per well.
The source uses established CD45.2-BV510 and CD45.2-BV786 co-stains at 1:100.
After staining, wash twice with 100 µL FACS buffer.

Proceed to acquisition if fixation is unnecessary. For intracellular targets, continue with the appropriate branch below.

title: Antibody Titration
text:
5. Intracellular or intranuclear titration
Prepare intracellular antibody dilutions in the permeabilization buffer specified by the selected kit. Do not use Super Bright Complete Staining Buffer for intracellular antibodies (Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS).

Foxp3/transcription-factor workflow — Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse

Prepare fixation buffer by combining one part fixation/permeabilization concentrate with three parts diluent. The source example uses 1 mL concentrate plus 3 mL diluent.
Prepare 1× permeabilization buffer by combining one part 10× stock with nine parts water.
Resuspend cells in 100 µL fixation buffer.
Incubate for 20 minutes at 4°C in the dark.
During fixation, add 100 µL permeabilization buffer to the first serial-dilution well and 50 µL to each successive well.
Add the antibody to the first well at 1:25, mix, and transfer 50 µL sequentially to generate 2× solutions for final dilutions of 1:50 through 1:800.
Leave the final control well without antibody.
Wash cells once with 100 µL permeabilization buffer, not FACS buffer.
Resuspend cells in the corresponding intracellular-antibody dilution.
Incubate for 30 minutes at 4°C in the dark.
Wash once with permeabilization buffer and once with FACS buffer.



Cytofix/Cytoperm workflow — Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse

After the surface-staining wash, add 100 µL Cytofix per well.
Incubate for 20 minutes at 4°C in the dark.
Prepare 1× permeabilization buffer by combining one part 10× stock with nine parts water.
Generate the 2× two-fold antibody dilution series in Cytoperm permeabilization buffer as described above.
Wash cells once with 100 µL permeabilization buffer.
Resuspend cells in the corresponding intracellular-antibody dilution.
Incubate for 30 minutes at 4°C in the dark.
Wash once with permeabilization buffer and once with FACS buffer.



General fixation option — Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS

Add 150 µL BioLegend fix buffer and incubate for 10 minutes, or use the preferred fixation/permeabilization conditions for the application.
Wash with 2 mL FACS buffer and centrifuge at 1,600 rpm for 4 minutes.
For an intracellular or intranuclear titration, repeat the serial-dilution approach using Perm/Wash buffer instead of FACS buffer.
Add any intracellular co-staining antibodies after fixation and permeabilization.

title: Antibody Titration
text:
6. Compensation controls — Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS

Vortex compensation beads thoroughly.
For each antibody fluorophore, combine one drop UltraComp eBeads with antibody at the selected titer. Use at least 0.5 µL antibody when the selected volume is lower.
Prepare an unstained control with one drop UltraComp eBeads.
For Live/Dead Blue, prepare a positive control with two drops ArC Amine Reactive beads plus 2 µL dye.
Prepare the Live/Dead Blue negative control with two drops ArC Amine Negative beads and no dye.
Incubate controls for at least 20 minutes in the dark.
Wash antibody-stained beads with 2 mL FACS buffer and centrifuge at 1,600 rpm for 4 minutes. Do not wash the positive or negative Live/Dead Blue controls in this source workflow.
When matching fixed samples, fix antibody compensation beads with 150 µL of 1% formaldehyde or PFA in HBSS for 15 minutes in a chemical hood. Do not fix the Live/Dead Blue controls in this source workflow.
Wash fixed beads with 2 mL FACS buffer and centrifuge at 1,600 rpm for 5 minutes.
Resuspend controls in 200 µL FACS buffer and keep at 4°C until acquisition.

For spectral cytometry, include an unstained-cell control to model cellular autofluorescence. Single-stained cells are optional but recommended. Beads are preferred when they represent the fluorophore appropriately.

title: Antibody Titration
text:
7. Acquire and select the titer

title: Transduction Retronectin 3
text: This page combines two Retronectin-based transduction workflows. The Retronectin loading volumes, spin duration, virus-production instructions, and post-transduction handling differ. Select one complete source-specific option for each difference and confirm current lab-approved conditions before use.

title: Transduction Retronectin 3
text:
Source files

Alex Monell — Transduction - High Quality
Nicole Sharping — NES 042924 CD8 T cell transduction and double transduction

title: Transduction Retronectin 3
section: 1. Prepare virus and activated CD8 T cells
text:
1. Prepare virus and activated CD8 T cells

Virus-production and detailed activation route
Derived from: Nicole Sharping.

Thaw and expand Plat-E cells beginning five days before transduction, then plate 2 × 106 cells per 10 cm plate two days before transduction.
Transfect Plat-E cells with 2 µg pCL-Eco, 6 µg total plasmid of interest, and 30 µL TransIT-LT1 in 700 µL serum-free DMEM. For double transduction, divide the 6 µg total plasmid across the plasmids of interest.
Coat flat-bottom 6-well plates with anti-CD3 (5 µg/mL for P14 or 10 µg/mL for wild-type CD8 cells), then activate isolated CD8 T cells with anti-CD28 and 50 U/mL hIL-2 for at least 24 hours.



Activation-only route
Derived from: Alex Monell.
Begin with CD8 T-cell isolation and activation. Alex’s source does not include packaging-cell or virus-production instructions.

title: Transduction Retronectin 3
text:
2. Coat and block Retronectin plates

Alex Monell coating route
Derived from: Alex Monell.

Use a non-tissue-culture-treated 6-well plate.
Prepare sufficient Retronectin mixture for the number of wells plus one extra well, add 1 mL per well, wrap the plate carefully with parafilm, and incubate at 4°C overnight.
On the transduction day, remove Retronectin, add 4 mL warmed TCM dropwise to each well, and block for 30 minutes at 37°C.



Nicole Sharping coating route
Derived from: Nicole Sharping.

Prepare Retronectin at 15 µg/mL in sterile PBS and add 1 mL per well of a non-tissue-culture-treated 6-well plate.
Seal the plate and incubate at 4°C overnight.
Remove Retronectin, add 4 mL R10 dropwise to block nonspecific sites, and incubate for 30 minutes at 37°C while warming the centrifuge to 37°C.

title: Transduction Retronectin 3
text:
3. Load virus and transduce cells

Alex Monell transduction route
Derived from: Alex Monell.

Thaw virus in a hot-water bath, then keep it on ice once thawed.
Remove blocking TCM, add 750 µL virus per well, and incubate for 30 minutes at 37°C. Replace with a fresh 750 µL virus aliquot and incubate another 30 minutes.
Pool cells, pellet at 1600 RPM for 4 minutes at room temperature, and prepare TCM plus IL-2 at the source’s stated 1:1667 dilution.
Add 500 µL cell suspension and 1.5 mL virus to each well. Spin at 1600 RPM and 37°C for 40 minutes, then incubate at 37°C for 24 hours.



Nicole Sharping transduction route
Derived from: Nicole Sharping.

Collect viral medium from Plat-E cells and pellet floating packaging cells.
Remove blocking R10, add 1 mL virus per well for 30 minutes at 37°C, then repeat with a second 1 mL virus aliquot for 30 minutes.
Collect activated T cells, pellet them, and resuspend them in remaining viral medium with 50 U/mL IL-2.
Add cells to virus-coated wells, wrap the plate in cellophane, and spin at 1600 RPM and 37°C for 45 minutes. Incubate overnight, then replace medium with fresh R10 plus IL-2 the next morning.

title: Transduction Retronectin 3
text:
4. Follow up after transduction

Alex Monell sorting and transfer route
Derived from: Alex Monell.
On Day 3, collect cell populations separately, wash wells with MACS buffer, pellet at 1600 RPM for 4 minutes, resuspend in MACS buffer, filter cells, sort them into FACS tubes with FBS, wash sorted cells, resuspend in PBS, and count before preparing for transfer.


Nicole Sharping culture route
Derived from: Nicole Sharping.
Maintain cells at 1 × 106/mL with R10 plus IL-2. At 5–6 days after activation, reduce IL-2 to 25 U/mL. Nicole’s source describes proliferation through days 7–10 and viability through days 10–14 after activation.

title: Transduction Retronectin 3
text:

Difference

Virus and T-cell preparation
Begins with CD8 isolation and activation; no Plat-E production procedure is specified. Source: Alex Monell
Gives a five-day Plat-E production timeline plus anti-CD3/anti-CD28/hIL-2 CD8 activation. Source: Nicole Sharping


Retronectin specification
Calls for a Retronectin mixture sufficient for wells plus one extra but does not state a final concentration in the source. Source: Alex Monell

Blocking medium

Virus-loading volumes
Uses two 750 µL virus incubations, then adds 1.5 mL virus with cells. Source: Alex Monell
Uses two 1 mL virus incubations, then resuspends cells in remaining viral medium. Source: Nicole Sharping


Spinoculation
1600 RPM at 37°C for 40 minutes. Source: Alex Monell
1600 RPM at 37°C for 45 minutes. Source: Nicole Sharping


Post-transduction plan
Day 3 cell collection, filtering, sorting, counting, and transfer preparation. Source: Alex Monell

Tissues except SI

title: Preparing mouse joints for histology
text:
Preparing mouse joints for histology
3.7% Formalin solution in PBS:

Dilute 37% Formalin 1 to 10 in PBS

14% EDTA solution:

Add 140 g free acid EDTA to 700 ml distilled H2O
On stir plate in the fume hood, add ammonium hydroxide 30 ml at a time until solution clears (about 90 ml total).
Add H2O to almost 1L. Check pH and adjust with ammonium hydroxide dropwise up to pH 7.2, then adjust final volume to 1L.

Sac mice, remove as much skin from legs as possible.
Harvest paws and knees; immediately fix in 3.7% formalin solution.
Fix for 1 day on shaker at RT.
Rinse with 14% EDTA solution.
Incubate in 14% EDTA solution on shaker at RT for 5 more days. Replace with new 5% EDTA solution daily.
Test if decalcified: bones should feel elastic. A test cut should not have resistance and not feel like cutting sand.
For paraffin embedding, place in 30%, 50%, and 70% ETOH for at least 30 min each prior to submitting to core lab.

title: Tissue Preparation for FFPE Embedding - Xenium
text:
Day 1

Materials:

6 well plate, 1.5mL epi, 15 mL conical
Pre-chilled 1x PBS
Ice
Cold 10% NBF (Sigma Aldrich HT501128)
Minutien pins (Fine Science Tools 2600220)
Scissors, forceps

Gut specific materials*:

Gavage, 10ml syringe
Mouse Intestinal Slicing Tool (MIST) (https://doi.org/10.1002/ame2.12228, DeLucia, et al.)
Silvalume 2.75 mm diameter, 7” length double point knitting needle (https://a.co/d/2F3BP1p)
Thick blotting paper
Clear western blot box
Scalpel Blade size #10 Gut

*as of 9/2/2024 we have no materials for small intestine embedding*


Protocol:

For all tissues: add cold 1x PBS to a 6-well plate on ice to preserve tissues after harvesting
Set shaker incubator in 220 to 4 degrees

If conflicting TD may have to use cloning incubator in 520

Put PBS and 70% EtOH in fridge for Day 2


Small Intestine:

Harvest the small intestine and store it on ice with cold PBS.
The time between harvesting and submersion in NBF should not exceed 30 minutes. The faster the tissue is fixed; the more RNA will be preserved.
Add cold PBS to a clean beaker and have a separate beaker for waste
Cut region of interest of the gut
Flush each section of the gut with 10ml of 1x PBS using a gavage needle, discarding flow-through into the waste beaker. Repeat with 10 mL from other end.
Moisten knitting needle with 1x PBS for ease of loading
Insert the needle through the intestinal lumen
Place loaded needle directly onto blotting paper
Place MIST gently on top of the loaded needle with even force
Along MIST’s cutting guide, use a scalpel to cut open the intestine longitudinally
Carefully remove the MIST and spread intestine onto the work surface as you remove the needle (villi will be facing up)
Add minutien pin to each corner of the tissue and along the edges as needed (4-8 pins along the edges)
Add pre-chilled 10% NBF to a plastic container and submerge the pinned tissue. Close lid.
Incubate in 10% NBF for 24 hours at 4ºC in the dark.



Mesenteric lymph node (mLN)

Harvest mLN in cold PBS
Place mLN in 1.5ml epi
Add 1ml of 10% NBF
Incubate for 24 hours on rocker at 4ºC in the dark



Spleen, Salivary Gland, Kidney

Harvest spleen in cold PBS
Add to 15 ml conical
Add 10 ml of cold 10% NBF

I bring 10mL of NBF in 15mL conical tubes directly to mouse room. Put spleen in PBS first then move to NBF

Incubate for 24 hours in shaker incubator (set to 4 degrees)



Prostate

Cut rubber squares and place in 6 well plate
Harvest prostate in cold PBS
Clean up and place organs in the same orientation on the rubber
Use 3 pins to pin the prostate on both seminal vesicles and the bladder
Add 8 mL of cold 10% NBF, or enough to submerge the tissue
Incubate 24 hours at 4ºC in the dark

Submerge tissue in pre-chilled 70% ethanol

Prepare a 2% agar solution and equilibrate the temperature to 45-50ºC in a water bath
Roll the gut into a Swiss roll with the villi facing out

Allow agar to solidify completely on ice

10.Place the Swiss roll stabilized with agar into a cassette labelled with a pencil and add to a bottle filled with chilled 70% ethanol
Send to Moore’s Cancer Center Histology Core for FFPE embedding *Can be stored short term in 70% ethanol at 4ºC



mLN, Spleen, SG, Kidney, and Prostate

Remove tissue from NBF and wash with cold PBS twice
Place tissue in 15mL or 50mL conical with 70% EtOH

Orientation should be specified in Fred Hutch form in the paraffin block

Add chilled 70% ethanol to tissue and incubate 3 hours*
Tell Lab Ops when sample is ready so they can take to Fred Hutch for FFPE embedding. I usually print FH histology form and give to Lab Ops and also email a copy to the FH histology core exphisto@fredhutch.org

*Can be stored short-term in 70% ethanol at 4ºC, up to 24h (overnight)

title: insitu_tetramer_CD8_Tcells
text:
PROTOCOL
1. Day 1: Fresh Tissue Sectioning and Primary Incubation

Use a scalpel to cut fresh tissue into small (approximately 0.5 cm wide by 0.5 cm tall) pieces. Separately glue each tissue to a plunger and embed them with 3 - 5 mL of 4% low-melt agarose in PBS. Label the plunger with the tissue information using a sticker. Put it in a chilled holder in an ice bucket to solidify.
Turn on the microtome and set the thickness of the sections to 200 µm. Install a razor blade on the microtome and insert the plunger mounted with tissue in the microtome bath.
Prepare phosphate-buffered saline with heparin (PBS-H) by adding 100 µg/mL or 18.7 U/mL heparin to PBS to preserve the RNA and to permit potential ISH applications downstream. Fill the microtome bath, covering the embedded tissue, with 100 - 120 mL of chilled, sterile PBS-H. Add PBS-H ice cubes to the bath to maintain the temperature at 0 - 2 °C. Start the microtome and cut the tissue into 200 µm sections.
Note: It is important to keep the tissues chilled on ice to minimize cellular activity within the tissues and because fresh tissue is easier to section when it is chilled. PBS alone can be used if there are no plans for downstream ISH.
ALTERNATIVELY: Use hand-held microtome
Alternatively, for tissues that do not cut well with a microtome (e.g., gut and lung), use a scalpel or razor blade to cut the tissue into thin strips as close as possible to 200 µm.
Label the lid of 24-well tissue culture plates with the experimental sample information and place the tissue chambers in the corresponding wells. Use a paintbrush to transfer the sections to a tissue chamber set in the well of a 24-well tissue culture plate containing 1 mL of chilled PBS-H.

NOTE: Reusable tissue chambers should be made prior to initiating staining. Tissue chambers can be made using a 14 mL polypropylene round-bottom snap-cap tube and wire mesh. Use a sharp razor blade to cut the bottom of a 14 mL polypropylene round-bottom snap-cap tube off. Cut the wire mesh in a circle to fit the hole at the bottom of the tube. Heat the wire mesh circle using a Bunsen burner until it is red-hot. Set the wire mesh circle down very quickly and push the tube onto the mesh. Check that the wire mesh is securely attached to the bottom of the tube and then carefully cut off the top of the tube at the 3 mL mark using a sharp razor blade. Put up to 3 tissue sections into each tissue chamber, or up to 1 cm2 of tissue per well. Keep at least one empty well between wells with different antibody combinations to avoid cross-contamination.

Proceed to the primary tetramer and antibody staining immediately after finishing the transfer of all cut sections into the tissues chambers. Keep the sections submerged and chilled in 1 mL of PBS-H at all times.
Incubate the tissue sections overnight with 0.5 µg/mL FITC-conjugated, peptide-loaded MHC-I tetramers diluted in PBS-H with 2% normal goat serum (NGS). Include mouse or other non-rabbit antibodies directed at extracellular epitopes of interest in this incubation (e.g., rat anti-CD8 antibodies diluted 1:500 in PBS-H with 2% NGS). Place 1 mL of diluted antibodies in each well.

NOTE: Care should be taken when selecting CD8 antibodies, as some can enhance and some can inhibit MHC tetramers binding to T-cell receptors4,21. The rat anti-human CD8 antibody described here is unstable and sometimes results in somewhat weak staining. It is used here for triple labeling because it is the only non-rabbit and non-mouse CD8 antibody tested that stained rhesus macaque CD8 T cells.

Use 1 mL of solution per well for the primary antibody and all subsequent incubations, and perform this and all subsequent incubations at 4 °C, with the plates on a rocking platform.
NOTE: Tissues should float freely in the chamber.

2. Day 2: Fixation and Secondary Incubation

After the primary incubation, wash the sections twice with 1 mL of chilled PBS-H for 20 min each wash. Do this by transferring the tissue chambers to a different 24-well tissue culture plate containing 1 mL of chilled PBS-H in the corresponding wells.
NOTE: Be careful not to drip contents from one experimental sample into another when moving between tissue chambers. For all subsequent incubations and washes, similarly transfer the tissue chamber to a clean plate containing the appropriate solution. Be sure to monitor the sections in the tissue chambers during the procedure to make sure that the sections do not get stuck to the sides of the tissue chambers. If they do, push them back into the solution.
Fix the sections with 1 mL of fresh PBS-buffered 4% paraformaldehyde for 2 h at room temperature (do not over-fix). Wash with cold PBS-H twice for 5 min.
Caution: Paraformaldehyde is toxic; wear appropriate personal protective equipment.
NOTE: If antigen retrieval and permeabilization is needed to detect intracellular epitopes, antigens can be retrieved by boiling the sections in 0.01 mol urea after the paraformaldehyde fixation.
Transfer the sections into 24-well culture plates containing 0.01 mol urea and place these plates in a microwave oven. Boil the sections three times for about 10 s each, for a total of 30 s.
NOTE: Be very careful, as boiling the solution can force the sections out of the wells. If this happens, use a paintbrush to push the sections from the sides of the tissue chamber or from the lid of the plate back into the bottom of the appropriate tissue chamber.
Prior to the secondary antibody incubation, permeabilize and block the tissue sections by incubating them in blocking solution containing PBS-H, 0.3% detergent (PBS-H-T), and 2% NGS on a rocker for 1 h at 4 °C. Perform subsequent antibody incubations with PBS-H-T/2% NGS.
For the secondary incubation, transfer the sections in the tissue chambers to wells containing rabbit anti-FITC antibody diluted 1:10,000 in PBS-H-T/2% NGS. Incubate overnight.
Perform counterstaining using mouse anti-CD20 antibody diluted 1:200 in PBS-H-T/2% NGS. For this option, retrieve the epitopes if needed, permeate the cells, and block prior to this incubation, as described above.

3. Day 3: Tertiary Incubation

After the second incubation, wash the sections three times in PBS-H at 4 °C for at least 20 min.
Perform a final incubation with the appropriate fluorescently labeled antibodies (e.g., goat anti-rabbit conjugated greenish yellow, goat anti-rat conjugated far red dye, and goat anti-mouse conjugated green dye antibodies diluted 1:5,000, 1:5,000, and 1:2,000, respectively, in PBS-H-T/2% NGS). Incubate overnight.
NOTE: At this point, the incubation can be extended for up to three days if needed. Keep the sections protected from light by wrapping the plates in tin foil during this incubation step and thereafter, as light quenches fluorophores.

4. Day 4: Mounting the Sections

Wash the sections three times in PBS-H for at least 20 min.
NOTE: If planning for downstream ISH19, fix the sections in 4% paraformaldehyde for 1 h to secure the tetramers and antibodies in place and then wash the sections twice with PBS-H for 5 min each.
Caution: Paraformaldehyde is toxic; wear appropriate personal protective equipment.
Use a paintbrush to transfer the sections to a microscope slide. Be careful not to poke the tissue too much. Coat each section with glycerol/gelatin containing 4 mg/mL n-propyl gallate or another mounting medium containing a fluorophore preservative. Cover with a coverslip.
Store the slides in a light-protected slide container at -20 °C. Rinse the tissue culture plates and remove the labels on the lids using alcohol.
NOTE: The plates can be reused.

5. Acquisition of Confocal Microscope Images

Capture high-resolution images with a confocal microscope, using the appropriate lasers and filters for each fluorophore (Figure 1A and B).
NOTE: In this example, a confocal microscope (see the Table of Materials) was used. Images were collected using the 561 nm laser at 20% power for the greenish yellow-labeled antigen-specific T cells, the 488-nm laser at 10% power for green-labeled CD20-expressing B cells, and the 640-nm laser at 15% power for far red-labelled CD8 T cells. The 20X objective and a numerical aperture of 0.8 were used.
Sequentially collect z-series at 3 µm (or other) intervals in the three channels in multiple 800 x 800 pixel fields. Construct a montage of the collected fields (Figure 1C-E). Name each montage image based on the information of the corresponding slide and save for analysis.
Perform quantitative image analysis using the respective confocal microscope analysis and quantification software or using ImageJ.

6. Quantitative Image Analysis
NOTE: Quantitative image analysis can be accomplished using confocal microscope analysis and quantification software or by using ImageJ software. Here, ImageJ was used as an example.

Open a confocal montage by dragging it to the ImageJ window (Figure 2A).
NOTE: ImageJ can directly open montages collected by many different confocal microscopes. If the montage cannot be directly opened by ImageJ, export the selected z-scan as a TIFF file to open it.
Duplicate the selected z-scan for analysis (“Image”-> “Duplicate”) (Figure 2B).
Split the different channels (“Image”-> “Color”-> “Split Channels”) (Figure 2C).
Draw the ROI for quantitative analysis in the corresponding channel to be objective and add it to the ROI manager by pressing “T” on the keyboard. Measure the area.
NOTE: The ROI manager of ImageJ shows the area in µm2 (Figure 2D).
Adjust the fluorescence brightness and contrast of the channel to be analyzed (“Image” -> “Adjust” -> “Brightness/Contrast”) (Figure 2E).
Flatten the ROI on the image (“ROI manager” -> “Flatten”) (Figure 2F).
Quantify the positive cells in the image using the “Multi-point” tool (Figure 2G).

title: Histology of the Gut–OCT
text:
Frozen HISTOLOGY of the GUT
01/2020 - LLB
Procedure for OCT sections:
1) Take down one mouse at a time (it’s a time-sensitive thing! Gut will lose its architecture super fast). 
2) Pull out gut (I typically grab the intestine by the stomach, cut it from the stomach and pull it vertically). Cut the 3-5cm piece you are interested in (I typically do ileum, but you can do duodenum, jejunum, ileum, colon). Put tissue on a paper tissue, squirt some PBS1x with pasteur pipette and remove feces by gently pushing with scissors. Cut/open the gut longitudinally, mucus facing up and muscle down. Keep it relatively moist with pasteur pipette+PBS1x. **Don’t worry about removing fat, it’s part of the natural structure of the gut and won’t hurt for OCT sectioning.
     *Don’t do any washing steps. Unnecessary and they will damage structure!
3) Have a cassette filled with OCT ready.
4) Make swiss roll with wooden stick (I use cotton swab sticks): place stick below (on the muscle side). Now roll gut put muscle touching stick, mucus is in the outside. 
     *When rolling don’t force tissue into roll. Move stick forward instead of force-rolling the tissue around it (tissue is super soft)
5) Once rolled place in cassette filled with OCT by putting stick vertical on cassette and pushing tissue down with forceps. Try to embed it flat. Add more OCT on top. 
- Procedure for Paraffin sections:
1) Take down one mouse at a time (it’s a time-sensitive thing! Gut will lose its architecture super fast). 
2) Pull out gut, remove feces by gently pushing with scissors, put on tissue and cut/open longitudinally, mucus facing up and muscle down. Keep it relatively moist with pasteur pipette+PBS.
     *Don’t do any washing steps. Unnecessary and they will damage structure!
3) Cut in 2-3cm pieces (one distal, medial, proximal). Have a cassette ready with 2 sponges with holes made by the cut plastic stick. 
4) Make swiss roll with wooden stick: place stick below (on the muscle side). Now roll gut put muscle touching stick, mucus is in the outside. 
     *When rolling don’t force tissue into roll. Move stick forward instead of force-rolling the tissue around it (tissue is super soft)
5) Once rolled place in cassette in between sponges (to flatten it). Remove stick, close cassette and dump in fixative (this has to be done within 10min after death). Fix in 10% Formalin solution (=4% Paraformaldehyde) +1mM CaCl2 in PBS1x for 24h at RT (24h preserves epitopes pretty well. Some people fix for 48h, but you risk losing epitopes).
6) After fixation, dump PFA in appropriate biohazard container, and wash with deoinized water twice (dump fixative, fill bottle with water - let sit for 5min for every wash).  
7) Place in 70% EtOH (70% EtOH preserves tissue for longer than just PBS).
8) Bring to the core for embedding/sectioning in 70% Ethanol. (Tissues can remain in ethanol for days/weeks before being sent in to the core)

title: RNA extraction & cDNA synthesis & RT-qPCR from CD8
text:
RNA extraction, cDNA synthesis, and RT-qPCR
Qiagen RNAeasy mini kit- Cell lysis and spin column

If purifying RNA from cell lines rich in RNases, or tissue, add either 10 µL β-mercaptoethanol (β-ME), or 20 µL 2 M dithiothreitol (DTT), to 1 mL Buffer RLT. Buffer RLT with β-ME or DTT can be stored at room temperature for up to 1 month.
Preassemble RNeasy® Mini spin columns with Waste Tubes (provided).
Make sure the ethanol has been added to buffer prior to starting
Harvest a maximum of 1e7 cells, as a cell pellet or by direct lysis in the vessel.
Add 350 ul of Buffer RLT supplemented with BME and pipette vigorously to disrupt the cell pellet. Can pause and freeze at -80 at this step. Keep cold.
If you freeze cells in RLT buffer, thaw at 37C quickly.
Apply 350 ul of cells/RLT buffer to a Qiashredder and spin at max speed for 2 min
Add 1 volume (350 ul if used 350 ul RLT lysis buffer) of 70% ethanol to the 350 ul of RLT that passed through the Qiashredder.
Mix well by pipetting, do not centrifuge.
Transfer up to 700 µL of the sample, including any precipitate, to a RNeasy Mini spin column placed in a 2 mL waste tube (supplied). Close the lid, and centrifuge for 15 s at ≥8000 x g. Discard the flow-through and reuse the waste tube.

Dnase digestion
Follow steps 1–4 of “Appendix D: Optional On Column DNase Digestion with the RNase Free DNase” in the QIAwave RNA Mini Handbook if using cultured cells to remove genomic DNA. These steps are:

Prepare DNase I stock solution before using kit for first time by dissolving lyophilized DNase I in 550 ul of RNase-free water. Do not open vial, inject water into vial using needle and syringe. Mix gently by inverting. Do not vortex. Let sit at RT for 10 min to dissolve.
For long-term storage, aliquot and store at -20. Do not refreeze aliquots.
After the sample has been spun through the RNeasy mini spin column, add 350 ul of buffer RW1 to the spin column. Close lid gently and centrifuge for 15 s at 8000g to wash column. Discard flowthrough
Add 10 ul of DNase I stock solution made above to 70 ul of buffer RDD for each sample. We made 800 ul total- 100 ul of DNase I and 700 ul of buffer RDD for 8 samples. Mix stock by inverting tube and centrifuge briefly to collect residual liquid from sides of tube. Do not vortex!
Add 80 ul of DNase I mix directly to RNeasy spin column membrane and incubate at RT for 15 min. Make sure to add DNase incubation mix directly to column membrane as digestion will be incomplete if it sticks to the column membrane.

Column wash and RNA elution

Add 350 ul of buffer RW1 to RNeasy spin column. Close lid gently, centrifuge for 15 sec at 8000xg. Discard flow through.
Add 500 ul of buffer RPE to spin column. Close lid gently, centrifuge for 15 sec at 8000xg. Discard flow through.
Add 500 ul of buffer RPE to spin column. Close lid gently, centrifuge for 15 sec at 8000xg. Discard flow through.
Place spin column in a new collection tube and spin at full speed for 1 min to dry membrane.
Place spin column in a new 1.5 ml collection tube with lid and add 30 ul of rNase free water directly to spin column membrane. Close lid, centrifuge for 1 min at 8000xg to elute RNA. If low amount of RNA, can incubate at RT for 3 min prior to 1 min spin.
For second elution step, add 30 ul of eluted RNA in step 10 back onto the column to increase RNA yield. Remember to incubate at RT for 3 min again before spin.

cDNA synthesis – Applied Bio High Capacity cDNA reverse transcriptase

Allow kit components to thaw on ice
Calculate the volume needed to prepare the fllowing reactions on ice
Prepare 2x reverse transcription master mix and place on ice when done. Make sure to make a no RT control where you don’t add reverse transcriptase and just add water to see how much junk there is.



10x RT buffer: 2 ul per 10 ul reaction
25x dNTP mix (100 mM): 0.8 ul per 10 ul reaction
10x RT random primers: 2 ul per 10 ul reaction
Multiscribe reverse transcriptase: 1 ul per 10 ul reaction
Nuclease-free H20: 4.2 ul per 10 ul reaction



Mix 2x mix gently
Pipette 10 ul of 2x RT master mix into each well/PCR tube
Pipette 10 ul of RNA sample into each well/tube. Pipette up and down to mix
Seal plate/tubes
Briefly centrifuge tubes to spin down contents and eliminate air bubbles
Place plate/tubes on ice until ready to load in thermal cycler.

Thermal cycler settings: Step 1: 25C for 10 min. Step 2: 37C for 120 min. Step 3: 85C for 5 min. Step 4: 4C for hold

Set reaction volume to 20 ul
Load and start run.

Flow to check for Thy1 knockout


Move cells from culture plate to v-bottom 96 well plate for flow


Wash 1x with FACS


Resuspend in 50 ul of master mix for 20 min at 4C



L/D APC-Cy7 (1:1000)


CD8b FITC (1:100)


Thy1.2 BV510 (1:100)



Wash 2x with FACS


Flow


qPCR
From this point onwards, work on ice.
Primer Dilution Prep

Determine how much primer is needed in qPCR reaction (1.25 ul FWD, 1.25 ul RVS primer per 1x master mix)
Dilute primers 1:5 in nuclease-free water
Vortex briefly and spin down each tube. These are your working primer solutions.

qPCR Reaction Setup
Prepare Reaction Mix:

Calculate the number of reactions needed per gene target (samples + controls + extras for pipetting error).
Prepare a master mix for each gene target (Target Gene and Housekeeping Gene) separately to ensure consistency. For N reactions, mix the following in a fresh tube:

SYBR Green Master Mix (2x): 12.5 μl * N
Respective Diluted Primer Mix: 1.25 μl * N
Nuclease-free water: (27 – MM which is 15 ul) = 12 ul ddH20

Vortex the master mix gently and spin down.
Aliquot 27 μl of the appropriate master mix into each well of your qPCR plate/tube.
Dilute cDNA samples 1:5 with nuclease-free water (3 ul of cDNA with 12 ul H2O)
Add 3 μl of cDNA sample to the corresponding wells. For NTC wells, add 3 μl of nuclease-free water instead of cDNA. Total reaction volume per well: 30 μl. For the no RT wells, add samples prepared in cDNA synthesis step and master mix. Total reaction volume per well: 30 ul.
Seal the qPCR plate/tubes securely. Briefly centrifuge the plate/tubes to collect the contents at the bottom of the wells and remove air bubbles.

qPCR Instrument Run

Place the plate/tubes into the qPCR machine.
Use Angelica’s standard SYBR Green protocol suitable for your master mix and instrument. A typical protocol is:

Initial Denaturation: 95°C for 2-10 minutes (check master mix recommendations)
Cycling (e.g., 40 cycles):

Denaturation: 95°C for 10-30 seconds
Annealing/Extension: 60-65°C for 30-60 seconds (ensure fluorescence data acquisition at this step)

Melt Curve Analysis: Standard melt curve program (e.g., 95°C for 15s, 60°C for 60s, then ramp slowly to 95°C with continuous fluorescence acquisition). This helps check for primer dimers or non-specific amplification.
Optimization: Cycling conditions, especially the annealing/extension temperature and time, may need optimization based on the specific primers, target sequence, and master mix used. Primer efficiency should ideally be validated.


Data Analysis
This describes the common Livak method (ΔΔCt).

Obtain Ct Values: Export the cycle threshold (Ct) values for all samples and controls for both the Target Gene and Housekeeping Gene from the qPCR software.

Validate Controls: Ensure NTCs show no or very late amplification (e.g., Ct > 35). Check No RT controls for minimal signal compared to cDNA samples.
Check Melt Curves: Verify single, specific peaks at the expected melting temperature for each gene.

Calculate ΔCt (Delta Ct) for each sample: Normalize the Ct value of the Target Gene to the Ct value of the Housekeeping Gene for each sample. ΔCt = Ct(Target Gene) - Ct(Housekeeping Gene)
Select a Control/Reference Sample: Choose one sample (or the average of a control group) as the reference calibrator (e.g., untreated sample, time point zero).
Calculate ΔΔCt (Delta-Delta Ct): Calculate the difference between the ΔCt of each sample and the ΔCt of the reference/calibrator sample. ΔΔCt = ΔCt(Sample) - ΔCt(Reference Sample)
Calculate Relative Expression Fold Change: Calculate the fold change in gene expression for each sample relative to the reference sample using the formula:


Note
If you calculate ΔCt as Ct(Housekeeping Gene) - Ct(Target Gene), the final formula becomes . Ensure consistency in your calculations.


Interpretation & Further Analysis: The calculated Relative Expression value represents the fold change in the target gene’s expression in a given sample compared to the reference sample, after normalization to the housekeeping gene.

Step 1: Open the Completed Run File

Open the CFX Maestro or CFX Manager software on the computer connected to your system.
Click on the View Post-Run Data tab or go to File > Open > Data File.
Select your completed .pcrd run file and click Analyze Data.

Step 2: View and Format the Data Sheets

By default, the software opens to the Quantification tab (showing your standard thermal cycling curves).
Click on the Melt Curve tab next to it.
Look at the lower half of the screen to find the data spreadsheets associated with that tab. You will see tabs like Melt Peaks, RFU Spreadsheet, and -d(RFU)/dT Spreadsheet. 

Step 3: Export All Data Sheets to Excel
The absolute fastest way to get all your thermal cycle and melt curve matrices at once is to export the entire workbook:

In the main top menu bar of the software, click on Export.
From the dropdown menu, select Export All Data Sheets to Excel.
Choose a destination folder (such as a USB drive or local directory), name your file, and click Save.

title: Labeling T cells with CFSE
text:
Labeling T cells with CFSE…Beautiful Peaks Guaranteed

Wash lymphocytes in PBS 0.1%BSA twice to remove FCS.
Resuspend at 2x 107 cells/mL in PBS 0.1%PBS which has been prewarmed to 37C. Add 2μL of 5mM CFSE stock (in DMSO) per mL of cells while vortexing for 10μM final. This step is very important for getting good, tight peaks: you want all of the cells to get exposed to the same concentration of CFSE at the same time (use a 50 mL tube if labeling more than 5 mLs of cells, also I would not suggest labeling more than 10 mLs at a time if possible).
Incubate t 37C in dark for 10 minutes.
Top off tube with cold RP20% FCS spin down and wash twice more.
For last wash, put cells through nytex and wash in RPMI no FCS, count before spinning down and resuspend in RPMI (no FCS) at appropriate concentration (don’t do this last wash until you are headed to the mousehouse).

title: Antibody purification
text:
Purification of Antibodies:
Equipment:
HiTrap Protein G column –
Peristaltic Pump or syringe
Collection tubes (FACS tubes work really well) with 100 ul of Tris pH 9.0
Protocol:
Important things to remember:
Peristaltic Pump:

Run Sodium Phosphate buffer pH 7.0 into the tubing to equilibrate it until it begins dripping out the side with the metal lock. Stop the flow.
Place column onto a metal stand
Attach the metal lock to the column using the red adaptor then continue the flow. This is known as adding it ‘drop-to-drop’, which prevents air from entering the column.
Run 5x the volume of the column (25 ml) of Sodium Phosphate buffer pH 7.0 over the column and save the flow through.
Begin running your antibody supernatant over the column…make sure to use a new collection tube once the supernatant reaches the column.
Once all of your supernatant has been collected, run another 5 volumes of Sodium Phosphate buffer pH 7.0.
Elute the antibody using 0.1M Glycine buffer, pH 2.8. 20 fractions of approximately 1 ml each is good. For this small a volume, 30 ml syringes work well to add the glycine. Just make sure to put the syringe on ‘drop-to-drop’ to avoid air entering the column.
Once eluted, attach the column onto the metal stand once again, and run 5 bed volumes of 20% EtOH through it. The column can be stored at 4°C until later use. The tubing can stay attached until later use.
Set up a 96-well plate with the following for each fraction (don’t forget pos and neg controls too!):

20 ul sample
20 ul biorad protein assay dye (Cat # 500-0006)
60 ul H20




Collect the fractions that turn the darkest blue – these contain the eluted antibody!
Use spin collection tubes to concentrate the antibody (see tube directions for how)
Use a protein assay kit (BioRad) to analyze the concentration of your antibody.

Harvest tissue into RPMI

Transfer to a 15 ml conical

Aspirate and discard supernatant

Aspirate and discard supernatant

text:
If it is not possible to validate the KO of a Crispr/Cas9 with Flow (or western), one can check if a deletion was introduced on the genomic DNA of the cells.
For that you need: ## Materials - At least 100.000 cells from your treated and control T cells - Kit to isolate genomic DNA (e.g. QIAamp DNA Blood Kits) - Primers to amplify the target region (see details below) - High-Fidelity Polymerase (e.g. Q5) - A PCR purification kit (e.g. DNA Clean & Concentrator-5)

title: Crispr KO validation
text:
Primer design
You need to sequence a stretch of DNA ~700bp enclosing the designed editing site. The projected break site should be located preferably ~200bp downstream from the sequencing start site. This region upstream of the break site is used to align the sequencing data of the test sample with that of the control sample.
I use use CHOPCHOP to design these primers. Under “Options” -> “Primers” select a product size between 500 and 800bp and a minimal distance from primer to target site of 200bp.



CHOPCHOP options


Next, click “Find target sites” and select your guideRNA. Here you can select one of the suggested primers.

Alternatively, you can design the primers as described here

title: ChIP protocol
text:
Goldrath Lab ChIP Protocol
Fixation:
-Harvest cells (between 10-60 million but 40 million is optimum) and place them in 10mL media or PBS
-Add 270ul 37% formaldehyde (to make 1% formaldehyde) and incubate for 10 minutes and RT
-Stop the reaction with 1000ul 1.25M glycine (to make .125M glycine) and incubate for 5 minutes at RT
-Spin the cells down and wash once with ice cold 10 mL PBS. You can flash freeze the cells at this point if you wish to sonicate at a later time.
-Spin again and resuspend in 1000ul Lysis Buffer. Add fresh protease inhibitors (PIC cocktail and benzamidine) to the solution. Incubate on ice for 5 minutes.
Sonication:
-Sonicate 8 times (amplitude 20%) for 10 seconds each time. Between each sonication rest the cells on ice for 30-60 seconds. Keep lysate on ice as much as possible and try to avoid creating bubbles. (use Branson 250 sonicator and 1/8 inch probe).
-Spin down sonicated lysate (5min at 13K rpm) to get rid of debris. Put the supernatant (the lysate) in a new eppendorf tube. The lysate can be stored at -80C or used immediately.
-To test the sonication efficiency take 50ul of lysate. Add 100ul of water and incubate overnight at 65C to reverse the crosslinks.
-Add 1 ul RNase A (stock at 100mg/ml) and incubate at 37C for 30 minutes. Add 2ul proteinase K (stock at 20mg/ml) and incubate at 55C for 1 hour.
-Extract DNA using Qiagen Qiaquik purification kit.
-Measure absorbance at 260nm (use a 1:50 dilution of DNA in 1X TE). Multiply by 2500 to get DNA in ug/ml.
-run 10ul of DNA on a 1% agarose gel to test sonication (should see a smear around 500-1000bp).
Immunoprecipitation:
-use 10ug of DNA/Immunoprecipitation (using more can decrease the efficiency of the pulldown).
-Dilute with 9 volumes of Dilution Buffer. Add protease inhibitors (PIC cocktail and benzamidine) to the solution.
-Add 2-10ug antibody and rotate overnight at 4C. Remember to save an input sample (no antibody added, leave at 4C until elution step).
-Add 30ul protein G agarose beads (preadsorbed against BSA and salmon sperm DNA from Cell Signaling Technology) to each IP and rotate for 2hours at 4C. Use tips with the ends cut off when handling the protein G beads.
-Spin down complexes for 30 seconds at 8000rpm and discard the supernatant. Resuspend the beads in 1mL WBI, rotate at 4C for 5minutes and spin as before.
-Repeat wash with WBII, WBIII and two times with 1X TE.
-Elute with 200ul Elution Buffer and shake for 30 minutes at 65C then reverse the crosslinks overnight at 65C. Remember to reverse crosslink your input sample as well (add 50ul of input to 200ul of Elution Buffer).
DNA extraction:
-Add 1ul of RNase A (stock at 100mg/ml) and incubate at 37C for 30minutes. Add 2ul of proteinase K (stock at 20mg/ml) and incubate at 55C for 1 hour.
-Spin down sample as before and transfer the supernatant to a new tube (this is the eluted DNA/protein complexes. Discard the beads).
-Extract DNA with Qiagen Qiaquik purification kit. Elute in 55ul elution buffer. Be sure to bind at 6000xg, other spins at max speed. Incubate elution buffer and column for 1 minute before spinning for maximum yield.

title: CB2.Calcium flux assay
text:
Purpose: to quantify calcium flux upon T cell activation.
Note: Started from Ca++ flux protocol from “Liu et al. “T Cell Receptor–initiated Calcium Release Is Uncoupled from Capacitative Calcium Entry in Itk-deficient T Cells” J. Exp. Med. 1998, and modified from this starting protocol.

Start from activated, transduced cells that spent at least 2 days in culture after transduction
Collect cells from same condition/congenic marker together and count them – mix cells 1:1
From here split cells in one tube for each stim condition you have below at step 11.
Stain 1.0-1.2x10^6 total cells per stim/tube with 50 nM X-Rhod-1 AM (1:25,000; Molecular Probes) and 0.02% Pluronic F-127 (1:100; Invitrogen) in HBSS-/- for 30 minutes at 37ºC with gentle agitation (pipette every 10 minutes). Stain samples in 300 µL. Always make 1 tube extra when preparing the mix. Optional: Keep unstained cells for later.
Wash 1 time with HBS; resuspend cells at 1x10^6 /mL with R10 and incubate for 45 minutes at 37ºC.
Incubate cells with anti-CD3-biotin (final: 10 µg/ml; 1:50 dilution form stock), anti-CD45.1-APC or anti-CD45.2-APC (1:200 dilution from stock) and Thy1.2-FITC (1:1,000 dilution from stock) in PBS for 20 mins at RT. Stain samples in 100 µL. Always consider 1 tube extra when preparing the mix.
Wash 3 times with HBS; resuspend at 1x10^6 /mL with R10 and keep at 37ºC until ready to use
When ready for acquisition spin cells down 1600 rpm for 5 minutes, resuspend as indicated in step 9 and transfer to FACS tubes. Each condition/tube you run wants 1.0-1.2x10^6 cells total.
When running your experiment on the Fortessa, cells will be run in 300uL HBSS with 0.5mM Ca++ (for stim a) or 300uL plain HBSS (for stim b & c), so stim conditions will be made at 10x concentrations in 10% of the volume (30uL):

Streptavidin (SA): final 40 µg/ml, make 10x (30 µL) [dilute stock 1:2.3, get 30µL from dilution]
Ionomycin: final concentration of 1 µg/mL, make 10x (30 µL) [dilute stock 1:100, get 30µL from dilution]
Ca++: final 0.5 mM, make 10x (30uL) [dilute stock 1:10, get 30µL from dilution]
TG: final 2 µM, make 10x (30 µL)

For stim b = dilute stock 1:100, get 30µL from dilution
For stim c = add 0.4 µL stock to 30 µL of stock Ryanodin

Xestospongin C: final 1 µM, make 10x (30 µL) [add 3.3 µL stock to 30 µL of stock TG+Ryanodin]
Ryanodin: final 100 µM, stock is already 10x – just add 30 µL from stock to sample when ready
EGTA: final 3 mM, stock is already 10x – just add 30 µL from stock to sample when ready

Wash cells, resuspend in 300uL HBSS with 0.5mM Ca++ (for stim a) or 300uL plain HBSS (for stim b), and set up Fortessa. Make sure to have unstained control for calcium flux dyes. X-rhod-1 AM (in PE-CF594 channel) gets brighter when binds to calcium, so set negative on unstained control.
Have stim conditions listed below; each sample gets run for minutes indicated below:

30sec baseline, +Ionomycin 5min
30sec baseline, +TG 3mins, +Ca++ 2mins, +EGTA 3min
30sec baseline, +TG/Ryanodin/Xestospongin 3mins, +Ca++ 2mins, +EGTA 3min

title: BTSSR viable Lymphocyte collection protocol 10222014
text:
PURPOSE:



To define a standard operating procedure for optimal fluid tissue (Blood) acquisition and for maintaining the quality of the fluid tissue (Blood) for the Biorepository Tissue Technology Shared Resources (BTTSR) of the UCSD Moores Cancer Center.





POLICY:



Policy on standard operating procedure for Peripheral Blood Leukocytes for Biorepository Tissue Technology Shared Resource.




WORKPLACE SAFETY:
Proper precautions on exposure to fluid tissue (blood) specimens, on handling tissue specimens, hazardous chemicals and biohazard as well as infectious waste by using the required Personal Protective Equipment when appropriate:
Eyewear
Mask
Apron
Gloves
Laboratory Gown
Proper hand washing: Hand washing should be done as often as possible especially after removing gloves and before handling food and before touching any clean surface. Hands should be washed with soap and warm water for at least 20 seconds.
Injury at work: Any injury must be reported to the appropriate staff or Project investigator within 24 hours to complete and sign an incident report.


Materials and/Supplies:

BD Vacutainer sodium Heparin blood collection tube
P-1000 pipetman
P-200 pipetman
P-1000,P-200 filter tips
Tube racks
10 ml serological pipets
5 ml serological pipets
Pipet man
Pre labeled 2.0 ml Cryovials
15 ml conicals
50ml conical
Eppendorf tube
Centrifuge
Density Gradient medium
Sterile disposable towels
Sterile gloves
Marking pens or pencils
Styrofoam containers
Chipped ice
-80 Freezer
LN2 freezer

Tissue Acquisition Policy

Fluid tissue (blood) acquisition are directed to the following:

Dr. Vandenberg – UCSD, Professor of Pathology and Director of Neuropathology. Director of Biorepository Tissue Technology Shared Resource of UCSD Moores Cancer Center 858-822-7661
Under our approved IRB protocol 090401 for human subject research
svandenberg@ucsd.edu
http://cancer.ucsd.edu
ccbr@ad.ucsd.edu
http://cancer.ucsd.edu/research-training/shared-resources/biorepository/Pages/default.aspx


Fluid tissue Collection (blood)

The patient must be consented on the IRB approved protocol. Plan and consent.
The consenting is performed by the research coordinator or the research associate.
Once the patient is consented the research coordinator or the research associate follow up for lab appointment and Phlebotomist collects blood 20 ml in sodium heparin blood collection tube
The research coordinator or the research associate will collect donor’s demographic data and Doctor’s details.
Confirm patient’s diagnosis and medical information from EPIC
De identified patient ID and assign Project Id # number.


Fluid Tissue Processing


Collection of Peripheral Blood Leukocytes from Venipuncture

Collect blood via venipuncture into sodium heparin blood collection (green top) tubes.
Warm density gradient medium (ie. Lymphoprep), dilution/wash medium (ie. DPBS or HBSS) and centrifuge to room temperature.
Aliquot 4 ml of room temperature density gradient medium into sterile 15 ml conical tubes (plan 2 tubes for each 10 ml tube of blood collected).
Wipe the outside of the blood collection tubes with 70% ethanol.
Carefully remove the caps from the blood collection tubes.
Decant blood into sterile 50 ml conical tube.
Add 8 ml of sterile room temperature wash medium to each blood collection tube.
Using a 10 ml pipette, transfer wash medium from blood collection tubes to 50 ml conical tube containing blood (approximately 1:1 dilution).
Mix diluted blood by inverting 50 ml conical tube 2-3 times.
Using a 10 ml pipette, carefully transfer 8-10 ml of diluted blood to each 15 ml conical tube containing density gradient medium. Deliver the diluted blood slowly to the top of the density gradient medium, being careful to not disrupt the medium/blood interface.
Centrifuge density gradient medium/blood at 1200 x g for 20 minutes at 20oC.
Remove tubes from centrifuge taking care to not disrupt the density medium/plasma interface. There will be multiple layers- red blood cells will be at the bottom of the tube below the density gradient medium, the density gradient medium will be above that, a thin layer of leukocytes (buffy coat) will sit atop the density gradient medium, and the diluted plasma will be the top layer.
Using a 5 ml pipette, collect the leukocytes from atop the density gradient medium. Transfer to a new sterile 50 ml tube. Combine leukocytes from all tubes from the same sample.
Add sterile wash buffer to final volume of 40 ml. Recover cells by centrifugation at 600 x g for 5 minutes at 4oC. Repeat 2x. Count cells.
Re-suspend cell pellet in ice cold heat-inactivated fetal bovine serum, 500 μl/starting tube of blood. Place on ice.
Using a 5 ml pipette and keeping the cells on ice, add freezing medium (ice cold FBS + 20% DMSO) dropwise with constant swirling to 1:1 dilution.
Aliquot cells into 3 cryovials. Place in -80oC freezer. Cells can be transferred to liquid nitrogen after 24 hours.

title: ID2-3Primers
text:
Primers
There are 4 PCR reactions used to distinguish the mice in this colony:
The FLP’d and un-FLP’d alleles can be distinguished by:
FLP_3_F + FLP_4_R will yield a band for the FLP’d allele at
Flp_deleted_3_F – ATCCTGCCTTTTATCCTCTTT
FLP_4_R - CCCTGGACCTATGAAGGCG
Gives a band of ~780 bp if the rearranged allele is present and no band otherwise.
FLP_4_F - CACTCACCATTTATTTAGTGGCAAAAG
FLP_4_R – CCCTGGACCTATGAAGGCG
Gives a band of ~390 bp if either the FLP’d OR Un-FLP’d allele is present. There is also a non-specific band at ~600 bp you can ignore.
The Cre-rearranged alleles can be identified by:
ID2KI_CRE_F_3 - ACTTTATACGAAGTTATATGTGAAATCGCT
ID2KI_CRE_R_3 – GAAGTTATGATCTAAGGCACCCG
This reaction gives a band of ~620 bp. There are also a few nonspecific bands that show up occasionally.
The WT allele can be identified by:
Id2/3_Geno_Wt_F_2 - CCTTTTATCCTCTTTCTCCCCAGG
Id2/3_Geno_R_2 – TAAGGCTCGGGGTAGCC
Gives a band of ~490 bp. This reaction does not amplify the KI allele.
All these reactions run on the program called “52” on the PCR machine and they all have the following recipe for a 25 ul reaction volume:
1 ul genomic DNA
5 ul 5x buffer
2 ul MgCl2
0.5 ul dNTPs
0.5 ul F primer
0.5 ul R primer
0.5 ul Taq
15 ul ddH20

title: Goldrath_ChIP protocol with dynabeads
text:
Goldrath Lab ChIP Protocol
Fixation:
-Harvest cells (between 5-10 million the more the better) and place them in 10mL media or PBS
-Add 270ul 37% formaldehyde (to make 1% formaldehyde) and incubate (better rotate) for 10 minutes at RT
-Stop the reaction with 500ul 2.5M glycine (to make .125M glycine) and incubate (better rotate) for 5 minutes at RT
-Spin the cells down and wash once with ice cold 10 mL PBS. You can flash freeze the cells at this point if you wish to sonicate at a later time.
-Spin again and resuspend in 300ul Lysis Buffer. Add 3ul each of fresh protease inhibitors (PIC cocktail [100x] and benzamidine[0.1M]) to the solution. Incubate on ice for 5 minutes.
Sonication:
-Sonicate 20 cycles 30s on/off by Bioruptor-plus [10 cycles 2x with a brief jostle in between]
-Spin down sonicated lysate (5min at 13K rpm 4°C) to get rid of debris. Put the supernatant (the lysate) in a new eppendorf tube. The lysate can be stored at -80°C or used immediately.
-To test the sonication efficiency take 30ul of lysate. Add 100ul of NFW and incubate overnight at 65°C to reverse the crosslinks (shake for the first hour).
-Add 1 ul RNase A (stock at 100mg/ml) and incubate at 37C for 30 minutes. Add 2ul proteinase K (stock at 20mg/ml) and incubate at 55C for 1 hour.
-Extract DNA using Zymo DNA Clean & Concentrate kit. (DNA fragment)
-Measure DNA with nanodrop
-run 10ul of DNA on a 1% agarose gel to test sonication (should see a smear around 300-500 bp).
-Can use the remaining DNA as input
Binding Ab to dynabeads for CHIP (4 hours or overnight)
-Make Blocking solution: 0.5%w/v BSA in PBS
-Suspend the dynabeads well
-Transfer 30uL of suspension (per ChIP) into a 1.5mL EP tube containing 1mL blocking solution
-Rotate to wash the beads with the blocking soluton for 5 minutes
-Place the tube on the magnet then remove the supernatant by pipette
-Repeat wash
-suspend the beads with 200uL Blocking solution
-Add Ab and rotate at 4 degree for more than 4 hours or O/N
-Wash the beads twice with blocking buffer and then WBI buffer
Immunoprecipitation:
-use 5-10ug of DNA/Immunoprecipitation (using more can decrease the efficiency of the pulldown). (Around 2-2.5x106 cells)
-Dilute with 9 volumes of Dilution Buffer. Add protease inhibitors (PIC cocktail and benzamidine) to the solution.
-Add it to washed dynabeads and rotate overnight at 4°C. Remember to save an input sample (leave at 4C until elution step).
-Spin down complexes for 30 seconds at 8000rpm and put on magnet and discard the supernatant. Resuspend the beads in 1mL WBI, rotate at 4C for 5minutes and spin as before.
-Repeat wash with WBII, WBIII and two times with 1X TE buffer.
-Elute with 200ul Elution Buffer and shake for 30 minutes at 65C then reverse the crosslinks overnight at 65C. Remember to reverse crosslink your input sample as well (add 30ul of input to 200ul of Elution Buffer).
DNA extraction:
-Add 1ul of RNase A (stock at 100mg/ml) and incubate at 37C for 30minutes. Add 2ul of proteinase K (stock at 20mg/ml) and incubate at 55C for 1 hour.
-Spin down sample as before and transfer the supernatant to a new tube (this is the eluted DNA/protein complexes. Discard the beads).
-Extract DNA with Zymo DNA Clean & Concentrate kit. Follow the instruction of the kit and Elute in 55ul elution buffer.
Reagents:

title: Infection with LMGP33
text:
Infection with LM-gp33

Swipe glycerol stock with sterile pipette tip. Grow overnight in 5ml BHI (brain heart infusion) media in shaker at 37’C.
In the morning, add 50ul of overnight stock to 5ml BHI media. Take 1ml and measure the OD. Should be pretty low ~.02-.03 OD600.
Place new mixture in shaker. It should reach around 0.1 OD in 2.5-3 hours.
Make calculations based on OD600 of 0.1=2x10^8 cfu/ml.
Infect i.v at 3x10^4 pfu/mouse.

Note:
LM-gp33 is much less virulent than LM-OVA. It needs to be grown overnight for it to reach optimal growth point.
Adjust infection concentration up for rechallenge.
Rechallenge? 5x10^5 pfu/mouse i.v

title: Determining Bacterial Burden
text:
Asymmetric T Lymphocyte Division in the Initiation of Adaptive Immune Responses
Four days after infection, quantitative bacterial burdens in spleens were determined. Mean bacterial burden of recipient mice (left to right, n = 3, 4, 4, 4) is expressed as a percentage relative to the burden of untransferred control mice. All groups were significantly protected relative to untransferred controls (P ≤ 0.006). After delayed challenge, distal daughters afforded significantly better protection than proximal daughters (*P = 0.03).
4d after challenge, recipient mice were sacrificed and quantitative bacterial burdens in the spleens were determined. Briefly, spleens were homogenized in 1% Triton X (Roche), and serial dilutions plated on brain-heart infusion (Sigma) agar plates
incubated overnight at 37C. P
The generation of protective memory-like CD8+ T cells during homeostatic proliferation requires CD4+ T cells
Bacterial infections.
Recombinant L. monocytogenes strains LM-OVA (expressing secreted ovalbumin protein) and wild-type strain 10403s were provided by H. Shen (University of Pennsylvania School of Medicine, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania) and J.T. Harty (University of Iowa, Iowa City, Iowa)34, 43. Bacteria were grown in tryptic soy broth (TSB) with 50 mug/ml of streptomycin to an absorbance at 600 nm of about 0.1. For challenge experiments about 0.61 times 105 to 1.0 times 105 CFU were injected intravenously. The actual number of bacteria injected was confirmed by dilution and growth on tryptic soy agar plates containing streptomycin.
Determination of CFU.
On various days after infection, spleens and livers were removed and placed in a 0.2% IGEPAL (Sigma) solution. Organs were homogenized and serial dilutions were plated onto TSB plates containing 50 mug/ml of streptomycin. Bacterial colonies were counted after plate incubation for about 24 h at 37 °C. Dashed lines on graphs (Figs. 1, 5 and 6) indicate the limit of detection (approximately 100 organisms).

title: NES 070515 Immunofluorescence staining protocol
text:
Cut blocks of tissue to obtain spleen, lymph node, and tumor sections. Cryostat should be set to -20 degrees C, sections at 7um thickness

If getting tissue fracturing, adjust temperature [try warmer] and thickness of section
Can also try very briefly warming surface of OCT block by rubbing it with your thumb to decrease tissue fracturing

Fix slides in -20° acetone for 20 minutes at -20° (put back into freezer). Blot excess acetone off edges by pressing into a paper towel, and let air dry for 10 minutes (or until visibly dry). At this point you can store slides at -80° indefinitely (make sure slides stay dry).
To stain, let slides come up to room temperature, then draw a circle around tissue with a hydrophobic pen. Allow at least 10 minutes for hydrophobic line to dry.
Rehydrate tissue with staining buffer by adding ~200uL buffer to each tissue circle. Let sit at RT for 30 minutes. Make the staining buffer as follows:


Staining Buffer
100ml 1x PBS
1ml (1%) normal rat serum (as needed by antibody isotype)
1ml (1%) normal mouse serum (as needed by antibody isotype)
1g (1%) BSA
100ul (0.1%) Tween-20


Use aspirator to remove staining buffer, then blot with a kim wipe to get slide as dry as possible, making sure to not touch the tissue.
Aliquot primary antibodies (diluted in ~100ul staining buffer), and incubate in humidity chamber (foil-covered baking tray lined with damp paper towels) for 30 minutes at RT.
Wash slides first with a stream of PBS (using a transfer pipette) to get rid of excess antibody, then place slides in staining buffer and set on rotator to wash for 10 minutes. Gently blot next to sample area to remove excess liquid. If there is still excess liquid, it can be removed via aspiration. Renew the hydrophobic line if necessary (if staining with different secondaries on the same slide). Aliquot secondary antibodies (diluted in ~100ul staining buffer) and stain for 30 minutes at RT.
Wash slides again as previously, the counterstain with DAPI. DAPI stock is frozen at -20 at 5mg/ml stock concentration. To make a long-term working solution, dilute 50ul stock 1:50 in PBS (this solution can be stored in fridge for up to 6 months). Stain tissue with working solution for ~1minute.
Mount samples using prolong diamond anti-fade mounting media (add 3 evenly-spaced drops of mounting media to the coverslip, then place the coverslip on the slide). Let the mounting media cure for 24 hours (or at least overnight) at room temperature, protected from light.
Slides should be viewed with fluorescent microscope ASAP. For long term storage of stained slides, place them wrapped in foil at -80°.

title: Lymphocyte prep_tissues
text:
Harvesting Kidney, Lung, Liver for Lymphoycte isolation
- Inject 3ug of iv antibody (ie 15ul CD8Ae780 + 185ul PBS). 3-4 min after, sack the mice and harvest organs of interest
- Harvest kidneys and Lungs and place in PBS 5% FBS or complete media and on ice
Kidneys:
- Make one cut with scissors to increase their surface area and cut 2x with tissue chopper (tissue shouldn’t be dry under chopper!)
- Transfer cut kidneys into pyrex conical containing a magnetic stirr bar and add 25ml of enzyme media (complete RPMI+0.5mg/ml Collagenase D)
- Stirr for 45min at 37C
- Filter through 70um cell strainer and mash with syringe plunger. Spin down, remove supernatant and re-suspend pellet in 5ml 44% Percoll** (transfer into 15ml round-bottom Falcon conical). 
- With a pasteur pipette go all the way to the bottom of the tube and slowly add 2.5ml of 67% Percoll
- Carefully place inside centrifuge and spin down at 2000rpm for 20min at 25C (NO brake!). 
- Collect interphase and place in 15ml conical. Fill up tube up to 15ml with RPMI5% FBS and spin down for 8min at 2000rpm.
- Remove supernatant and re-suspend pellet in suitable volume (1ml of complete RPMI) for counting.
- Proceed with counting/staining
** To make 100% Percoll: mix 9 parts of Percoll stock with 1 part of 10X PBS.
   - To make 44% or 67% Percoll, use 100% Percoll as explained above and dilute in PBS+5%FBS
Lungs:
- Cut x2 w tissue chopper and place in 25ml of enzyme media (complete RPMI+0.5mg/ml Collagenase D) in pyrex conical + stirr bar
- Stirr for 45min at 37C
- Filter through 70um cell strainer and mash with syringe plunger. Spin down, remove supernatant and re-suspend in 2ml ACK lysis buffer. Incubate at RT for 5min.
- Wash and spin down
- Re-suspend in counting volume (2ml). Count and continue with staining. 
Liver:
- Cut liver with tissue chopper
- Press through 70um cell strainer
- Re-suspend in 20ml cold PBS/3% FBS
- Spin for 7min at 1500 rpm, remove SNT, re-suspend in 20ml (wash x3 times)
- Spin again, remove SNT, re-suspend
- Spin again (last time)
- Re-suspend in Isotonic Percoll (34% final). 
    Per liver use 25ml of isotonic percoll.
    To make 100ml (4 livers) —>     62.5ml PBS1x
                                                      3.75ml PBS 10x
                                                      33.75ml Percoll
    *Make at RT. Use 25ml per liver
- Spin at 1750rpm for 12min at RT. Brake ON. 
- Harvest pellet (RBC + lymphocytes), aspirate fat and everything else. With vaccum! Pellet is very loose
- Wash in 10ml Facs buffer
- Re-suspend in ACK, leave for 4-5min
- Filter through mesh
- Count and stain

title: ExvivoPolyfunctionality_Gp33
text:
Ex vivo peptide re-stimulation to assess cytokine production by antigen-specific CD8 T cells
LLB 2020

Whole splenocytes (whole blood or tissue) - maximum concentration of 1x10^7 cells/ml (I plate 2x10^6 cells in 200ul). Doing a higher concentration won’t work.
Re-suspend cells in:

TCM + 1ug/ml of GP33-41 peptide + GolgiPlug (1:1000) + 1:100 of anti-CD107a (conjugated to your preferred fluorophore) and incubate at 37C for 5h.
Make the negative control (no peptide) by pooling a little bit of cells from all samples: TCM + 1ug/ml Brefeldin A + 1:100 of anti-CD107a

After 5h;

Spin down flick to remove supernatant
Stain with live/dead stain + anti-CD8 (and congenic markers etc) in PBS1x for 10-15min at RT.
Wash and re-suspend in Cytofix/Cytoperm (BD kit) 20 min @4C (in the fridge).

Wash off fix, and resuspend in FACS buffer. *Cells can be left in the fridge overnight (or for 2-3 days until acquisition).
On the day of acquisition, spin down and remove PBS/facs buffer.
Re-suspend cells in Perm Buffer 1X (eBioscience kit/FoxP3 kit) containing:

anti-IFNg (1/100)
anti-TNFa (1/100)
anti-IL-2 (1/100) – PE (*Important: IL-2 only works in PE)

Stain for 30min at 4C
Wash off stain, and re-suspend in volume for acquisition

PANEL
CD107a-FITC
CD8a-PerCP-5.5
IL-2-PE
IFNg-e450
TNFa-APC
CD45.1-BV711
CD45.2-PE-Cy7

text:
RNA Isolation: DATE:­­­­­­__________
Before Beginning:

wipe down bench w/ WET paper towel to remove dust
make sure FILTERED tips are being used
Pour eppi tubes that will be used onto paper towel, NEVER USE FINGERS to reach in and grab!
Get a new Aliquot of Chloroform into Eppi tube.

Isolation:

add 1ul of glycoBlue as a carrier
add 100ul of Cholorform for every 0.5mL of Trizol and shake (not vortex) vigorously for 15 seconds.
Incubate them at RT for 2-3 minutes.
Spin @ 11,000rpm for 15’ at 2-8oC
Transfer aqueous layer (clear top layer) into a new tube.

RNA Precipitation:

add 250ul isopropyl alcohol and mix well
incubate samples at RT for 10’
spin at 11,000 rpm for 10’ at 2-8oC
there should be a blue pellet visible at bottom

RNA wash and Resuspension:

aspirate off supernatant
wash pellet w/ 1ml cold 70% Ethanol
vortex and spin at 9,000rpm for 5’ at 2-8oC
aspirate all but 100ul of ethanol and then repeat steps until ALL ETOH is removed.
Lay on Eppi tubes on side to allow further drying.
Resuspend the pellet in 10ul of DepC H2O and put on Ice for immediate use or -20oC freezer.

DNase Treatment of RNA:
RNA _________________ 10 ul
10X DNase Buffer ______ 2.5 ul
DNase ________________0.5 ul
DepC H2O _________ ___ 12 ul

incubate at 37oC for 20’
vortex DNase inactivation reagent
add 5ul of DNase inactivation reagent/ tube
incubate at RT for 2’
centrifuge 1’ at 10,000 rpm
pipette up supernatant, do not disturb beads.

Making cDNA from isolated RNA:

use individual PCR tubes w/ lids. Add the following to each tube.

2ul ___ Random Hexamers


1ul ___ 10mM dNTP mix
8ul ___ total RNA
2ul ___ sterile H2O

run RT program on PCR machine. Allow machine to reach 65oC, and place tubes in machine for 5’.
Pause the machine. Take out the samples and place on ICE for 1’.
Add the following to each tube:

4ul ___ 5X First-Strand Buffer



1ul ___ 1M DTT
1ul ___ RNase OUT
1ul ___ Superscript III RT


Samples were then placed in PCR machine. Resume RT program:

5’ @ 25oC



60’ @ 50oC
15’ @ 70oC

qPCR DATE:____________

every sample in triplicate
need naïve for negative control
need house keeping primer (GAP)

title: Cell Culture Basics
text:
First you need to find out what media your cells need to grow in and whether your cells are adherent or not.




Aspirate and discard media (only if your cells are adherent to the bottom)
Wash cells with PBS
Add minimum amount of trypsin (just enough to lightly cover the bottom of the flask or plate), shake, and put back at 37°C/6% CO2 incubator
After about 5 minutes, once all the cells have been released from the bottom, add media and transfer cell suspension to a conical tube
Spin 1800 rpm for 5 minutes
Aspirate and discard supernatant
Resuspend cells in some volume of media
Count (if required)
Plate cells at desired concentration
Put in 37°C/6% CO2 incubator





Freezing media = 20% serum and 10% DMSO in media (store in aliquots at -20°C)
Count cells and resuspend cells in freezing media such that they are at 4 x 106 cells/ml
Aliquot into cryotubes up to ~1.5 ml
Put at -80°C overnight
Put tubes in liquid nitrogen storage

title: Isolate splenocytes
text:
Isolate spleenocytes

Harvest mouse spleen in eppie tube containing cell media.
Fill petri dish with 5 ml T cell media (TCM).
Transfer spleen into petri dish.
Use rough sides of 2 microscope slides to grind the spleen.

*tips: keep the 2 slides at 90 angle to avoid too much capillary action

Rinse slides with 1 ml TCM before discarding.
Pipet up and down to dissociate cells
Transfer to 15 ml conical tube.
Rinse petri dish with 1 ml TCM and transfer to conical. Discard dish.
After a few seconds, debris will settle.
Transfer sup to a new conical.
Filter through nitrex (70 um)
Spin down at 1600 rpm, 4 min. Discard sup.
Ack pellet using 2 ml Ack for 7 mins.
Fill up the tube with TCM and spin down (same settings). White pellet should be visible.
Resuspend in 1 ml TCM.
Mix 10 ul of cells in 10 ml sheath for counting.

title: Setting up PCR
text:
Setting up PCR


Use computer program to calculate correct volumes for PCR mixture based on the number of DNA samples that need to be run. (#of samples + 2)
Make sure that all reagents are diluted to the concentration used by the program. Also check that you have the correct oligos.
Add 1μl of each DNA sample to separate wells on a PCR plate, check wells.
Combine all reagents other than the Taq and the DNA itself.
Remove the Taq from the freezer and add to the mixture, vortex.
Pipette 24 μl of the mixture into each well containing DNA.
Start desired program on PCR machine. Once the block reaches 95° C, place the plate into the machine and seal with film immediately.
Close lid of machine until program is complete.

title: Updated Pancreas Single-Cell Dissociation for Flow
text:
Procedure

Euthanize by CO2 asphyxiation followed by cervical dislocation; remove the pancreas rapidly (about 1–2 minutes).
Place pancreata in 5 mL medium without FBS and keep on ice until all samples are collected.
Mince finely for 2 minutes. Return to a 15 mL conical and add 7.6 mL medium without FBS, for a total volume of approximately 12.6 mL.
Add 1.4 mL 10× dissociation buffer per pancreas.
Warm quickly to 37°C in a 37°C water bath for 10 minutes.
Transfer to a 37°C rocking incubator.
Incubate for 20 minutes at 37°C, rocking and triturating gently every 10 minutes.
Let tissue pieces settle. Transfer supernatant to a new 15 mL tube and centrifuge 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend in 5 mL medium with FBS and keep on ice.
Add fresh dissociation buffer to the remaining tissue. Incubate 20 minutes at 37°C, rocking and triturating gently every 10 minutes with LoBind tips. Add DNase as needed and repeat for three total collections.
Prepare 10 mL medium with FBS in a new 50 mL conical with a nylon strainer on top.
Pour harvested tubes through the strainer, mash through a 100 µm strainer with a plunger, and wash the strainer with 10 mL medium with FBS.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend in 5 mL medium with FBS.
Perform a viable cell count using AO/PI or Trypan Blue and save dissociation images.

text:
IEL and Lamina Propria prep

3 minutes prior to sacrifice, inject mice retro-orbitrally w/ 200 uL antibody mix (15 uL CD8a-APCcy7 + 185 uL PBS)
Sacrifice mice, remove small intestine and spleen, place in ice cold RP5 or CMF, and trim off fat
Place paper towels on desk and wet w/ CMF
Wet gut w/ CMF, cut out Peyer’s patches and clean out the poop
Cut the small intestine in half lengthwise and then cut intestine into small (~1 cm pieces)
Place in flask and wash 2X w/ CMF, pour out contents carefully so no gut comes out
Dump out CMF carefully and replace w/ ~50 mL DTE, place on 37°C stir plate for 30 min
Pour contents into 50 mL conical with cell strainer
Wash out flask 1X w/ DTE and add to 50 mL conical

If preparing lamina propria:

Transfer contents of cell strainer back into flask and add ~30 mL of collagenase solution
Incubate for 45 min at 37° while stirring
Pour contents into 50 mL conical with cell strainer
Wash out flask 1X w/ DTE and add to 50 mL conical

Proceed as follows below for both IEL and lamina propria

Spin at 1600 rpm for 4 min
Make sure you see a pellet, then pour supernatant out and wipe top of conical
Resuspend each sample in 5 mL 44% percoll solution, make sure pellet is well resuspended
Place glass pasteur pipette in conical and add 2 mL 67% percol solution to top of pipette to make a bottom layer. Don’t disturb after adding!
Spin at 21°C at 2000 rpm for 20 min, set acceleration to 4 and brake to 0
Check for an interphase between the two layers and transfer it to 15 mL conical (usually about 3 mL)
Fill to top with PBS then spin at 2000 rpm for 5 min

If interphase remains, take out the top layer, add PBS, and spin again

Resuspend pellet in 250 uL of RP5
Count and stain IEL
Keep on ice and analyze by flow the next day

text:
Preparation of Il-15 complexes for injection
Sterile 0.1% BSA (w/v in PBS) solution
Recombinant Human IL-15 (R&D 247-IL-005/CF), make 100ng/ul aliquots. Store at -80C
Recombinant Human IL-15 R alpha Fc Chimera (R&D 147-IR-100), dilute to 0.5ug/ul. Store at 4C.
