title: Tamoxifen treatment
text:
The Cre recombinase recognizes a specific DNA fragment called loxP and mediates site specific deletion of larger DNA between two loxP sites. Concerning the mechanism of Cre-loxP system, a single Cre recombinase recognizes two directly repeated loxP site, then the Cre excises the loxP flanked (floxed) DNA. If a gene is flanked by two loxP sites, this gene (or a part of a gene) is excised leading to a functional knockout of that gene.






NoteMore usages for the loxP Cre sysyem





Of course, the Cre-LoxP system can do more than just knockouts. Depending on the orientation of the loxP sites, it can invert parts of DNA. Or is a STOP codon is flanked by loxP sites, the expression of a gene can be turned on.



More background information and illustrations can be found on the JAX website: Cre Lox Breeding for Beginners,
It is important to keep in mind, that the floxed allele is only excised when a Cre recombinase is expressed. We can hence create lineage specific knockouts by fusing fusing the Cre enzyme to the expression of a lineage specific gene. For example a CD4-Cre deletes the floxed allele in all cells that ever expressed CD4. This leads to a KO in CD4 and also CD8 T cells, since CD8 T cells express CD4 and CD8 in the DP stage in the thymic development. Another commonly used Cre is a Lck-Cre or Gzmb-Cre.
However, with these systems, it is not possible to timely control the kockout of a gene. To address that, a different version of the Cre recombinase can be used: Cre-ERT2. Here, the Cre is fused to a mutated form estrogen receptor, that does not bind to estrogen, but only tamoxifen. These Cre-ERT2 fusion proteins are sequestered in the cytoplasm and can therefor not induce DNA recombination of DNA in the nucleus. Only upon binding to tamoxifen, this fusion enzyme translocates to the nucleus and becomes functionally active. We can exploit that and treat mice with tamoxifen at certain times to activate the Cre-ERT2 and induce KO (or reporter expression) at chosen time points.
In the case of the Hic1 floxed mice, I use a Cre-ERT2 that is included in the ROSA26 locus and expressed constitutively. If we isolate P14 cells and transfer them into new recipients, we can induce the KO (iKO) specifically in P14 cells by administration of tamoxifen. The best control to use is a CreERT2- Hic1fl/fl P14, that also contains the loxP sites, but does not express the Cre fusion enzyme.

If a gene is flanked by two loxP sites, this gene (or a part of a gene) is excised leading to a functional knockout of that gene.

Of course, the Cre-LoxP system can do more than just knockouts. Depending on the orientation of the loxP sites, it can invert parts of DNA. Or is a STOP codon is flanked by loxP sites, the expression of a gene can be turned on.



More background information and illustrations can be found on the JAX website: Cre Lox Breeding for Beginners,
It is important to keep in mind, that the floxed allele is only excised when a Cre recombinase is expressed. We can hence create lineage specific knockouts by fusing fusing the Cre enzyme to the expression of a lineage specific gene. For example a CD4-Cre deletes the floxed allele in all cells that ever expressed CD4. This leads to a KO in CD4 and also CD8 T cells, since CD8 T cells express CD4 and CD8 in the DP stage in the thymic development. Another commonly used Cre is a Lck-Cre or Gzmb-Cre.
However, with these systems, it is not possible to timely control the kockout of a gene. To address that, a different version of the Cre recombinase can be used: Cre-ERT2. Here, the Cre is fused to a mutated form estrogen receptor, that does not bind to estrogen, but only tamoxifen. These Cre-ERT2 fusion proteins are sequestered in the cytoplasm and can therefor not induce DNA recombination of DNA in the nucleus. Only upon binding to tamoxifen, this fusion enzyme translocates to the nucleus and becomes functionally active. We can exploit that and treat mice with tamoxifen at certain times to activate the Cre-ERT2 and induce KO (or reporter expression) at chosen time points.
In the case of the Hic1 floxed mice, I use a Cre-ERT2 that is included in the ROSA26 locus and expressed constitutively. If we isolate P14 cells and transfer them into new recipients, we can induce the KO (iKO) specifically in P14 cells by administration of tamoxifen. The best control to use is a CreERT2- Hic1fl/fl P14, that also contains the loxP sites, but does not express the Cre fusion enzyme.

title: Tamoxifen treatment
text:
Make a Tamoxifen stock






Warning



Tamoxifen is a hazardous substance and must be handled with care!


Dissolving tamoxifen is tedious. The “old” protocol that was used in the Goldrath lab, made a stock of tamoxifen (100mg/ml) in pure ethanol first and then further diluted that fresh in sunflower oil (1:10 dilution). However, that did not work very well for me.
Instead I am following the combination of the old protocol and the protocol that can be found on the JAX website.

Procedure

Dissolve tamoxifen in sunflower oil at a concentration of 10 mg/ml by shaking overnight at 37°C. Tamoxifen is light sensitive, and should be made and stored in a light‐ blocking vessel (amber, or foil wrapped).
Tamoxifen is very hard to dissolve. It helps to vortex frequently and brake up larger clumps with a pipette or syringe.
I have also had good success in sonicating the Tamoxifen solution briefly.
At the end, the oil should appear clear and without any remaining clumps.
After tamoxifen is in solution, store at 4°C for the duration of injections and according the the Kaech lab aliquots can be frozen and stored at -20 C for longer time periods.

title: Tamoxifen treatment
text:
Treatment

Inject 100ul of the 10mg/ml tamoxifen solution i.p. into mice using a 26G needle. There is some resistance, but it should not be too hard to inject the oil with the 26G needle.
The resulting dose is 1mg per mouse per injection (similar to Milner et al. (2017) or Lin et al. (2022))
Mice are treated for 4-5 consecutive days to yield optimal recombination. Then I wait 3-5 days before checking protein deletion, this is the fastest it can happen.

Anti-PD1/CTLA4 in vivo blockade in B16-challenged mice

Cell line

Inoculate mice with cancer cells

Trypsin and count cells

Count cells

Bring cancer cells on ice to mouse room
Shave mice

Day 7
P14 transfer

Harvest four spleens from P14 mice.
Homogenize spleen over 70 um filter
Centrifuge at 1600 RPM for 4 min and dump
Resuspend pellet in 1-2 ml ACK and incubate at room temp for 5-6 min
Neutralize with 3-4 ml of media
Take aliquot for flow
Wash aliquot 1x with FACS
Stain aliquot with surface stain master mix for 20 min at 4C

CD8b- BV510
CD45.1- BV786
CD45.2- FITC
VA2- PE

While aliquots are staining, count cells

7.74e6/ml, 40 ml, 75% viability
309 million cells from four spleens, 75% viability

At end of stain, wash cells 2x with FACS
Take to flow
Take lymphocytes 🡪 then frequency of Va2 in CD8b/CD45.1+ gate and calculate what percentage of CD8b+Va2+ of cells

0.95 (Va2)* 35% CD8b+CD45.1+ of (singlets 🡪lymphocytes) gate
0.33 * 309e6 = 101e6 P14

Dual isotype

title: Goldrath IEL and LPL Isolation
text:
IEL Isolation:
1. Turn on hot plate and add DTE to DTE solution
2. Bring reagents to appropriate temperature
-CMF on ice (ice bucket)
-DTE solution and collagenase solution (if isolating LP)to 37oC (water bath)
-Percolls to RT (bench)
3. Resect small intestine from mouse (we put it in RPMI+5% serum on ice until ready to isolate cells)
4. Cut out peyers patches; Push out fecal content; Cut longitudinally to flatten intestine and then cut intestine into ~ 1cm pieces (laterally)
5. Place pieces into 125ml Erlenmeyer flask w/30ml CMF. Let pieces settle; pour off supernatant. (discard). Repeat wash with another 30ml CMF; pour off supernatant. (discard)
6. Add 35ml DTE solution and a stir bar; spin on hot plate for 30 min@37oC
7. Pour off supernatant through a cell strainer into clean 50ml conical. Wash flask/intestine pieces with additional DTE solution and top up the 50ml conical. Put on ice. (These are your IEL’s)

*if you are isolating cells from LP start this prep now by returning all intestine pieces to the flask and adding 30ml collagenase Type I solution (see LP protocol).

8. Spin down IEL and discard supernatant. Resuspend pellet in 5ml 44% Percoll + transfer to 15 ml round bottom tube. Underlay 2ml of 67% Percoll (we do this with Pasteur pipettes).
9. Centrifuge @RT for 20 min @2000rpm (4 Acceleration and 0 BRAKE!)
10. Remove lymphocyte interface into 15ml conical and top off tube with RPMI+5% serum.
11. Centrifuge @4 oC for 10min @2000rpm (with brake). The resultant pellet are your purified IELs.
LPL Isolation
1. Add Collagenase to solution
2. Bring reagent to appropriate temperature
-Collagenase to 37oC (water bath)
-Percolls to RT (bench)
3. Add 30ml Collagenase solution to intestine pieces (post-IEL prep); spin on hot plate for 45min @37<sup>oC
4. Pour off supernatant through cell strainer into new 50ml conical (These are your LP cells)
5. Centrifuge @4 oC for 5 min @1600rpm; Resuspend pellet in 5 ml 44% Percoll; transfer to 15 ml
round-bottom tube; Underlay with 2ml of 67% Percoll (with Pasteur pipette)
6. Centrifuge @RT for 20 min @2000rpm (4 Acceleration and 0 BRAKE!)
7. Remove lymphocyte interface into 15ml conical and top off tube with RPMI+5% serum.
8. Centrifuge @4 oC for 10min @2000rpm (with brake). The resultant pellet are your purified LPLs.

title: Mouse Anesthesia
text:
Mouse Anesthesia
Using Ketamine-Xylazine

Prepare anesthetic solution under sterile conditions:


draw 200ul of ketamine solution (100mg/ml) and
100ul of xylazine solution (20mg/ml) using an insulin syringe.
Add 1700ul of dd H2O (-> 10ug/ul Ketamine, 1ug/ul Xylazine)
Aliquot in two Eppi tubes, store at 4C


For shorter duration of anesthesia dilute anesthetic solution with another 500ul of ddH2O (-> 8ug/ul Ketamine, 0.8ug/ul Xylazine)
Prior to anesthesia weigh mouse. Prepare 10ul of anesthetic solution for each g of body weight.
Inject i.p. or s.c.
Monitor respiration and fill out Post-Anesthetic recovery record. Stay with mouse until it fully recovers (takes about 2h after injection!)

Ketamine: used 80-100mg/kg
Xylazine: used 5-10mg/kg

title: DNA extaction from tails
text:
Extraction of DNA from mouse tails

Place small piece of tail or ear in 400 μl of tail juice and incubate overnight at 55° C. Vortex and proceed to step 3.

2. If frozen, thaw sample in incubator.

Add phenol-chloroform IMA (25:24:1) to tail juice mixture at approximately 1:1 ratio (~400μl) in fume hood, mix well.
Spin samples in centrifuge for 5 min. at 12,000 rpm (room temperature).
Add 100μl TE (pH 8.0) to one well for every sample in a clean 96 well plate.


6. Obtain a new set of eppendorf tubes and pipette in ~400 μl of ethanol.


Remove tubes from centrifuge and pipette top layer (aqueous-phase DNA) into the tubes with ethanol, avoiding any phenol layer or interface (sludge).
Mix tubes with DNA + ethanol until white clumps of DNA are visible.
Use pipette tip to remove each clump of DNA into a well containing the TE. If difficult to remove DNA, centrifuge in order to force the DNA to pellet.
Cover wells and seal sides with tape until further use. 4° C for near term or -20° C for longer storage.
Dispose of phenol-chloroform in container in fume hood, return to refrigerator.

Negative control: CT2 or B6 and H2O

Place in PCR machine

TipTouchdown PCR





A touchdown PCR tries to minimize the incidence non-specific, contaminating products. text:
Gel Electrophoresis

Make agarose gel (more % agarose for small fragments)

All PCRs can be run on a 2.5% TAE gel

2.5g agarose + 100ml TAE for small gel
5g agarose + 200ml TAE for large gel

Add 4μL EtBr for small gel; > 20 samples
Add 8μL EtBr for large gel; < 20 samples

Microwave gel bottle for 1.5 - 2 minutes until agarose has dissolved; add EtBr (mix well) and let cool
Pour liquid into gel mold; pop/move bubbles to the bottom with pipet tip
Carefully insert combs and let cool for 10 - 15 minutes (until hardened)
Remove combs & place gel into easycast
Fill easycast with 1x TAE to cover gel
Load 10μL gene ladder in the first lane; 15μL of sample in other lanes
Run gel @ 90-120V

UBC Cre & tdTomato: 35 min
Hic1 fl, Hic1 Cre and Zeb2: 1h
If there is no good separation for the bands, extend running time.

title: 072226 in vitro tumor growth and injection protocol
section: A. Preparing frozen tumor cells for inoculation
text:
A. Preparing frozen tumor cells for inoculation

Tumor cells are stored in the liquid nitrogen storage tank or −150°C chest freezer. Use the storage map to locate the cells and remove the vial from the map once it has been removed from storage.
Carefully and quickly remove the frozen vial(s) from the storage rack, then return the rack to the liquid nitrogen tank.
Rapidly thaw tubes in a 37°C water bath or on the skirt of the hood, then move them to the hood.
Open the vial(s), remove the thawed medium with a 1 mL pipette, and transfer to a culture dish (15 mm). Add the appropriate cell medium (R10, D10, or other) in a volume that covers the plate (20 mL for a 15 mm plate).
Place the plate in a culture incubator and grow cells until the plate is approximately two-thirds to three-quarters confluent. The appropriate confluence may vary by tumor-cell type and may require optimization.
When cells have reached the desired confluence:

Remove the plate from the incubator and carefully aspirate the medium.
Wash once with cold sterile PBS and aspirate.
Add 5 mL trypsin and incubate in the cell-culture incubator for approximately 5 minutes at 37°C.
Add 5 mL medium. Gently wash the plate with a pipette while tilting it to release cells from the plastic surface.
Collect the cell suspension in a 15 mL conical tube and remove a 10 µL aliquot to count cells. Spin the tube while counting.

objectID: protocols/mice/Tumor/072226 in vitro tumor growth and injection protocol.html#b.-tumor-cell-injections
href: protocols/mice/Tumor/072226 in vitro tumor growth and injection protocol.html#b.-tumor-cell-injections
title: 072226 in vitro tumor growth and injection protocol
text:
B. Tumor-cell injections

Resuspend cells at the concentration appropriate to the experiment, based on a 100 µL injection volume. The source gives 250,000 cells per injection for B16-GP33 and 1 × 106 cells per injection for MC38-GP33 as examples. Resuspend cells in PBS or medium for injection.
Transfer cells to Eppendorf tubes or 50 mL conical tubes that accommodate a syringe, and place on ice in disposable tip boxes for transport to the animal facility.
Use 28-gauge insulin syringes. The source suggests approximately one syringe per cage because needles lose sharpness with repeated injections.
In the animal-facility procedure room, prepare the anesthesia chamber:

Place the clear plastic chamber in the hood.
Check oxygen-tank and isoflurane levels; replace or refill as appropriate.
Open the oxygen tank and set isoflurane to 3 or 3.5. Confirm that oxygen is flowing and that the vaporizer reads 1.5–2.0 psi.
Place clean paper towels in the chamber, place mice inside, and wait for slow, deep breathing and no movement.
Remove mice, shave the back area with clippers, and return them to the chamber. Ear punches may be performed at this stage for identification.

Ensure that tumor cells are resuspended by inverting the tube or vortexing. Draw 100 µL cell suspension for each mouse into a syringe.
For subdermal injection, position the back skin by rolling it over a finger or pulling it upward, then insert the needle with the bevel facing up.
Inject 100 µL subdermally, avoiding puncture through the skin that could allow tumor-cell medium to leak and cause unequal doses.
A large bubble should form on the mouse’s back. After injection, weigh the mouse and record its weight, then return it to its home cage. Keep completed cages outside the hood until all mice have recovered before returning cages to the animal room.
After inoculations are complete, return cages to the animal room and put away the isoflurane vaporizer apparatus. If the holding chamber is soiled with urine or feces, wash it; the source instructs not to use ethanol or other cleaners that damage the plastic.

section: C. Monitor mouse weight and tumor growth
text:
C. Monitor mouse weight and tumor growth

Monitor tumor growth and begin animal treatments when tumors reach the size or date appropriate to the experiment.
Record observations and mouse weight at each monitoring step. The source states that monitoring and paper records are required by UCSD and must be kept in the mouse room.
Use the following tumor-stage observation schedule from the source:

Stage 1: No visible, palpable, clinical, or behavioral signs of tumor burden — monitor weekly.
Stage 2: Visible or palpable tumors, or changes in appearance or behavior — monitor twice weekly.
Stage 3: Any signs of morbidity or mortality, or subcutaneous tumor diameter greater than 1.5 cm — monitor daily. The source states that animals must be euthanized when a tumor reaches 2 cm in any direction.

title: 04.20.21 Tumor injection protocol
text:
Tumor Injection Protocol
1) Remove media from B16 tumor cells
2) Rinse once with 5 mL PBS
3) Add 5 mL Trypsin
4) Put in Incubator for 5 min
5) Tap plate to dislodge most cells
6) Add 5 mL of D10 to stop Trypsin enzymatic rxn
7) Transfer to 15 ml Conical
8) Take 10uL of resuspended cells (mix tube just before pipetting to make sure you get the most accurate cell count possible) and put in 1 well of V-bottom plate in order to count
9) Spin cells down 1500 RPM for 5 minutes
10) Count cells while spinning
11) Resuspend in fresh d10 to get a concentration of 2.5 million cells/ml (so that 250,000 cells will be in 100 ul)
12) also replate ~1 million B16 to a new 15cm plate to continue culturing them in vitro
13) Put resuspended cells on ice
14) Bring cells plus 3 syringes to mouse room (use orange capped insulin syringes for the injection, located above Amir’s bench)
15) Grab 2 cage mice for 10 total mice (the ones in the middle rack against the wall that have “Nicole” on them) *these are B6 mice from Jax, will have a white cage card with a Jax sticker too
16) Expose mice to isoflurane
17) Shave backside of mice
18) Prepare syringe by moving plunger, then taking up media + cells, flick to make sure all air bubbles raise to the top, move plunger up and down slowly to remove all bubbles, make sure media is coming from top of syringe, do not hit plastic with syringe, point syringe away from self at all times
19) Hold mice up by the back
20) Insert syringe at about 30 degree angle (or less, the needle should be fairly parallel to your forfinger and thumb holding the skin) to the horizontal and then pull syringe up slightly to make sure the needle has pierced the skin, but has not gone through all layers of the skin of the mice. Make sure a nice bubble appears in the skin after the injection to make sure you’ve done the injection correctly!
21) turn off the oxygen and isoflurane when you’re done!
22) Return mice to mouse room, clean up hair in hood

Label a 96-well plate with cage numbers and N/L/R for each mouse.
Take the blood tube from above Anh’s desk and add 100 µL to each well; prepare extra wells as needed.

text:

title: Mouse Genotyping Protocol
text:
Tail and bleed mice

Scruff mice and ear punch them with N/L/R for each mouse.
Hold the mouse by the scruff and the base of the tail with your ring finger.
Snip the tail into a tube.
While holding the tail base, squeeze down the tail to release blood into the well.
Dry the tail on a paper towel.

title: Mouse Genotyping Protocol
text:
Process tails

Add 400 µL tail juice to each tail tube.
Shake at 55°C and 1,000 rpm for 1 hour.
Add 150 µL 5 M NaCl to each sample and vortex.
Centrifuge at maximum speed for 5 minutes.
Transfer 400 µL supernatant to a new tube.
Add 250 µL isopropanol to each sample and vortex.
Centrifuge at maximum speed for 5 minutes.
Pour off the supernatant.
Wash the pellet with 500 µL 70% ethanol and vortex.
Centrifuge at maximum speed for 5 minutes.
Pour off the supernatant.
Dry tubes upside down over paper towels in a chemical hood for 1 hour.
Resuspend in 200 µL ultrapure water and store at −20°C until use.

title: Mouse Genotyping Protocol
text:
Process blood

Add 100 µL 1× ACK to each well and incubate 5 minutes at room temperature.
Centrifuge at 2,000 rpm for 1 minute and discard supernatant.
Add 50 µL Fc block to each well and incubate 10 minutes at 4°C.
Add 150 µL FACS buffer to each well, centrifuge as above, and discard supernatant.
Add 100 µL antibody cocktail per sample and incubate 15 minutes at 4°C in the dark:

CD8a PE-Cy7 (1:200)
CD45.1 eFluor 450 (1:200)
CD45.2 FITC (1:200)
APC Vα2 (1:200)

Add 150 µL FACS buffer to each well, centrifuge, and discard supernatant.
Prepare compensation controls: use half a drop of vortexed beads with 1 µL antibody per color; incubate 15 minutes at room temperature in the dark; add 200 µL FACS buffer to bullet tubes and refrigerate until running.
If fixing: add 100 µL fixation buffer and incubate 15 minutes at 4°C; add 150 µL FACS buffer, centrifuge, discard supernatant, then add 100 µL FACS buffer and transfer to bullet tubes.
If not fixing: add 100 µL FACS buffer and transfer to bullet tubes.

title: Mouse Genotyping Protocol
text:
Run PCR

Resuspend 10 µL primer stock in 90 µL ultrapure water.
Make master mix according to the appropriate sheet.
Combine 24 µL master mix with 1 µL tail DNA.
Run PCR:

AR: use TOUCHDOW on the rightmost machine, or an equivalent touchdown protocol.
UBC-Cre: use GENO_TD on the middle machine.

The run takes approximately 90 minutes.

title: Mouse Genotyping Protocol
text:
Run gel
While PCR is running, make the gel.

Set out the gel tray, gel basin, and required combs.
For a small 2.5% gel, combine 2.5 g agarose with 100 mL 1× TAE in a 250 mL flask.
For a large 2.5% gel, combine 5 g agarose with 200 mL 1× TAE in a 500 mL flask.
Microwave for 1 minute; swirl. Microwave for 30 seconds; swirl. Microwave for 20 seconds; swirl until flash boiling stops. Confirm agarose is fully melted, then cool under running cold water while swirling until the flask is safe to handle.
Add 4 µL EtBr for a small gel or 8 µL for a large gel and swirl.
Pour into the gel basin. If it leaks, place ice around the sides to stop the leak.
Let harden for about 20 minutes. Meanwhile, fill the main running basin to the line with TAE.
Remove combs once hardened. Place gel in the running apparatus and add enough TAE to cover it.
Load 7 µL ladder and 10 µL samples.
Run at 100 V and image. Orient red to red and black to black: the red lead is at the lower end of the gel and the black lead is toward the ladder.

AR gel: 45 minutes.
UBC-Cre gel: 45 minutes.

title: Blood prep for genotyping
text:
Preparation for blood - genotyping


Bleed animal into 50 μl EDTA in a microfuge tube
If the blood is fresh, spin at max for 30 seconds. If you are not going to use it that day, put it at 4°C for one day.
If the blood is a day old, there should already be a pellet, so you don’t need to spin it down.
Aspirate and discard supernatant
Add 0.5 ml Ack and vortex
Incubate at room temp for 5 minutes
Spin at max for 30 seconds
Aspirate and discard supernatant
Wash with ~1 ml FACS buffer and vortex
Spin at max for 30 seconds
Aspirate and discard supernatant

If you are not FC blocking go to step 15.
If you are not FC blocking and are not biotin labeling, go to step 20.

Make master mix of 50 μl FACS buffer/sample plus 0.25 μl FC block/sample (e.g., if you have 8 samples, mix 400 μl FACS buffer + 2 μl FC block)
Add 50 μl of your master mix to each sample to resuspend the pellet and vortex
Incubate on ice for at least 5 minutes

If you are NOT biotin labeling your samples, proceed to step 20.

Add 0.5 μl of your biotin antibody per sample
Incubate on ice for 15 minutes
Wash with ~1.5 ml FACS buffer and vortex
Spin at max for 30 seconds
Aspirate and discard supernatant
Make master mix of 50 μl FACS buffer/sample
Add 50 μl of your master mix to each sample to resuspend the pellet and vortex
Incubate on ice for 10 minutes in the dark
Wash in ~1.5 ml FACS buffer and vortex
Spin at max for 30 seconds
Aspirate and discard supernatant
Add 50 μl FACS fix buffer and vortex
Put sample on ice or at 4°C until you run flow cytometry

Genotyping OT-I mice by flow cytometry

Bleed mice to type animals and coordinate with ear punch so we know which mice is what genotype in the cage
Put blood into FACS tubes with 2 mls of RBC lysis buffer
Wash 2x with lysis buffer
Stain with master mix diluted in RBC lysis buffer for 20 minutes at 4C.

Run flow on the samples to determine P14 status

title: spleen&lymph node cell prep
text:
Cell Prep from Lymph nodes and/or Spleen

Spleen and/or lymph nodes should be in ~5 ml RPMI buffer.
Put a cell strainer in a 6 cm petri dish containing ~5 ml RPMI.
Pour tissue into cell strainer
Using the bottom of a syringe plunger, grind tissue through cell strainer
Remove cell strainer and transfer RPMI + cells to a 15 ml conical
Spin at 1800 rpm for 5 minutes
Aspirate and discard supernatant
Resuspend pellet in 1 ml Ack buffer and incubate at room temp for 1 minute
Add ~13 ml RPMI and mix
Spin at 1800 rpm for 5 minutes
Aspirate and discard supernatant
Resuspend pellet in whatever volume RPMI and pour into a 50 ml conical through a cell strainer
Take an aliquot and count cells – multiply the number of cells counted in a 16 square area by 104 multiplied by your dilution factor multiplied by your total volume to give you the total number of cells
Spin the resuspension at 1800 rpm for 5 minutes
Aspirate and discard supernatant
Resuspend final pellet in desired media at your desired concentration
Yeah!

title: Spleen processing
text:
Take spleen from mouse & store in plate with some media (RP5)
Prepare ~3ml of RP5 media in a small petri-dish for each spleen
Grind up the spleen in the media with 2 microscope slides using the rough surface
Use some RP5 to rinse the slides and collect remaining cells into the petri-dish





Get a 15ml conical tube and place a nitex filter over the opening
Transfer the spleen cells from petri-dish over to the conical tube by passing it through the filter
After all the cell with media has been transferred, rinse the petri-dish with some RP5 and transfer the contents through the filter to collect any remaining cells on the dish to the tube.





After all the cells are collected, centrifuge tube at 1600RPM for 4 minutes
Discard the supernatant and save the pellet
Add 1mL of 1X ACK to the tube with pelleted cells and let lyse for ~5 minutes or until the cell mixture looks clear and lysed

Dilute the ACK if the concentration is not 1X

After cells are lysed, centrifuge tube at 1600RMP for 4 minutes
Discard supernatant and save the pellet

We should have a white pellet at this point

Resuspend pellet in 1mL of RP5/TCM/MACS for next step.

title: Liver Preparation Protocol
text:
Liver Preparation Protocol
1. Chop livers into small pieces with a razor blade. Push liver pieces through a 70um filter into a 50ml conical tube using plenty of 5% BGS + PBS to wash through. Push through using the bottom of a syringe.
2. Wash all liver cells twice in 40 mL PBS+5% BGS. Spin at 1600rpm for 8 minutes each time (centrifuge should be at room temp). The second washing step is actually worthwhile as it leads to better separation.
3. Spin cells in 25 mL 37% Percoll at 1750rpm for 25 minutes. To make a Percoll working solution, add 8.5ml Percoll to 16.5ml PBS (25ml total).
4. At this point the lymphocytes will be at the bottom of the conical with a layer of hepatocytes near the top of the gradient. You can aspirate off the hepatocytes at this point and proceed with the lymphocytes as normal.
5. Ack the lymphocytes. I normally do this for 2-3 minutes, as the erythrocytes are hard to get rid of in the liver. I resuspend in 250ul 5% BGS in order to count the cells.
6. Stain as normal.

text:
MYCO-PCR
MRC 10/2019
Order Primers
You will need to order multiple forward and reverse primers to detect multiple species of mycoplasma.
Forward primers

   Myco-5-1   CGCCTGAGTAGTACGTTCGC
   Myco-5-2  CGCCTGAGTAGTACGTACGC
   Myco-5-3  TGCCTGAGTAGTACATTCGC
   Myco-5-4  TGCCTGGGTAGTACATTCGC
   Myco-5-5  CGCCTGGGTAGTACATTCGC
   Myco-5-6  CGCCTGAGTAGTATGCTCGC

 Reverse primers

   Myco-3-1  GCGGTGTGTACAAGACCCGA
   Myco-3-2  GCGGTGTGTACAAAACCCGA
   Myco-3-3  GCGGTGTGTACAAACCCCGA

Prepare Primer Mix
Dissolve each primer to a final concentration of 100 µM. Mix all forward primers together to reach a final concentration of 10 µM each. For example, if you want to prepare 100 µl primer mix, take 10 µl of each forward primer and add 40 µl of water. Mix all reverse primers in a similar fashion.
Prepare Sample
Take 100 µl of cell culture supernatant from a dense culture (80-100% confluent) into a 1.5ml tube (or media, sera, whatever you want to test). Heat the sample for 5 min at 95°C (to denaturate it) and spin it for 2min in a bench centrifuge at maximum speed.

title: CB8.Ex vivo restim
text:
EX VIVO RESTIMULATION OF P14 CELLS
Freshly isolated TILs and splenocytes were counted and incubated in 200 μL of standard T cell medium containing 1× Protein Transport Inhibitor Cocktail (1:500, eBioscience, 00-4980-93) and gp33 peptide (1 μM final, KAVYNFATC; Anaspec) on a U-bottom 96-well for 4 hours. Spike in some naïve splenocytes (same congenic as recipient mice) by resuspending the naïve spleen in 5 mL of medium and plating 30 µL per well.
Restimulated cells were then transferred into V-bottom plates, washed twice, blocked with Fc-receptor blocking medium (prepared from in-house hybridoma supernatant), and stained for surface molecules, followed by intracellular staining to assess effector molecules and cytokine production.
Aliquots of cells treated similarly but without cognate peptide were used as negative controls for cytokine production; 1× Cell Stimulation Cocktail (1:500, eBioscience, 00-4970-93) was used as a positive control. Plain medium was used as a negative control.
Note: if not counting you can plate 2/3 or 1/4 of TILs and dLN or 10 µL of SP (resuspend in 1 mL).

Procedure

Low percentage agarose for large fragments

Use 0.5 - 1% for 6 kb of fragment for better separation, or 2% for 100 - 800 bp.

If doing 0.7%, get 0.7g of agarose into one of the gel flasks, put into weighing scale.
Add 100 mL of TAE buffer to the flask.
Put in microwave 2 min. Shake to dissolve crystals.
Pour the gel cage into the box.
Then put the boiling glass into water to cool until its safe enough to touch.
Pipette 4 µL EB into the cooled glass (10 mg/ml EtBR).
Add the comb to the top of the cage wide teeth down.
Add the solution to the cage. Let dry for about 30-45 min.
Put the dried gel into the gel running box with the holes facing up.
Fill with TAE buffer until the gel is fully submerged.
Add 10 ul of Generuler 1kb plus ladder.
Add a 1:6 dilution of 6x orange to the DNA you want to run in the gel. For instance 30 ul DNA, add 5 ul of 6x orange.
Put the DNA into one of the wells on the gel and keep track of which one it is.
Connect black wire to the top of the box (negative) and red to the bottom of the box (positive).
95 V, 30 A, 300 W. Time 30:00 min - Run

title: Subcloning into LZRSpBMN
text:
Subcloning into LZRSpBMN-linker-IRES-EGFP:
So far our preferred sites are BamHI, XhoI, and NotI. SfiI does not seem to exist.
We digest 25-50μg of the vector, separate on a 1% agarose gel overnight, and isolate the cut vector by electroelution. We ethanol precipitate, resuspend in water, quantitate by OD and agarose gel.
If we get good results with the ligations and the negative controls are good, we aliquot the remaining cut vector into 100ng portions with 1μl of 10X ligase buffer with ATP and store at -70oC for later ligations.
Ligations are done at 14oC overninght with 100ng of cut vector and an insert ratio of 1:1 or 1:3. If we are using the cut vector for the first time, we also include a vector alone with ligase and without as our negative controls.
Sequence primers: forward dw189 5’ gca tcg cag ctt gga tac ac 3’
reverse dw190 5’ ctc aca ttg cca aaa gac gg 3’
The reverse primer will give some sequence at the cloning site but will die off quickly due to the large number of g’s at the 3’ end of the MCS. We usually confirm with internal forward primers specific to the insert.
These primers can also be used to screen colonies by PCR:
1.5mMMg, .125mM dNTPs, 1 μM each primer with an annealing of 57oC
Empty vector=272bp.
We transform into Epicurian Coli XL10-Gold Ultracompetent Cells (Stratagene). The clones are always grown at 30oC with 75 μg/ml Carbenicillin.
Once we have sequence confirmation, we proceed to transfections.

title: Pathway analysis in scRNA with UCell
text:
Get gene signatures
This function get the MSigDB pathways. If a pathway ends witt _UP and + will be added to the gene to mark it as up-regulated. Vice versa, if there the pathways ends with _DN a - will be added.
Additionally if there are two pathways containing the UP and DOWN signatures, they will be merged. E.g. GOLDRATH_EFF_VS_MEMORY_CD8_TCELL_UP and GOLDRATH_EFF_VS_MEMORY_CD8_TCELL_DN will be merged in GOLDRATH_EFF_VS_MEMORY_CD8_TCELL. In that list, the genes that are up-regulated are marked by a + and the down-regulated genes by a -
library(magrittr)

#' getMSigDBPathways
#'
#' @param categories MSigDB categories. Can be "H" or "C1" - "C8".
#' @param species Species to get the pathways for. Default: Mus musculus
#'
#' @return A names list. If specificed in MSigDB, the direction of the genes in specified by + and -
getMSigDBPathways <- function(categories, species = "Mus musculus"){
  pathways <- msigdbr::msigdbr(species = species)
  
  pathways <- pathways %>% 
    dplyr::filter(gs_cat %in% categories)
  
  pathways <- pathways %>% 
    # check if the pathways names ends with _DN or _UP
    # if yes, add a "-" or "+" to the end of the gene name
    dplyr::mutate(gene_symbol = dplyr::case_when(
      stringr::str_detect(gs_name, "_UP$") ~ paste0(gene_symbol, "+"),
      stringr::str_detect(gs_name, "_DN$") ~ paste0(gene_symbol, "-"),
      TRUE ~ gene_symbol
    )) %>% 
    # remove the _UP and _DN from the pathway name. 
    # this allows to combine these to by splitting using the shortend name
    dplyr::mutate(gs_name_short = stringr::str_remove(gs_name, "_UP$|_DN$"))
  
  pathways <- split(pathways$gene_symbol, pathways$gs_name_short)
  return(pathways)
}
Let’s see how that works in an example. Note that we need to set the specied to “Homo sapiens” as we are using a human scRNA dataset. But the function can be used the same way with mice data.
# Example
pathways <- getMSigDBPathways(categories = c("C2", "C7"), species = "Homo sapiens")

# a small function to show head and tail. this is just to recude the output a little bit
ht <- function(d, m=5, n=m){
  # print the head and tail together
  list(HEAD = head(d,m), TAIL = tail(d,n))
}

ht(pathways$GOLDRATH_EFF_VS_MEMORY_CD8_TCELL, 10)
## $HEAD

## 
## $TAIL
##  [1] "TYMS+"   "TYROBP+" "UBE2N+"  "UBE2T+"  "UCHL5+"  "UCK2+"   "VPS45+"  "WEE1+"   "XBP1+"   "YBX3+"

“Differential expression” with limma
Using the limma package we can see which pathways are differentially between two clusters. But for that we need to switch rows (=observations) and columns (=samples/cells).
In this example we will compare cluster3 (B cells) vs cluster 0 and 2 (CD4 cells).
library(limma)

design <- model.matrix(~0+seurat_clusters, data=pbmc@meta.data)

fit <- lmFit(t(scores), design = design)

cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(seurat_clusters3 - (seurat_clusters0 + seurat_clusters2)/2,
                            levels=design)
fit <- contrasts.fit(fit, contrasts = cont.matrix)
fit <- eBayes(fit)
## Warning: Zero sample variances detected, have been offset away from zero
# topTable gives the overall significant genelists (F statistics)
top <- topTable(fit, number = Inf) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  tibble::rownames_to_column("pathway")

title: Perpare the input
text:
In this part we will create the input files for pySCENIC using scanpy. Ultimately, this results in a loom file, that we use as a starting point for the pySCENIC pipeline.
You can use either a jupyter nootbook (run jupyter lab) or visual studie code to run the code.

title: Perpare the input
text:
Load the requires libraries
import anndata
from os import listdir
import pandas as pd
import scanpy as sc
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import pyscenic
import loompy as lp
import re

title: Perpare the input
text:
Create the anndata object
Here, we import the cellranger output and create an anndata object. For that, I created a small helper function, that loads multiple mtx files and combines them in a single anndata object.
The function assumes a folder called datasets with the following structure:
└── ty
    ├── Blood 1
    │   ├── barcodes.tsv.gz
    │   ├── features.tsv.gz
    │   └── matrix.mtx.gz
    ├── Blood 2
    │   ├── barcodes.tsv.gz
    │   ├── features.tsv.gz
    │   └── matrix.mtx.gz
    ├── Blood 3
    │   ├── barcodes.tsv.gz
    │   ├── features.tsv.gz
    │   └── matrix.mtx.gz
    ├── Fat 1
    │   ├── barcodes.tsv.gz
    │   ├── features.tsv.gz
    │   └── matrix.mtx.gz
    ├── Fat 2
    │   ├── barcodes.tsv.gz
    │   ├── features.tsv.gz
    │   └── matrix.mtx.gz
    ├── Fat 3
    │   ├── barcodes.tsv.gz
    │   ├── features.tsv.gz
    │   └── matrix.mtx.gz
    ...
We can then load all samples in the subfolder ty by running load_dataset(dataset = 'ty').
# Function to load the dataset
def load_dataset(dataset):
    # List as folder (=samples) in dataset
    samples = listdir(path = 'datasets/' + dataset + '/')
    samples = ['datasets/' + dataset + '/' + s for s in samples]
    # Read in all Samples
    # This takes up to two minutes....
    adata = [sc.read_10x_mtx(path = s, cache=True)  for s in samples]
    # Merge them
    adata = adata[0].concatenate(adata[1:])
    # Create further annotation
    # add back the samples name
    adata.obs['sample'] = adata.obs['batch'].apply(lambda x: samples[int(x)])
    # extract the tissue from the sample name
    adata.obs['tissue'] = adata.obs['sample'].apply(lambda x: re.findall(r"(\w+)[ 0-9]{0,2}$", x)[0])
    # add the datsset
    adata.obs['dataset'] = dataset
    return adata


# load the dataset
adata = load_dataset(dataset = 'ty')
As a results, you get a anndata object with all the samples. Here we have 52463 cells and 27463 genes.

sc.settings.verbosity = 3             # verbosity: errors (0), warnings (1), info (2), hints (3)

Basic filtering

sc.pp.filter_cells(adata, min_genes=200)

Basic QC
# Let’s assemble some information about mitochondrial genes, which are important for quality control.
adata.var['mt'] = adata.var_names.str.startswith('mt-')  # annotate the group of mitochondrial genes as 'mt'
sc.pp.calculate_qc_metrics(adata, qc_vars=['mt'], percent_top=None, log1p=False, inplace=True)
sc.pl.violin(adata, ['n_genes_by_counts', 'total_counts', 'pct_counts_mt'],
             jitter=0.4, multi_panel=True)
sc.pl.scatter(adata, x='total_counts', y='pct_counts_mt')
sc.pl.scatter(adata, x='total_counts', y='n_genes_by_counts')

{{< lightbox src="" caption="" >}} {{< lightbox src="pySCENIC_part1_11_2.png" caption="" >}} {{< lightbox src="pySCENIC_part1_11_3.png" caption="" >}}
We use this plots to set cutoffs of the maximal number of genes (anything above that might be doublets) and the maximal percentage of allowed mitochrondial genes.
# Do the filtering
adata = adata[adata.obs.n_genes_by_counts < 3000, :]
adata = adata[adata.obs.pct_counts_mt < 12, :]
Again, we have reduced the size of our object a little bit.
adata
View of AnnData object with n_obs × n_vars = 47399 × 16402
    obs: 'batch', 'sample', 'tissue', 'dataset', 'n_genes', 'n_genes_by_counts', 'total_counts', 'total_counts_mt', 'pct_counts_mt'
    var: 'gene_ids', 'feature_types', 'n_cells', 'mt', 'n_cells_by_counts', 'mean_counts', 'pct_dropout_by_counts', 'total_counts'

Save loom file
We save our filtered anndata object with the raw counts as a loom file. We use this as the input for the pySCENIC platform.
# create basic row and column attributes for the loom file:
row_attrs = {
    "Gene": np.array(adata.var_names) ,
}
col_attrs = {
    "CellID": np.array(adata.obs_names) ,
    "nGene": np.array( np.sum(adata.X.transpose()>0 , axis=0)).flatten() ,
    "nUMI": np.array( np.sum(adata.X.transpose() , axis=0)).flatten() ,
    "tissue": np.array(adata.obs['tissue'])
}
# Only create this once
lp.create( 'pySCENIC_input.loom', adata.X.transpose(), row_attrs, col_attrs)



Normalization
We continue following the basic 10x PBMC tutorial from scanpy the normalize the counts and create a clustering and dimenstional reductions. This will be used for further visualizations of the pySCENIC results.
# Save counts in a new layer
adata.layers['counts'] = adata.X
# Total-count normalize (library-size correct) the data matrix X to 10,000 reads per cell, so that counts become comparable among cells.
sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum=1e4)
# Logarithmize the data:
sc.pp.log1p(adata)

# save log counts to a layer
# this is not really needed, but can be helpful if you do further analysis or run MAGIC on the dataset
adata.layers['logcounts'] = adata.X

Select the highly variable genes that will be used for PCA and UMAPs.
# Identify highly variable genes
# use the dataset as batchkey
sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(adata, min_mean=0.0125, max_mean=3, min_disp=0.5)

title: Visualize TF binding sites in a Peak
text:
Generate the plot
Using this table, we can create a plot showing where the TF motif is found within the peak/region. We can put that in a small helper function.
library(tidyverse)

#' plotTFSites
#' 
#' Plots the locations of TF within a peak/region
#'
#' @param data A dataframe with the following columns: 
#' - tf: name of the transcription factor
#' - start: starting position of the motifs
#' - stop: stop position of the motif
#' - strand: + or -
#' - score: A score that is used for the alpha value in the plot
#' @param start Starting position of the range that should be plotted. Default 0
#' @param end End position of the range. Default max(data$stop)
#'
#' @return A ggplot2 object
plotTFSites <- function(data, start = 0, end = max(data$stop)) {
  # Set the TF as a factor, this is important for plotting
  # you could also change the order of the TF in the plot
  # by changing the levels of the factor here
  data$tf <- as.factor(data$tf)
  # reverse the order of the levels so, so that they appear alphabetically later
  levels(data$tf) <- rev(levels(data$tf))
  
  # Time to plot
  ggplot(data = data) +
    # draw rectangles for the TF binding sites
    geom_rect(
      mapping = aes(
        xmin = start,
        xmax = stop,
        ymin = as.numeric(tf) - .5,
        ymax = as.numeric(tf) + .5,
        fill = strand,
        alpha = score
      )
    ) +
    # add a theme to the plot
    ggthemes::theme_few() +
    # don't expand the y scale, this way the boxes go right to the border of the plot
    # also use custom labels with the TF names
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = levels(data$tf),
      breaks = seq_len(length(levels(data$tf))),
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
    # set the limits of the x axis 
    # to include the full range of the peak
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(start, end)
    ) + 
    # modify the transparency to a range from 0 to max(score)
    scale_alpha_continuous(limits = c(0, max(data$score))) +
    # use the color scheme from the NEJM
    paletteer::scale_fill_paletteer_d(palette = "ggsci::default_nejm") +
    # add horizontal lines between the TF, use the same color as for the border color of the plot
    geom_hline(yintercept = seq(1.5, length(levels(data$tf))),
               size = .3,
               color = '#4D4D4D')
}

Example
And here’s an example of how it could look like.
data <- read_tsv(file ="fimo.csv")

# we only want to keep tf that occur more than twice
tf_keep <- count(data, tf) %>%  filter(n >2) %>% pull(tf)
data <- data %>% 
  filter(tf %in% tf_keep)

plotTFSites(data)






Figure 1: Exemplary Plot

title: Co-expression of two genes
text:
In Seurat you can scale and blend expression values to visualize coexpression of two features by using the blend parameter in FeaturePlot. But you cannot change the color scale then, which can be quite ugly.
Here is a example of how you can create a similar function that allows you to use your own color scale.

title: Co-expression of two genes
text:
Code
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(magrittr)
library(Seurat)


seu <- readRDS("path/to/seurat_object.rds")

#' Blend colors
#' 
#' this is a function that we use to blend the colors. It takes the arctan
#' from the x and y vector. This results in a value between 0 and pi/2.
#' We can convert that to a range between 0 and 1  and map this value to
#' the color scale defined in col_fun.
#' The if `use_alpha=TRUE` is used, the alpha value of the color is set to the maximum of
#' either `x` and `y`. If `use_alpha=FALSE`, the individual RGB values are multiplied with
#' the maximum of `x` or `y`
#'
#' @param x A value between 0 and 1
#' @param y A value between 0 and 1
#' @param col_fun A color function defined by `circlize::colorRamp2` ranging at least from 0 to 1
#' @param bg Integer. Color for the backgroud. Raning from 0=black to 1=white
#'
#' @return The blended color as HEX
blend <- function(x, y, col_fun, bg) {
  col = col_fun(atan2(y, x) / pi * 2, return_rgb = TRUE)
    
  alpha = pmax(x, y)
  beta = 1 - alpha
  return(rgb(bg * beta + col[, 1] * alpha,
             bg * beta + col[, 2] * alpha,
             bg * beta + col[, 3] * alpha))
  

}




#' Max' Better Overlay Plot
#' 
#' Plot two parameters in a Single Cell Object at the same time.
#'
#' @param seu A `Seurat` object
#' @param gene1 String. Gene 1
#' @param gene2 String. Gene 2
#' @param col_fun col_fun A color function defined by `circlize::colorRamp2` ranging at least from 0 to 1. Passed on to `blend`
#' @param bg Integer. Color for the backgroud. Raning from 0=black to 1=white. Passed on to `blend`
#' @param n Integer fo the number of bins for the color scale.
#'
#' @return An assembled ggplot
MaxBetterOverlayPlot <- function(seu, gene1, gene2, 
                                 col_fun=circlize::colorRamp2(c(0,0.5,1), c('red', 'blue', 'green'), space = "XYZ"),
                                 bg=.2,
                                 n = 10)
{
  data <-  FetchData(
    object = seu,
    vars = c(gene1, gene2),
    slot = 'data'
  )

  colnames(data) <- c('x', 'y')
  
  data <- cbind(data, Embeddings(seu[['umap']]))
  
  max_x = max(data$x)
  max_y = max(data$y)  
  
  p1 <- data %>% 
    mutate( col = blend(x = x/max_x, 
                        y = y/max_y,
                        col_fun = col_fun,
                        bg = bg)) %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x=UMAP_1,
               y=UMAP_2,
               color = col)) +
    geom_point() +
    scale_color_identity() +
    ggthemes::theme_few()
  
  p2 <- tidyr::expand_grid(x=0:n, y=0:n) %>% 
    mutate(col = blend(x = x/n, 
                       y = y/n,
                       col_fun = col_fun,
                       bg = bg)) %>%
    mutate(x = x/n * max_x,
           y = y/n * max_y) %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x=x,y=y, fill=col)) +
    geom_raster() +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = 'none') +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    xlab(gene1) + ylab(gene2) +
    ggthemes::theme_few()
  
  p1 + p2
  
}

MaxBetterOverlayPlot(seu, 'Itgae', 'Klrg1')
MaxBetterOverlayPlot(seu, 'Itgae', 'Klrg1', bg = .95)
MaxBetterOverlayPlot(seu, 'Itgae', 'Klrg1', bg = 0)

# range need to be from 0 to 1
my_colors = circlize::colorRamp2(c(0,.3,.6,1), c('red', 'pink', 'green', 'orange'))
MaxBetterOverlayPlot(seu, 'Itgae', 'Klrg1', bg = .2,
                     col_fun = my_colors)

MaxBetterOverlayPlot(seu, 'Itgae', 'Klrg1', bg = .2,
                     col_fun = my_colors,
                     n = 100)

title: Download and align RNA Seq files
section: Downlod the RNA Seq data: fastq files
text:
Downlod the RNA Seq data: fastq files
Nextflow provides a pipeline that automatically download the data from GEO: https://nf-co.re/fetchngs. In this example, we will download files from GSE198874. On the bottom of that page, you can see a link SRA Run Selector. Click on that. On the next page click on Accession List to download the file. Save it! Next, on you computer (I use TSCC), create a directory for you project. e.g. mkdir MY_EXCITING_PROJECT && cd MY_EXCITING_PROJECT. Within that, create a folder where we download the fastq files. E.g. mkdir 01_download_fastq. To run nextflow on the TSCC, we need to create a config file to tell the programm which queues to use. Eg home-yeo or condo. Create a file using vim called nextflow.config with the following content:
process {
    executor = 'pbs'
    queue = 'home-yeo'
}
singularity.cacheDir = '/home/mheeg/scratch/nextflow/singularity'
The singularity.cacheDir is optional.
Let’s start the pipeline and download the files:
# activate the conda environment
conda activate nextflow

# start the pipeline
nextflow  run nf-core/fetchngs\
    --input  01_download_fastq/SRR_Acc_List.txt\
    --outdir 01_download_fastq\
    -profile singularity
Depending on the number of samples and the internet speed, this might take a while.

section: Align the samples using the nextflow pipeline
text:
Align the samples using the nextflow pipeline
Using the fastq files, we can run the rnaseq pipeline to align the samples. Let’s create a new subfolder for that anaylsis: mkdir 02_RNA-Seq. Within that folder, we need to create a samplesheet. Luckily, we can start by copying a template from the fetchngs pipeline that we ran above: cp 01_download_fastq/samplesheet/samplesheet.csv 02_RNA-Seq/ Use your favorite editor (vim, what else?) to modify the file: It needs four columns: sample, fastq_1, fastq_2, and strandedness. After editing it, mine looked as follows:

NTC 1,01_download_fastq/fastq/SRX14493516_SRR18358794_1.fastq.gz,01_download_fastq/fastq/SRX14493516_SRR18358794_2.fastq.gz,auto
NTC 2,01_download_fastq/fastq/SRX14493517_SRR18358793_1.fastq.gz,01_download_fastq/fastq/SRX14493517_SRR18358793_2.fastq.gz,auto

Next, we can run the pipeline. This performs QC, trimming and alignment. Make sure that you have the nextflow conda environment still activated.
nextflow run nf-core/rnaseq \
    --input 02_RNA-Seq/samplesheet.csv\
    --genome GRCm38\
    -profile singularity\
    --igenomes_base /home/mheeg/projects/igenomes/\
    --outdir 02_RNA-Seq -resume
The --igenomes_base is optional, but it is a lot faster if you don’t need to download the genome every time. Once this is done, we can import the counts into DESeq2.

title: Download and align RNA Seq files
text:
Basic analysis in DESeq2
Importing the data into R is quite easy. One of the outputs of the pipeline is an rds file with the counts data. The file can be found in the follwoing location: ./02_RNA-Seq/star_salmon/salmon.merged.gene_counts.rds. For the analysis, you don’t need to use the supercomputer anymore. Any laptop should be fast enough. So copy that file to your computer. We can then import that, make some minor adjustments and finally run DESeq2.

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2)
  library(DESeq2)
})

# Set a custom theme for the plots, not requiered, but it looks better
theme_max <- function(base_size = 12, base_family="Avenir Next"){ 
    theme_bw(base_size = base_size, base_family = base_family) %+replace%    #replace elements we want to change
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(), 
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#EEEEEE", colour = NA)
    )
}
theme_set(theme_max())

# Setup the dds object
# Import the summarized Experiment
gse <- readRDS("salmon.merged.gene_counts.rds")
# Lets remove the replicate from the sample name
# we will use this for the desgin in DESeq2
gse$condition <- sub("_.*", "",gse$names)
gse$replicate <- sub(".*_", "",gse$names)
# Some 'count' have small rounding errors (eg 10.0001)
# We need to convert that to integers for DESeq2
assay(gse, 'counts') <- as.matrix(round(assay(gse, 'counts')))
# Create the DESeq2 dataset.
dds <- DESeqDataSet(gse, ~condition)

dds <- DESeq(dds)


PCA plots
vsd <- vst(dds, blind = FALSE)
plotPCA(vsd, intgroup="condition") + theme_max()

title: Convert human genes to mouse
text:
Converting human gene symbols to mouse gene symbols in R.
convertHumanGeneList <- function(x){
    require(biomaRt)
    human = useEnsembl(biomart = "genes", dataset = "hsapiens_gene_ensembl")
    mouse = useEnsembl(biomart = "genes", dataset = "mmusculus_gene_ensembl")
    genesV2 = getLDS(attributes = c("hgnc_symbol"), 
                     filters = "hgnc_symbol", 
                     values = x , 
                     mart = human, 
                     attributesL = c("mgi_symbol"), 
                     martL = mouse, 
                     uniqueRows=T)
    new_symbols <- unique(genesV2[, 2])
    return(new_symbols)
}

Column purification of streptavidin-bound cells

Attach MACS column to magnet
Pre-treat MACS column with 3 mL MACS buffer and discard flow-through
Run cell solution through column, collecting flow-through
Wash column three times (3X) with 3 mL MACS buffer
Centrifuge at 1600 rpm for 4 min and discard supernatant

title: Treg isolation
text:
Treg isolation
Spleen/LN processing:

Sac WT B6 mice. Process LN and spleen from each mouse through 70 and 40 um.
Count cells.

Treg MACS isolation
Magnetic labeling of non-CD4+ cells + labeling of CD25+ cells
*Work fast and keep all reagents on ice
MACS enrichment of Tregs/Tconvs: primary labeling reagent will leave all non-CD4+ T cells bound on the LD column. Secondary labeling reagent will label CD25+ cells so flow through from LD column = Tconvs on column = Tregs.

Determine cell number:






Centrifuge cells at 300xg for 10 min, aspirate supernatant completely
Resuspend pellet in 40uL of MACS buffer per 107 cells:

WT: ___ million cells, Resuspend in ___ ul of MACS

Add 10uL of the CD4+CD25+ Regulatory T cell Biotin antibody cocktail per 1e7 cells






Incubate for 10 min in the fridge (2-8C)
Add 38uL of MACS buffer, 20uL of anti-biotin MACS beads, and 2uL of CD25 PE antibody per 1e7 cells






Mix well and incubate for an additional 15 min in the fridge

Magnetic separation: Depletion of non-CD4+ T cells

Place LD column in the magnet, rinse with 3 ml of MACS buffer
Apply cell suspension onto the column
Collect the cells that pass through – THIS IS THE CD4+ T CELL POPULATION
Wash the column with 2x1mL of MACS buffer and collect
Take off column from magnet and wash 2x with 1 ml to get the non-CD4 T cell population

Magnetic Labeling of CD25+ T cells

Centrifuge suspension for 5 min at 300xg, aspirate completely
Resuspend cell pellet in 90uL of buffer
Add 10uL of anti-PE microbeads
Mix well and incubate for 15 min in the fridge
Bring to 500uL volume in MACS buffer
Magnetic Separation: positive selection of CD4+CD25+ Regulatory T cells
Place MS column in the magnetic field, rinse with 500 uL of MACS buffer
Apply cells to column: FT IS TCONVS –SAVE
Wash with 2x 500 uL MACS buffer – SAVE
Remove column from separator and add place on a collection tube
Add 1mL of buffer to column and immediately flush out beads by firmly pressing on column with plunger (2x)
Confirm Treg isolation by flow

CD4: BUV496
CD8: BUV737
GITR: BV711
CD25 PE*
Foxp3 APC

title: Ficoll protocol for removing dead cells
text:
Usually used when culturing cells in vitro & prior to transfer in vitro

Condense in vitro cell culture into 5ml media by spinning cells down and removing excess media (do not condense more than 50ml to 5ml, or you will overload your gradient) and transfer into a 15ml conical tube. After removing media, make sure cells are well resuspended in remaining 5ml media.
Gently layer 2ml Lymphocyte Separation Media (aka Ficoll – in Hedrick TC fridge) into the bottom of the 15ml conical, being careful to keep a distinct interface between the media and Lymphocyte Separation Media by pipetting slowly and preventing air bubbles. Can also use glass pipette like we use for percoll to layer in ficoll.
Spin cells at 2000 RPM for 15 minutes in chilled centrifuge.
After the spin, the live cells can be found at the interface between the media and Lymphocyte Separation Media, while the dead cells will be found at the bottom of the tube. Carefully pipette live cells into a fresh tube, wash cells with additional media, and spin down again.

title: 080221 in vitro TRM - Zaph lab, NES optimized
text:
Materials
- naïve CD8 T cells
- anti-CD3e Ab
- anti-CD28 Ab
- Dulbecco’s PBS
- complete RPMI (cRPMI)

-RPMI 1640 media,
-Fetal Calf Serum,
-Hepes 1M,
-L-glutamine 200 mM,
-Pen strep 5000 units,
-5*10-2M β-mercaptoethanol

Cytokines
- hIL-2
- Mouse IL-15
- Mouse TGFβ
- Retinoic acid ≥98% (HPLC) powder
➡ Retinoic acid prep:
1. 0.0015 g/ml for 5 mM stock in ETOH in black tubes, store at -20deg
2. 1:1000 dilution in PBS (5 μM working dilution, use day-of only (i.e., make fresh every time))
3. Add 1:250 into polarisation stock for final conc. 10 nM
Method
1. Coat a flat bottom 6-well plate with anti-CD3 (1 μg/ml for TRM, 3ug/ml for control/effector T cells) in 1ml PBS per well, and place at 37deg for 3hr.
2. Per mouse, harvest the spleen and peripheral lymph nodes. Magnetically isolate CD8 T cells per lab protocol.
3. PBS is removed after 3hr and enriched CD8+ T cells are gently plated at a density of 5 million cells per well in complete RPMI (cRPMI - a media containing RPMI supplemented with 10% FCS, 2.5% 1M HEPES, 1% 200 mM L-glutamine, 1% PenStrep (10000 U/ml penicillin + 10000 μg/ml streptomycin) and 0.1% 5*10-2M β-mercaptoethanol) along with 2ug/ml anti-CD28 and 50U/ml IL2. I usually do 2ml media per well. Plates are incubated at 37 ̊C in 5% CO2.
4. After 24hr, cells are taken off stimulation, washed with cRPMI, spin down, and replate either with 25U/ml IL2 for control/effector T cells or with TRM polarizing media: 25U/ml IL-2, 10ng/ml IL-15, 10ng/ml TGFβ and 10nM retinoic acid.
5. Cell media is doubled every 48hr with new cytokines added only for the volume of media added. Old media is not removed. A fresh working dilution of atRA is needed every time additional media is added since atRA is light sensitive.
6. Cells can be used/analyzed on day 7.

title: ICS_GP33 peptide restim
text:
Intracellular cytokine stain/peptide restim
Reconstitute peptide

Dissolve gp33-41 in DMSO. If 1 mg of peptide, reconstitute peptide in 250 ul media to get 4 mg/ml

Lymph node and spleen collection

Take all lymph nodes and spleen
Process through 70 and 40 um filters
Flow stain or start peptide stim
Count cells
To start peptide stim, plate 5% of spleen (250 ul from 5 ml of spleen resuspended in media) into well in 96 well u-bottom plate
If some samples are a little lower or higher, this is okay. Use a standard volume across samples (use cell count to relate back to spleen)
Spin plate at 1500 RPM for 3 min

Make stim media (gp33 + Golgi Plug)

Calculate the amount of media you will need by multiplying your number of samples by 200 ul. Account for unstim here. You can make an unstim sample for each mouse (just golgi plug in media no gp33) or a pooled unstim sample per tissue.
Add Golgi Plug to media at 1:500 (500x cocktail)
Partion off the amount you will need for stim vs unstim into two separate tubes
To the stim tube, add peptide. To the unstim tube, add nothing.

Prepare peptide for stim

When time to use the peptide, make an intermediate dilution of 1:10 with media to get to 0.4 mg/ml (0.4 ug/ul
Then, add 1 ul (at 0.4 mg/ml) for every 1 ml of media to bring final concentration to 0.4 ug/ml
Flick plate and resuspend in media supplemented with gp33 + golgi plug (stim samples) or golgi plug (unstim samples)
Incubate at 37C for 4-6 hours

text:
Ex vivo peptide restim: OVA/OT-I
Plate cells from dLN, tumor, spleen

Plate cells. 2 million cells per sample is a good starting point. Add spleen (~5% which is 250 of 5 ml), lymph nodes (all), tumors (all). Plate however many plates you need according to map. Remember to include unstim wells as these will be the best control for cytokines.
Spin plate at 1500 RPM for 3 min and flick. Resuspend in R10 +/- peptide detailed below.
Proceed with ICCS plate first and setting up ex vivo stim and then while ICCS plate is incubating, proceed with surface staining

Ex vivo stimulation 
Reagents needed:

Golgi plug (Golgi plug has BFA and Golgi stop has monensin)
OVA 257-264 peptide
R10 media




Make up dilution of R10 +stim condition (no stim, OVA257-264 peptide)


Make enough for 200 ul per well (R10 + golgi plug for unstim controls, R10 + golgi plug + peptide for experimental wells, or R10 + golgi plug + PMA for positive control).


Add in a 1:1000 dilution of Golgi Plug into media before distributing to three groups. I have 10 mls for each condition, so 30 mls total (e.g. add 30 ul of GP into media and then divide into each condition)




Unstim: do not add peptide but should have golgi plug
For OVA 257-264: From -80 stock make an intermediate 1:1000 dilution in R10 to go from 3 mM to 3 uM (e.g. 3 ul into 3 mls). Then add into media as a 1:300 solution (e.g. add 33.3 ul of 1:1000 solution into 10 mls of R10) 




Add 200uL of each master mix to appropriate wells. Mix well. 


Incubate cells at 37 for 4 hours. 


During 4-hour incubation, continue protocol with other panels. After 4-hour incubation, proceed with protocol with surface staining + ICCS plate.

title: Human PBMC Ex vivo Dynabead multiday stim
text:
Ex vivo anti-CD3/28 Dynabead multiday stim of human PBMC to measure cytokine production
Donor Vial info:
PBMC cell count:
If using fresh PBMC:
PBMC isolation from whole blood in CPT tube

Invert CPT tube 2-4 times
Centrifuge CPTs at 1800 G for 30 minutes at room temperature, 9-1 acceleration/deceleration (handle with care and keep tubes upright after centrifuging). 
Remove plasma layer being careful not to disrupt cell layer (cloudy layer between CPT gel and plasma).   
Pour remaining plasma and cells from CPT tubes into a 50 mL Falcon tube 


NOTE:  No more than 6 CPTs per 50mL Falcon tube, if you have more than 6 divide them evenly into 2 or more Falcon tubes (they can be combined at the lyse step). 


Rinse CPTs 2-3x using ≈ 7mL of RPMI by pipetting up and down.
Dispense each wash from the CPTs into the 50 mL Falcon tube along with the cells in step 4
Bring Falcon tube volume up to 50 mL using RPMI 
Centrifuge at 1500RPM for 5 minutes at RT, aspirate the supernatant, mechanically disrupt pellet by raking
Resuspend cells in 10 ml High Yield Lyse (Thermofisher) and incubate at RT for 10 mins.
Bring volume up to 50 mL using RPMI, mixing gently. 



Centrifuge at 1500RPM for 5 minutes at RT, aspirate the supernatant, mechanically disrupt pellet by raking, resuspend in 2 mL to count cells. Cell count: average dilution 1:5 in 4% trypan blue (80ul trypan plus 20uL cells)

If using frozen PBMC:
Thawing cryopreserved PBMC for immunophenotyping
Protocol modified from here: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6060642/

Place a cryopreserved PBMC vial in a 37°C water bath. Submerge the cryovial halfway and thaw for 60 seconds.
PBMCs were frozen at 6-7 million cells in 1ml of freezing medium for 1 min.
Add 1 mL of warmed (37°C) complete RPMI slowly dropwise to the thawed PBMCs against the side of the cryovial using a transfer pipette.
Pipette the thawed PBMCs into 5 mL (per vial so 10 ml if thawing two vials) of complete RPMI in a 15ml conical tube that has been warmed to 37°C (no pipetting). Make sure to wipe down the tube
Rinse the cryovials once with 1 mL of warm complete RPMI, pipette the PBMCs into the conical tube with the cell mixture.
Incubate the PBMCs for 5 minutes in the 37°C water bath.
Take aliquot to count cells.

Cell Count Pre-Rest: 1.76e6/ml. 98% viability. 2.5 mls. 4.4e6 cells total.

Centrifuge the PBMCs for 10 minutes at 300xg at room temperature.
Pour off the supernatant. This will leave a small amount of complete RPMI behind that aids in pellet resuspension.
Add 1 mL of pre-warmed complete RPMI. Mix by flicking or racking the tube (avoid pipetting up and down).
Incubate the PBMCs for one hour at 37°C in a CO2 water jacketed incubator (37°C, 5% CO2, 95% humidity). Leave the cap of the conical tube slightly loose so that gas transfer can occur.
Centrifuge the PBMCs for 10 minutes at 300xg at room temperature.
Resuspend in complete RPMI to 10e6/ml.
Take aliquot to count cells

Cell Count Post-Rest:
Multi-day anti-CD3/28 Dynabead stimulation


Prepare CD3/CD28 beads (Invitrogen Dynabeads Human T-Activator CD3/CD28) 


Vortex 30 seconds 


Add beads to 1.5 mL conical (15 ul per 1 ml sample in manufacturer protocol)


Add 1 mL FACS 


Vortex 30 seconds 


Place on magnet 1-2 minute 


Remove supernatant


Add equal parts R10 to the bead volume used in step 4 (resulting concentration beads to R10 ratio is 1:1)


Add media to well of 48 well plate, correct up to 1 ml (1 ml – 100 ul cells – 15 ul beads = 885 ul of media


Plate 1-1.2 million cells in 100 ul into R10 in 48 well plate *Easier on cells to add media first then cells then beads*


Add washed beads to cells in media in 48 well plate. 15ul of anti-CD3/28 beads per well of 1 ml media.


Add protein, antibody of interest or PBS as a control to respective wells.


Incubate 1-3 days


Four hours prior to harvest, add GolgiStop at 1 ug/ml


Surface stain

After 4 hrs, spin and dump supernatant.
Add surface stain master mix to samples. Ab at 1:100
Stain all samples in surface antibody cocktail at room temp for 20 minutes, covered in foil. Make comps during this time. Make FMOs!
Add 1 ml of FACS, spin, dump supernatant. Repeat.

Live/Dead staining

Stain each sample with 1 ml live dead (1 ul L/D Aqua per 1 ml PBS)

LIVE/DEAD™ Fixable Aqua Dead Cell Stain Kit, for 405 nm excitation Thermofisher, L34965 *Live/dead stain is on same channel as CD14, CD19 to serve as a dump channel on BV510*

Incubate at room temp for 10 mins, covered in foil.
Wash 1x with FACS

Cytokine and transcription factor staining

Make fixation buffer (1:3 fix to diluent)
Add 250uL/sample. Fix perm= 5mL fix, 15mL diluent
Incubate for 20min at 4C in dark.
At end of fixation incubation, wash 1x with 1X perm buffer (1:10 dilution with diH20)
Stain with fluorochromes for 25-30 min at 4C in dark in perm buffer.
Wash 1X with perm buffer. Wash 1X with FACS.
Resuspend samples in 100uL FACS, transfer to microtubes, and flow.

Notes

Pour off the supernatant. This will leave a small amount of complete RPMI behind that aids in pellet resuspension.
Add 1 mL of pre-warmed complete RPMI. Mix by flicking or racking the tube (avoid pipetting up and down).
Incubate the PBMCs for one hour at 37°C in a CO2 water jacketed incubator (37°C, 5% CO2, 95% humidity). Leave the cap of the conical tube slightly loose so that gas transfer can occur.
Centrifuge the PBMCs for 10 minutes at 300xg at room temperature.
Resuspend in complete RPMI to 10e6/ml.
Take aliquot to count cells

Cell Count Post-Rest:
Multi-day anti-CD3/28 Dynabead stimulation


Prepare CD3/CD28 beads (Invitrogen Dynabeads Human T-Activator CD3/CD28) 


Vortex 30 seconds 


Add beads to 1.5 mL conical (15 ul per 1 ml sample in manufacturer protocol)


Add 1 mL FACS 


Vortex 30 seconds 


Place on magnet 1-2 minute 


Remove supernatant


Add equal parts R10 to the bead volume used in step 4 (resulting concentration beads to R10 ratio is 1:1)


Add media to well of 48 well plate, correct up to 1 ml (1 ml – 100 ul cells – 15 ul beads = 885 ul of media


Plate 1-1.2 million cells in 100 ul into R10 in 48 well plate *Easier on cells to add media first then cells then beads*


Add washed beads to cells in media in 48 well plate. 15ul of anti-CD3/28 beads per well of 1 ml media.


Add protein, antibody of interest or PBS as a control to respective wells.


Incubate 1-3 days


4 hour PMA restimulation

Pipette up and down thoroughly to resuspend cells and transfer to flow tubes and place on magnet 1-2 min to remove Dynabeads 
Aspirate supernatant (including cells; leaving beads behind) and transfer to clean flow tubes 
Wash flow tubes still containing beads by washing well in 48 well plate with 500 ul of FACS, then transfer FACS used to wash well into the respective tube on the magnet
Take tube off magnet, vortex, and put the tube back on the magnet and let sit on magnet for 1-2 min 
Repeat steps 3-4 once more
Aspirate the supernatant while tube is still on the magnet as in step 2 and add supernatant to appropriate flow tubes already containing cells debeaded in step 2.
Discard tubes containing CD3/CD28 beads 
Spin flow tubes with cells at 1500 RPM for 5 min 
Dump supernatant, wash in 1 ml of FACS, and dump supernatant 
Resuspend samples in 500 ul of R10 media only (for unstim controls), or 500 ul of R10 with 1 mg/ml of PMA, 0.7 mg/ml of ionomycin, and 1 ul/ml of GolgiStop into each tube besides unstim.

Surface stain

After 4 hrs, spin and dump supernatant.
Add surface stain master mix to samples. Ab at 1:100
Stain all samples in surface antibody cocktail at room temp for 20 minutes, covered in foil. Make comps and FMOs during this time.
Add 1 ml of FACS, spin, dump supernatant. Repeat.

Live/Dead staining

Stain each sample with 1 ml live dead (1 ul L/D Aqua per 1 ml PBS)

LIVE/DEAD™ Fixable Aqua Dead Cell Stain Kit, for 405 nm excitation Thermofisher, L34965 *Live/dead stain is on same channel as CD14, CD19 to serve as a dump channel on BV510*

Incubate at room temp for 10 mins, covered in foil.
Wash 1x with FACS

Cytokine and transcription factor staining

Make fixation buffer (1:3 fix to diluent)
Add 250uL/sample. Fix perm= 5mL fix, 15mL diluent
Incubate for 20min at 4C in dark.
At end of fixation incubation, wash 1x with 1X perm buffer (1:10 dilution with diH20)
Stain with fluorochromes for 25-30 min at 4C in dark in perm buffer.
Wash 1X with perm buffer. Wash 1X with FACS.
Resuspend samples in 100uL FACS, transfer to microtubes, and flow.

Notes

title: Human PBMC Ex vivo Dynabead multiday stim_prolif&apoptosis
text:
Ex vivo anti-CD3/28 Dynabead stim of human PBMC to measure proliferation and apoptosis
Donor Vial info:
PBMC cell count:
If using fresh PBMC:
PBMC isolation from whole blood in CPT tube

Invert CPT tube 2-4 times
Centrifuge CPTs at 1800 G for 30 minutes at room temperature, 9-1 acceleration/deceleration (handle with care and keep tubes upright after centrifuging). 
Remove plasma layer being careful not to disrupt cell layer (cloudy layer between CPT gel and plasma).   
Pour remaining plasma and cells from CPT tubes into a 50 mL Falcon tube 


NOTE:  No more than 6 CPTs per 50mL Falcon tube, if you have more than 6 divide them evenly into 2 or more Falcon tubes (they can be combined at the lyse step). 


Rinse CPTs 2-3x using ≈ 7mL of RPMI by pipetting up and down.
Dispense each wash from the CPTs into the 50 mL Falcon tube along with the cells in step 4
Bring Falcon tube volume up to 50 mL using RPMI 
Centrifuge at 1500RPM for 5 minutes at RT, aspirate the supernatant, mechanically disrupt pellet by raking
Resuspend cells in 10 ml High Yield Lyse (Thermofisher) and incubate at RT for 10 mins.
Bring volume up to 50 mL using RPMI, mixing gently. 



Centrifuge at 1500RPM for 5 minutes at RT, aspirate the supernatant, mechanically disrupt pellet by raking, resuspend in 2 mL to count cells. Cell count: average dilution 1:5 in 4% trypan blue (80ul trypan plus 20uL cells)

If using frozen PBMC:
Thawing cryopreserved PBMC for immunophenotyping
Protocol modified from here: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6060642/

Place a cryopreserved PBMC vial in a 37°C water bath. Submerge the cryovial halfway and thaw for 60 seconds.
PBMCs were frozen at 6-7 million cells in 1ml of freezing medium for 1 min.
Add 1 mL of warmed (37°C) complete RPMI slowly dropwise to the thawed PBMCs against the side of the cryovial using a transfer pipette.
Pipette the thawed PBMCs into 5 mL (per vial so 10 ml if thawing two vials) of complete RPMI in a 15ml conical tube that has been warmed to 37°C (no pipetting). Make sure to wipe down the tube
Rinse the cryovials once with 1 mL of warm complete RPMI, pipette the PBMCs into the conical tube with the cell mixture.
Incubate the PBMCs for 5 minutes in the 37°C water bath.
Take aliquot to count cells.

Cell Count Pre-Rest:

Centrifuge the PBMCs for 10 minutes at 300xg at room temperature.
Pour off the supernatant. This will leave a small amount of complete RPMI behind that aids in pellet resuspension.
Add 1 mL of pre-warmed complete RPMI. Mix by flicking or racking the tube (avoid pipetting up and down).
Incubate the PBMCs for one hour at 37°C in a CO2 water jacketed incubator (37°C, 5% CO2, 95% humidity). Leave the cap of the conical tube slightly loose so that gas transfer can occur.
Centrifuge the PBMCs for 10 minutes at 300xg at room temperature.
Resuspend in complete RPMI to 10e6/ml.
Take aliquot to count cells

Cell Count Post-Rest: 9.9e5/ml. 97% viability. 2.47e6 cells total.
Anti-CD3/28 Dynabead stimulation


Prepare CD3/CD28 beads (Invitrogen Dynabeads Human T-Activator CD3/CD28) 


Vortex 30 seconds 


Add beads to 1.5 mL conical (15 ul per 1 ml sample in manufacturer protocol)


Add 1 mL FACS 


Vortex 30 seconds 


Place on magnet 1-2 minute 


Remove supernatant


Add equal parts R10 to the bead volume used in step 4 (resulting concentration beads to R10 ratio is 1:1)


Add media to well of 48 well plate, correct up to 1 ml (1 ml – 100 ul cells – 15 ul beads = 885 ul of media


Plate 1-1.2 million cells in 100 ul into R10 in 48 well plate *Easier on cells to add media first then cells then beads*


Add washed beads to cells in media in 48 well plate. 15ul of anti-CD3/28 beads per well of 1 ml media.


Add protein, antibody of interest or PBS as a control to respective wells.


Incubate 1-3 days


After Stimulation cell processing and surface staining

Pipette up and down thoroughly to resuspend cells and transfer to flow tubes and place on magnet 1-2 min to remove Dynabeads 
Aspirate supernatant (including cells; leaving beads behind) and transfer to clean flow tubes 
Wash flow tubes still containing beads by washing well in 48 well plate with 500 ul of FACS, then transfer FACS used to wash well into the respective tube on the magnet
Take tube off magnet, vortex, and put the tube back on the magnet and let sit on magnet for 1-2 min 
Repeat steps 3-4 once more
Aspirate the supernatant while tube is still on the magnet as in step 2 and add supernatant to appropriate flow tubes already containing cells debeaded in step 2.
Discard tubes containing CD3/CD28 beads 
Spin flow tubes with cells at 1500 RPM for 5 min 
Dump supernatant, wash in 1 ml of FACS, and dump supernatant 
Add master mix. Ab at 1:100
Stain all samples in surface antibody cocktail at room temp for 20 minutes, covered in foil. Make comps and FMOs during this time.
Add 1 ml of FACS, spin, dump supernatant. Repeat.

Live/Dead staining

Stain each sample with 1 ml live dead (1 ul L/D Aqua per 1 ml PBS)

LIVE/DEAD™ Fixable Aqua Dead Cell Stain Kit, for 405 nm excitation Thermofisher, L34965 *Live/dead stain is on same channel as CD14, CD19 to serve as a dump channel on BV510*

Incubate at room temp for 10 mins, covered in foil.
Wash 1x with FACS

Ki67 staining

Make fixation buffer (1:3 fix to diluent)
Add 250uL/sample. Fix perm= 5mL fix, 15mL diluent
Incubate for 20min at 4C in dark.
At end of fixation incubation, wash 1x with 1X perm buffer (1:10 dilution with diH20)
Stain with nuclear fluorochromes for 25-30 min at 4C in dark in perm buffer.
Wash 1X with perm buffer. Wash 1X with FACS.
Resuspend samples in 100uL FACS, transfer to microtubes, and flow.

Caspase staining

Caspase staining cannot be performed on fixed cells. If performing intracellular staining, do not perform caspase staining.
Thaw caspase 3/7 reagent (CellEvent™ Caspase-3/7 Green Flow Cytometry Assay Kit Thermofisher, C10427)
While thawing, move caspase samples to flow tubes/microtubes and wash again. Aspirate or dump, as long as 100 ul is left in tube.
Heat block the samples that you want to have more cell death (eg- positive control, comp controls). Let samples sit on heat block at 65C for 5 min. An FMO for caspase 3/7 and an FMO for 7AAD is especially important here. Heat block both of them here.
Make caspase stock solution—add 1 ul of caspase reagent to 1 ml of FACS (1:1000 dilution), add 100ul of solution to each tube of 100ul FACS already there (1:2000 final dilution) and incubate at 37C for 30 min. *Manufacturer says 1:1000 but this is very bright, 1:2000 is better.
Make 7AAD stock solution (after diluting in DMSO)
After making the stock solution, add 2.5 ul of 7AAD to 500 ul of FACS (1:200 dilution). Add 50ul of this solution to each sample tube that already has 200ul FACS in it from caspase staining (1:1000 final dilution). *Requires flow samples to be run immediately after caspase 3/7/7AAD stain as there is not quech step afterwards. Have compensation and experiment ready to run samples. You can batch the time you add caspase and 7AAD by tissue type so some samples are not incubating while you’re running the other tissues. This step is especially time sensitive, plan accordingly or you will have overstaining with the reagents.

Notes

title: CB18.Red blood cell lysis with ACK buffer
text:
Red Blood Cell lysis with ACK buffer (CB18)
Materials:

ACK buffer 1X
sample
Sterile physiological saline solution (NaCl 0,9%. Baxter) or 1X PBS /HBSS
Falcons (50mL)

ACK 10X buffer preparation

Make it in H20 (final volume 200 mL)



Store at 4°C
At the moment you need: dilute in H20 to obtain 1X solution and allow it to reach the room temperature. Do not store.

Protocol

Add 5-10 mL of ACK Lysing Buffer to the cell pellet.
Allow the blood sample plus ACK Lysing Buffer to incubate at room temperature for 3 – 5 minutes. Lysis of the red cells should be evident during this incubation.
Collect the white blood cells by centrifugation at 1600 rpm for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant, leaving approximately 50 uL to avoid disturbing the pellet.
Gently mix the cells and the remaining fluid, then add 10 mL sterile physiological saline solution.
Collect the cells by centrifugation at 1600 rpm for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant. The cells are ready for further analysis.
